```markdown
# Two-Ingredient Ice Cream Recipe System

## Ingredients and Preparation Time
- INPUT: 1/2 cup of honey
- INPUT: 2 1/2 cups of cream (35% fat)
- INPUT: 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract (optional)
- INPUT: A teensie bit of vanilla bean (optional)
- OUTPUT: Prep time is 10 minutes.
- OUTPUT: Freeze time is 6 hours.

## Step-by-Step Recipe Instructions

START:

PROCESS: Begin with the initial preparation.

  PROCESS: Whip the cream.
    INPUT: Take 1.5 cups of whipping cream.
    DECISION [IF]: Is vanilla extract being used?
      - Yes: INPUT: Add 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract to the cream.
      - No: Continue without vanilla extract.
    PROCESS: Whip the cream (with vanilla extract if added) until it forms stiff peaks.
    OUTPUT: Whipped cream with stiff peaks.
    PROCESS: Refrigerate the whipped cream.

  PROCESS: Prepare the honey and cream mixture.
    PROCESS: Heat the honey.
      INPUT: Take 1/2 cup of honey.
      PROCESS: Heat the honey on low heat until it is very runny.
      OUTPUT: Runny honey.
    INPUT: Take the remaining 1 cup of cream.
    PROCESS: Combine the runny honey and 1 cup of cream.
      DECISION [IF]: Is vanilla bean being used?
        - Yes: INPUT: Grate in a teensie bit of vanilla bean into the mixture.
        - No: Continue without vanilla bean.
    PROCESS: Stir the honey and cream (and vanilla bean if added) until well blended.
    OUTPUT: Well-blended honey/cream mixture.

  PROCESS: Combine whipped cream and honey/cream mixture.
    PROCESS: Add the honey/cream mixture to the refrigerated whipped cream.
    PROCESS: Whisk the mixture until well blended.
    OUTPUT: Ice cream mixture ready to be frozen.

  PROCESS: Freeze the ice cream mixture.
    PROCESS: Place the ice cream mixture in the freezer.
    PROCESS: Freeze for approximately 6 hours.
    DECISION [IF]: Has the mixture reached the consistency of ice cream after 6 hours?
      - Yes: OUTPUT: Ice cream is ready to be served.
      - No: PROCESS: Continue freezing until the desired consistency is achieved.

END: The ice cream is ready to enjoy.
```

instruct00780.title: A Basic Clean for Outdoor AC Units
instruct00780.text: With summer approaching soon comes the time to turn on the AC to keep the house cold. You might notice that your electric bill spikes up more than expected or that your house is just having trouble staying cold. If it's been more than a few years sense your last AC unit cleaning (or you cant remember ever having them cleaned) then its probably time for a clean. It's a fairly easy process so save some money by doing it yourself! Whenever doing ANY work with electronics its important to turn the electricity off and check voltage on the unit with a multimeter. Again, DO NOT WORK ON LIVE ELECTRONICS. For this particular project the risk isn't as much to do with shock (though this still exists and adding water to the mix is even more reason to be cautious) but more to do with fear of the unit turning on and spinning fan blades. Most units should have an electronics box near the unit on the outside of the building. Open it up and flip the switch to the OFF position. The tool list for this project isn't a long one. A ratchet set, flat head screwdriver, a multimeter, and maybe a mallet are all you will need. I prefer using a ratchet set over the flat head simply because I find flat heads tedious to use. The metal shielding surrounding the unit needs to be removed. Go around the unit removing the screws holding the shield on and once they are all removed it should come off with little trouble. Using a garden hose with low/no pressure spray the outside to remove buildup of dust, dirt, leaves, and whatever else is stuck on the side. The units pictured are extreme examples of buildup. Much less buildup can still cause issues in cooling. Start by spraying off the outside at an angle and the buildup will come off in a 'Peeling' fashion. Then finish up by spraying from the inside out to clean out debris stuck within the fins. (When the buildup is high the fins wont allow enough water to get through to effectively clean the outside without first spraying the outside) While the unit is open I clean out any debris that has built up at the bottom of the unit. Continue spraying around until the unit appears clean. Use very low pressure to avoid bending fins, just an open hose end should do. All that's left is putting the unit back together, cleaning up, and turning the electricity back on. You should notice an improvement in cooling in your house and you didn't have to spend $100+ to get it. Final notes: Not all units are the same. This second unit pictured is different in that the side shielding is "capped" by the top piece instead of screwing into the side. Your unit will more than likely differ slightly from the two pictured but the concept is the same regardless of the unit.Also, this is a very basic cleaning of the units. It will improve efficiency greatly in the unit. However, a good professional service will be much more thorough.Read comments below for additional ideas anddiscussion

```markdown
# AC Unit Cleaning Process

## Summary
This process provides a step-by-step guide on how to clean an AC unit to improve its efficiency and cooling performance. Cleaning is recommended if the unit has not been serviced in a few years or if there is noticeable difficulty in keeping the house cool. The instructions include safety precautions, tools required, and cleaning methods.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the AC unit cleaning process.

### SAFETY CHECK:
- PROCESS: Ensure the electricity to the AC unit is turned off.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the electricity off?
  - Yes: Proceed to voltage check.
  - No: Turn off the electricity before proceeding.
- PROCESS: Use a multimeter to check the voltage on the unit.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the unit free of electrical voltage?
  - Yes: Proceed with cleaning.
  - No: Do not proceed until voltage is confirmed to be absent.

### TOOL GATHERING:
- INPUT: Gather required tools - ratchet set, flat head screwdriver, multimeter, and possibly a mallet.

### REMOVING METAL SHIELDING:
- PROCESS: Use the appropriate tool to remove screws from the metal shielding around the unit.
- DECISION [IF]: Are all screws removed?
  - Yes: Remove the metal shielding.
  - No: Continue removing screws until all are removed.

### CLEANING THE EXTERIOR:
- INPUT: Use a garden hose with low/no pressure.
- PROCESS: Spray the outside of the unit at an angle to remove buildup.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the buildup peeling off?
  - Yes: Continue to next step.
  - No: Adjust spraying technique or increase pressure slightly.

### CLEANING THE INTERIOR:
- DECISION [IF]: Is there high buildup?
  - Yes: Spray from the inside out after exterior is done.
  - No: Proceed with spraying from the inside out directly.
- PROCESS: Continue spraying until debris is removed and fins are clean.

### CLEANING THE BASE:
- PROCESS: While the unit is open, clean out any debris at the bottom.

### FINISHING UP:
- PROCESS: Inspect the unit to ensure it appears clean.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the unit clean?
  - Yes: Proceed to reassemble.
  - No: Continue cleaning until satisfied.

### REASSEMBLING THE UNIT:
- PROCESS: Reattach the metal shielding with screws.
- DECISION [IF]: Are all screws secured?
  - Yes: Finish reassembly.
  - No: Continue securing screws until all are in place.

### RESTORING POWER:
- PROCESS: Turn the electricity back on to the unit.

### OUTPUT:
- The AC unit is cleaned and reassembled, potentially improving cooling efficiency without the cost of professional service.

### FINAL NOTES:
- STORE/DATABASE SUBROUTINE: Be aware that AC units can vary in design.
- PROCESS: Adapt the cleaning process to the specific design of your unit.
- OUTPUT: Remember that this guide provides basic cleaning instructions, and professional service may be more thorough.

### END:
- The AC unit cleaning process is complete.
```

instruct00583.title: How to Cut Drop Through Truck Mounts on a Longboard
instruct00583.text: This is my first instructable, but im going to show you how to make drop through cut outs in your longboard deck. Im using Randal RII series truck. If you don't know the difference between drop though mount and top mount, top mount is where the board is mounted on top of the trucks, and drop though is where the deck is mounted on the bottom of the truck, and the truck goes through the deck. The benefits to drop mount are that it makes pushing easier because you aren't as high off the ground. Also it makes for a lower center of gravity. I have Randal II trucks and on their website you can download a PDF file of the template for the drop through cut out. The first step is to print out the template and cut out the cut out section, align the holes with the holes on your deck, then draw the template on the deck. I held the template in place by putting the bolts through the template and the deck. Next, you want to gather all your tools. You dont have to use the tools i used, but these are them: a hole saw bit that fits the templates dimensions a wood bore bit an angle grinder a few different drill bits and a file Use the hole saw bit to drill a hole that is as wide as the template toward the nose of the board. (The long stretched hole was already there on my deck) With the angle grinder cut 2 lines towards the center of the board. The cut a line perpendicular to those that will make the notches on the side. Drill with the wood bore a hole through that makes the end of the cut out. Then drill with the drill bit 2 holes they will make the corners of the hole. Then punch out the cut out. It looks kind of messy but you clean it up with the file in the next step. Using the file, file the edges and make the lines straight, dont forget to file the notches on the side. Take your base plate and test fit it every so often, filing a little more off every time till it fits tight. The last step is to mount the baseplate! Make sure to put washers where the nuts touch the deck so they don't damage it. Repeat all the steps to the other side and you are set!

```markdown
# Summary of Making Drop Through Cutouts in a Longboard Deck

## START:
- Begin the process of creating drop through cutouts for a longboard deck using Randal RII series trucks.

## INPUT: 
- Obtain the following materials and tools:
  - Randal II trucks
  - PDF template for the drop through cutout from the Randal website
  - Printer and paper
  - Cutting tool (e.g., scissors)
  - Bolts
  - Hole saw bit (matching the template dimensions)
  - Wood bore bit
  - Angle grinder
  - Drill bits (various sizes)
  - File
  - Baseplate
  - Washers

## PROCESS: [Print and Prepare Template]
- Print out the drop through cutout template.
- Cut out the cutout section from the printed template.

## PROCESS: [Align Template]
- Align the template holes with the holes on the longboard deck.

## PROCESS: [Draw Cutout]
- Secure the template in place by inserting bolts through both the template and the deck.
- Trace the template onto the deck.

## PROCESS: [Gather Tools]
- Collect all necessary tools for the cutting process.

## PROCESS: [Drill Initial Hole]
- Use the hole saw bit to drill a hole at the nose of the board, within the boundary of the template.

## DECISION: [Is there a pre-existing hole?]
  - IF Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - IF No: Use the angle grinder to cut two lines towards the center of the board.

## PROCESS: [Cut Lines]
- With the angle grinder, cut two lines towards the center of the board.

## PROCESS: [Cut Notches]
- Cut a line perpendicular to the previous cuts to create the notches on the side.

## PROCESS: [Drill End Hole]
- Use the wood bore bit to drill a hole that marks the end of the cutout.

## PROCESS: [Drill Corner Holes]
- Drill two holes with the drill bit to form the corners of the cutout.

## PROCESS: [Remove Cutout]
- Punch out the cutout section.

## PROCESS: [File Edges]
- Use the file to straighten the edges and clean up the cutout, including the notches.

## PROCESS: [Test Fit Baseplate]
- Continuously test fit the baseplate, filing away more material for a tight fit.

## OUTPUT:
- A neatly filed cutout in the deck that fits the baseplate snugly.

## DECISION: [Does the Baseplate Fit Perfectly?]
  - IF Yes: Proceed to mounting the baseplate.
  - IF No: Continue filing until it fits perfectly.

## PROCESS: [Mount Baseplate]
- Mount the baseplate onto the deck, ensuring to place washers where the nuts touch the deck to prevent damage.

## DECISION: [Is the other side done?]
  - IF Yes: Proceed to the END.
  - IF No: Repeat all the steps for the other side.

## END:
- The process of making drop through cutouts in the longboard deck is completed.
```

instruct00153.title: Homemade Paracord
instruct00153.text: Here is a fun craft project that will give you a basic understanding of how paracord is made. Here we are going to make an eight strandcasing with a three strand core. Real military grade paracord has a 32 strand casing & a seven strand core. But theprocess is the same for both. For this Project we are going to make a kumihimo wheel & eightbobbins out ofcardboard this is going to be the jig to braid the outer casing. For your fist time get two differentcolors of thread this will help you from getting to confused as you braid. For this braid we will use green & purple. To braid up the casing for your paracord you will need to make a kimihimo wheel & eightbobbins out of some thick cardboard. Step 1. draw out two circles one within the other one. The outer around 6-7 inch. & the inner 1-2 inch. then 16 marks on theoutercircle inequaldistances from one an other. Step 2. cut out the two circles & make 1/2 inch cuts on the 16 marks. step 3. Then draw & cut out the bobbins out with 1/2 inch. cuts on each end. You will need four threads in one color & four in another color each around 3ft . This is for the outer casing in this example we are using four green & four purple. Then three in some other color for the core threads here we are using white thread. Step 1. to load the eight threads of purple & green thread on the bobbins by first wedging one end of a thread in one of the notches on the bobbin. Then wrap the thread around the bobbin then wedge the other end in the other notch. Step 2. take the eight treads of green & purple that you just put on the bobbins, plus the three white threads that will be used as the core & tie them together. Step 3. put the knot in the center of the kimihimo wheel & wedge the eight threads of green & purple in the slots cut around the wheel alternating colors. then just leave the white thread free. The braid is simple to do. Just take your time & enjoy. Step 1. all the green threads jump over the purple threads moving counter clock wise. Step 2. all the purple threads jump over the green threads moving clock wise. step 3. repeat steps 1 & 2 as needed. The white threads do nothing. This is a fun craftprojectto as you watch T.V. # Paracord Craft Project Summary

```markdown
## System Overview:
The system described is a craft project to create a simplified version of military-grade paracord. The system uses a homemade kumihimo wheel and bobbins out of cardboard to braid an eight-strand casing with a three-strand core using thread. The inputs are cardboard, thread, and basic crafting tools, and the output is a handmade paracord.

## Process Steps:

### START:
- Begin the paracord craft project.

### PROCESS: Create Kumihimo Wheel and Bobbins
- INPUT: Thick cardboard.
- PROCESS: Draw two concentric circles on cardboard, the outer one with a diameter of 6-7 inches and the inner one with a diameter of 1-2 inches.
- PROCESS: Mark 16 equal distances around the outer circle and make 1/2 inch cuts at each mark.
- PROCESS: Cut out the circles to complete the kumihimo wheel.
- PROCESS: Draw and cut out eight bobbins from cardboard with 1/2 inch cuts on each end.

### PROCESS: Prepare Threads for Casing and Core
- INPUT: Eight threads of two different colors (four green, four purple) each 3 feet long for the casing. Three threads of a third color (white) for the core.
- PROCESS: Load the eight threads onto the bobbins.
  - PROCESS: Wedge one end of a thread into a notch on a bobbin, wrap the thread around, and secure the other end in the opposite notch.

### PROCESS: Assemble the Kumihimo Wheel
- PROCESS: Tie the eight colored threads (green and purple) and the three white core threads together at one end.
- PROCESS: Place the knot in the center of the kumihimo wheel.
- PROCESS: Wedge the eight colored threads into the wheel's notches, alternating colors, leaving the white core threads free.

### PROCESS: Braid the Paracord
- START BRAIDING:
  - DECISION [IF]: Are all green threads over the purple threads?
    - Yes: Move to the next step.
    - No: PROCESS: Move all green threads over the purple threads counterclockwise.
  - DECISION [IF]: Are all purple threads over the green threads?
    - Yes: Move to the next step.
    - No: PROCESS: Move all purple threads over the green threads clockwise.
  - PROCESS: Repeat the above two steps until the desired length of braid is achieved.
  - OUTPUT: The braided outer casing of the paracord.

### END:
- The craft paracord is now complete.

Note: The white core threads remain inactive during the braiding process and this craft project serves as an introduction to kumihimo braiding techniques.
```

instruct00829.text: A pizzadilla is a rediculously easy to make meal, perfect for new cooks, kids, and college students.Basically, we are going to make a quesadilla in a cast iron skillet, put our favorite toppings on top, and broil it to make the cheese all melty. The most basic version of the pizzadilla consists of the following ingredients:Flour tortillas that fit snuggly in your cast iron skilletA small amount of vegetable or olive oilCheese (i'm using an Italian cheese blend) Pizza sauce (from a jar is totally fine)PepperonisYou will also need a cast iron skillet, range, and oven with broiler.There are infinite ways to gussy up the recipe, such as:Adding chicken to the quesadilla portiontwo different cheeses (one for the quesadilla and one for the pizza part)add tons more meat to the topI am a fan of red onions on my pizza Place a rack in your oven about 5-6 inches from the broiler, preheat the broiler, and put your cast iron skillet over medium heat.Place about a teaspoon of vegetable or olive oil in the skillet and use a brush to coat the bottom of the skillet.Don't make the mistake that I made of overheating your cast iron cookware. It conducts heat very, very well. Anything above medium heat will probably lead to burned tortillas. Before you get carried away making your delicious meal, make sure all of your toppings are prepped. Now place a tortilla into the skillet. Add a nice layer of cheese on top of that, making sure not to get any cheese between the tortilla and the skillet (it will burn!)Top the cheese with the second tortilla.Check to see if the bottom tortilla is nicely browned after a minute or two, and use a large spatula to flip it over. At this point you can kill the heat on the stove.Now quickly top the tortilla with a layer of pizza sauce, cheese, pepperoni, and whatever toppings your heart desires.Immediately, plop your skillet in the oven under the broiler using a protective glove of some sort. It will take anywhere from 45 seconds to 2 minutes for the top of your pizza to become hot and bubbly.Make sure you check on it frequently! I have accidentally burned the pizzadilla in this step several times! I suggest checking in after 30 seconds to see if it is done or not.Depan, cut, and enjoy your crazy simple meal!I attached a video of me walking through the steps. Hope it helps. Enjoy your food!

```markdown
# Pizzadilla Preparation System

## Summary
This system describes the process of making a pizzadilla, a simple meal that combines the elements of a quesadilla and a pizza. It involves using a cast iron skillet to cook a tortilla with cheese, adding pizza toppings, and then broiling it to melt the cheese. The process is suitable for new cooks, kids, and college students.

## Steps

### START:
- Begin the pizzadilla preparation process.

### INPUT:
- Gather the following ingredients:
  - Flour tortillas sized to fit the cast iron skillet
  - Vegetable or olive oil
  - Italian cheese blend or preferred cheese
  - Pizza sauce
  - Pepperonis
- Gather the following equipment:
  - Cast iron skillet
  - Range
  - Oven with broiler
- Optional additional ingredients (e.g., chicken, different cheeses, more meats, red onions).

### PROCESS: [Preheat and Prepare]
- Place a rack in the oven approximately 5-6 inches from the broiler.
- Preheat the broiler.
- Set the cast iron skillet on the range over medium heat.

### PROCESS: [Oil the Skillet]
- Pour about a teaspoon of vegetable or olive oil into the skillet.
- Use a brush to evenly coat the bottom of the skillet.

### DECISION [IF]: [Overheat Check]
- Is the skillet on a heat setting above medium?
  - Yes: Reduce heat to medium to prevent burning the tortillas.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

### PROCESS: [Prep Toppings]
- Ensure all pizza toppings are prepared and ready to be used.

### PROCESS: [Assemble Quesadilla Base]
- Place one tortilla into the skillet.
- Add a layer of cheese on top of the tortilla, avoiding contact with the skillet to prevent burning.

### PROCESS: [Cook Quesadilla]
- After a minute or two, check if the bottom tortilla is browned.
- Use a large spatula to flip the quesadilla over.

### DECISION [IF]: [Browning Check]
- Is the bottom tortilla nicely browned?
  - Yes: Turn off the heat and proceed.
  - No: Continue cooking until browned, then turn off the heat.

### PROCESS: [Add Pizza Toppings]
- Quickly top the flipped tortilla with pizza sauce, additional cheese, pepperoni, and any other desired toppings.

### PROCESS: [Broil Pizzadilla]
- Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven, placing it under the broiler.
- Use a protective glove to handle the hot skillet.

### PROCESS: [Monitor Broiling]
- Wait for 45 seconds to 2 minutes for the cheese to become hot and bubbly.
- Frequently check the pizzadilla to avoid burning.

### DECISION [IF]: [Doneness Check]
- Is the pizzadilla hot and bubbly on top?
  - Yes: Remove from the oven and proceed to OUTPUT.
  - No: Continue broiling and checking every 30 seconds until done.

### OUTPUT:
- The final product is a cooked pizzadilla.

### PROCESS: [Serve Pizzadilla]
- Remove the pizzadilla from the skillet.
- Cut into preferred serving sizes.

### END:
- Enjoy the pizzadilla meal.

## Additional Resources
- A video walkthrough of the steps is provided for further guidance.
```

instruct00768.text: ok so instructable number two. so this one came to me when I posted my last one and I saw the jury rig contest and it suddenly hit me that there was a much quicker and easier method to achieve the same sort of result. so using only a pen, credit card and a pair of scissors this stand was created. now I've entered it in the epilog contest as well because I thought I would be a good idea to make them from styrene sheet plus you could make these in to maded to order business cards from different materials with your name etched on them. so grab any unwanted credit card or similar sized card you don't really use any more. mine is a card I was given when I attended a scaffold training course as you can see in th second picture it's also a usb flash drive ok so measure the thickness of your mobile. Now Mark out a slot wide enough and leave it 1/2"(12mm) from the top. once your happy where your slot is cut it out. one thing to remember is to follow the shape of your phone seeming as some phones have curved backs this will help with stability. Now all I did to get the desired angle for the cut was to slot the phone and card together and eye it up against the end of a table until I was happy with the angle the phones screen would be facing. Once happy cut the corner off all I did then was add a strip of insulation tape to the edge to stop any scratches. now its ready to slot straight on to your phone. HAPPY VIEWING. I have also tried this with a gym members card which is slightly thinner than a credit card and was unstable. as you can see in the picture I have added a T shaped piece of insulation tape plus added a couple of other pieces of tape to make sure the slot is a snug fit on my phone. plus one more thing I have thought about is that some phones have a curved back so when cutting the slot make sure to follow the profile of your phone this should also help with stability.

```markdown
# DIY Mobile Phone Stand System

## Summary Representation

### START:
- Start the process of creating a mobile phone stand using a pen, credit card, and scissors.

### INPUT:
- Gather materials: unwanted credit card or similar-sized card, pen, scissors, and insulation tape.

### PROCESS: Measure Phone Thickness
- Measure the thickness of the mobile phone to determine the width of the slot needed in the card.

### PROCESS: Mark Slot Position
- Mark out a slot on the card that is wide enough for the phone's thickness, leaving a 1/2" (12mm) gap from the top of the card.

### DECISION [IF]: Is Slot Position Satisfactory?
  - [YES]: Proceed to cutting out the slot.
  - [NO]: Re-evaluate the position and re-mark if necessary.

### PROCESS: Cut Out Slot
- Once satisfied with the slot position, cut it out carefully.

### PROCESS: Ensure Slot Matches Phone's Shape
- Adjust the slot to follow the shape of the phone if it has a curved back for better stability.

### PROCESS: Determine Desired Angle
- Slot the phone into the card and adjust the angle by eyeing it up against the end of a table until satisfied with the viewing angle of the phone's screen.

### PROCESS: Cut Off Corner for Angle
- Cut the corner of the card off at the determined angle.

### PROCESS: Apply Insulation Tape
- Add a strip of insulation tape to the edge to prevent scratches.

### OUTPUT:
- The basic mobile phone stand is now ready to use.

### DECISION [IF]: Is Stand Unstable with Thinner Card?
  - [YES]: Proceed to stabilize with T-shaped tape.
  - [NO]: End the process as the stand is stable.

### PROCESS: Stabilize with T-Shaped Tape
- If using a thinner card like a gym membership card and the stand is unstable, apply a T-shaped piece of insulation tape for stability.

### PROCESS: Ensure Snug Fit
- Add additional pieces of tape to the slot to make sure the phone fits snugly without wobbling.

### END:
- The mobile phone stand is complete and ready for "HAPPY VIEWING."
```

instruct00390.title: Marinated Cucumbers and Tomatoes
instruct00390.text: Growing up in the backwoods of West Virginia, this dish was a staple of reunions in the "Hollar." A refreshingly crisp dish perfect for a noontime meal. It's extremely healthy and helpful in rehydration. There aren't many ingredients in this so it's super simple to make. 3 medium sized cucumbers(or 1 and a half large ones) 3 tomatoes White distilled vinegar 1 medium sized red onion Water Salt(optional) Oil Large bowl with lid(or cling wrap) Paring knife Cutting board 1 cup measuring cup 1/3 cup measuring cup Chef knife(optional) Wash the cucumbers and tomatoes. Stem the tomatoes, cut the bottoms and any bad spots off. First half, then half, then half the tomatoes again. So your left with 8 wedges of tomato. Add them to your bowl. Slice the ends off the cucumbers(I'm not really sure if it's true but my aunt always used to say you slice into a cucumber until you hit the seeds because it the ends don't absorb the marinade as well). So it may take a few tries to find the right spot. Then slice the cucumbers in 1/4" all the way down the length. Add them to your bowl as well. My absolute least favorite part of making this is slicing the onion. Not because it's difficult, I'm just a wimp. I also like to wear gloves and use a bigger knife for this part, but neither is necessary. Cut the ends off the onion and husk the outer dried layers off. Next slice the whole onion in 1/4" slices. Separate into rings and dispose of the middles. Add to your bowl. Measure out 3 cups of the White Distilled Vinegar, add to your bowl. Measure out 3 cups of water and add to the bowl also. Add 1/3 cup of oil. Mix! After everything is mixed thoroughly, I like to make sure all the cucumbers and tomatoes are submerged or at least in the marinade. Cover your bowl with either a lid or cling wrap and refrigerate to taste. I say that because some people like it in as little as two hours afterwards, but my roommate likes it after 24 hours. Start with 6 or overnight and taste it. I usually serve as a side with lunch meat sandwiches. Enjoy! Side note: This will feed 6-8, or 1 with a serious veggie habit.

```markdown
# Cucumber Tomato Salad Recipe

## Ingredients:
- 3 medium-sized cucumbers (or 1 and a half large ones)
- 3 tomatoes
- White distilled vinegar
- 1 medium-sized red onion
- Water
- Salt (optional)
- Oil
- Large bowl with lid (or cling wrap)
- Paring knife
- Cutting board
- 1 cup measuring cup
- 1/3 cup measuring cup
- Chef knife (optional)

## Equipment:
- Large bowl with lid or cling wrap
- Paring knife
- Cutting board
- 1 cup measuring cup
- 1/3 cup measuring cup
- Chef knife (optional)

## Steps:

START:
- Gather all ingredients and equipment.

PROCESS: Wash Vegetables
- INPUT: 3 medium-sized cucumbers, 3 tomatoes
- Wash the cucumbers and tomatoes thoroughly.

PROCESS: Prepare Tomatoes
- INPUT: 3 tomatoes
- OUTPUT: Tomato wedges
- Use a paring knife to stem the tomatoes, cut the bottoms and any bad spots off.
- Cut each tomato into 8 wedges.
- Add the tomato wedges to the large bowl.

PROCESS: Prepare Cucumbers
- INPUT: 3 medium-sized cucumbers
- OUTPUT: Cucumber slices
- Slice the ends off the cucumbers, avoiding the seeds.
- Slice the cucumbers into 1/4" slices down the length.
- Add the cucumber slices to the bowl.

PROCESS: Prepare Onion
- INPUT: 1 medium-sized red onion
- OUTPUT: Onion rings
- Cut the ends off the onion and remove the outer dried layers.
- Slice the onion into 1/4" slices.
- Separate the slices into rings and discard the middles.
- Add the onion rings to the bowl.

PROCESS: Add Liquids
- INPUT: White distilled vinegar, water, oil
- OUTPUT: Mixture in bowl
- Measure 3 cups of white distilled vinegar and add to the bowl.
- Measure 3 cups of water and add to the bowl.
- Measure 1/3 cup of oil and add to the bowl.

PROCESS: Mix Ingredients
- Mix all ingredients in the bowl thoroughly.
- Ensure all cucumbers and tomatoes are submerged or at least touching the marinade.

PROCESS: Refrigerate
- Cover the bowl with a lid or cling wrap.
- STORE: Place the bowl in the refrigerator.

DECISION [IF]: Determine Marination Time
- IF marination time is known (e.g., 2 hours, 6 hours, overnight, 24 hours)
    - OUTPUT: Marinated salad ready for serving after specified time.
- ELSE
    - OUTPUT: Check taste after 6 hours or overnight and decide if additional marination time is needed.
```

instruct00566.title: Survival Hardtack
instruct00566.text: The outdoors can be as fun as it is unforgiving and if you are not prepared for the worst then it can also be deadly. We have much to learn from the outdoorsman of the past. The survival methods they used were proven and should be used to increase survival even today. Food is important when surviving because it is the only way to replenish energy. You can survive with very little food and I will show you a way to easily carry some with you. Hardtack is a dense bread that has minimal water and can last months without modern refrigeration. It is true to its name and has a reputation for being hard as brick. Historically, it has helped armies and sailors make long trips by packing wooden casks with this hard bread. Making it is simple and it requires only whole wheat flour, salt and water. First, measure 4 cups of flour. 4 cups of flour weighs 480 grams.Next, measure 2 cups of water and dissolve 4 teaspoons of salt into it. Then, mix the water slowly into the flour until it is a stiff dough. All the water may not be used. The dough should not be sticky but instead firm and moldable. Roll out the dough to a thickness of inch. Cut 3 inch square pieces and press into the dough holes similar to store bought crackers. Put the hardtack on a un-greased pan and bake at 375 for 30 min. flip and bake for another 30 min.They will keep for a year or longer if stored air tight.

```markdown
# Hardtack Preparation Process

## START
- Begin the process of making hardtack, a long-lasting survival food.

## INPUT: Ingredients and Measurements
- Measure 4 cups of whole wheat flour (480 grams).
- Measure 2 cups of water.
- Measure 4 teaspoons of salt.

## PROCESS: Dissolve Salt
- Dissolve the 4 teaspoons of salt in the 2 cups of water.

## PROCESS: Mix Ingredients
- Gradually mix the saltwater into the flour to form a stiff dough.
  
## DECISION: Is all the water used?
  - IF YES: Proceed to the next step.
  - IF NO: Use only enough water to achieve the required dough consistency.

## PROCESS: Adjust Dough Consistency
- Ensure dough is not sticky but firm and moldable.

## PROCESS: Roll Out Dough
- Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/2 inch.

## PROCESS: Shape Hardtack
- Cut the dough into 3-inch square pieces.
- Press holes into the dough pieces, resembling store-bought crackers.

## PROCESS: Bake Hardtack
- Place the hardtack pieces on an ungreased pan.
- Bake in an oven preheated to 375 degrees Fahrenheit for 30 minutes.

## PROCESS: Flip Hardtack
- After 30 minutes, flip the hardtack pieces over.

## PROCESS: Continue Baking
- Bake for an additional 30 minutes.

## OUTPUT: Finished Hardtack
- Remove the hardtack from the oven once fully baked.

## PROCESS: Store Hardtack
- Store the hardtack in an airtight container.

## DECISION: Is the storage airtight?
  - IF YES: Proceed to end the process.
  - IF NO: Find an appropriate airtight container for storage.

## END
- The hardtack is now ready for long-term storage and can be kept for a year or longer.
```

```markdown
# Fluffy Slime Making Process

## START:
- Begin the process of making fluffy slime.

## INPUT:
- Gather the following materials and ingredients:
  - Small bowl
  - Baking soda (1 tablespoon)
  - Eye wash or eye drops
  - A separate bowl
  - Liquid glue (1/2 cup)
  - Shaving cream or liquid foaming soap (1/2 cup)
  - Food coloring (optional)
  - Plastic bag or container for storage

## PROCESS: [Preparation of Baking Soda Mixture]
- Add 1 tablespoon of baking soda to the small bowl.
- Pour enough eye wash over the baking soda to cover it.
- Swirl the mixture until the baking soda and eye wash are fully combined.

## PROCESS: [Preparation of Glue Mixture]
- In the separate bowl, mix together 1/2 cup of glue and 1/2 cup of shaving cream.
- Add food coloring if desired color is needed.
- Fold the two ingredients together until they are well combined.

## PROCESS: [Combining Mixtures to Form Slime]
- Add the eye wash and baking soda mixture to the bowl containing the glue and shaving cream mixture.
- Mix the contents thoroughly until a putty-like slime begins to form.

## PROCESS: [Kneading the Slime]
- Knead the slime for approximately three minutes.

## STORE:
- Place the kneaded slime in a contained space and shut it.

## DECISION [IF]: [Slime Resting Time]
- Has the slime rested for about an hour or two?
  - Yes: Proceed to OUTPUT.
  - No: Continue to let the slime rest.

## OUTPUT:
- After the resting time, the slime is ready to be played with.

## PROCESS: [Storage Instructions]
- To store the slime, place it in a plastic bag or a container with a lid.

## END:
- The process of making fluffy slime is complete.
```

instruct00268.title: Cake in a Jar
instruct00268.text: These tiny delights make the perfect gifts for any occasion. Make up a batch to keep on hand for sudden cravings, give as favors for your next party, or send to loved ones overseas. The cakes will remain moist and delicious for up to 6 months! What better way to show someone you care than a personalized cake in a jar!Check out this amazing story about a 36-year-old government issue cake, and soldier who ate it!For more info on cute jarred treats (and how I prepared the jars), see Pie in a Jar! To speed things along, I used a boxed cake mix. Everyone agreed it tasted like a boxed cake mix. I was ok with that for the purpose of illustrating the technique (no need to make this two instructables worth of instructions!) but will definitely go from scratch next time.So find your favorite cake mix and supporting ingredients, or make it from scratch. The best part about making your own is that you can make half of one kind and half of another!You'll also need a bunch of canning jars - straight sides, wide mouthed. I got the wee-est ones I could find for cuteness' sake. You can definitely make them in bigger jars.Boil or wash the jars to sterilize them. You'll want brand-spanking-new lids to make a tight seal when you're done.The box mix made enough batter to fill 16-20 jars! Make the batter according to the directions on the box.Or look here for some inspiration to make your own!Fill the jars about half-way with batter. If you fill them too full, you can always squish them down, or cut the tops off. But too much batter will result in them flowing over the sides of the jars.Place in a baking dish for ease of handling. Bake according to directions for cupcakes, and check for doneness. These are about cupcake size, but your jars may be larger and need more time.When they're done, close the lids on 'em. They're self-sealing, and you'll be able to see the seal forming!Alternatively, you can add a chocolate ganache* to the top before sealing. Make sure to screw those caps on while the cakes are still hot though, to get that all-important seal.* To make ganache: Heat 1 cup cream in a small sauce pan over medium heat. Bring just to a boil, watching very carefully because if it boils for a few seconds, it will boil out of the pot. When the cream has come to a boil, pour over 9oz chopped chocolate, and whisk until smooth. Allow the ganache to cool slightly before pouring over cake. This is one little beauty I popped onto a plate - but no need, they're easy to eat right out of the jar!Once you've sealed these little treats, lable and date them. Then you're ready to serve, ship, or store.Enjoy!UPDATE:According to user precision: "We've been doing these for years, they are great! I've got some right now that are over 6 months old, and I wouldn't hesitate to eat them."

```markdown
# Cake in a Jar Preparation System

## START:
- Begin the Cake in a Jar Preparation System.

## INPUT:
- Gather ingredients for a boxed cake mix or scratch ingredients for a homemade cake.
- Obtain canning jars with straight sides and wide mouths, preferably small for cuteness.
- Ensure brand-new lids are available for sealing the jars.

## PROCESS: Sterilize Jars
- Wash the jars thoroughly or boil them to sterilize.
- Ensure jars are completely dry before use.

## INPUT:
- Prepare the cake batter following the instructions on the cake mix box or from a homemade recipe.

## PROCESS: Fill Jars
- Fill the canning jars about half-way with the prepared batter.
- DECISION [IF]: Is there too much batter in the jars?
  - Yes: Remove excess batter or squish down the cake.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

## PROCESS: Bake Cakes
- Place the filled jars in a baking dish for ease of handling.
- Bake the jars according to the cupcake instructions provided by the cake mix or recipe.
- DECISION [IF]: Are the cakes done?
  - Yes: Proceed to seal the jars.
  - No: Continue baking until done, then proceed to seal the jars.

## PROCESS: Seal Jars
- Immediately close the lids on the jars after baking to create a tight seal.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the seal forming correctly?
  - Yes: Proceed to optional ganache addition.
  - No: Check if the lids are properly placed and re-seal.

## PROCESS [OPTIONAL]: Make Ganache
- Heat 1 cup of cream in a saucepan until it just boils.
- Pour the heated cream over 9oz of chopped chocolate.
- Whisk until the ganache is smooth.
- Allow ganache to cool slightly.

## PROCESS: Add Ganache
- DECISION [IF]: Are you adding ganache to the cakes?
  - Yes: Pour the ganache over the cakes before sealing the jars.
  - No: Skip this step.

## OUTPUT:
- The cakes in jars are now ready.

## PROCESS: Label and Date Jars
- Label the jars with the contents and date of preparation.

## END:
- Serve, ship, or store the cakes in jars. They will remain moist and delicious for up to 6 months.
```

instruct00341.title: Multi-purpose Holder From Kitchen Whisk
instruct00341.text: This Instructable shows you how to build a multipurpose holder for displaying everything from fruits & vegetables to your beloved cellphone charger using a simple metallic kitchen whisk. You'll need a pincer tool, a metallic kitchen whisk (thanks to HBB for this one) and both of your hands. First of all you need to remove that metallic holder piece in the center of the whisk. Use a pincher to cut the metal next to the holes of each "arm" of the whisk. Then you can remove the metallic holder. Bend up one of the petal-shaped whisk part so that it is perpendicular to the handle. Make it a little curved up so that it can sustain the weight of a small object. Leave the petal which is planar to the "wall holder" so that it can rest along the wall ( see next step ) Fold up all "petals" except one : the petal which is in the same plane as the "wall holder" will act as a stabilizer. Make sure the stabilizer touches the wall all the way. You can make it more "round" for more stability Stability can be further enhanced with blue-tack (patafix) or hanging a small load to the stabilizer petal.

instruct00840.title: Candy Cane Marbled Monogram Ornaments
instruct00840.text: ** If you like this tutorial I would love it if you voted for me in the Holiday Gifts Contest. Banner to vote on top right. ** I recently saw a marbleized nail technique on Pinterest and was so inspired to try it. After several attempts I finally got the nail technique down and decided to do something more unique with it. Taking the glass ornaments that I purchased from Michael's Craft Supply, I created a water marble ornament. You can check out my video tutorials on how to marbleize an ornamentand how to water marble nails. For more simple unique crafts please visit me athttp://thecheesethief.com/ Materials: 1 glass ornament 2 bottles of nail polish 1 vase/cup (large enough to fit half the ornament, but not too big) filled half way with filtered tap water I used Orly French White and OPI All Lacquered Up for these images. These nail polish brands seem to work the best for this technique. Do experiment with different nail polishes as all of them do not work the same for this. 1. Prepare your workspace. Place a towel or newspaper underneath for easier cleanup. 2. First shake both bottles of nail polish so the nail polish is nicely mixed. 3. Unscrew the tops of both bottles. This will help you work fast. 4. Drip one color of the nail polish into the cup of water. 5. Drip the other color into the water and keep alternating. (It is ok if the tip of the nail brush touches the water, but it is better if you can get a big glob to drip off the wand and drop onto the surface of the water.) 6. Working quickly alternate for 4-6 times. If you are just starting off I would start with 4 -5 drips or rings. When you get better you can do more. 7. Taking a toothpick start from the center of the nail polish and pull outwards to make a pattern. 8. It is easier to work from the inside out because the inside nail polish was just dripped so it is still wet. Once you get the pattern you want dip your ornament in slowly for 10 seconds. Remove and let dry ( i put it on top of a smaller cup). For amonogrammedornament cut the initial with tape. Paint on clear nail polish first to seal the sticker seams (this will help withseeping). If you want a more opaque monogram you can paint another base color over the monogram. Follow the same instructions for water marbling. Some tips for water marbling with nail polish. 1. Use the smallest cup possible that will fit your ornament 2. Experiment with different brands and colors of nail polish 3. Use clean filtered room temperature water every time. 4. if your polish seems to dry too fast, where when you drag the pattern it pulls the whole surface up, then try only swirling a pattern in the inner most rings 5. To help reduce water spots, dip ornament in slowly and blow off any water drops once ornament is lifted. Avoid shaking the water too much also 6. Work fast! You can check out my video tutorials on how to marbleize an ornament and how to water marble nails.

```markdown
# Water Marble Ornament Creation Process

## START:
- Begin the process of creating a water marble ornament.

## INPUT:
- Gather the following materials:
  - 1 glass ornament
  - 2 bottles of nail polish (preferably Orly French White and OPI All Lacquered Up)
  - 1 vase/cup, large enough to fit half the ornament
  - Filtered tap water
  - A towel or newspaper
  - Toothpick
  - Optional: Tape and clear nail polish for monogramming

## PROCESS: [Prepare Workspace]
- Lay down a towel or newspaper to protect the workspace.

## PROCESS: [Prepare Nail Polish]
- Shake both bottles of nail polish to ensure they are well mixed.

## PROCESS: [Prepare Nail Polish Bottles]
- Unscrew the tops of both nail polish bottles for quick access.

## PROCESS: [Fill Vase/Cup]
- Fill the vase/cup halfway with filtered tap water.

## PROCESS: [Drip Nail Polish Into Water]
- Drip one color of nail polish into the cup of water.
- Continue to alternate drips of the two nail polishes into the water for 4-6 times.

## DECISION: [Is This Your First Attempt?]
  - IF 'Yes': Limit the drips to 4-5.
  - ELSE: Proceed with more drips as skill improves.

## PROCESS: [Create Pattern with Toothpick]
- Use a toothpick to drag patterns from the center of the nail polish outwards.

## DECISION: [Is the Pattern Satisfactory?]
  - IF 'Yes': Proceed to the next step.
  - ELSE: Adjust the pattern as necessary.

## PROCESS: [Dip Ornament]
- Slowly submerge the ornament into the water for 10 seconds.

## PROCESS: [Remove and Dry Ornament]
- Remove the ornament from the water and place it on a smaller cup to dry.

## DECISION: [Do You Want a Monogrammed Ornament?]
  - IF 'Yes': Proceed to monogramming steps.
  - ELSE: Skip to the final steps.

## PROCESS: [Monogramming (Optional)]
- Cut out the initial with tape and apply to the ornament.
- Paint on clear nail polish to seal the sticker seams.
- Apply an additional base color for opacity if desired.
- Follow the same water marbling instructions.

## PROCESS: [Water Marbling Tips]
- Use the smallest cup possible that fits the ornament.
- Experiment with different nail polish brands and colors.
- Use clean filtered room temperature water for each new ornament.
- Avoid dragging the pattern too much if the polish dries quickly.
- Dip the ornament slowly to reduce water spots and avoid shaking the water.

## OUTPUT:
- The final product is a unique water marble ornament.

## END:
- The process of creating a water marble ornament is complete.
```

instruct00010.title: Cut Your Own Long Hair
instruct00010.text: This is a fantastic trick I found for cutting long hair all by yourself! I came across it on a long hair forum while googling how to do it. I've been cutting my own long hair for about a year now, and I love it. Plus, it saves quite a bit of money depending on how often you get a trim. Keep in mind that I can't recommend it for curly hair because I have the straightest & thinnest hair ever. I also can't promise this is the most precise method, but with a little care you get your hair nice and straight. :) And big thanks to audreyobscura for photographing this and supplying gifs! a scrunchiea pair of scissors for hair a brush a handheld mirror Make sure the scrunchie is made from a slick fabric, something that grabs the hair will make this tricky. Also make sure you're using the right scissors - scissors that you'd use for cutting random things around the house are not ideal. You can get some nice hair scissors for $10-15 at any drugstore. I like to cut my hair right after I've washed it and it's totally dry. You want your hair to be dry and free of tangles when you cut it. :) It's also a good idea (especially the first time you do this) to employ a hand held mirror and large wall mirror so that you can see how what you're doing in the back. :D Part your hair as you normally would. (I've included a photo to show you what the top of my head looks like during this bit!) It's important to part your hair as you normally would - if you brush it all back, it won't fall as it normally does. After you cut and remove the scrunchie, it will be the farthest thing from straight when it's parted again. If you don't normally part your hair, you might want to play around with using a middle part - I think that may be the safest. Then use the scrunchie to tie your hair into a low ponytail - right at the top of your neck. Make sure this is in the middle of your head! Use your hand mirror to check it. :) Gently pull the scrunchie down the length of your hair, being careful to not pull it to one side. This can take a fair bit of practice. Keep checking with the hand mirror as you go! If your hair is especially long, you might want to pull from the bottom as shown in the second photo. This method is a little trickier, and I don't do it often, but it's doable. Leave 3-4 inches of hair below the scrunchie. Hold the scrunchie and the hair below the scrunchie firmly and gently bring it around to the front. If you sense that it's shifted, you might want to give it another go. The hair that you'll be cutting should look fairly straight across - though not perfect because hair is always growing at different speeds! A good rule of thumb here is to cut very little at a time. 1/2 inch tops! instruct00804.title: How to Cook Bacon in the Oven
instruct00804.text: Cooking your bacon in the oven is the most efficient way to cook it as far as I'm concerned. Using your oven makes cooking bacon for a crowd nice and easy and frees up your stovetop for all the other breakfast foods you're undoubtably wanting to stuff your face with. :DAnd the best part? The bacon comes out nicely cooked every time and the trays clean up easily.Read on to learn how to cook perfect bacon in the oven. P.S. Lots of commenters are recommending cooking it at a lower temp. I have never ever had smoke or god forbid, FIRE, happen when cooking these at 400 F, but if you skip the parchment paper there's a chance - you don't want the bacon directly on the hot sheet pan. Use your best judgement if your oven runs hot. :) a rimmed baking sheetparchment paperbaconan oven set to 400 FAnd that's it! Dead simple. Lay the bacon down on the parchment paper so none of the pieces are overlapping. If you overlap them, they won't crisp up as well. Bake for 15-20 minutes at 400 F or until it's as crispy as you like! Don't flip it, just let it hang out.If you're doing multiple trays of bacon, switch the racks they're on halfway through.The first photo is the bacon 8 minutes in - the second is the finished bacon after 16 minutes. :) Once it's done, shake off the excess fat and drain on paper towels.For extra credit, strain the drippings and store them in your fridge. :D

instruct00018.title: Remove Scratches From a CD/DVD With Vaseline (Petroleum Jelly)
instruct00018.text: Vaseline (Petroleum Jelly) can be used for chapped lips, dry skin, and for getting rid of head lice; but how about making CDs and DVDs readable again? Well, it does that too. There are also other ways to do this on the Instructables website, but I will show you the one that I believe works best. Before you start removing scratches from your CDs and DVDs, you should grab your materials. To perform the directions in this Instructable, you will need the following materials: - Soft Cloth or Disc Cleaner/Repair - Petroleum Jelly (Vaseline, Store Brand, etc.) - Minor to severely scratched discs Now it's time to apply the petroleum jelly. I will demonstrate both ways to do this (the tissue and the disc cleaner). **UPDATE** Thanks to all of the comments, I have learned that you should not rub in small circular motions as show in picture #1, but instead follow inner perimeter of the disk. Once that is done, you will need to get rid of the excess grease. If you did it with a tissue, get a damp clothand start scrubbing. (Do NOT use rubbing alcohol unless you want a warped disc) If you did it with that disc cleaner on the other hand, just hit the start button, wait for it to finish, and repeat the directions above. All clean! As you can see, there are no more visible scratches. If this didn't work for you, try peanut butter. Rumor has it that it works. If there are any improvements that need to be made, please do not hesitate to comment.

```markdown
- INPUT: Soft Cloth or Disc Cleaner/Repair device
- INPUT: Petroleum Jelly (Vaseline or Store Brand)
- INPUT: Minor to severely scratched discs

## PROCESS: Apply Petroleum Jelly
- Apply a small amount of petroleum jelly onto the disc.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the application tool a tissue?
  - Yes: Proceed with the tissue application method.
  - No: Proceed with the disc cleaner application method.

### Tissue Application Method
- PROCESS: Apply petroleum jelly with a tissue.
- PROCESS: Follow the inner perimeter of the disc when applying.

### Disc Cleaner Application Method
- PROCESS: Apply petroleum jelly using the disc cleaner.
- PROCESS: Use the device's start button to begin the application process.

## PROCESS: Remove Excess Petroleum Jelly
- DECISION [IF]: Was the application done with a tissue?
  - Yes: Use a damp cloth to remove excess petroleum jelly.
    - OUTPUT: A clean disc with no visible scratches.
    - DECISION [IF]: Are there still visible scratches?
      - Yes: Try an alternative method with peanut butter.
      - No: End the process here.
  - No: Use the disc cleaner to remove excess petroleum jelly.
    - OUTPUT: A clean disc with no visible scratches.
    - DECISION [IF]: Are there still visible scratches?

- PROCESS: Follow the inner perimeter of the disc when applying.
- PROCESS: Use a damp cloth to remove the peanut butter and excess grease.
- OUTPUT: A clean disc that should be readable again.

## END:
- The disc is now clean and should be free of visible scratches.
- If the disc is still not readable, consider professional repair or replacement.
```

instruct00656.title: How to Make an Instant Slushy
instruct00656.text: How to make an instant slushie. Want a to make any drink into a delicious semi-frozen drink called a slushy? Usually this means putting your desired drink in the freezer and waiting until it reaches the desired state of being froze, however with this awesome method you can have a frozen slushie drink in just a few minutes! We have also provided a video tutorial on how to make an instant slushy. so be sure to give it a watch for more elaborated instructions. What you will need:- A drink (any drink will work for making a slushy)- 2 Plastic Bags - Some ice- Salt Pour the drink into one of the plastic bags. Make sure that you seal the plastic bag completely to ensure no spills. Put the plastic bag with the drink in it inside of the other plastic bag. Again, make sure that the plastic bag with drink in it is completely sealed. Fill the outer bag with ice. Make sure to leave enough room to be able to close the bag. Pour salt into the outer bag. You should be pouring the salt on top of the ice. How will this work? Salt and ice create a chemical reaction that "superchill" your inside drink. This will require quite a bit of salt. Now seal the outer plastic bag that is containing everything and shake. Shake the bag for a good 3 - 5 minutes or until you can visually see the drink become a slush state.WARNING : The bag will get very cold, so consider using a towel to shake and handle the bag. After shaking the bag for about 5 minutes, the inside drink will have became a slushy! Do this with any drink including soda, juice, or just water! If this tutorial was confusing in any way, be sure to take a look at our video tutorial on how to make an instant slushy - How to Make an Instant Slushy . We have also given a few pictures to what the slushy will look like. Thanks for reading!

instruct00645.title: Candle Powered Hot Air Balloon
instruct00645.text: Build a candle powered hot air balloon using painter's plastic, balsa wood, and birthday candles. Cut the plastic and heat-seal the edges. Layout your materials on a large sheet cardboard. Pull out approximately 6 feet of the painter's plastic and cut it forming a sheet 9 x 6 ft. It's important to have plastic that is 1/2 mil (12 microns) or thinner. Thicker plastic is too heavy to fly. Fold the sheet in half along the 9 ft side forming a two-ply sheet 4.5 x 6 ft. Use a hot knife to seal the two 4.5 ft edges. An electric hot knife makes this really easy, but it can also be done with an old metal knife heated over a flame. Check your edges and correct any large holes. A few small holes won't cause problems. Melt candles together and attach them to balsa. Again, an electric hot knife makes this step a breeze. A heated fork can achieve the same results. Make sure to do both sides. Once the candles are attached together, melt them to the middle of a piece of balsa wood 3/16 x 1/8 x 36 inches. Assemble the balsa frame. Make an "H" with the 36 in balsa and candle piece and two 3/16 x 1/8 x 30 in balsa sticks. Make the joints with a small piece of clear tape. Tape the balloon to the balsa frame. Use a stick inside the balloon to hold the plastic away from the candles and light them. Keep holding the plastic up until enough hot air has filled the balloon to inflate it. It's an amazing feeling when your creation first gets lift and starts to take off. At this stage, there's about ten thousand things that could go wrong. Carefully think everything through before you actually do it. I tied some thread to mine so I could fly it inside our warehouse without it getting away and setting the place on fire. It will drip a lot of hot wax, so keep it over the cardboard if possible. Also, if you let the candles burn all the way down, the balsa will catch on fire. I am currently experimenting with other types of candles to prevent this. Fly safe!

```markdown
# Candle Powered Hot Air Balloon System

## Materials Needed
- Painter's plastic (1/2 mil or 12 microns thickness)
- Balsa wood sticks (sizes: 3/16 x 1/8 x 36 inches, 3/16 x 1/8 x 30 inches)
- Birthday candles
- Electric hot knife or metal knife and flame source
- Clear tape
- Large sheet of cardboard (for workspace)
- Stick (to hold plastic away from candles)
- Thread (optional for indoor flight control)

## Process Steps

START: Begin the construction of a candle powered hot air balloon.

INPUT: Gather all materials required for the construction.

PROCESS: Lay out the materials on a large sheet of cardboard to protect the working surface.

PROCESS: Pull out approximately 6 feet of painter's plastic and cut it to form a sheet that is 9 x 6 ft.

DECISION [IF]: Is the plastic 1/2 mil (12 microns) or thinner?
  - Yes: Proceed with the construction.
  - No: Replace with the correct thickness of plastic, as thicker plastic will not fly.

PROCESS: Fold the plastic sheet in half along the 9 ft side to form a two-ply sheet that is 4.5 x 6 ft.

PROCESS: Use a hot knife to heat-seal the two 4.5 ft edges of the plastic sheet.

DECISION [IF]: Are there any large holes in the edges after sealing?
  - Yes: Correct the large holes.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

PROCESS: Melt birthday candles together using a hot knife or heated fork and attach them to the middle of a balsa wood stick (3/16 x 1/8 x 36 inches).

PROCESS: Assemble the balsa frame by forming an "H" with the 36-inch balsa and candle piece and two 30-inch balsa sticks.

PROCESS: Use clear tape to make the joints of the balsa frame.

PROCESS: Tape the balloon (sealed plastic) to the balsa frame.

PROCESS: Use a stick inside the balloon to hold the plastic away from the candles.

PROCESS: Light the candles.

DECISION [IF]: Has enough hot air filled the balloon to inflate it?
  - Yes: Continue to monitor the balloon as it gains lift.
  - No: Keep holding the plastic up until it inflates.

DECISION [IF]: Is the balloon flying safely?
  - Yes: Enjoy the sight of your creation taking off.
  - No: Troubleshoot and address any issues that prevent safe flight.

PROCESS: (Optional) Tie some thread to the balloon for indoor flight control to prevent it from getting away.

DECISION [IF]: Are the candles dripping a lot of hot wax?
  - Yes: Keep the balloon over the cardboard to catch the wax.
  - No: Continue to monitor the balloon.

DECISION [IF]: Are the candles close to burning all the way down?
  - Yes: Extinguish the candles to prevent the balsa from catching fire.
  - No: Continue to monitor the balloon.
```

instruct00095.title: How to Remove a Dent From Wood
instruct00095.text: After moving some furniture, I inevitably damaged some of it by dropping a heavy tool on it. I'm going to show you the technique I used to fix it and remove the dent without using wood filler. This technique works great for wood floors and dining room tables, too. I did this at TechShop. The trick is pretty simple. We're going to use an iron to steam the dent out of the wood. You'll need the following: An iron Paper towel. I used a shop towel but anold t-shirt orrag will work, too Water Put a dab of water on the affected area. Not too much. Just enough to cover the dent(s). Cover it with your paper towel/rag. At this point, the water will wick through the material. That's fine. Now, with your iron on its highest setting, hold it over the affected area and make small movements back and forth and in circles. Press down firmly and continue until your paper towel is dry. It won't take long to evaporate. At this point, the wood fibers are absorbing the water and should expand back to where they were originally. Continue this process and repeat by adding more water until the dents rise up to be flush with the rest of the material. At this point, the area around your dents should be pretty smooth. However, depending on the damage, you may still see an outline from where it was. Use some sandpaper to go over the area lightly. It won't take much and you'll be able to get your piece back to looking like nothing ever happened to it!

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Wood Dent Repair Technique

## System Overview
The system described is a method for repairing dents in wood without using wood filler. It utilizes the application of heat and moisture to make the wood fibers expand and fill out the dent. The system's inputs are a set of tools and materials, and the output is the repaired wood surface.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the wood dent repair process.

### INPUT:
- Gather the necessary materials: iron, paper towel or rag, and water.

### PROCESS: [Preparation]
- Identify the dented area on the wood that needs repair.

### PROCESS: [Apply Water]
- Put a dab of water on the dented area.
  - DECISION [IF: Is the amount of water enough to cover the dent(s)?]
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Add more water until the dent(s) are covered.

### PROCESS: [Cover with Towel]
- Cover the dented area with a paper towel or rag.
  - DECISION [IF: Does the water wick through the material?]
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Adjust the material to ensure water can wick through.

### PROCESS: [Apply Heat]
- Set the iron to its highest setting.
- Hold the iron over the covered dented area.
- Make small movements back and forth and in circles.
- Press down firmly.

### PROCESS: [Check Towel Dryness]
- Continue ironing until the paper towel or rag is dry.
  - DECISION [IF: Is the paper towel or rag dry?]
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Continue ironing until it is dry.

### PROCESS: [Repeat Water Application]
- Observe the dented area.
  - DECISION [IF: Are the dents flush with the rest of the wood surface?]
    - Yes: Proceed to the sanding step.
    - No: Repeat the water application and ironing process.

### PROCESS: [Sanding]
- Once the dents are flush, lightly sand the area.
  - DECISION [IF: Is the area smooth and damage outline gone?]
    - Yes: The repair is complete.
    - No: Continue sanding lightly until smooth.

### OUTPUT:
- The final output is a repaired wood surface with dents removed.

### END:
- The wood dent repair process is completed.
```

instruct00504.title: Cardboard Gramaphone Passive Speaker
instruct00504.text: I've always loved the aesthetic of old gramophones and finally sat down and made one. It will boost the volume of your music only a little bit, but it sure looks cool! Cardboard Box cutters ScissorsTapeGlue gun and glueCutting matPrint out of all SVG pattern pages(Fuzzy assistant not necessary, but always nice) Cut out all of the pieces of the SVG pattern. Add 2-3 inches to the 4 stem bits of the bell(the ones with the square ends). Add more if you want it to be taller than mine ended up being.Lay out all the pieces of the template and cut out of cardboard. Make sure that all the pieces of both the octagonal bowl and bell are drawn on the grain of the cardboard so that they bend the way you want. The corrugated stripes are 90 degrees from the direction you want the pieces to bend. (See pictures) On all the pieces for the bowl and the bell bevel the edges by compressing the side-saddle with a hard object. I used the handle for my scissors. This will make it easier to put the sides together. Also pre-bend the curved pieces. You don't want to have to do this while you're taping them together. It won't end well. Take the first 2 sides of the bowl and tape together starting at the longest side and working down. Repeat for all the other sides the same way. You will end up with a spiral of cardboard and will have to unwind it to tape the last side. Alternate taping the last side with taping the bottom of the bowl so that all the sides line up. Once taped glue the inside of the bowl with a glue gun to strengthen it. The tape the bottom and sides of the base together. Glue all inside seems. Do not attach the top yet. (my camera eat these pics sorry) Score all the fold lines with the tip of the scissors and then fold to match photos. Glue the back flaps down and then push up through the opening in the top until the flaps line up with the underside of the top. Glue down all five of the flaps on on three of the sides. (The flap on the bottom doesn't get glued down. It just rests against the bowl once everything is glued up) Start with the center bottom piece and tape starting at the very edge of the bell working down to the base. Match up the edges the whole way down. The cardboard may fight you on this but it is possible to do. This is why you pre-bent thing earlier. Then tape the bottom piece to the other side. Do this for the side pieces as well to end up with 5 pieces taped together. Once that's done brace open the sides and glue along all the inside seams. Now tape the top center piece to the 2 upper side pieces and then press open and glue. Now tape the 3 piece group and5 piece group and tape together along seems. This is the hardest part and it would be helpful to have an extra set of hands (or be an octopus)Glue the last 2 seems in the bell and far down as your glue gun will let you and you're done! Just square off the bottom so everything is even. Slide the bowl into the base. It will be a close fit. Tape the bell to the square opening in the top and glue down. Then place top with bell onto the base and glue along all 8 sides. And now enjoy your new cardboard gramophone!The pattern is sized to fit an iPhone 6 Plus. The phone in the picture is and old iPhone 3.

```markdown
# Cardboard Gramophone Creation Process

## START:
- Begin the process of creating a cardboard gramophone.

## INPUT: Materials Needed
- Cardboard
- Box cutters
- Scissors
- Tape
- Glue gun and glue sticks
- Cutting mat
- SVG pattern printouts

## PROCESS: Prepare Template and Cardboard
1. Cut out all SVG pattern pieces.
2. Extend the 4 stem bits of the bell by 2-3 inches for height adjustment.
3. Lay out all pieces on cardboard, aligning with the grain for proper bending.
4. Bevel edges of bowl and bell pieces using a hard object to compress cardboard edges.
5. Pre-bend the curved pieces to facilitate assembly.

## PROCESS: Assemble the Bowl
1. Tape the first two sides of the bowl starting from the longest side.
2. Repeat taping for all other sides to form a spiral shape.
3. Unwind the spiral to tape the last side and alternate with taping the bowl's bottom.
4. Glue the inside of the bowl for reinforcement.
5. Tape the bottom and sides of the base together, then glue all inside seams.
6. Hold off attaching the top of the base.

## PROCESS: Prepare the Bell
1. Score all fold lines on bell pieces.
2. Fold to match reference photos.
3. Glue back flaps of the bell, leaving the bottom flap unglued.

## PROCESS: Assemble the Bell
1. Begin with the center bottom piece and tape from top edge of the bell to the base.
2. Align edges carefully and tape the bottom piece to the other side.
3. Repeat for side pieces, resulting in 5 taped bell pieces.
4. Glue inside seams of the bell for stability.
5. Tape the top center piece to the two upper side pieces, then glue.
6. Join the 3-piece and 5-piece groups together and tape along seams.
7. Glue the last seams inside the bell as far as possible.

## PROCESS: Final Assembly
1. Even out the bottom of the bell to ensure it is level.
2. Slide the bowl into the base, securing it tightly.
3. Tape and glue the bell to the square opening on the top.
4. Place the top with the bell onto the base, then glue all sides.

## OUTPUT:
- Completed cardboard gramophone.

## DECISION: Is the phone size compatible with the pattern?
- IF Yes: Proceed to enjoy the new cardboard gramophone.
- ELSE No: Adjust the pattern size to fit the phone before starting the process.

## END:
- The cardboard gramophone creation process is complete.
```

instruct00527.title: Waffle Fries
instruct00527.text: Making perfect waffle fries at home is easier than you would think. In fact, there really is not much to it at all. Once you know the trick, you can feast on waffle fries to your heart's content. No longer do you have to go to fine eating establishments such as Chick-fil-A to endulge in such a delicacy. These waffle fries are perfect for any backyard barbecue, big game night, or romantic evening. In fact, you can even spice things up a bit more by adding some cajun seasoning. The only necessary ingredient is a potato. I used 4 large russet potatoes and found this made plenty of fries. Beyond that, you may also want to consider adding some cajun seasoning. However, this is not entirely necessary.In terms of other materials, you will need a crinkle cutter, a pot filled half-way with oil for deep frying (or a deep fryer), a frying basket, and a food thermometer for measuring the temperature of the oil.(Note: This page includes affiliate links. This does not change the price of the items linked to.) To cut the waffle fries, slice downward on the end of a potato with a crinkle cutter.Rotato the potato 90 degrees, and slice downward again.Repeat this process until the entire potato is sliced.This may take some practice to get the perfect waffle cut. Bring the oil up to 375 degrees.If you have a deep fryer like I do, then fill the basket about a quarter of the way up with uncooked fries and then submerge it in the fryer.If you are just using a pot, carefully dump the fries into the oil without splashing.Let the fries cook for about 5 minutes or until golden brown and then remove them from the oil. Let the fries cool off on a baking pan covered with paper towels.If you plan to add a seasoning, now is the time to sprinkle it on. Consume waffle fries vigorously with ketchup or (if uncultured) your dip of choice. You can even share them with friends or family if you are feeling generous.If you have no friends or family, having a basket full of waffle fries is great for making new friends! Did you find this useful, fun, or entertaining? Follow @madeineuphoria to see my latest projects.

```markdown
## Ingredients and Materials

    - INPUT: Baking pan.
    - INPUT: Paper towels.

    - PROCESS: Share the waffle fries with friends or family if desired.
    - OUTPUT: Enjoying the waffle fries.

- END: The process of making and serving waffle fries is complete.
```

instruct00263.title: Dremel Repair
instruct00263.text: So my Dremel 395 died mid project! No power no strange noises! it was just mocking me and acting like it was unplugged!I figured that since it didn't smell of burning metal I should be able to get it going again. I did notice that it was running hot for the past little while.First unplug the tool.Check to see if the shaft spins freely, if not you may have a bearing problem. You can sometimes free up a bad bearing with light oil but noisy bearings mean mechanical damage and it should be replaced as soon as possible. If the bearings are bad then the whole armature will need to be replaced. this is available online for around $17.If it does then next check the brushes. These are under small blue screw caps on my tool. They should remove easily and have lots of carbon "brick" left.On my tool one came out easily while the other separated from the spring and remained in the brush holder.So it looks like I have a stuck brush which has worn down and no longer makes contact with the commutator (more later)! This explains the no power situation! Remove the hanging clipRemove the body screws, mine were torx 15Gently separate the body halves making sure that no small parts fall out, like the shaft lock assembly at the nose of the tool.Remove the motor assembly from the body making sure to note which side is up with respect to your dis-assembly order.Remove the rubber spacer at the rear of the motor shaftGently pull the brush block assembly rearward to remove it. Use a rounded tool like a screwdriver shaft and gently push the stuck brush out of the brush block.Check for damage, in this case there was none and I was able to re-use the brushes and brush block. Gently dress any warped or melted plastic with a needle file or sand paper. Reattach the spring to the brush using mild force.Test for proper fit by inserting the brush to make sure that it doesn't bind.I suspect that the heat was caused by a dirty and worn commutator ( where the brushes contact the rotor), which in turn caused the brush to melt into the carrier.Using a very fine sand paper ( 800 grit) clean and dress the commutator until it is shiny and smooth. Clean the black lines between the segments of the commutator using a brass brush to remove any chance of shorting. The brushes go in last! Severely worn brushes should be replaced!The brush holder connects to the motor assembly via friction fit contacts. Gently press them into place.Reattach the rubber spacer to the rear bearing and place the motor into the housing. Place the other half of the housing in place and test that to motor freely spins, if it grinds, open the case and flip the magnet assembly of the motor over and re-install, it should be smooth now.Screw the case shut.Look for a dark line on one edge of the brushes, if there is one, then this installs in the direction of the arrow. Dark line in the direction of travel. Install the brush caps.Plug in the tool and test. If it doesn't spin at this point then you most likely have a burned out switch, unfortunately that will need to be replaced. The switch is available online for around $16.Mine now works better than it has in a very long time!Now back to the original project...

```markdown
# Dremel 395 Repair Process

## START:
- Unplug the Dremel tool. (Safety first)

## PROCESS: Check Shaft Spin
- Check if the shaft spins freely.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the shaft not spinning freely?
  - Yes: Proceed to PROCESS: Address Bearing Issue.
  - No: Proceed to PROCESS: Check Brushes.

## PROCESS: Address Bearing Issue
- INPUT: Light oil.
- Attempt to free up the bearing with light oil.
- OUTPUT: Temporary fix for the bearing.

## DECISION [IF]: Are bearings noisy?
  - Yes: Replace bearings as soon as possible.
  - No: Continue with the next step.

## INPUT: Replacement armature (if bearings are bad)
- Purchase a replacement armature online (approximately $17).
- STORE: Replacement armature for later use.
- END: If armature replacement is required, the process for brush check will be irrelevant.

## PROCESS: Check Brushes
- Locate and remove the small blue screw caps to access the brushes.
- Remove the brushes and inspect for adequate carbon "brick".

## DECISION [IF]: Did one brush come out easily and the other did not?
  - Yes: Proceed to PROCESS: Address Stuck Brush.
  - No: Proceed to PROCESS: Reassemble if brushes are okay.

## PROCESS: Address Stuck Brush
- Remove the hanging clip.
- INPUT: Torx 15 screwdriver.
- Remove the body screws with the Torx 15 screwdriver.
- Gently separate the body halves, ensuring no small parts fall out.
- Remove the motor assembly, noting its orientation.
- Remove the rubber spacer at the rear of the motor shaft.
- Gently pull the brush block assembly rearward to remove it.
- Use a rounded tool to push out the stuck brush from the brush block.
- Check for damage and dress any warped or melted plastic with a needle file or sandpaper.
- Reattach the spring to the brush using mild force.
- Test for proper fit by inserting the brush.

## PROCESS: Clean and Dress the Commutator
- INPUT: 800 grit sandpaper, brass brush.
- Clean the commutator with sandpaper until shiny.
- Clean the black lines between the segments with a brass brush.

## PROCESS: Reassemble Motor Assembly
- Reattach the brush holder to the motor assembly.
- Reattach the rubber spacer to the rear bearing.
- Place the motor into the housing.
- Ensure the motor spins freely; if not, adjust the magnet assembly.

## PROCESS: Close Housing and Install Brushes
- Screw the housing shut.
- Observe the direction of the dark line on the brushes.
- Install the brushes according to the direction of the arrow (dark line in the direction of travel).
- Install the brush caps.

## PROCESS: Test the Tool
- Plug in the tool and test it.

## DECISION [IF]: Does the tool not spin?
  - Yes: Proceed to PROCESS: Replace Switch.
  - No: OUTPUT: The tool is now functioning properly. END.

## PROCESS: Replace Switch
- INPUT: Replacement switch (approximately $16).
- Replace the burned-out switch with the new one.
- OUTPUT: The switch is replaced, and the tool should function.

## END:
- The Dremel tool is now repaired and ready for use.
- Return to the original project.
```
