instruct00889.title: Hot Air Soldering Gun From a Desoldering Iron With a Vaccume Pump
instruct00889.text: Here I'll show you how I converted my desoldering iron into a hot air soldering gun. Some may ask why is this tut when there is the easier one wit the iron from digikey. Well the answer is, digikey doesn't ship to europe and all I managed to find here is this type of desoldering irons. One more thing is that this conversion is totaly reversible, you can use your desoldering iron to desolder in just one minute - no modifications to the stock irons are made. What you will need for this tutorial 1. Desoldering iron 40W with a built-in vaccume pump - $ 6 2. One bottle cap 3. One screw 5x20mm 4. One fishtank air pump - $ 6 5. 1m (3ft) flexible hose-pipe - $ 0,3 6. 1cm of hard hose-pipe 7. 1m (3ft) thin copper wire You will need a drill machine and 2,7 or 3mm drill bit so let's start... First we need a desoldering iron. I bought mine for 4 EUROs or about US$6 from the local electronics shop. It is 40W and you can find the same at ebay. First we must disassemble our desoldering iron. It has a body, a yellow cylinder, a spring and a piston. The spring and the piston we don't need, so we pack them together, in case we deceide to use the iron as it is meant to be used. Now we need a bottle cap. These caps are used with many bottles, mainly bottles for chemicals or from the drugstore. I was wondering how to put the hose from the air pump into the yellow cylinder, when I found that this cap fits perfectly to it. This is easier to find I think. We need 5mm screw, that is about 20mm long. The idea is to drill a hole through it. I try drilling with a 2mm bit, but I broke it, so I dill a hole with a 2,7mm - no troubles this time. I think any fishtank air compressor will do the job. However I was looking for a cheap one, but with variable speed control. It turns out that the speed control cost much than I was ready to spend, but found this 200L/h with 2 speeds for 4 EUROs or US$6. I thought - that's what I was looking for. The same can be found on ebay too. 1m or 3ft from the propper sized hose-pipe will be sufficent, it costs me about 30 cents. You will notice that, when the piston is removed, the yellow cylinder becomes loose and we need something to press it against the body. I use about 1cm of somekind of a hard hose-pipe I've got at home. You can use whatever you find fit. Now that we have everything ready, we just need to connect the parts. With this assembly I managed to get as high as 240'C, enough to melt a sn63/pb37 alloy but just not enough to reflow a smd board. So I made just one more tunning of the device. You'll need about 1m or 3ft of thin wire, copper will be best, then wind this wire into a coil with a 1,5mm diameter. I wound it around a watchmaker screwdriver, but everything that is 1,5mm, hard and stright will do. Now put this coil into the desoldering iron shaft. This way, the coil will be heated from the iron, and when the air flows through it, it will release more heat than the bare shaft itself. With this tuning the temperature rised to above 310'C, that is high enough to reflow the smd parts. So you have a Hot air soldering gun for just under 10 EUROs or US$15. One more tunning. I sewed myself a strap to hold the yellow cylinder to the iron body, but you can use a rubber band or scotch tape.

```markdown
# Hot Air Soldering Gun Conversion Guide

## System Overview
The system converts a desoldering iron into a hot air soldering gun, which is reversible and allows for desoldering when needed. The conversion requires a set of materials and tools, which are assembled into a hot air soldering gun capable of reaching temperatures sufficient for soldering tasks.

### Materials and Tools Required
- START: Begin the conversion process.
  - INPUT: Desoldering iron (40W with built-in vacuum pump) - $6
  - INPUT: Bottle cap
  - INPUT: Screw (5x20mm)
  - INPUT: Fish tank air pump - $6
  - INPUT: Flexible hose-pipe (1m or 3ft) - $0.3
  - INPUT: Hard hose-pipe (1cm)
  - INPUT: Thin copper wire (1m or 3ft)
  - INPUT: Drill machine
  - INPUT: Drill bit (2.7 or 3mm)

### Disassembly of Desoldering Iron
- PROCESS: Disassemble the desoldering iron.
  - OUTPUT: Separated body, yellow cylinder, spring, and piston.
  - STORE: Spring and piston for potential future use.

### Preparing the Bottle Cap
- PROCESS: Select a bottle cap that fits onto the yellow cylinder.
- PROCESS: Drill a hole through the screw using a 2.7mm bit.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the hole drilled successfully?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Attempt drilling again with an appropriate drill bit size.
- OUTPUT: Bottle cap with a hole for the screw.

### Acquiring Air Pump and Hose
- PROCESS: Choose a fish tank air pump with variable speed control.
- PROCESS: Acquire 1m of flexible hose-pipe.
- OUTPUT: Air pump and hose ready for assembly.

### Stabilizing the Cylinder
- PROCESS: Use a piece of hard hose-pipe to stabilize the yellow cylinder within the iron body.
- OUTPUT: Stabilized yellow cylinder.

### Assembly of the Hot Air Gun
- PROCESS: Connect the air pump hose to the yellow cylinder using the prepared bottle cap.
- PROCESS: Secure the yellow cylinder to the iron body using a strap, rubber band, or tape.
- OUTPUT: Functional hot air soldering gun.

### Temperature Tuning
- PROCESS: Wind thin copper wire into a coil with a 1.5mm diameter.
- PROCESS: Insert the copper coil into the desoldering iron shaft.
  - DECISION [IF]: Does inserting the coil increase the temperature adequately?
    - Yes: The hot air gun is now capable of reflowing SMD parts.
    - No: Adjust the coil or consider additional tuning.
- OUTPUT: Enhanced hot air soldering gun with increased temperature capability.

### Final Output
- OUTPUT: A hot air soldering gun for under 10 Euros (or $15).
- END: The conversion process is complete.
```

instruct00241.text: My favorite Chinese food, next to Chow Mein, is Beef Broccoli. I really love Beef Broccoli. He hates those things called "vegetables" and especially Broccoli. He is one of those people that can taste the bitter in broccoli, so I get all of his broccoli when we eat out! (YEAH!). He would prefer that I never make it. So when he is out of town I have Chinese food, especially Beef Broccoli. Well this weekend he is out of town and I am going to make Beef Broccoli, so I will be extra happy. This is one way to make it. Ingredients 1 lbs. boneless beef chuck roast, sliced into thin strips (I bought it sliced that way) 1 cup beef broth 1/2 cup soy sauce 1/3 cup brown sugar 1 tablespoon sesame oil 3 garlic cloves, minced 4tablespoons cornstarch 4tablespoons sauce from the crock pot after being cooked 16 oz.Broccoli florets Supplies: Slow Cooker/Crockpot Measuring cups Measuring spoons Spoons Chef Knife (not shown, google it) Place beef in a crock pot. In a small bowl, combine beef broth, soy sauce, brown sugar, oil, and garlic. Do you know the easy way to peal garlic cloves. # Beef Broccoli Recipe System

```markdown
## Ingredients and Supplies
- START: Begin the recipe process.
- INPUT: Gather the following ingredients and supplies:
  - 1 lb. boneless beef chuck roast, sliced into thin strips
  - 1 cup beef broth
  - 1/2 cup soy sauce
  - 1/3 cup brown sugar
  - 1 tablespoon sesame oil
  - 3 garlic cloves, minced
  - 4 tablespoons cornstarch
  - 16 oz. broccoli florets
  - Supplies: Slow Cooker/Crockpot, Measuring cups, Measuring spoons, Spoons, Chef Knife

## Preparing the Sauce
- PROCESS: Mince the garlic cloves using the flat side of a chef knife.
- INPUT: In a small bowl, combine the following ingredients:
  - Beef broth
  - Soy sauce
  - Brown sugar
  - Sesame oil
  - Minced garlic
- PROCESS: Stir all the sauce ingredients together.

## Cooking the Beef
- INPUT: Place the beef strips into the crockpot.
- PROCESS: Pour the mixed sauce over the beef in the crockpot.
- PROCESS: Stir the beef and sauce to ensure the beef is well coated.
- PROCESS: Put the lid on the crockpot.
- PROCESS: Cook on low for 4-5 hours.

## Thickening the Sauce
- PROCESS: After 4-5 hours, take 4 tablespoons of sauce from the crockpot.
- INPUT: In a cup, combine the sauce with 4 tablespoons of cornstarch.
- PROCESS: Stir the cornstarch and sauce mixture until smooth.
- INPUT: Add the cornstarch mixture back into the crockpot.
- PROCESS: Stir well to combine with the beef and sauce.

## Adding the Broccoli
- INPUT: Add the broccoli florets to the crockpot.
- PROCESS: Stir the broccoli into the beef and sauce to combine.
- PROCESS: Cover the crockpot.
- PROCESS: Cook on high for an additional 30 minutes. The sauce must boil to thicken.

## Serving
- OUTPUT: Serve the beef broccoli over hot cooked rice or by itself.
- END: Enjoy the meal.
```

instruct00489.title: How to Make Pumpkin Pie Pancakes From a Mix
instruct00489.text: I love homemade pancakes, the kind where you start with flour and go from there...they always taste wonderful! But to be honest, I don't always have the time to measure out a bunch of ingredients - I want to toss something together and feed my hungry boils and ghouls (er, boys and girls). So I came up with the lazy way!Ingredients: 1 1/2 cups pancake mix 1 tsp Pumpkin pie spice 1 large egg 1 Tbsp brown sugar, packed 1 Tbsp vegetable oil 1 tsp Vanilla 3/4 cup canned or pureed pumpkin (or fresh cooked) 1/2 cup waterIf you need to use up the rest of your pumpkin, make a batch of Spiced Pumpkin Pillow Cookies with Ginger Cream Cheese Frosting! Or, make a double batch! Pancakes keep in the freezer for up to 3 months, and reheat very well! Step 1 - Prep your Griddle If using an electric griddle, heat to 375 Degrees F. If using a pan, heat until drops of water dance and evaporate immediately (med. heat). When the griddle/pan is ready, lightly grease the griddle with butter. You don't need a lot! Step 2 - Measure & Mix In a medium bowl, mix the pancake mix and spices together. Measure flour by lightly spooning it into the measuring cup, then leveling off with the back of a knife. In another bowl, whisk the egg and the brown sugar together. Stir in the oil, the pumpkin, and most of the water. Add the liquid ingredients to the dry ingredients. Stir with a spatula until just combined adding more water to obtain the right consistency.If you have time, refrigerate the batter for 30 minutes before you start cooking the pancakes. Step 3 - Cook the Cakes Use a 1/4 cup measuring cup to pour your batter. Pour fast, leaving a 2" space between each pancake. Let them cook until the edges start to look firm/crispy, and bubbles form in the middle. Using a flat spatula,carefully slide it under each pancake. Using your wrist, quickly flip the pancakes. Let the pancakes cook for another minute or two. the second side may be a little lighter in color than the first, this is okay!Don't worry if your first attempts aren't perfect, you will get better with practice! Step 4 - Eat! They can be kept warm in a 200 degrees F oven, but they're best eaten right out of the pan. Serve with your favorite toppings, like syrup...or smear with honey butter!These are a great Sunday morning breakfast, but we like to make them on Halloween for dinner, so we have full bellies before trick or treating (less candy eaten on the sly that way).

```markdown
# Pancake Making System

## Summary
This system describes the process of making homemade pancakes using a pancake mix with added pumpkin pie spice and other ingredients to create a flavorful breakfast option. The system includes steps for preparing the griddle, mixing ingredients, cooking the pancakes, and serving them. It also suggests using leftover pumpkin to make Spiced Pumpkin Pillow Cookies and provides storage advice for pancakes.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the pancake making process.

### INPUT: Ingredients and Tools
- 1 1/2 cups pancake mix
- 1 tsp Pumpkin pie spice
- 1 large egg
- 1 Tbsp brown sugar, packed
- 1 Tbsp vegetable oil
- 1 tsp Vanilla
- 3/4 cup canned or pureed pumpkin (or fresh cooked)
- 1/2 cup water
- Griddle or pan
- Medium bowls
- Whisk
- Spatula
- Measuring cups
- Butter for greasing

### PROCESS: Preheat Griddle
- IF using an electric griddle:
  - Heat to 375 Degrees F.
- ELSE IF using a pan:
  - Heat until drops of water dance and evaporate immediately (medium heat).
- Lightly grease the griddle with butter.

### PROCESS: Mix Dry Ingredients
- In a medium bowl, mix the pancake mix and pumpkin pie spice together.

### PROCESS: Mix Wet Ingredients
- In another bowl, whisk the egg and brown sugar together.
- Stir in the vegetable oil, vanilla, pumpkin, and most of the water.

### DECISION: Is batter consistency correct?
- IF No:
  - Add more water to obtain the right consistency.
- ELSE:
  - Proceed to next step.

### DECISION: Do you have time to refrigerate the batter?
- IF Yes:
  - Refrigerate batter for 30 minutes.
- ELSE:
  - Proceed to cooking.

### PROCESS: Cook Pancakes
- Use a 1/4 cup measuring cup to pour batter onto the griddle, leaving a 2" space between each pancake.
- Cook until edges firm up and bubbles form in the middle.
- Carefully flip the pancakes with a spatula and cook for another minute or two.

### OUTPUT: Pancakes Ready
- The pancakes are cooked and ready to be served.

### PROCESS: Serve Pancakes
- Keep warm in a 200 degrees F oven if not eating immediately.
- Serve with favorite toppings, such as syrup or honey butter.

### END:
- The pancake making process is complete.

## Additional Notes:
- To use up leftover pumpkin, make Spiced Pumpkin Pillow Cookies with Ginger Cream Cheese Frosting.
- Pancakes can be stored in the freezer for up to 3 months and reheated.
- The recipe is especially recommended for a Halloween dinner to ensure full bellies before trick-or-treating.
```

```markdown
# MCreator Mod Creation Step-by-Step Summary

## Introduction
START:
- Acknowledge that MCreator is for beginners and that learning Java and using Forge is recommended for serious modding.
- Note that the tutorial is based on an outdated Minecraft version and may not align with the user's experience.
- Advise that proceeding with MCreator is for learning purposes only.

## Mod Creation with MCreator
PROCESS: Install MCreator
- INPUT: Ensure MCreator is installed properly before starting the mod creation process.

PROCESS: Begin Mod Creation
- INPUT: Type in the name of the mod in the text box, ensuring there are no spaces.
- INPUT: Choose the mod type, selecting "Block" for this tutorial.

PROCESS: Create Block Texture
- Navigate to "Resources" and select "Create item/block texture".
- DECISION [IF]: Is there an image available for the texture?
  - Yes: Proceed to load the image.
  - No: END (Cannot proceed without an image.)

PROCESS: Load and Use Image
- Click "Load Image..." and select the desired picture for the texture.
- Click "Use" to confirm the selection.
- INPUT: Choose "Block" as the texture type.

PROCESS: Name the Texture
- INPUT: Type a name for the texture with no spaces.

PROCESS: Assign Texture to Block
- Click the blue-bordered side and select the texture.
- DECISION [IF]: Did MCreator auto-fill all sides with the selected texture?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Manually assign the texture to each side.

PROCESS: Configure Block Properties
- Navigate through the block main menu to set properties like hardness, resistance, luminance, sound, etc.
- INPUT: Change the "Name in GUI" to the desired block name.
- Feel free to explore and modify other settings.

PROCESS: Set Particle Effects
- Review the particle menu and adjust settings if necessary.
- OUTPUT: Default particle settings are applied unless changed.

PROCESS: Add Events to Block
- Click "Add Event" for the desired condition (e.g., "on block right-clicked").
- Select an event, like "Strike Lightning", and add it.

PROCESS: Define Crafting Ingredients
- Click on a crafting slot and select the required block or item from the menu.
- Repeat for all ingredients needed for crafting or smelting the block.

PROCESS: Set World Generation Parameters
- Click the world generation button and edit the lower and upper bounds, frequency, and other settings as desired.

PROCESS: Finalize and Export Mod
- Wait for the console to confirm "Task Return Code Check OK".
- Click "My Workspace" and select "Export the Mod".
- INPUT: Fill in details about the mod and click "Recompile and Export".
- Choose the location to save the mod file (zip or jar).

OUTPUT: The mod file is created, and the user becomes a mod developer.

## Post-Creation Steps
PROCESS: Install and Use the Mod
- If Forge has not been run on the account, do so now.
- Place the mod file (zip) into the `%appdata%/.minecraft/mods` folder.
- Run Forge to use the mod in Minecraft.

END: Enjoy the mod and celebrate by grabbing some food.
```

instruct00608.title: DIY Repurposed Vintage Schwinn Bicycle Flower Display
instruct00608.text: My grandfather bought this Vintage Schwinn Bicycle for my aunt over 45 years ago. He got more use out of it than my aunt ever did. I remember as a child watching him ride this classic bike. Not only could he ride it but he actually did a trick with it that the whole neighborhood absolutely loved to see him do and often requested when they saw the bike outside of the garage. He would ride this bike backwards. Yup that's right, he would climb on facing the back tire and drive up and down the street peddling backward.I wanted a piece of my grandfather with me at all times, he was my mentor growing up, and so I proudly display this bike out in front of my home not only as a great planter for flowers but also in remembrance of the man I love. It took me a few years to actually paint it a different color and I was hesitant about doing so. But I knew that if I did not it would probably rust away in the garage. I did not want that to happen. So I came up with this beautiful flower stand that I actually have fallen in love with year after year. It makes an awesome springtime display full of colorful flowers in a wicker basket. For more ideas visit my instructables page or my website An old vintage bicycle3-six packs of flowerspotting soil1-wicker basket 3 cans rustoleum yellow spray paintplastic sheeting for lining the wicker basket scissorswire Remove the wheels and chain assembly from the bicycleUsing some plastic sheeting spread it out in a well ventilated outdoor area wide enough that the bike will fit in the center.Starting from the bottom start spraying your paint in a side to side motion flip the bike right side up and repeat the process of spraying until you get and even coat on the bikelet dryrepeat steps 3 and 4 for a more even coatrepeat as necessary and let completely dryreinstall the wheels and chain assembly and stand upright find a wicker basket that will fit your bike nicely the wicker basket I used was about twelve inches in diameterusing some wire, go through the bottom of the basket and around the newspaper holder on the bike. wrap the wire securely to the bikes frame.You may need to find ways to attach the wire in different locations so that your basket will stand up to strong winds and still stay attached.line the wicker basket with plastic sheetingpunch some holes through the bottom of the plastic sheeting so water can drain outfill the wicker basket with potting soil and wetplant your flowersdisplay proudly

```markdown
# Vintage Schwinn Bicycle Transformation into a Flower Stand

## System Overview
This system transforms a vintage Schwinn bicycle into an outdoor flower stand. The process involves painting the bicycle, attaching a wicker basket, lining it with plastic sheeting, and planting flowers. The bicycle serves as a decorative and memorial piece to remember a loved one. 

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the transformation of the vintage Schwinn bicycle into a flower stand.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Bicycle
- INPUT: An old vintage bicycle.
- OUTPUT: Bicycle prepared for painting.

### PROCESS: Remove Bicycle Parts
- Remove the wheels and chain assembly from the bicycle.
- STORE: Set aside the removed parts.

### PROCESS: Set Up Painting Area
- INPUT: Plastic sheeting.
- OUTPUT: Area prepared for painting.
- Spread plastic sheeting out in a well-ventilated outdoor area, ensuring it's wide enough for the bike.

### PROCESS: Paint the Bicycle
- INPUT: 3 cans of Rustoleum yellow spray paint.
- OUTPUT: Painted bicycle.

#### PROCESS: First Coat of Paint
- Start spraying paint in a side-to-side motion from the bottom of the bicycle.
- Flip the bike right side up and repeat the spray process for an even coat.
- Let the bike dry.

#### DECISION [IF]: Is the first coat of paint even?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: Repeat the painting process for a more even coat.

#### PROCESS: Additional Coats of Paint
- Repeat the painting and drying process as necessary until the desired coverage is achieved.
- Let the paint completely dry.

### PROCESS: Reassemble the Bicycle
- Reinstall the wheels and chain assembly.
- Stand the bicycle upright.
- OUTPUT: Painted and reassembled bicycle.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Wicker Basket
- INPUT: 1 wicker basket, approximately 12 inches in diameter.
- OUTPUT: Basket ready to be attached to the bicycle.

#### PROCESS: Attach the Basket to the Bicycle
- Use wire to secure the basket through the bottom and around the newspaper holder on the bike.
- Wrap the wire securely to the bike's frame.
- OUTPUT: Wicker basket attached to the bicycle.

#### DECISION [IF]: Is the basket secure?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: Find additional attachment points for the wire to ensure the basket is stable.

### PROCESS: Line the Wicker Basket
- INPUT: Plastic sheeting, scissors.
- OUTPUT: Lined wicker basket ready for soil.

- Line the wicker basket with plastic sheeting.
- Punch holes in the bottom of the plastic for water drainage.

### PROCESS: Plant the Flowers
- INPUT: 3 six-packs of flowers, potting soil.
- OUTPUT: Flower-filled wicker basket.

- Fill the lined wicker basket with potting soil and wet it.
- Plant the flowers in the soil.

### OUTPUT: Display the Flower Stand
- Proudly display the bicycle with the flower-filled wicker basket in front of your home.

### END:
- The transformation of the vintage Schwinn bicycle into a flower stand is complete.
```

instruct00348.title: Reclaimed Wood Table
instruct00348.text: After using a cheap plastic card table as my only table for nearly two years I decided it was time for a change. I had seen some large wooden tables that I liked and figured that I could make one myself. I also used reclaimed wood to make this table so it's a bit cooler looking (and environmentally friendly!).The finished product is heavy, but not too bad. I'm using Douglas Fir which is a bit soft. Marks will show on the table, but to me that is okay. You may want to adjust your wood choice if you like something different. To make this table I used three pieces of reclaimed Douglas Fir. Each piece was 3"x10"x5'. I ended up buying five of them from M Fine Lumber in Brooklyn. They came from this 25' piece of wood that they were nice enough to cut into pieces for me.As far as other consumables go you'll need some wood glue, tenons (or biscuits), and some table legs. I got some of these from Ikea. Here's the link to the legs.I also used a hammer and vice grips to remove nails, a circular saw, a mortiser, a rubber mallet, sander, and a drill/screwdriver. If you use reclaimed lumber it will likely come to you really dirty, not straight, and covered in total crap.The first thing I did was go over each piece with a hammer and a pair of vice grips to remove the nails and other interesting metal objects that had found their way into the wood over the course of it's previous life. This is really important because if there's any metal left in the wood it can mess up your tools when you use them on it (I suppose this could also cause an accident where you could be injured or killed. Be careful). It's probably a good idea to use a metal detector to make sure you got everything out.After the metal was removed I decided to use my sander with a very rough abrasive in it to remove all the crap on the outside of the wood. This made the rest of the process a lot cleaner which is important to me because I'm doing all this in the same space that I live in.Next you're going to want to use your saw to make sure all the corners are at 90 degree angles. I used my circular saw, but a table saw would probably be better. Actually what would be great is a jointer. I don't have one of those though, so I'm making do with what I have. I used my Domino to cut mortises in the pieces and then glued them together with tenons in place. There are 28 mortises in the table. I imagine you could get by with less, but I was a little nervous about this falling apart. I sanded the surfaces to make sure they were smooth and splinter free. I started with 60 grit and then went up all the way to 220 to make sure it was very smooth. This makes a huge difference so I think it's worth spending some time on.The legs are from Ikea. I think they are for expanding a countertop. We've been using them at my work to build desks for people so I figured they would be great for this too. They cost about $30 each so not too bad. I like the contrast of the metal to the natural wood. I used General Finishes Arm R Seal which is a penetrating resin. This stuff was really easy to apply and has a nice look. You should put a few coats on so that the finish is sturdy enough to withstand some abuse from moisture and hot plates.Hope you enjoy it! It was fun to make and really rewarding to use every day!

instruct00573.title: Hidden Room Under the Stairs
instruct00573.text: Seems the problem is, there is never enough space. My mission is to find every speck of useful space in my house. knowing that there was a large space under my stairs that wasn't being used was driving me insane. But I didnt want to just put an ugly door or a fake air vent in the side of my stairs. So I came up with the Idea of recessed shelves with one set of the shelves being a secret door. Please be gentle this is my first instructable. I took a lot of pictures to help me get the idea across. enjoy. First you need to find the empty space. The larger portion under the stairs is taken up by my pantry. Cut a hole in the wall preferably when your wife isnt home. Be careful of any potential wires or plumbing that may be in the wall. I couldnt wait to put things under there. There is a 6ft christmas tree, 4 plastic tubs, kids rocking chair, a wreath and various other small items. It sure beats going into the attic every Christmas. Make a 2x4 frame for a door and attach a piece the drywall you cut out to the back of it to make a door. Finish cutting out the rest of the drywall to the size that you want your shelves to be. cut 2x4's to fit across the bottom to cover the hollow spots in the wall. frame out the top with 2x4's and add wood to any wall studs to make them wider so they can be covered with a 1x4. cut 1x4's to trim around the outside of the unit like in the pictures. spray the backside of the drywall that is exposed with spray texture to match the rest of your wall. then paint trim and drywall. I had to add half inch strips of wood by the hinges to compensate for the thickness of the drywall for the piece of trim that will be added on top of it. I also added a gate latch to the back of the door at this time you can see how it works in the final video. cut the final two strips of 1x4 to cover wall stud and the stud with hinge. Then paint. the trim that is over the door hinge is held in place with magnets. I then cut 1 inch strips of molding to go around the inside corners of the sections leaving gaps for the shelves to go into. I glued all of these in place. I cut a pre-laminated 4x8 sheet of wood for the shelves then added white plastic trim to front of each shelf. OK so here are pictures and a video of the final product. There were a few scratch my head moments along the way but all in all it wasn't so bad once I got up the nerve to cut that first hole. again this was my first istructable so be nice and if you liked it please vote for me in the Weekend Projects Contest. Thank you.

instruct00002.title: Egg in an Avocado Hole
instruct00002.text: A quick and healthy recipe to start your morning off right. Egg in an Avocado Hole is delicious and has definitely become a staple in my breakfast routine and maybe yours too! Breakfast can be tough, we're not always ready to eat first thing in the morning. Even if we are hungry, it often seems to be easier to grab a sugary cereal than simply make a healthy and nutritious breakfast. I've been looking for a stand-in breakfast recipe for sometime now to through into my breakfast routine. I stumbled upon this one in theEpicuriousblog the other day and didn't want to wait for them to publish the elusive recipe (they were going to wait a day), so I started researching and came across the one I'm sharing in this Instructable. As a final bonus, this recipe can easily be gluten-free or paleo friendly! Ingredients: Two Eggs One Avocado Spoon Knife Baking Dish SmallBowlOptional Garnishes: Salt Pepper Kale Strips Bacon Chives Cheese Hot Sauce Get Creative!! Turn your oven on to 425 F.While it's heating up you can prepare your avocado. Start by slicing your avocado in half lengthwise. Remove the pit and compost it. Using your spoon, gently scrape and scoop out a small portion of the hole left by the pit in your avocado. This will allow you to fit more egg into your avocado half. Crack your eggs into a bowl. Using a regular teaspoon or tablespoon, gently scoop one of your yolks out of the bowl and place it into one of your avocado halves. Fill the remainder of the space in your avocado with egg white.Repeat with the second egg and avocado half. Place your freshly egged avocado halves in a small baking dish. You'll want your avocados to be fairly snug so that they don't tip over letting the egg run out of the center. I've found that my bread loaf baking dish is perfect for most larger avocados. If you need to find a smaller vessel or use tin foil to secure your avocados from rolling. Bake your Egg in an Avocado Hole for 15-20 minutes at 425F depending on your oven and how well done you like your eggs. Once baked to your preferred egg doneness, remove your baking dish from the oven and allow the avocados to cool for roughly a minute before removing them from the dish. Salt and pepper to taste.Top with your favorite garnishes. I listed a few of mine in step 1 in the Ingredients section, but get creative! Serve with some fresh fruit and enjoy! Some people also like them served with toast so they can spread the buttery avocado and delicious yolk on a crunchy piece of toast.

instruct00150.title: Make Crystal Clear Ice!
instruct00150.text: in this instructable I will show you how to make crystal cear ice without any special equipment! it is super easy! you will be surprised! the filtered water is much more pure and clean! one of the things that causes the cloudiness of the ice is dust and extra minerals in the water - the filtered water is much better for our clear ice! this is very simple but very effective! - Boil the water , and than let it cool. - after it is cool , boil the water again! - this is it! you are done ! explanation : the double boiling eliminates dissolved air in the water and decomposes minerals in the water ! dissolved air + minerals +dust are the causing of the cloudy look! this is the difference between regular ice (cloudy) and the crystal clear ice- after following the process!I hope you find this instructable useful and fun! enjoy your crystal clear ice!

```markdown
# Crystal Clear Ice Making Process

## Summary Representation

START: Begin the crystal clear ice-making process.

INPUT: Gather filtered water.

PROCESS: Boil the filtered water for the first time.

PROCESS: Allow the boiled water to cool down to room temperature.

PROCESS: Allow the water to cool down to room temperature after the first boil, ensuring it's not too hot for the second boil.

DECISION [IF]: Check if the water has been boiled for the second time.

  - No: Repeat the boiling process until the water has been boiled for the second time.

PROCESS: Let the double-boiled water cool down again to room temperature, preparing it for the freezing process.

OUTPUT: Freeze the cooled, double-boiled water to produce crystal clear ice.
```

instruct00011.title: Deli Style Roast Beef
instruct00011.text: Do you love roast beef sandwiches but hate paying deli meat prices? If YES, then keep reading. I will show you how to make deli style roast beef at home for a fraction of the cost. Things your gonna need: An oven preheated to 200 F. A roast of course. I use an eye round beef roast.Olive Oil Spices: Salt, pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder. Feel free to add your own flare. A meat thermometer is necessary. And some sort of roasting pan. Start by coating the meat in olive oil. Then sprinkle with salt and pepper followed by onion powder and garlic powder. The meat should be well coated on all sides.**I just had an idea. Mix equal parts salt, pepper, onion, and garlic. Spread on a cookie sheet and roll the meat in it. I'll give it a try next time. Time to cook the meat. Place the roast on a rack or a pan. You can line the pan with foil for easier clean up. Insert a meat thermometer all the way into the meat. Put the meat into a 200 F oven. Plan on cooking for 30min/lb of meat. My roast was 2.5lb, so I set the timer for 1.5 hr. What you want is an internal temperature of 125-130 F. This will insure that the meat is cooked but at the same time keep it a nice pink color and retain the moisture needed. My meat thermometer doesn't go low enough so after 1.5 hours I checked the roast with another thermometer that won't survive the oven. First reading: 106 F, not done yet. I put it back in for 30 min. Overall, It took another hour to reach temp, so for me it was 1hr/lb meatCooking temps:Rare: 120-130 F (50-55 C) This is what I'm aiming for.Medium-rare: 130-140 F (55-60 C) This will probably be okay if you cook it a little longer, should still be pink in the middle.Medium (with a touch of pink): 140-150 F (60-65 C) I think this is too much for roast beef, slightly pink in the center but dryerWell-done: 150-165 F (65-75 C) Over cooked, meat will be cooked through and dry. After 2.5 hrs, the internal meat temperature was almost 128 F. At this point, the meat needs to rest. Cover it in foil and let it sit for 30 minutes more. While it rests it will continue to cook and distribute the juices. It will drip a lot at this point. After the resting period I like to slice a piece off to make sure the meat is a good pink color. If you cook it too high you will get a pink center and brown outer portion, which is fine, but I like it rare. The meat looks good, so now I like to chill the meat in the refrigerator. It will be much easier to slice when it is cold. Of course if you can't wait, you can take a few slice now to hold you over. Once fully chilled, use a meat slicer or a sharp knife and cut the meat as thin as possible. Now that you have your roast beef, make a sandwich. I like to use sourdough bread with mayo and creamy horseradish topped off with cheddar cheese. I don't know how long this will store in the frig because it never lasts more than a couple of days. Enjoy.

```markdown
# Deli Style Roast Beef Recipe

## System Overview:
The system represents the process of making deli-style roast beef at home. The input is the raw materials and the output is a prepared roast beef suitable for sandwiches.

## Process Steps:

### START:
- Preheat the oven to 200 F.

### INPUT:
- Gather the following ingredients and tools:
  - Eye round beef roast
  - Olive oil
  - Salt
  - Pepper
  - Onion powder
  - Garlic powder
  - Meat thermometer
  - Roasting pan (optionally lined with foil)

### PROCESS: [Coating the meat]
- Coat the meat evenly in olive oil.
- Mix equal parts of salt, pepper, onion powder, and garlic powder.
- Spread the spice mix on a cookie sheet and roll the meat in it to coat all sides.

### PROCESS: [Cooking the meat]
- Place the roast on a rack in the roasting pan.
- Insert the meat thermometer into the thickest part of the meat.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the oven preheated to 200 F?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: Wait until the oven reaches the correct temperature.

### PROCESS:
- Cook the meat in the oven for 30 minutes per pound.
  - For example, for a 2.5 lb roast, set the timer for 1.5 hours.

### DECISION [IF]: Has the timer elapsed?
- Yes: Proceed to check the internal temperature.
- No: Continue cooking.

### PROCESS: [Checking internal temperature]
- Check the internal temperature of the meat aiming for:
  - Rare: 120-130 F
  - Medium-rare: 130-140 F
  - Medium: 140-150 F
  - Well-done: 150-165 F

### DECISION [IF]: Is the internal temperature at least 125-130 F?
- Yes: Proceed to the resting phase.
- No: Continue cooking and check every 30 minutes until the desired temperature is reached.

### PROCESS: [Resting the meat]
- Once the desired temperature is reached, remove the roast from the oven.
- Cover the roast with foil and let it rest for 30 minutes.

### DECISION [IF]: Has the meat rested for 30 minutes?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: Continue resting.

### PROCESS: [Slicing the meat]
- After resting, optionally check for the desired pink color by slicing off a piece.
- Chill the meat in the refrigerator to make slicing easier.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the meat fully chilled?
- Yes: Proceed to slice the meat.
- No: Continue chilling.

### PROCESS:
- Using a meat slicer or a sharp knife, slice the roast beef as thin as possible.

### OUTPUT:
- The final product is thinly sliced deli-style roast beef.

### PROCESS: [Making a sandwich]
- Prepare a sandwich using the roast beef, sourdough bread, mayo, creamy horseradish, and cheddar cheese.

### END:
- Enjoy your homemade deli-style roast beef sandwich.

## Notes:
- The storage time in the refrigerator is not specified as the roast beef typically does not last more than a couple of days before being consumed.
```

instruct00677.title: Brussels Sprout Salad
instruct00677.text: Thisbrussels sprout salad falls under the category of "ugly but tasty" - it's absolutely delicious, but it is nearly impossible to make it look nice. If you like brussels sprouts, this is a quick and easy recipe to use them in - goes by much faster than roasting them, and it's a good excuse to eat lots of bacon. pound of brussels sprouts red wine vinegar OR fresh lemon juice 4-5 strips of bacon 2-3 cloves of garlic salt and pepper Cook the bacon however you like - well done or fatty - doesn't matter! Leave the fat in the pan for now. Cut off the stalks of the brussels sprouts and take over the very outermost leaves. Then slice them thinly so they start to break apart. :) Mince your garlic. Pour off some of the bacon fat - you just want a couple of tablespoons in the pan. Turn the heat to medium and add in the sliced brussels sprouts. Let them cook until they've wilted a bit and then add in the garlic. Stir everything around until the garlic becomes fragrant and coated in the fat. Add the bacon back in, and then put in about a 1/2 tablespoon of vinegar or lemon juice. Scrape the bottom of the pan and stir everything well. At this point, test the sprouts for doneness. If they're not tender enough for you, turn the heat down to low and put the lid on. Cook them until the texture is right. :D Once the sprouts are well cooked, do one last taste test for vinegar, salt and pepper. Add more as needed and serve! It's best warm or room temp - when it gets colder the bacon fat starts to solidify. :)

```markdown
# Brussels Sprout Salad Recipe System

## Ingredients:
- 1 pound of brussels sprouts
- Red wine vinegar OR fresh lemon juice
- 4-5 strips of bacon
- 2-3 cloves of garlic
- Salt
- Pepper

## Procedure:

### START:
- Begin with the preparation of ingredients.

### PROCESS: Cook Bacon
- INPUT: 4-5 strips of bacon.
- OUTPUT: Cooked bacon and bacon fat.
- Cook the bacon to your preferred doneness.
- STORE the bacon fat in the pan for later use.

### PROCESS: Prepare Brussels Sprouts
- INPUT: 1 pound of brussels sprouts.
- OUTPUT: Prepared brussels sprouts.
- Cut off the stalks of the brussels sprouts and remove the very outermost leaves.
- Slice the brussels sprouts thinly so they start to break apart.

### PROCESS: Mince Garlic
- INPUT: 2-3 cloves of garlic.
- OUTPUT: Minced garlic.
- Mince the garlic and set aside.

### PROCESS: Adjust Bacon Fat
- DECISION [IF]: Is there excess bacon fat in the pan?
  - Yes: Pour off excess bacon fat, leaving only a couple of tablespoons.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

### PROCESS: Cook Brussels Sprouts
- INPUT: Sliced brussels sprouts.
- OUTPUT: Wilted brussels sprouts.
- Turn the heat to medium and add the sliced brussels sprouts to the pan with bacon fat.
- Cook until the brussels sprouts have wilted.

### PROCESS: Add Garlic
- INPUT: Minced garlic.
- OUTPUT: Garlic-infused brussels sprouts.
- Add the minced garlic to the pan.
- Stir until the garlic becomes fragrant and coated in the fat.

### PROCESS: Reintroduce Bacon
- INPUT: Cooked bacon.
- OUTPUT: Brussels sprouts with bacon.
- Add the cooked bacon back into the pan.

### PROCESS: Add Vinegar or Lemon Juice
- INPUT: 1/2 tablespoon of red wine vinegar OR lemon juice.
- OUTPUT: Brussels sprouts with added acidity.
- Add the vinegar or lemon juice to the pan.
- Scrape the bottom of the pan and stir well.

### DECISION [IF]: Are the brussels sprouts tender enough?
  - Yes: Proceed to final seasoning.
  - No: Continue cooking.

### PROCESS [ELSE]: Continue Cooking
- Turn the heat down to low.
- Cover the pan with a lid.
- Cook until the brussels sprouts reach the desired tenderness.

### PROCESS: Final Seasoning
- INPUT: Salt and pepper to taste.
- OUTPUT: Seasoned brussels sprout salad.
- Do a taste test for vinegar, salt, and pepper.
- Adjust the seasoning as needed.

### OUTPUT: Serve Brussels Sprout Salad
- The salad is best served warm or at room temperature.
- Note: If the salad gets too cold, the bacon fat may solidify.

### END
```

```markdown
# Structured Summary of "Hiding Files in an Image"

## System Overview
This system describes the process of hiding secret files within an image, using a Unix-based OS with compression tools and the `cat` command, or Windows with a compression tool. The system takes secret files and an image as inputs and outputs an image with the hidden files embedded within it. Additionally, the system requires a password to secure the compressed files.

### Inputs
- Unix-based OS or Windows with compression tools
- Secret files
- Innocent image (PNG or JPG format)
- Password for compression

### Outputs
- New image file with embedded secret files

## Process Steps

### START
- Begin the process of hiding files in an image

### PROCESS: Prepare Environment

### END: Hidden File Image Created

- Rename the extension of `newimage.png` to `out.rar`

### PROCESS: Open Archive Manager

### PROCESS: Enter Password and Extract Information
- INPUT: Enter the password used during compression
- Extract the secret files from the `out.rar` file
- OUTPUT: Access the secret files

- The secret files are now successfully extracted and accessible
```

instruct00198.text: With just a few items you may have around the house you can build a soldering, gluing, or assembly jig. Its an extra pair of helping hands. 1. Items required: a) 2 five inch pieces of 12 gauge copper wire which can be taken from home wiring cable, b) two solderless ring lugs, c) two mini alligator clips, d) a 3" x3" block of wood or decorative molding - available at your local home improvement store, e) one small wood screw (and a suitable drill bit for the pilot hole). Use a wood screw (pan head type) to secure the two ring lugs to the base. Use it as a soldering jig, gluing jig, assembly fixture, photo stand, or however you see fit.

instruct00543.title: Chalkboard Paint Jars
instruct00543.text: Every mad scientist needs jars and those jars need labels, and since I like to reuse my jars the jar labels would need to bere-writable. Luckily, making re-writable labels for glass jars is easy with chalkboard paint. All you need to make your own chalkboard paint jarsischalkboard paint, painter's tape, and chalk. Not only will your jars be quickly relabeled, you'll easily be able to distinguish between yourcoffee beans,marshmallows, dried monkey brains, and whatever else you have stored in your jars.You'll have the cutest jars for your lab this side of the Bride of Frankenstein. Enough talk, let's make some chalkboard paint jars! tools: foam paint brush painters' / masking tape straight-edged bladematerials: clean glass jars chalkboard paint . Using painters tape or masking tape, masking off the area you want to make writable.Be creative with your area shape, it does not have to be a rectangle. You can just as easily make a circular or abstract pattern. I made a few different rectangular shapes and one with two writable areas. Dip your foam brush into the paint and apply a thin coat to the masked area of your jars. I found that brushing around the curve of the jar achieves a more uniform coating than brushing top to bottom. It's easy to apply too much paint when doing this, so start with just a light coat and work your way up. Stand jars upright and leave until dry to the touch,about 30 minutes. After your paint has dried for at least 30 minutes it should be safe to remove the masking tape. Removing the tape while the paint is slightly tacky allows for a cleaner edge at the masked edges. Using a straight-edged blade, gently scrape away any places where the paint bled under the mask or any other places on your jars. Go slow and work the blade away from yourself when possible. Your chalk paint may not be totally dry yet after removing the masking tape. Dry time will vary depending on how thick your coats were applied. Your paint should be completely dry to the touch and no dark or wet looking patches anywhere. Mine took about an hour to completely dry, if in doubt let dry for another hour. Now, fill your jars with whatever you like and mark the jar's contents with chalk! The application and marking for your jars are endless. Did you make your own chalkboard paint jars? I want to see it!Happy making :)

```markdown
# Chalkboard Paint Jars Creation System

## Steps to Create Re-writable Chalkboard Labels on Jars

### START:
- Begin the process of creating re-writable chalkboard labels on jars.

### PROCESS: Gather Materials
- INPUT: Collect the following materials:
  - Foam paintbrush
  - Painter's tape or masking tape
  - Straight-edged blade
  - Clean glass jars
  - Chalkboard paint
  - Chalk

### PROCESS: Prepare the Jars
- Using the painter's tape or masking tape, mask off the area on the glass jars where the chalkboard paint will be applied.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the desired shape for the label area creative (not a rectangle)?
    - Yes: Proceed with creating a circular or abstract pattern.
    - No: Create a rectangular shape or desired geometric pattern.
  - OUTPUT: Jars with a designated area masked off for paint.

### PROCESS: Apply Chalkboard Paint
- Dip the foam brush into the chalkboard paint.
- Apply a thin coat of chalkboard paint to the masked area of the jars.
  - PROCESS: Ensure uniform coating.
    - Brush around the curve of the jar rather than top to bottom to achieve a more even coat.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the paint applied too thickly?
    - Yes: Start with a light coat and add additional thin layers as needed.
    - No: Proceed to the next step.
  - OUTPUT: Jars with a thin coat of chalkboard paint applied to the masked area.

### PROCESS: Drying Phase
- Stand the jars upright.
- Leave the jars to dry until they are dry to the touch, approximately 30 minutes.
  - OUTPUT: Jars with a dry coat of chalkboard paint.

### PROCESS: Remove Masking Tape
- After at least 30 minutes of drying, carefully remove the masking tape.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the paint slightly tacky?
    - Yes: Remove the tape now for a cleaner edge.
    - No: If completely dry, proceed with caution to avoid chipping the paint.
  - OUTPUT: Jars with chalkboard paint and clean edges where the tape was removed.

### PROCESS: Clean Up Edges
- Using a straight-edged blade, gently scrape away any excess paint that bled under the tape or elsewhere on the jars.
  - PROCESS: Be cautious while scraping.
    - Work the blade away from yourself to avoid injury.
  - OUTPUT: Jars with clean, precise chalkboard paint edges.

### PROCESS: Final Drying Phase
- Allow the paint to completely dry, checking for no dark or wet looking patches.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the paint fully dry?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Let the jars dry for an additional hour or until fully dry.
  - OUTPUT: Jars with fully dried chalkboard paint ready for use.

### PROCESS: Use Jars
- Fill the jars with the desired contents.
- Use chalk to label the jar's contents on the chalkboard painted area.
  - OUTPUT: Labeled jars ready for display and use.

### END:
- The process of creating re-writable chalkboard labels on jars is complete.
```

instruct00097.title: Homemade Air Freshener Gel
instruct00097.text: I wanted to share my experience with making these easy and useful Air Freshener Gels. A relatively low cost Do-It-Yourself room air freshener, you may have all the ingredients already! I keep one in each vehicle and at my desk at work. The total time it takes to make is about five to six (5-6) minutes and then twenty-four (24) hours to solidify.Materials & Equipment: Three (3) to four (4) jars, capable of holding 1/2-cup of fluid each. I used four (4) clean and recycled baby food jars, and each jar holds 1/2-cup of mixture. Food Coloring Essential Oil or Room Fragrance drops (Can be purchased at a craft store, but I found one on sale for $2 at Wal-mart.) Two (2) cups of water, divided into two 1-cup amounts Four (4) envelopes unflavored gelatine (one 1-oz box) One (1) tablespoon of salt Kitchen equipment such as a whisk, a pan to boil the water and spoons (plastic or metal) to mix the concoctionPrepare: Pour a few drops of food coloring of your choice into each jar. Next, pour one (1) teaspoon (minimum) of essential oil into each jar. You may want to add more if you desire a stronger scent emanating from the end result. I did not use more than two teaspoons and was pleased with the one teaspoon result.Boil and Mix: Bring one (1) cup of water to a boil. Add all four (4) envelopes of gelatine to the boiling water and whisk until dissolved. (I estimate it dissolved in about a minute.) After the gelatine dissolves, add the remaining cup of water and then the salt. After the salt dissolves, remove the pan from the heat and pour into the prepared jars. Try pouring the mixture into the jars within a few minutes of removing the pan off of the heat. NOTE: Please be careful as the mixture will be very hot! My husband held the pot with a steady hand for the photo. However the second time I did this by myself, I made a mess everywhere and spilled the gelatine mixture on the counter. You may want to use a funnel to put the gelatine mixture in the jars. I used a broken clothespin to stir the gelatinous combination, but suggest using plastic spoons. Use them quickly as the heat from the water could make them melt slightly. Let the now fragrant gel mix solidify at room temperature for at least 24-hours. Can you believe that's it? The scent and solid mixture will disintegrate over time. The one in my car has lasted over a month. The one in my bathroom has lasted over a month but probably will be ready to clean out in another week. I estimate that one jar would last from four to six (4-6) good weeks of scent dispersion. Make sure the lid is off the container to enjoy! Thanks for reading and I hope you post pictures of your gels.The original Pinterest pin for this is here: DIY Air Fresheners.

```markdown
# Air Freshener Gel System

## Summary
This system outlines the process of creating DIY air freshener gels. The output is a set of homemade air freshener gels stored in jars, which can last for 4-6 weeks. The process involves mixing a gelatin solution with essential oils and food coloring, then allowing it to solidify.

## Steps

### START:
- Begin the air freshener gel preparation process.

### INPUT: Materials and Equipment
- Gather 3-4 jars (1/2-cup capacity each)
- Food coloring
- Essential oil or room fragrance drops
- 2 cups of water (divided)
- 4 envelopes of unflavored gelatin (1-oz box)
- 1 tablespoon of salt
- Kitchen equipment (whisk, pan, spoons)

### PROCESS: Prepare Jars
- Pour a few drops of food coloring into each jar.
- Add 1 teaspoon of essential oil into each jar (adjust quantity for desired scent strength).

### PROCESS: Boil and Mix Solution
- Boil 1 cup of water.
- Add 4 envelopes of gelatin to boiling water.
- Whisk until gelatin is dissolved.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the gelatin dissolved?
- Yes: Proceed to next step.
- No: Continue whisking until gelatin is dissolved.

### PROCESS: Complete Solution
- Add the remaining 1 cup of water to the mixture.
- Add 1 tablespoon of salt.
- Whisk until salt is dissolved.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the salt dissolved?
- Yes: Proceed to next step.
- No: Continue whisking until salt is dissolved.

### PROCESS: Pour into Jars
- Remove pan from heat.
- Carefully pour the mixture into the prepared jars.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture poured without spilling?
- Yes: Proceed to next step.
- No: Clean any spills and try pouring again using a funnel if necessary.

### PROCESS: Stir and Solidify
- Stir the mixture in the jars to ensure proper distribution of color and scent.
- Let the jars sit at room temperature to solidify for 24 hours.

### OUTPUT:
- The air freshener gels are now ready to use.

### PROCESS: Use and Maintenance
- Place the air freshener gels without the lid to enjoy the scent.
- Monitor the gels as the scent and solid mixture will disintegrate over time.

### DECISION [IF]: Has the air freshener gel lasted over a month?
- Yes: Continue usage until scent fades or gel disintegrates.
- No: Replace with a new batch if necessary.

### END:
- The process of creating and maintaining air freshener gels is complete.
```

instruct00444.title: Geometric Sculpture From 72 Pencils
instruct00444.text: George W. Hart is a sculptor of constructive geometric forms (and writer of the Math Monday columns at Make), and I've long been an admirer of his work. Reproducing his art is far from trivial - I once tried to build his Chronosynclastic Infundibulum, but broke so many CDs I gave up in disgust. However, I recently discovered that Alejandro Erickson, instructable-r and self-confessed mathemagician, lives in the same city as me and runs workshops on geometric construction, so we hired him for an afternoon. He was the great geometry guru we'd hoped he'd be, and he kept 6 kids and 3 adults well entertained and busy making tensegrities. As a special request, he also taught two of us how to make a replica of Hart's 72 pencils sculpture (Hart made a limited edition of 19 unique examples of these). It took a couple of leisurely hours to build and glue, and with supervision was surprisingly easy to make. It can be assembled inexpensively using wooden pencils (conveniently sold in packs of 72!), a few rubber bands and a little superglue, in pretty much exactly the same way as Alejandro makes his Hexastix sculptures (see below for the video). The hexagonal cross-section of the pencils make them a very natural fit for this geometric form, as the holes in the lattice are themselves hexagonal. The erasers are arranged tetrahedrally with respect to one another; the volume enclosed by the pencils is a rhombic dodecahedron. It's a neat piece of art that I'm pleased to own; many thanks to George W. Hart for the inspiration and Alejandro for the instruction!I made a variant of this sculpture using 76 pencils, in which the pencils form six-pointed stars rather than hexagons. I used colored pencils for that one, but couldn't find a nice set of exactly 76. There are good sets of 72 colored pencils available, though.NOTE: Want to make this even easier? Check out https://www.instructables.com/Easy-72-Pencil-Sculpture/, which uses a 3D printed template to make assembly fast and straightforward.Video: Follow Alejandro's instructions, but build only as far as a hexagon consisting of a ring of 18 pencils, removing the inner pencils as you go. If you find the erasers aren't arranged tetrahedrally (as I did), just invert one ring one pencil at a time until your sculpture looks like the original. Superglue the joints before removing the rubber bands. Happily, lots of people have made this sculpture, and some of them have shared their builds with me. They've often been very creative too, using among other things BBQ skewers, copper pipe, pvc and toothpicks! Thanks to guerroloco, jayefuu, EVM, akarod79, palmsco, mrpesas, XP1 and innovationcreation for sharing.

instruct00782.title: Low Carb, High Protein Pizza With Homemade Sauce
instruct00782.text: Ever been craving pizza, but you're on a high protein or low carb diet? This is the answer to your craving - a pizza crust without wheat or yeast, but delicious and you don't need a fork to eat it. For the pizza crust, you will need: 2 eggs 1 8oz package cream cheese or Neufchatel cheese, brought to room temperature 1 cup parmesan cheese - shredded or grated 9x13" baking pan cooking spray to coat pan For the sauce, you will need: 1 6oz can tomato paste 1/2 cup sangria 1 1/2 tablespoons dried oregano 1 1/2 tablespoons dried basil 1/4 teaspoon salt 4 cloves of garlic, minced Toppings of your choice, we used 1 1/2 cups shredded mozzarella and sliced pepperoni. Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. In a large mixing bowl, combine the eggs, cream cheese and parmesan and mix well with a fork or spatula. Don't panic if the mix looks very wet and runny, it will firm up as it bakes. Coat the 9x13" baking pan with the cooking spray, then spread the mixture to cover the bottom of the pan. Place pan on a rack in the middle of oven and bake for 30 minutes, or until crust is firm and lightly browned. In a medium bowl, mix tomato paste,oregano,basil,salt andgarlic, then add sangria to thin the mixture to a spreadable, but not too thick consistency. Adjust seasonings to taste. Remove baking pan from oven when crust is lightly browned on top. Stand to cool for a few minutes. It is normal for the crust to shrink as it bakes. Increase oven temperature to 425 degrees. Spread the sauce over the crust, then add toppings of your choice. A nice thick bed of mozzarella helps everything stick together. We covered our pizza with a lot of pepperoni. Place pan back in oven and bake for about 15 minutes, until cheese is bubbling and it looks delicious. Remove from oven and let stand a while; it will be too hot to eat for about 10 minutes. Remove from pan, slice and enjoy.

instruct00859.title: Make a Wide Sturdy Handle With the Portuguese Sinnet
instruct00859.text: Messenger bags are great but sometimes the long shoulder strap gets tangled when you're trying to make a quick exit or easy entrance. Since they all seem to have a couple of 'D' rings on the back, I decided to make a quick short strap that won't get hung up on stuff as I drag it out of the car to avoid the coming zombie apocalypse. But the problem is that if it's too narrow, it's too uncomfortable to use zombies or no. So, enter the Portuguese Sinnet (also known as Solomon Bar and referenced as knot #2496 in Ashley's Book of Knots). Here's the front and back of my messenger bag. The distance between the middle of the 'D' rings is about 6.5 inches (16.5cm for those metricly inclined). I started with a length of #550 paracord 82 inches long (2.08m). I also had the following: x. lighter x. scissors x. 2 12.5 inch (35cm) pieces of thin (2 mm) cord Start by folding the cord in half and running it through one of the 'D' rings. Next take a strand and run it through the opposite 'D' ring (I went 'over' the ring as you can see). Now do the same with the other. Note: I've rotated the image to make it a little easier to reference. Take the length on the right and bring it over the two main strands. Now take the left strand and pass in over the strand that was just brought over and then pass it under the two main strands and through the loop that was made by the first strand. Now that I have my first knot made, I'll refer to the strands as they are in their "current" position not as they started out. Tighten up the first knot and take the strand on the right and place it underneath the two main strands. Now take the left strand and pass it under the strand that was just moved over now put it over the two main strands and into the loop that was just created by the right strand. The key to making a flat (non-spiral) Portuguese Sinnet is to keep the strand that is on the bottom on the bottom during the next knot. If you keep the same strand on the top-bottom-top-bottom order you get a real nice double-helix. Now that I've made about 5 inches (13cm) of the bar, I need to get set to pull the remaining strand ends back into the sinnet body. Middle the two 12.5 inch pieces and place them inside the next knot. Now the trick to finishing up is to tie the sinnet snug enough to keep it looking good but not so tight that you won't be able to pull the remains through. In the second pic, you can see how it looks once it's all knotted up and ready to finish off. Now that we've got it all knotted up, it's time to finish up by pulling the remains into the body which will hold them inside just by friction alone. In this image, I've arranged it in a more top to bottom to make more sense. Take the "top" strand and place it "behind" the 'D' ring and through one of the 'finishing loops'. Be sure to leave enough slack in it so that it's easier to pull it into the body (pic 3). Now pull it through. In the forth pic you'll see how it looks just before pulling it completely through. Now take the bottom strand and pass it "over" the 'D' ring and through the loop and pull through the body. Now that everything is pulled through, it looks like this. To dress it up, just cut them off but not too close to the body because you'll want to but a flame to the ends to seal them. After they are sealed, push them into the body and cover over (see 3rd pic). Now it's all set and you can bug-out "fast"!!! Cuz let's face it....even though zombies move slow, they've ate the brains of everyone that thought they have plenty of time.....

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Messenger Bag Strap Creation Using Portuguese Sinnet Knot

## System Overview:
The system is designed to create a short, comfortable strap for a messenger bag using the Portuguese Sinnet knot technique. The final output is a non-tangled, easy-to-use strap that facilitates quick access to the bag.

### Inputs:
- A length of #550 paracord, 82 inches long (2.08m)
- Two 'D' rings on the messenger bag
- Lighter
- Scissors
- Two 12.5 inch (35cm) pieces of thin (2 mm) cord

### Output:
- A short, flat, non-spiral Portuguese Sinnet strap attached to the messenger bag.

## Process Steps:

### START:
- Begin the system to create a short strap for a messenger bag.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Paracord
- INPUT: Take the #550 paracord, 82 inches long.
- PROCESS: Fold the paracord in half.

### PROCESS: Attach Paracord to 'D' Rings
- PROCESS: Run the folded paracord through one 'D' ring at the midpoint.
- PROCESS: Take one strand and run it through the opposite 'D' ring, going over the ring.

### PROCESS: Start the Portuguese Sinnet Knot
- PROCESS: Rotate the bag for ease of reference.
- PROCESS: Take the right strand and bring it over the two main strands.
- PROCESS: Take the left strand, pass it over the right strand, under the two main strands, and through the loop created by the right strand.
- OUTPUT: The first knot is completed.

### PROCESS: Continue the Portuguese Sinnet Knot
- PROCESS: Tighten the first knot.
- PROCESS: Place the right strand underneath the two main strands.
- PROCESS: Take the left strand, pass it under the right strand, over the two main strands, and into the loop created by the right strand.

### DECISION [IF]: Check Strand Position for Flat Sinnet
- IF the bottom strand remains consistent as the bottom strand for each knot,
  - PROCESS: Continue knotting to maintain a flat sinnet.
- ELSE:
  - PROCESS: Adjust strand position to ensure the bottom strand remains consistent.

### PROCESS: Measure the Sinnet Length
- PROCESS: Continue knotting until approximately 5 inches (13cm) of the sinnet is made.

### PROCESS: Prepare to Finish the Sinnet
- INPUT: Middle the two 12.5 inch pieces of thin cord.
- PROCESS: Place the middle thin cords inside the next knot.

### DECISION [IF]: Check Knot Tension
- IF the sinnet is snug but not too tight,
  - PROCESS: Continue to the next step.
- ELSE:
  - PROCESS: Adjust the tension to allow for the strands to be pulled through later.

### PROCESS: Finish the Sinnet Knot
- PROCESS: Arrange the sinnet for finishing.
- PROCESS: Take the top strand, place it behind the 'D' ring and through a finishing loop, leaving slack.
- PROCESS: Pull the top strand through the sinnet body.
- PROCESS: Take the bottom strand, pass it over the 'D' ring and through the loop, pulling through the body.

### PROCESS: Dress the Strap
- PROCESS: Cut the excess strands, leaving enough to seal with a flame.
- PROCESS: Use a lighter to seal the ends of the strands.
- PROCESS: Push the sealed ends into the sinnet body for a neat finish.

### OUTPUT:
- The short strap for the messenger bag is complete and ready for use.

### END:
- The system to create a short strap for a messenger bag using the Portuguese Sinnet knot is concluded.
```

instruct00041.title: Popup Facebook Picture
instruct00041.text: UPDATE:Hey everyone! All the pictures in the comments look awesome, and I've seen all kinds of people use this (Freddie Wong for example... sweet!) but unfortunately, Facebook's been changed and this doesn't work at all anymore. There are ways to do something similar and I'm working on an all new Instructable, but until then, this instructable will serve as a memorial of the older more simple Facebook...UPDATE UPDATE:I've got some fun ideas to try out when the new Facebook "Timeline" profile hits... Whenever that is. Look out for a new Instructable whenever Facebook releases that. This how to make your Facebook Profile Picture look like it's transparent, or popping out of the page! You can even do what I did and make it look like it's behind the page, poking out! Here's what you need to make your pop-up picture!-A Camera, or a picture that you want to use.-Photoshop, or the GIMP, or even Paint will do.-The attached picture. (right click and save as) First, get your picture.Try to pick one that would make an interesting pop-up. If you are going to be making it look like you are peeking out from behind the white part of the page, hold a big white piece of paper in front of you to make the next step easier. Now, using Photoshop, or the GIMP, or some other image editing program that supports layers, cut out your image and get rid of the background. If you don't know how to go that, Google it.Then, after it's cut out, copy it and paste it onto the background image. (You'll have to right click and save that image) You'll probably have to resize your image because the background image is very small.Keep in mind, if you want to the image to be taller, you can't add height to it. You need to make the bottom part, the white part, longer. If you resize the grey/blue part, the image won't line up. When you set the finished image as your profile picture, the line in Facebook's layout matches with the line in the picture, making a seamless transparent image.If it doesn't line up, move the image up or down a few pixels and try again. Also, keep in mind, Facebook changes its layout a lot, making the image not line up. When it does, I'll try to update this Instructable.UPDATE: I've been told by people here and friends on Facebook that the image doesn't always line up. This could be for several reasons like different monitor resolutions or browser settings, etc. So keep that in mind.UPDATE AGAIN: If you do it, make a screen capture and put it in a comment down below! You can censor your name, like I did, if you want, but I just want to see how these come out!

instruct00885.title: Easy Garlic Bread and Cheese
instruct00885.text: I LOVE the garlic bread and cheese from Pi**a H*t, but find the garlic bread you buy from supermarkets pales in comparison so I invented my own recipe which is so easy to make and everyone who's tried it says its even better than the huts! Ingredients needed: French bread Butter/Margarine Tube of Garlic paste (or fresh garlic peeled and crushed) Extra virgin olive oil herbs (parsley or mixed herbs - whatever you fancy) Cheese grated (mozzerella or chedder - again whatever you fancy) Cut your bread sticks into thickish slices diagonally and arrange on a tray (I cover the tray with foil for easy clean up afterwards).liberally sprinkle olive oil on the slices and put under a hot grill. Right - while the bread is toasting, its time to prepare the garlic butter.Choose a microwave safe cup or ramakin, put some butter or marg in it and zap it in the microwave for about 30-40 seconds.Then squirt in a helping of garlic paste (or your peeled and squashed garlic cloves - use a garlic press) and some herbs.Zap it again until all the butter/marg has melted nicely. Your bread should now be nicely toasted, remove the tray and flip your slices. Add a good teaspoon of the butter/garlic mix to each slice, stir the mix well as the garlic tends to sink to the bottom. Once all covered, return the tray to the grill to toast the other side. If you don't want the cheese, once the slices have toasted they are ready... for cheese, read on! The final step is to add your favourite cheese topping and melt it again under the grill. I like to add a light sprinkling of herbs on top of the cheese for appearance. Once the cheese is all melted and bubbling - its time to dish them out and collect the thanks of those you share them with. Let me know if you try this and enjoy them. Caroline x

```markdown
# Homemade Garlic Bread with Cheese Recipe

## Ingredients
- French bread
- Butter/Margarine
- Garlic paste (or fresh garlic)
- Extra virgin olive oil
- Herbs (parsley or mixed herbs)
- Grated cheese (mozzarella or cheddar)

## Equipment
- Tray
- Foil (optional for easy cleanup)
- Microwave-safe cup or ramekin
- Grill
- Garlic press (if using fresh garlic)
- Teaspoon

## Process Steps

### START
- Begin with preparing the ingredients and equipment.

### PROCESS: Prepare Bread
- INPUT: French bread
- Cut the French bread into thick diagonal slices.
- Arrange the slices on a tray.
  - If desired, cover the tray with foil for easy cleanup.

### PROCESS: Toast Bread
- INPUT: Extra virgin olive oil
- Liberally sprinkle olive oil over the bread slices.
- Place the tray under a hot grill.
- Wait for the bread to toast on one side.

### PROCESS: Prepare Garlic Butter
- INPUT: Butter/Margarine, Garlic paste or fresh garlic, Herbs
- While bread is toasting, take a microwave-safe cup or ramekin.
- Add butter or margarine to the cup.
- Microwave for about 30-40 seconds.
- Add garlic paste or crushed garlic cloves.
- Add herbs.
- Microwave again until the butter/margarine has melted completely.

### PROCESS: Check Toasted Bread
- DECISION: Is the bread nicely toasted on one side?
  - IF Yes: Proceed to flip the slices.
  - IF No: Continue toasting and check again.

### PROCESS: Apply Garlic Butter
- OUTPUT: Toasted bread with one side done
- Flip the toasted bread slices on the tray.
- OUTPUT: Flipped bread slices ready for garlic butter
- Stir the garlic butter mixture well.
- Add a good teaspoon of the garlic butter mix to each bread slice.

### PROCESS: Toast the Other Side
- Once all slices are covered with garlic butter, return the tray to the grill.
- Toast the other side of the bread.

### DECISION: Adding Cheese?
- IF Yes: Proceed to add cheese.
- IF No: 
  - OUTPUT: Garlic bread is ready without cheese.
  - END

### PROCESS: Add Cheese
- INPUT: Grated cheese
- Sprinkle a generous amount of grated cheese over the toasted garlic bread slices.
- Optionally, add a light sprinkling of herbs on top of the cheese.

### PROCESS: Melt Cheese
- Place the tray back under the grill.
- Wait until the cheese is melted and bubbling.

### OUTPUT: Garlic Bread with Cheese
- Once the cheese is melted and bubbling, the garlic bread with cheese is ready.

### END
- Serve the garlic bread with cheese and enjoy the compliments from your guests.
```

instruct00615.title: TWO COLOR PARACORD FISHTAIL BRACELET
instruct00615.text: Making a two color paracord fishtail bracelet. The things you will need 1. Paracord your choice on colors 2. Lighter or something to burn the ends. Torch lighter is the best 3. Cutting devise. 4. Hemostat. 5. Tape measure I live in the Bay Area so black and orange Giants baby. Cut your cords to length and burn the ends. I used two lengths of 12 feet each to have plenty left over. I also used a jig to do this but it is not a requirement. You will want to cow hitch both cords through one end of your buckle. I used a 5/8 buckle which seems to be a good size. This is where you start sizing. Whatever size you are going to make it make sure you measure. I use a cloth tape because it is a little easer to handle. You can also use a mark on the cord for the size wrist. When measuring measure from the very end of the female side of the buckle to the point of connection on the male side ( so not all the way to the end of the male side). Adjust your cow hitch so two cords closest (in photo) go through the male end of the buckle and are about an inch towards the female end,. You can tape them if you wish. Almost time to start your weave make sure everything is tight and ready to go. Start your weave. Again make sure everything is snug and start weaving. In this photo I started with the outermost cord which is orange. Bring orange over the first two and under the second two. Orange goes around and back under the side it started on. Do the same with black all the way to the end. Make is tight and push the entire knot towards the weaved end. As you near the end it gets quite difficult. This is where your hemostat will come in. # Two-Color Paracord Fishtail Bracelet System

```markdown
## Summary Representation

### Start
START: Begin the process of making a two-color paracord fishtail bracelet.

### Process
PROCESS: Gather all necessary materials for the bracelet.

### Inputs
INPUT: Two lengths of paracord in chosen colors.

INPUT: Cutting device.
INPUT: Hemostat.
INPUT: Tape measure.

PROCESS: Cut both paracord lengths to 12 feet each to ensure excess material is available.
PROCESS: Burn the ends of the cords using the lighter to prevent fraying.

### Decision on Jig Usage
DECISION [IF]: Is a jig being used to assist in bracelet making?
    OUTPUT [YES]: Use the jig as per its instructions.
    OUTPUT [NO]: Proceed without a jig.

### Attaching to Buckle
PROCESS: Cow hitch both cords through one end of the buckle (using a 5/8 inch buckle is recommended).

### Sizing the Bracelet
PROCESS: Measure the bracelet size using a cloth tape measure for ease of handling.
PROCESS: Mark the cord at the size of the wrist, measuring from the end of the female side of the buckle to the connection point on the male side (not to the very end of the male side).
PROCESS: Adjust the cow hitch so that the two cords closest to the viewer in the photo go through the male end of the buckle, leaving about an inch toward the female end.
DECISION [IF]: Do you want to tape the cords?
    OUTPUT [YES]: Tape the cords for stability.
    OUTPUT [NO]: Proceed without taping.

### Preparing for Weave
PROCESS: Ensure that everything is tight and ready for weaving.

### Weaving Process
PROCESS: Start the weave, ensuring that it is snug.
PROCESS: Begin with the outermost cord (in this example, orange) and weave it over the first two cords and under the second two.
PROCESS: Loop the orange cord around and back under the side it started on.
PROCESS: Repeat the same process with the black cord, alternating with the orange, and continue all the way to the end, pushing the entire knot towards the weaved end.

### Decision on Tightness and Hemostat Usage
DECISION [IF]: Is the weave getting difficult to continue due to tightness?
    OUTPUT [YES]: Use the hemostat to assist in pulling and tightening the cords.
    OUTPUT [NO]: Continue weaving without the hemostat.

### Finishing the Weave
PROCESS: Pack as much cord as possible into the weave, attempting to finish with the black cord running to the orange cow hitch.

### Final Touches
PROCESS: Cut the excess cord and burn the ends, pressing down to ensure there are no sharp or uncomfortable edges.

### Output and End
OUTPUT: The completed two-color paracord fishtail bracelet is now ready to wear or use.
END: The process of making the bracelet is complete.
```

instruct00813.text: So I got this idea from another persons instructable and decided to do one of my own. His is here https://www.instructables.com/id/Pallet-shelves/. I liked his but had never made an instructable and decided to give it a try. # Pallet Shelving Unit Construction System

```markdown
## Summary
This system describes the process of creating shelving units from wooden pallets to organize items such as camping and boy scout equipment. The system includes sourcing materials, preparing pallets, constructing the shelves, and ensuring their stability.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a pallet shelving unit.

### INPUT:
- Obtain wooden pallets, preferably for free from local sources like a roofing company.
- Acquire a box of 3 or 4-inch screws.
- Purchase four six-foot 2x4s per shelving unit.

- Anchor the shelving unit to the wall to prevent rocking and enhance safety.
```

instruct00814.title: 15-Minute Halter Top (T-shirt Hacks Contest)
instruct00814.text: Need a halter top RIGHT FREAKING NOW? Here's how to make a stylish, no-sew top in just 15 minutes with an old T-shirt and a pair of scissors. For this project you will need: A T-shirt A pair of scissors I know, you might have to go to some kind of T-shirt-hacking specialty store to get these. Turn the T-shirt inside out and cut off the collar and sleeves, removing as little excess fabric as possible. If you want a lower neckline, you can cut a little more out of the front of the collar, but I would wait to do this until the end after you've tried it on. (You can always alter this shirt more later.) Make a straight cut along the imaginary line that connects the bottoms of the sleeve holes. Open this flap and lie it flat. To start making the straps, start cutting on one side of the neck hole in a line that curves slightly towards the middle of the back panel. When you've done this on both sides, the straps should lie flat and make a rounded "V" shape with the neckline. Trim along the straps until they are about three or four inches wide. Avoid cutting more fabric away from the body of the shirt. Ta da! A stylish halter top in about 15 minutes.

```markdown
- A stylish, no-sew halter top

- Begin with a T-shirt and a pair of scissors.

- Cut off the collar of the T-shirt.
```
