```markdown
- Begin cutting on one side of the neck hole in a line that curves slightly towards the middle of the back panel.

### PROCESS: Create symmetrical straps
- Repeat the strap cutting process on the other side to ensure both straps are symmetrical and lie flat.

### PROCESS: Trim the straps
- Trim along the straps until they are about three or four inches wide, being careful not to cut more fabric away from the body of the shirt.

- The result is a stylish, no-sew halter top.

- The process is complete.
```

instruct00436.title: Zombie Mouth Cupcake
instruct00436.text: For the zombie genre lovers: Creating a realistic zombie mouth cupcake for Halloween, using fondant and food coloring. Make a basic cupcake with your chosen flavor, (mine are vanilla cupcake).For the topper, you'll need to color your fondant (I used Wilton) as follows: for the skin tissue- use small drop of Ivory gel paste food coloring with a tiny drop of rose. for the gums- use a drop of rose with a tiny drop of red for the teeth- use a drop of Ivory. We will start with the baseof the topper, roll the skin tissue fondant about 1/8 inches thick, and by using a round cookie cutter about the same size of your top surface of your cupcake, cut a circle and place it on top of a cup or a small bowl to support the topper while working and give it the shape of a dome. To shape the gums, create twosmall snakes of the "gum fondant", flat them a little, and by using a "Dresden tool", create the cavities for the teeth and make the dents between every tooth.Attach to the circle base by using a wet brush. (the pre-made cavities should face one another). Make the teeth- shape smallpieces of ivory fondant to the shape of teeth, including their roots, let them dry for about an hour. you may use tylose powder or CMC to make them sturdier. when they are firm, take each tooth and push it to it's designated cavity in the gums we've made earlier. make sure to apply it by using a wet brush to stick the root to it's place. You may skip one or two, to make the impression the zombie had lost a tooth... Now, take the leftover "skintissue" fondant and roll it really thin. break it to little pieces and apply around the gums, creating effect a ripped skin around the gums. it doesn't have to be accurate.Let dry completely before coloring. To finish the realistic effect,we will create:fresh blood finish: mix red coloring gel with drops of vodka of lemon extract dried blood- mix red with a drop of royal blue and add drops of vodka/lemon extract. using a brush, apply the "fresh blood" color mix around the torn skin tissue, apply the "dried blood" color mix around the gums, especially where the gums meet the skin tissue. and around the teeth contour, and the dents, to give it a more 3D impression. Let it dry, and assemble the cupcake topper on top of the frosting of your cupcake. My hubby did... :)

```markdown
# Realistic Zombie Mouth Cupcake Creation Process

## Ingredients and Tools
- Vanilla cupcakes (or chosen flavor)
- Fondant (Wilton brand recommended)
- Ivory gel paste food coloring
- Rose gel paste food coloring
- Red gel paste food coloring
- Round cookie cutter
- Dresden tool
- Small cup or bowl
- Wet brush
- Tylose powder or CMC (optional)
- Vodka or lemon extract
- Royal blue gel paste food coloring
- Paintbrush

## Fondant Coloring
START: Begin the cupcake topper process.

INPUT: Ivory, rose, and red gel paste food coloring.
PROCESS: Color the fondant for different parts of the mouth.
- For skin tissue: mix a small drop of Ivory with a tiny drop of rose.
- For gums: mix a drop of rose with a tiny drop of red.
- For teeth: use a drop of Ivory.

## Base of Topper
PROCESS: Roll the skin tissue fondant to 1/8 inches thick.
INPUT: Round cookie cutter.
PROCESS: Cut a circle with the cookie cutter.
PROCESS: Place the fondant circle on a cup or bowl to form a dome shape.
STORE: Set aside the base to support the topper while working.

## Gums
PROCESS: Create two small snakes of gum-colored fondant.
PROCESS: Flatten the snakes slightly.
INPUT: Dresden tool.
PROCESS: Use the Dresden tool to create cavities for the teeth.
PROCESS: Make dents between each tooth.
INPUT: Wet brush.
PROCESS: Attach gums to the circle base with the wet brush.
STORE: Ensure the pre-made cavities face one another.

## Teeth
PROCESS: Shape small pieces of ivory fondant into teeth, including roots.
DECISION [IF]: Have the teeth dried for about an hour?
- Yes: Continue to the next step.
- No: Wait until they are firm.
PROCESS: Add tylose powder or CMC to teeth for sturdiness (optional).
INPUT: Wet brush.
PROCESS: Insert each tooth into its designated cavity.
PROCESS: Use a wet brush to adhere the tooth in place.
DECISION [IF]: Skip a tooth to create a missing tooth effect?
- Yes: Skip one or two teeth placements.
- No: Place all teeth.

## Torn Skin Effect
PROCESS: Roll leftover skin tissue fondant very thin.
PROCESS: Tear into small pieces.
PROCESS: Apply pieces around gums to simulate ripped skin.
STORE: Let the fondant dry completely.

## Coloring Effects
PROCESS: Create fresh blood and dried blood color mixes.
- Fresh blood: Mix red coloring gel with vodka or lemon extract.
- Dried blood: Mix red with a drop of royal blue and add vodka/lemon extract.
INPUT: Paintbrush.
PROCESS: Apply fresh blood mix around the torn skin.
PROCESS: Apply dried blood mix around gums and teeth for depth.
STORE: Let the coloring dry.

## Assembling Topper on Cupcake
PROCESS: Place the topper on the frosted cupcake.
OUTPUT: Finished realistic zombie mouth cupcake.

END: The process is complete.
```

instruct00559.title: How to Hard Boil an Egg
instruct00559.text: How to cook, peel and serve a hardboiled egg. Before you do anything else wash your hands, no one wants to get sick or have dirt in there food. -Egg(s) duh -Heat source -Pot (the kind for cooking) -Water You need to put the egg in the pot then fill it up with room temp. water until the egg is fully covered. Put the pot with the egg in it over on the stove, turn your stove on medium heat. This is the boring part, there is no way to really speed up this part because you don't want the egg to get to hot to quickly or else it will crack. When the egg reaches a full or rolling boil you need to start your timer (or just look at the clock). For a hard boiled egg, boil for 7 minuets For a soft boiled egg, boil for 3 minutes I attached a video of the egg at a full boilHere is the video (I also posted It on youtube) Now you have let the egg boil and want to get to it, and save a trip to the hospital. 1. Put the pot with water and egg under the sink on an angle (so the water dumps out) 2. Turn your sink on cold and let it run for a few second 3. Remove egg, the egg will be cool to touch but still really hot on the inside This is pretty simple but I'll post it anyway. 1. First take your egg then hit in on a hard surface so you get a nice crack in it. 2. Put your nail under the crack and begin to pull away the shell. There should be a shell layer then under that there should be a "skin" type layer. You want to get under the skin layer. 3. I find it easier to rotate the egg while I'm shelling it. I personally like to put it in the fridge till its cool (takes like an hour), then eat it with mustard. Alternatively you could make a deviled egg, by cutting the egg in half lengthwise scraping the yellow yolk out, then you mash the yolk up in a bowl with a fork. After which you add some mayonnaise and mustard to, put back in the egg and sprinkle with paprika, I'll post this one later. Special Thanks to my mom who taught me everything I know about cooking, Including how to boil an egg.

```markdown
# How to Cook, Peel, and Serve a Hardboiled Egg

## Preparation
START:
- INPUT: Egg(s), Heat source, Pot, Water
- PROCESS: Wash your hands thoroughly to ensure cleanliness.

## Cooking the Egg
- PROCESS: Place the egg(s) in the pot.
- INPUT: Fill the pot with room temperature water until the egg(s) are fully covered.
- PROCESS: Place the pot on the stove.
- PROCESS: Turn the stove on to medium heat.
- DECISION [IF]: Has the water reached a full or rolling boil?
  - Yes: Proceed to start the timer.
  - No: Continue heating without proceeding to the next step.

- PROCESS: Start the timer for the desired egg consistency.
- INPUT: For a hard boiled egg, set the timer for 7 minutes.
- INPUT: For a soft boiled egg, set the timer for 3 minutes.

## Cooling the Egg
- PROCESS: Once the timer ends, move the pot under the sink at an angle to drain the water.
- PROCESS: Turn on cold water and let it run over the egg(s) for a few seconds.
- OUTPUT: The egg(s) should be cool to the touch but still hot inside.

## Peeling the Egg
- PROCESS: Take the egg and tap it on a hard surface to create a crack.
- PROCESS: Insert a nail under the crack and begin to peel away the shell.
- PROCESS: Ensure to get under the 'skin' layer beneath the shell.
- PROCESS: Rotate the egg while peeling for ease.

## Serving the Egg
- DECISION [IF]: Will you refrigerate the egg?
  - Yes: STORE the egg in the fridge until cool (about 1 hour).
  - No: Proceed to serve immediately.

- OUTPUT: Serve the cooled egg with mustard, or prepare it as a deviled egg.
  - PROCESS (For Deviled Egg): Cut the egg in half lengthwise.
  - PROCESS: Scoop out the yolk and mash it in a bowl.
  - INPUT: Mix mayonnaise and mustard into the mashed yolk.
  - PROCESS: Refill the egg whites with the yolk mixture.
  - PROCESS: Sprinkle with paprika.

END: Enjoy your hardboiled egg, served as desired.

## Acknowledgment
- PROCESS: Special thanks to the author's mom for teaching the cooking skills shared in this guide.
```

instruct00313.title: Envelope Napkin Fold
instruct00313.text: With Thanksgiving fast approaching, it's time to start planning your table settings! The envelope napkin fold is a simple and elegant addition that allows you to personalize your family's meal by including a greeting card, menu, or place card within the folded napkin. (See Step 10 for more insert ideas.)SuppliesAll you need to make these are 20 x 20 square napkins. They can be any color and material. Although I recommend using a cotton over linen, as linen (I found out doing this instructable) has bias stretch which makes it a bit harder to get even folds and doesn't hold a crisp fold well. TIP: If you'd like crisper, more paper-like folds, iron the folds as you go!Let's get started! Lay a square napkin down on a clean work surface so that it's open all the way. Iron if needed. Grab a hold of the right hand corner nearest you and fold it over to meet the opposite upper left corner. Straighten out the edges so that they all meet up. Turn the triangle so that the longest side is parallel to you and the table's edge. Fold the left corner in so that it sits JUST past the midway point of the long side of the triangle, like pictured. Now repeat for the right hand corner. Take the lower left corner and bring it in to the bottom midpoint of the now 'house' shaped napkin. Press the new left side fold down. Repeat on the right side. Take both bottom corners and bring them up to rest just below the top right corners. Press down the new folds. Take the top point of the envelope 'flap' and bring it down (or close it) to complete the envelope. Use your envelope napkins to include a personalized 'letter' or card to each guest's plate. Some ideas for what this could be are:holiday greeting cardmenuplace cardfamily photos from past celebrationsholiday story or poemcoloring cards with pencil crayons for kidsgame cards: trivia, scavenger hunt, etc.I hope you all have a wonderful holiday!! And if you decide to give these a try, please send me pictures via the comments section below. I'd love to see how yours turn out!And to get a jumpstart on Christmas dinner table setting ideas, check out my Christmas Tree Napkin Fold instructable.

```markdown
# Envelope Napkin Fold Step-by-Step Guide

## Supplies:
- 20 x 20 square napkins (any color and material, cotton recommended over linen)
- Iron (optional for crisper folds)

## Instructions:

START:
- Lay a square napkin flat on a clean work surface.

PROCESS: [Ironing the Napkin]
- INPUT: Iron if the napkin requires crisper folds.

PROCESS: [Creating the Base Triangle]
- Grab the right-hand corner nearest you.
- Fold it over to meet the opposite upper left corner.
- Straighten out the edges for alignment.

PROCESS: [Positioning the Triangle]
- Turn the triangle so the longest side is parallel to the table's edge.

PROCESS: [Folding the Left Corner]
- Fold the left corner in, slightly past the midpoint of the long side.

PROCESS: [Folding the Right Corner]
- Repeat the same fold for the right-hand corner.

PROCESS: [Folding the Lower Corners]
- Take the lower left corner and bring it to the bottom midpoint.
- Press down the new left side fold.
- Repeat the same fold for the right side.

PROCESS: [Creating the Envelope Shape]
- Bring both bottom corners up to rest just below the top right corners.
- Press down the new folds.

PROCESS: [Completing the Envelope]
- Take the top point of the envelope 'flap.'
- Bring it down to complete the envelope.

OUTPUT: [Personalized Envelope Napkin]
- Place a personalized 'letter' or card inside each napkin envelope.

DECISION [IF]: Is there a need for more insert ideas?
    IF YES: Consider including a holiday greeting card, menu, place card, family photos, holiday story or poem, coloring cards with pencil crayons for kids, or game cards like trivia or scavenger hunt.
    IF NO: Proceed to the end of the process.

END: [Completion]
- Enjoy the holiday and encourage guests to share pictures of their napkin creations.

## Additional Note:
- For Christmas dinner table setting ideas, refer to the Christmas Tree Napkin Fold instructable.
```

instruct00781.title: Floppy Disk IR Camera Hack
instruct00781.text: For the past seven years, I've had a broken digital camera lying around. It is still able to take pictures, but it is almost impossible to use on account of a broken screen. The fundamental problem is that sometimes the menu will accidentally get turned on, and not being able to see the screen, I can't turn off the menu and take pictures (without removing the batteries to reset the camera). I've been trying to figure out what to do with this camera as long as I can remember.For a while I was considering converting it to a near IR camera, but I was reluctant to make another one after having already made one for 62 Projects to Make with a Dead Computer (p. 200). However, I changed my mind about this when I learned that it was possible to use the material inside floppy disks as a visible light filter (for viewing near IR light). This sounded really cool and so I decided to give this a try. Not only does this totally work, it also adds another level of computer reuse to the version demonstrated in the book (as it provides a way to reuse floppy disks in addition to cameras).It has been fun going around shooting pictures and discovering all of the interesting results when I upload the photos at home. You will need:An obsolete digital cameraA floppy diskA mini screwdriver setPinsScissorsGluePlease note that some of the links on this page contain Amazon affiliate links. This does not change the price of any of the items for sale. However, I earn a small commission if you click on any of those links and buy anything. I reinvest this money into materials and tools for future projects. If you would like an alternate suggestion for a supplier of any of the parts, please let me know. You can make a visible light filter using a the plastic inside most floppy disks.Rip apart the floppy disk and be careful not to get your fingerprints on the plastic disk. Take the disk and cut a small plastic square that is slightly larger than your CCD. Open up your camera case. Place your screws aside somewhere safe. Once the case is open, locate the lens assembly on the front of the camera. Carefully detach the lens assembly from the circuit board to find the CCD chip. Set aside these screws somewhere safe as well. The visible light filter is a thin piece of glass located either directly atop the CCD or behind the last lens of the assembly. It is easy to spot because it looks reddish to purplish and changes color when it is rotated.Simply pick it free with your fingers (being careful not to touch the CCD/lenses). Your camera will now let IR light through to the sensor. Place the visible light filter that you just made over top of the CCD. Using your pin, place a few tiny drops of glue in each corner to hold it in place. When the glue has dried, reassemble the camera using all of the screws that you set aside earlier. Did you find this useful, fun, or entertaining? Follow @madeineuphoria to see my latest projects.

```markdown
# Infrared Camera Conversion Process

## Summary
This process involves converting an obsolete digital camera into an infrared (IR) camera using the plastic from a floppy disk as a visible light filter. The camera's existing visible light filter is removed and replaced with a cut-out piece of floppy disk plastic. This enables the camera to capture near-infrared light, adding a new use to both old cameras and floppy disks.

## Step-by-Step Representation

### START:
- Begin the process of converting an obsolete digital camera into an infrared camera.

### INPUT: Gather Materials
- INPUT: Obsolete digital camera
- INPUT: Floppy disk
- INPUT: Mini screwdriver set
- INPUT: Pins
- INPUT: Scissors
- INPUT: Glue

### PROCESS: Prepare the Floppy Disk Filter
- Disassemble the floppy disk without leaving fingerprints on the plastic disk.
- Cut a small plastic square from the floppy disk, slightly larger than the camera's CCD.

### PROCESS: Disassemble the Camera
- Use the mini screwdriver set to open the camera case.
- STORE: Place the removed screws in a safe location.
- Locate the lens assembly and carefully detach it from the circuit board to access the CCD chip.
- STORE: Place these screws in a safe location as well.

### PROCESS: Remove the Existing Visible Light Filter
- Identify the visible light filter, which appears reddish to purplish.
- DECISION: Is the filter directly atop the CCD or behind the last lens?
  - IF Yes: Proceed to remove the filter.
  - IF No: [END] The camera may not be suitable for this conversion.

### PROCESS: Remove the Filter
- Carefully pick the visible light filter free with fingers, avoiding contact with the CCD or lenses.
- OUTPUT: The camera is now modified to let IR light through to the sensor.

### PROCESS: Install the New Visible Light Filter
- Place the floppy disk plastic square over the CCD.
- Use a pin to apply tiny drops of glue in each corner to secure the filter.

### DECISION: Has the Glue Dried?
  - IF Yes: Proceed to reassemble the camera.
  - IF No: Wait until the glue has dried before proceeding.

### PROCESS: Reassemble the Camera
- Reattach the lens assembly to the circuit board.
- Use the previously stored screws to close the camera case.

### OUTPUT: Infrared Camera
- OUTPUT: The camera is now capable of taking infrared photographs.

### END:
- The infrared camera conversion process is complete.
```

instruct00116.title: Shirt and Tie Card
instruct00116.text: Ties certainly are a fail-safe gift on Father's Day, so why not feature them in your card this year? Simple and sweet, this shirt and tie card is sure to make Dad smile. Also, the shirt pattern can be worked off of pretty easily. Invites to a luau? Find paper that looks like a Hawaiian shirt. Geeky friend? Add a pocket protector and some leaky pens. Bond, James Bond? Make a blazer,cummerbund, andbow-tie...you get the idea. Turns out you don't need much to make this card: 1 sheet legal-seized paper (8 1/2-by-14-inch) some patterned paper for the tie scissors optional: glue I didn't have any decorative paper that was big enough for the shirt, so I simply opted for some standard white paper from my printer, and some origami paper for the tie. If you're working with patterned paper for your shirt, place it facedown. Otherwise, go ahead and fold in half vertically. Unfold. Line up left edge with centerline fold, and crease. Do the same on the right side, and unfold. Fold the top-left corner in and line it up with the nearest crease, making a triangle. Do the same thing on the right side. Pinch together outside points of each triangle so they meet, and crease. Make sure you're only creating the fold on the triangle. *note: holding a camera in one hand while folding with the other causes for some awkward photos. If you're using both hands, this will go smoother than my pictures let on. While still pinching the triangles, fold down the top edge. It should fall into place nicely (see pictures), so go with it. These are your sleeves! Turn paper upside down, and flip. Fold down a tiny bit of the top edge. This is your collar! Flip paper over again, and fold down the top left and right corners so tips meet at centerline. Now it looks like a collar! Now simply fold paper so the bottom edge slides under the collar, and you have your completed shirt. Making the tie is relatively simple and free form. Simply cut out the desired shape (are you going for skinny black tie? bow tie? up to you!) and glue to the front of the shirt. It's important to glue to just the front of the shirt and not the collar, as you still want to be able to open the card. Write a note, slip it in, address the envelope, seal with a kiss, and send that card off! Who's the best child ever? You are.

```markdown
# Shirt and Tie Father's Day Card System

## Inputs:
- 1 sheet of legal-sized paper (8 1/2-by-14-inch)
- Patterned paper for the tie
- Scissors
- Optional: glue

## Outputs:
- A completed shirt and tie card

## Process:

START: Begin creating the shirt and tie card.

PROCESS: Select paper for the shirt.
  - IF the paper is patterned, place it facedown.
  - ELSE use standard white paper.

PROCESS: Fold the paper in half vertically to establish a centerline.
  - Unfold the paper after folding.

PROCESS: Align the left edge with the centerline and crease.
  - Repeat the same process on the right side and unfold.

PROCESS: Fold the top-left corner inwards to line up with the nearest crease, forming a triangle.
  - Repeat the same process on the top-right corner.

PROCESS: Pinch together the outside points of each triangle so they meet, and crease the fold on the triangle only.

PROCESS: While pinching the triangles, fold down the top edge to form the sleeves of the shirt.
  - Turn the paper upside down and flip it.

PROCESS: Fold down a small section of the top edge to create the collar of the shirt.
  - Flip the paper over again.

PROCESS: Fold down the top left and right corners so the tips meet at the centerline, shaping the collar.

PROCESS: Fold the paper so the bottom edge slides under the collar to complete the shirt.

PROCESS: Cut out the desired shape of the tie from patterned paper.
  - DECISION: Choose the style of the tie (skinny, bow, etc.).

PROCESS: Glue the tie to the front of the shirt, making sure not to glue the collar so the card can be opened.

OUTPUT: Write a personal note inside the shirt card.

PROCESS: Place the card in an envelope, address it, and seal it with a gesture of affection.

END: Send off the card to the recipient.
```

instruct00538.title: Photoshop: Classic Black and White Photo Techniques.
instruct00538.text: An alternative way to make a black and white photo in Photoshop, NOT just by clicking Mode -> Grayscale. Check inside for more detail. The original color photo was taken at Wat Sam Kor Temple, Chacheongsao, Thailand during my friend's ordination. Normally if you only choose Mode -> Grayscale, you can only get a Black and White image like this, the resulting color is too flat. By using the alternative way, you can make a photo like this. First: Choose Image -> Adjustment -> Hue/Saturation Setting, set it to -100%. Second: Choose Image -> Adjustment -> Levels, choose the "Set black point" and choose a dark area on your photo, see how the overall color changes. In this photo I choose the right-side of the forehead. Same as previous step, Set the White Point. This time I choose the left arm of the other monk (right hand side of the photo). Add some noise from the Filter menu, I use about 25 in this image, and choose also "monochromatic" at the Add Noise dialog box. Under the menu Select -> All, then Select -> Modify -> Border, this time I choose 50, but it depends on the size of your photo. Then choose Select -> Feather, and this time I use 30, but it also depends on your image size. Choose Image -> Adjustment -> Curve, darken the border area. The finished image is like a developed B/W using old film.

```markdown
- Open Photoshop with the desired color photo.

## PROCESS: Convert to Black and White with Hue/Saturation
```

instruct00024.title: Authentic Pretzels
instruct00024.text: These pretzels are boiled in baking soda solution for that unique chewy texture. I served these with mustard for dipping at a Grey Cup party and they went over really well. They are quite simple to make but will really impress your guests. This recipe makes 16 palm sized soft pretzels. 1-1/2 C Water 1 Tbsp Sugar 1 Packet Yeast 1 tsp Salt 1 Tbsp Oil or Butter ~4-1/2 C Flour 1/2 C Baking Soda Course Salt Mix 1-1/2 C Warm Water 1 Tbsp Sugar 1 Packet Yeast and let sit 10 minutes. Stir in1 tsp Salt 1 Tbsp Oil or Butter 2 C Flour Stir in as much additional Flour as you can then turn onto a floured board and knead for 7 to 8 minutes, adding flour as necessary.Important: do not add baking soda to dough! Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl and rest in a warm place for 1 hour. In the mean time bring 8 C of water and 1/2* C Baking Soda to boil in a large pot, and heat oven to 450F. *Some people have found this to be too much. If you are worried cut it back to 1/3 or a 1/4 cup. Punch down dough and divide into 16 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a rope 16 to 20 inches long. To form pretzel shape, fold rope in half, twist twice and fold over. Press lightly to stick everything together and place directly into boiling water. Boil each pretzel for 1-2 minutes, turning once. With a slotted spoon transfer to a cookie sheet lined with parchment paper and sprinkle with course salt. Boil or dip? Some recipes call for dipping the pretzels in the baking soda solution but not boiling them. This gives the same chewy texture but allows the pretzels to puff up a lot more in the oven. Bake pretzels for 10 minutes at 450F. Transfer immediately to a cooling rack.

```markdown
# Soft Pretzel Making System Summary

## Ingredients Required
- Water

- Yeast

- Oil or Butter
- Flour

- Coarse Salt

## Equipment Required
- Large pot
- Bowl
- Baking sheets
- Parchment paper
- Slotted spoon
- Cooling rack

## Process Steps

START:
  - INPUT: 1-1/2 C Warm Water
  - INPUT: 1 Tbsp Sugar
  - INPUT: 1 Packet Yeast
  - PROCESS: Mix water, sugar, and yeast and let sit for 10 minutes.

PROCESS:
  - INPUT: 1 tsp Salt
  - INPUT: 1 Tbsp Oil or Butter
  - INPUT: 2 C Flour
  - PROCESS: Stir in salt, oil/butter, and 2 cups of flour.

  - PROCESS: Stir in as much flour as possible.

PROCESS:
  - PROCESS: Turn dough onto a floured board.

PROCESS:

  - PROCESS: Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl.

PROCESS:

PROCESS:
  - INPUT: 8 C Water

PROCESS:

PROCESS:

PROCESS:

PROCESS:
  - PROCESS: Roll each piece into a rope 16 to 20 inches long.

PROCESS:
  - PROCESS: Form each rope into a pretzel shape.

PROCESS:
  - PROCESS: Place pretzels directly into boiling baking soda solution.

PROCESS:
  - PROCESS: Boil each pretzel for 1-2 minutes, turning once.

PROCESS:
  - PROCESS: Transfer boiled pretzels to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.

PROCESS:
  - INPUT: Coarse Salt
  - PROCESS: Sprinkle boiled pretzels with coarse salt.

DECISION [IF]: Boil or dip the pretzels?
  - Boil: CONTINUE
  - Dip: CONTINUE (Note: Dipping allows pretzels to puff more in the oven.)

PROCESS:
  - PROCESS: Bake pretzels for 10 minutes at 450F.

OUTPUT:
  - OUTPUT: Baked pretzels.

PROCESS:
  - PROCESS: Transfer pretzels to a cooling rack.

END:
```

instruct00312.title: Deodorant
instruct00312.text: In 5 minutes, you can make your own natural deodorant at home without all that icky Alzheimer's disease! Using a few simple ingredients, you can make your own all-natural, skin soothing deodorant, scented exactly the way you like it. It's so simple and gratifying, you'll never go back! To make your own deodorant, gather up:Corn starchBaking sodaCoconut oilEssential oils (opt. - adds smellpretty!)Vitamin E (opt. adds ooohskinsoft!)An empty container to be filled with your new deodorantSome great essential oils for deodorant also act as antimicrobials (since bacteria is what causes the smell, using something to wipe them out is even better!) While the oils of bay, cinnamon, clove and thyme are the most inhibitory, they can also lead to major sensitivity in the pit-ular area. # Natural Deodorant Creation Process

```markdown
## Ingredients and Materials
- Cornstarch
- Baking soda
- Coconut oil
- Essential oils (optional)
- Vitamin E oil (optional)
- Empty deodorant container
- Colored tissue paper (optional, as a flag)

## Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of making natural deodorant.

### INPUT:
- Gather all required ingredients and materials.

### PROCESS: Mixing Dry Ingredients
- Combine 1/4 cup (60mL) of cornstarch with 1/4 cup of baking soda in a mixing bowl.

### INPUT:
- Add essential oils to the mixture.
  - [IF] Essential oils are desired:
    - PROCESS: Add 8 drops of lavender and 3 drops of sandalwood essential oil (or any preferred blend).
  - [ELSE]:
    - Skip adding essential oils.

### INPUT:
- Add wet ingredients to the mixture.
  - PROCESS: Add 2 tablespoons of coconut oil to the bowl.
  - PROCESS: Add a few drops of vitamin E oil (optional) to the mixture.

### DECISION: Is the coconut oil of a higher melting point?
  - [IF] Yes:
    - OUTPUT: The mixture will have a more solid consistency.
  - [ELSE]:
    - OUTPUT: The mixture may be softer and have a lower melting point.

### PROCESS: Combining Ingredients
- Mush all the ingredients together until a silky mass is formed.

### DECISION: Does the mixture have the right consistency?
  - [IF] Yes:
    - Proceed to the next step.
  - [ELSE]:
    - PROCESS: Adjust the mixture by adding more coconut oil or dry ingredients until the desired consistency is achieved.

### PROCESS: Filling the Container
- Fill the empty deodorant container with about an inch of the mixture.

### DECISION: Is a usage flag desired?
  - [IF] Yes:
    - INPUT: Cut out a piece of colored tissue paper.
    - PROCESS: Place the tissue paper flag into the container on top of the deodorant.
  - [ELSE]:
    - Skip adding a flag.

### PROCESS: Complete Filling the Container
- Fill the rest of the container with the deodorant mixture.

### PROCESS: Cleanup and Labeling
- Clean up the container's exterior.
- Create and apply a custom label to the container (optional).

### PROCESS: Setting the Deodorant
- Allow the deodorant to set up for a day or two.

### OUTPUT:
- The final product is a natural, homemade deodorant ready for use.

### END:
- The process of making natural deodorant is complete.
- Use the deodorant liberally and encourage others to do the same.

## Additional Notes
- The deodorant does not prevent sweating, as it does not contain aluminum.
- Sweating is natural, and the discomfort associated with it can be overcome.
- Essential oils act as antimicrobials to reduce odor-causing bacteria.
```

instruct00575.title: Crispy Ground Beef Tacos Recipe
instruct00575.text: Tacos have been one of the few things I do well and that's probably because I've been making them since I was a teenager. In this recipe I'll also show you how easy it is to make crispy taco shells. Nobody should ever have to suffer through store bought crispy shells. You can also replace the beef with diced up chicken breast. Here's what you'll need. This makes about 10 tacos. Cook and prep time is about 45 minutes.1lb ground beef1 med. onion1 container of fresh salsa (mild/med/hot your choice)1 teaspoon cumin powder1-2 tomatoes1 cup of shredded cheddar cheese.1 head of lettuce1 package of corn tortillas (12 count)1 cup of vegetable oil (enough to fill your fry pan about 1/2 inch)1 can refried beans (if you want to stretch your beef to make more tacos)I'm hungry already, it must be lunch time. Chop of the onions as small as you like.Add onions and ground beef to largish fry pan.Put them on medium heat and mix them up. Once the beef is browned.Add 1 teaspon of cumin.Add all of the fresh salsa.Mix and cook for about 15-20 minutes. Do not cover. You don't want it too wet at the end, but it will be juicy. Grate your cheese.Sharpen your knife. Cut up the tomatoes.Wash and dry your lettuce. Pour your vegetable oil in an 8" fry pan.Put it on med/low heat. You can test if it's ready by putting a small dash of water from your finger and if it starts popping, you're ready.Each tortilla will only take a couple of minutes to cook.Place a tortilla in the oil, after a minute or so, flip it, then take it out. You'll have to experiment to see how crispy you like your shells, the longer you cook them, the crispier they will get. If you make them way ahead of time, don't make them too crispy, then you can warm them in the oven just before you're ready to eat without them getting too hard.Place your shells on a paper grocery bag or a bunch of paper towels to soak up the excess oil. Now put your tacos together with quantities that fit your appetite.Put in the beef.Then the cheese.Then the tomatoes.Then the lettuce. My favorite step, beer and tacos. It's usually my second as I can't resist having one while I'm cooking.If you were thinking ahead, you would already have a beer glass in the freezer.

```markdown
# Taco Preparation System

## Ingredients and Utensils Input
- INPUT: 1lb ground beef
- INPUT: 1 medium onion
- INPUT: 1 container of fresh salsa (mild/med/hot)
- INPUT: 1 teaspoon cumin powder
- INPUT: 1-2 tomatoes
- INPUT: 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese
- INPUT: 1 head of lettuce
- INPUT: 1 package of corn tortillas (12 count)
- INPUT: 1 cup of vegetable oil
- INPUT: 1 can refried beans (optional)
- INPUT: Beer (optional)
- INPUT: Knife, fry pan, 8" fry pan, grater, paper towels or grocery bag

## Cooking Process
START:
- PROCESS: Chop onions into small pieces.
- PROCESS: Add onions and ground beef to a large fry pan.
- PROCESS: Turn the heat to medium and mix beef and onions.
- DECISION: Is the beef browned?
  - IF YES: Proceed to add spices.
  - IF NO: Continue cooking until browned.
- PROCESS: Add 1 teaspoon of cumin powder to the browned beef.
- PROCESS: Add the fresh salsa to the beef and onion mixture.
- PROCESS: Mix and cook for 15-20 minutes without covering.

## Preparing Crispy Taco Shells
- PROCESS: Grate the cheddar cheese.
- PROCESS: Sharpen the knife and cut up the tomatoes.
- PROCESS: Wash and dry the lettuce.
- PROCESS: Heat 1 cup of vegetable oil in an 8" fry pan over med/low heat.
- DECISION: Is the oil ready for frying?
  - IF YES: Begin frying tortillas.
  - IF NO: Continue heating and test again.
- PROCESS: Fry each tortilla for a couple of minutes, flipping once, until desired crispiness is achieved.
- PROCESS: Place fried shells on paper towels or a grocery bag to drain excess oil.

## Assembling Tacos
- PROCESS: Add beef mixture to the taco shells.
- PROCESS: Add shredded cheese on top of the beef.
- PROCESS: Add diced tomatoes on top of the cheese.
- PROCESS: Add lettuce on top of the tomatoes.
- OUTPUT: Finished tacos ready to be served.

## Optional Steps
- DECISION: Are refried beans being used to stretch the beef?
  - IF YES: Add refried beans to the taco assembly process after beef.
  - IF NO: Skip this step.
- DECISION: Is beer being served with tacos?
  - IF YES: Serve beer with tacos.
  - IF NO: Skip this step.
- DECISION: Was a beer glass put in the freezer ahead of time?
  - IF YES: Use the chilled glass for the beer.
  - IF NO: Use a regular glass or skip if not serving beer.

END: The process of making and assembling tacos is complete.
```

instruct00366.title: Tyvek Projector Screen
instruct00366.text: Make a projection screen very quickly and very cheaply with TYVEK, a PVC pipe, rope, and plumbing pipe. I started out thinking I'd do 16' x 9' then realized that was too large, so went with 9' x 7'. Remember you want a roughly 3:4 height to width ratio for most video formats. unprinted tyvek might be better for rear projection. Home Depot has it, as do others. Roll out on a clean surface (or clean side up) and cut to your required dimensions. I used 10' length of plumbing glavanized steel. Note the printed size is face down on dirty floor. Buttered side up ! I cut a much longer piece of TYVEK, 16x9, and rolled the extra onto the bar. this is good for 2 reasons, a) if ever i need a white backdrop i have the extra length b) rolling the tyvek up gets rid of the invariable kinks that occur when taping. Large diameter PVC might be stiff enough to be straight, but not the 1-1/2" stuff i had which is why i went to steel. At the other end (that will hang down) I used just plain PVC, 1/2 I have been using packing tape. Works a treat for this application though TYVEK tape might also be good (let me know) Because I cut the roll way long (16x9) and am only using (9x7) i stop the rest rolling off by clamping at the top with quick clamps. Allows flexibility in projection size. Your very own large projection screen. I had the printed TYVEK, so not good for rear projection, but excellent image quality for front projection.

```markdown
# Projection Screen System Using TYVEK

## System Overview:
The system is designed to create a projection screen using TYVEK, PVC pipe, rope, and plumbing pipe. The steps will include measuring and cutting materials, assembling the frame, and mounting the TYVEK screen. The final product is a 9' x 7' projection screen suitable for front projection with the option to extend to 16' x 9' for a white backdrop if needed.

## System Steps:

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a projection screen.

### PROCESS: Determine Screen Size
- INPUT: Desired video format ratio (3:4 height to width).
- DECISION [IF]: Is the initial desired size (16' x 9') too large?
  - Yes: Adjust the size to 9' x 7'.
  - No: Proceed with the 16' x 9' size.

### PROCESS: Acquire Materials
- INPUT: TYVEK material, PVC pipe, plumbing galvanized steel, rope, packing tape or TYVEK tape, quick clamps.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Workspace
- Ensure the workspace has a clean surface or lay the TYVEK clean side up.

### PROCESS: Measure and Cut TYVEK
- INPUT: Dimensions for the screen (9' x 7').
- OUTPUT: Cut TYVEK material to the required dimensions.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Top Bar
- INPUT: 10' length of plumbing galvanized steel.
- OUTPUT: Steel bar to support the top edge of the screen.

### PROCESS: Attach TYVEK to Top Bar
- Roll the excess TYVEK onto the steel bar.
- OUTPUT: TYVEK attached to the bar, with extra length rolled up.

### PROCESS: Prevent Unrolling
- Use quick clamps to stop the extra TYVEK from unrolling.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Bottom Bar
- INPUT: Length of PVC pipe (1/2").
- OUTPUT: PVC pipe to weight down the bottom edge of the screen.

### PROCESS: Assemble the Screen
- Connect the TYVEK to the top steel bar and the bottom PVC pipe.
- Use rope to hang the screen from the top bar.

### PROCESS: Secure the Screen
- Use packing tape or TYVEK tape to secure the TYVEK to the bars.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the TYVEK for rear projection?
  - Yes: Use unprinted TYVEK.
  - No: If TYVEK is printed, use it for front projection only.

### OUTPUT: Complete Projection Screen
- A 9' x 7' projection screen with the option to extend to 16' x 9'.

### END:
- The process of creating a TYVEK projection screen is complete.
```

```markdown
## System Overview
The system takes in minimal materials to create a simple kite that can fly. The user must follow the step-by-step instructions to fold the paper correctly, attach the string, and then fly the kite safely in an open area.

- One sheet of paper (A4 or letter size)
- String

### Process Steps

#### PROCESS [Fold Paper]:

#### PROCESS [Mark Diagonals]:

#### PROCESS [Collapse Paper]:

#### OUTPUT:

- The kite-making process is complete.

### Additional Notes
- The user is encouraged to make variations and play with the design.
- For further information and inspiration, visit the blog at http://papelyviento.tumblr.com.
- This design is suitable for beginners and is not too complex.
```

instruct00479.title: Anti-3D Glasses
instruct00479.text: So you want to go see the latest blockbuster with in-your-face 3D effects...but your significant other doesn't share your enthusiasm. In fact, many people find that 3D movies causesnauseaand headaches. What to do? Leave them at home? See 2D instead? Nonsense! Those aren't solutions. Instead, build a pair of Anti-3D glasses for them! 2 pairs of Polarized 3D glasses. (Mine were "Master Image" by far the easiest ones to work with)Small flathead screwdriverRazor blade/Scissors Most of the theaters these day are using "Passive 3D" technology. The glasses have radiallypolarizedlens, one clockwise, one counter-clockwise. The image on the screen is projected through two polarized lenses, again, one clockwise, one counter-clockwise. The glasses allow the light from only one projector to reach each eye, therefore each eye sees a slightly different picture creating the 3D effect. To see this in action, put a pair of 3D glasses on and hold another pair facing you. Close one eye and slowly turn the pair of glasses you are holding. You'll see one lens turn almost completely dark. Switch eyes and the other lens will be dark. Our Anti-3D glasses will be modified so that each eyereceives the same image. Insert the screwdriver and carefully pop off the arms. Using the screwdriver carefully pop off the lens retainer piece. Be sure to leave the lenses where they are. Youdon'twant to mix them up! Repeat on second pair. Exchange the two lenses as shown in the photo. Due to how the lenses are made, we have to keep them facing the same direction as they originally were in the glasses. Using the retainer piece as a template, trim the edge of the lens off so it will fit into the frame. Snap the retainer piece and arms back on, and you're done! There will be a small gap at the inside corner of the lens that was trimmed. It's far enough in the corner that itshouldn'teffect your viewing, but if it does you can cover it with a small piece of electrical tape. Now hit the theater and enjoy the glorious flatness of 2D! The Real D brand of glasses are becoming much more popular these days so you might not be able to find the Master Image ones that I used. You can still follow the same procedure on Real D glasses, but it will be a bit more complicated as you will have to carefully snap apart a glued seam, and then re-glue it upon assembly.

```markdown
# Anti-3D Glasses Creation Process

## Inputs:
- 2 pairs of Polarized 3D glasses (preferably "Master Image" brand)
- Small flathead screwdriver
- Razor blade or Scissors
- (Optional) Electrical tape

## Outputs:
- 1 pair of Anti-3D glasses

## Process Steps:

### START:
- Begin the process of creating Anti-3D glasses.

### PROCESS: [Prepare the Work Area]
- Ensure you have a clean and organized workspace to begin the modification of the glasses.

### INPUT: [Gather Materials]
- Acquire 2 pairs of polarized 3D glasses and tools (screwdriver, razor blade/scissors, electrical tape).

### PROCESS: [Understand the Technology]
- Recognize that Passive 3D technology uses radially polarized lenses to create a 3D effect by projecting two images, one clockwise and one counter-clockwise.

### PROCESS: [Test the 3D Glasses]
- Put on a pair of 3D glasses and hold another pair in front of you to observe the polarization effect.

### PROCESS: [Disassemble the First Pair of Glasses]
- Use the screwdriver to carefully remove the arms of the glasses.
- Pop off the lens retainer piece, ensuring the lenses remain in place to avoid mixing them up.

### PROCESS: [Disassemble the Second Pair of Glasses]
- Repeat the disassembly process on the second pair of glasses.

### DECISION: [Are the Lenses Correctly Positioned?]
  - IF 'Yes': Proceed to exchange the lenses.
  - ELSE: Ensure lenses are facing the same direction as originally placed before proceeding.

### PROCESS: [Exchange the Lenses]
- Swap one lens from each pair to the other, maintaining their original orientation.

### PROCESS: [Trim the Lenses]
- Use the retainer piece as a template to trim the excess edge off the lens so it fits into the frame.

### PROCESS: [Reassemble the Glasses]
- Snap the retainer piece and arms back onto the frame.

### DECISION: [Is there a Gap in the Lens?]
  - IF 'Yes': Proceed to cover the gap.
  - ELSE: No action needed, proceed to the next step.

### PROCESS: [Cover the Gap] (Optional)
- If there is a small gap at the corner of the lens, cover it with a small piece of electrical tape.

### OUTPUT:
- The Anti-3D glasses are now ready to use.

### PROCESS: [Consider Alternative Brands]
- If "Master Image" glasses are not available, you can apply the same process to "Real D" glasses, with additional steps to carefully snap apart the glued seam and re-glue upon assembly.

### END:
- The process of creating Anti-3D glasses is complete. Enjoy the movies in 2D!
```

instruct00761.title: Freehand Glass Etching
instruct00761.text: I am making personalized shot glasses for each of my friends this year (or coffee cups for those who don't partake). This is a bit different from standard etching in that it does not use a stencil: for small curved glasses like these, stencils don't quite stick. I also included basic instructions for custom stenciling, just in case... So, while the manufacturer recommends glass etching products for stencils it's possible to use it like paint. The wine glasses I did last year were hugely popular, so I hope these are a success too. You will need: 1 jar of Armour Etch (from most craft stores, possibly from a hardware store?) 1 (or more) glasses or any object made out of glass 1 paintbrush And since etching cream is really nasty and caustic: 1 pair of gloves eye protection If you want to stencil your design you'll want some vinyl contact paper. Make sure it's sticky enough, but even then you may have trouble getting it to cling to a rounded surface. You can also use plastic stickers to create a 'negative' image, e.g., a frosted glass with non-frosted polka dots. This is a project for adults, in fact, you have to have an ID to even BUY this stuff. Your product might be different from mine, so read all of the directions that come with it! Clean and dry all of your glassware thoroughly. Use the brush to draw your design, or the first stage of your design. With larger designs, you will need to stagger the painting so that all of the areas are etched evenly. OR If you are using a stencil, apply it at this point... Or apply a solid sheet of vinyl and use a fine blade to cut out your design. Smooth out any bubbles, as they will leave gaps in your design. Fill in the open areas with cream, and brush it back and forth evenly. After the first stage of etching cream has been applied, set it aside for about 7 minutes. Paint your next glass, or check your email, just don't let the glass etching cream get all over! After 7 minutes, come back and wash and dry your glass. Finish as many parts of your design in as many stages as you need. I used 2 stages, one for the flower, and one for the branches. Glass etching is fast, and fairly inexpensive!

```markdown
# Personalized Glass Etching System

## Inputs
- Armour Etch (glass etching cream)
- Glasses or any glass objects
- Paintbrush
- Gloves
- Eye protection
- Vinyl contact paper (optional for stenciling)
- Fine blade (optional for stencil cutting)

## Outputs
- Personalized etched glassware

## Process

### START:
- Begin the personalized glass etching process.

### INPUT:
- Gather all required materials.

### PROCESS: [Safety Precautions]
- Put on gloves and eye protection to handle etching cream safely.

### DECISION [IF]: [Is a stencil being used?]
  - Yes: Proceed to stencil application steps.
  - No: Proceed to direct painting steps.

### IF YES [Stencil Application]:
  - INPUT: Apply the vinyl contact paper to the glass.
  - PROCESS: Use a fine blade to cut out the design from the vinyl.
  - PROCESS: Smooth out any bubbles in the vinyl to prevent gaps in the design.

### IF NO [Direct Painting]:
  - PROCESS: Clean and dry the glassware thoroughly.
  - PROCESS: Use the paintbrush to draw the design directly onto the glass.

### PROCESS: [Applying Etching Cream]
- Apply a layer of Armour Etch over the design area.
- Brush the cream evenly back and forth.

### PROCESS: [Etching Time]
- Let the etching cream sit on the glass for about 7 minutes.

### DECISION [IF]: [Is the etching time up?]
  - Yes: Proceed to rinse the glass.
  - No: Wait until 7 minutes have passed.

### IF YES [Rinsing]:
  - PROCESS: After 7 minutes, wash and dry the glass to remove the etching cream.

### DECISION [IF]: [Are there additional design stages?]
  - Yes: Repeat the etching process for remaining design stages.
  - No: Proceed to the end of the process.

### IF YES [Additional Stages]:
  - PROCESS: Apply etching cream to the next stage of the design.
  - PROCESS: Wait for another 7 minutes, then rinse and dry the glass.
  - OUTPUT: Continue this process until all parts of the design are complete.

### OUTPUT:
- Final personalized etched glassware.

### END:
- The personalized glass etching process is complete.
```

instruct00173.title: Making a Probiotic Ginger Beer
instruct00173.text: Incorporate probiotic bacterial into ginger-based beverages! Yum. Some simple ingredients, a few items from around the kitchen and within 2-3 weeks you can have your own DIY probiotic ginger beer. Place 1 cup of filtered water in a pint jar Add 2 teaspoons of freshly grated ginger root (skin and all) Stir in 2 teaspoons of evaporated cane sugar, tighten lid and shake. Cover* and Store in a warm place, add 2 teaspoons of cane sugar and ginger root each day. In 2-7 days, when it starts bubbling, it is active and ready for the next step. Use right away for best results. * I use a coffee filter and rubber-band to cover the pint jar. Bring 2 quarts of water to a boil Add about 2 inches of ginger root, grated, for a mild flavor (up to 6 inches of ginger for a more intense flavor) Add 1-1/2 cups of sugar. Boil the mixture for about 15 minutes. Let mixture come to room temperature When cool strain the ginger out. Add the juice of two lemons Add the strained ginger bug And now add enough water to make a 1 gallon. -Ginger beer plant does not tolerate chlorinated water. Tap water left out overnight or mineral water should be fine. When bottling use sealable bottles. Screw-top recycled plastic bottles, rubber gasket style or gallon jug jars can be used. Transfer from mason jar to sealable bottle using a funnel. Leave to ferment in a warm place for about two weeks Refrigerate before opening. Carbonation. The force is strong.

```markdown
# DIY Probiotic Ginger Beer System Summary

## Ingredients and Materials Input
- Filtered water
- Fresh ginger root
- Evaporated cane sugar
- Pint jar with lid
- Coffee filter and rubber band (for covering the jar)
- Large pot for boiling
- Lemons
- Chlorine-free water (tap water left out overnight or mineral water)
- Sealable bottles (screw-top plastic, rubber gasket style, or gallon jug jars)
- Funnel

## Steps

### Starting the Ginger Bug
START: Initiate the ginger bug preparation process.
INPUT: Add 1 cup of filtered water to a pint jar.
INPUT: Add 2 teaspoons of freshly grated ginger root.
INPUT: Add 2 teaspoons of evaporated cane sugar.
PROCESS: Tighten the lid and shake the jar to mix ingredients.
PROCESS: Replace the tight lid with a coffee filter secured by a rubber band.
STORE: Place the jar in a warm location.
PROCESS: Add 2 teaspoons of cane sugar and ginger root daily.
DECISION [IF]: Check if the mixture is bubbling after 2-7 days.
    IF YES: Proceed to the next step.
    IF NO: Continue daily feeding and checking for bubbling.

### Preparing the Ginger Beer Base
PROCESS: Bring 2 quarts of water to a boil in a large pot.
INPUT: Add 2-6 inches of grated ginger root to the boiling water, depending on desired intensity.
INPUT: Add 1-1/2 cups of sugar to the boiling water.
PROCESS: Boil the mixture for about 15 minutes.
PROCESS: Allow the mixture to come to room temperature.
PROCESS: Strain the ginger out of the cooled mixture.
INPUT: Add the juice of two lemons to the strained mixture.
INPUT: Add the active ginger bug to the lemon-ginger mixture.
INPUT: Add enough chlorine-free water to make 1 gallon of liquid.
PROCESS: Stir to combine all ingredients.

### Bottling the Ginger Beer
PROCESS: Transfer the ginger beer mixture into sealable bottles using a funnel.
STORE: Place the sealed bottles in a warm location for fermentation.
PROCESS: Allow the ginger beer to ferment for about two weeks.
DECISION [IF]: Check if the fermentation process is complete after two weeks.
    IF YES: Proceed to the next step.
    IF NO: Continue fermentation and check periodically.
OUTPUT: Fermented ginger beer ready for refrigeration.
END: Fermentation process is incomplete or unsuccessful after an extended period.

### Finishing the Ginger Beer
PROCESS: Refrigerate the ginger beer bottles before opening.
OUTPUT: Carbonated, refrigerated DIY probiotic ginger beer ready to enjoy.
```

instruct00351.title: How to Make a Hot Bikini Out of Old T-Shirts
instruct00351.text: Hey gals,When summer time comes around , I think one of the worst things is finding a cute bathing suit that fits right. And when you do find one, its expensive! Well here's a way you can make your own bathing suit from t-shirts...that way you can customize it to fit and make it your own.For more DIY fashion tips and How to's subscribe to our iTunes store and check out our website, Threadbanger. First, you need 1 extra large T-shirt..but if you like the mismatched look decide on two different colored shirts. Cut the bottom hem off both shirts and take the top shirt and cut 2 one inch wide strips off the bottom, making sure to cut through both layers of fabric. Then take those 2 strips and cut both of them in half twice so you end up with 4 equal strips. (we'll call them strips 1,2,3, and 4) Take your bottom shirt and cut 2 one inch wide strips of the bottom. Cut one of the strips in half once, so you have one long strip (call it strip 5). and Cut the other in half twice, so you have two equals strips (strips 6,7). (You should have a total of seven strips.) Ok, now take your top shirt and cut 9 inches of the bottom, making sure to cut through both layers of fabric. Pin both of the layers together and from now on consider it one piece of fabric. as Megan put it in her book "to prevent the wet t-shirt contest look" Sketch a triangle that measures 10 inches across the bottom and 8 inches down both sides. If you want, make a paper pattern first....we just freehanded it. Now create an arched bottom to the triangle. the lowest point should fall one inch below the bottom of the triangle. Then turn your fabric in a half circle, and sketch another triangle of the same dimensions. Pin the triangles and cut them out. Flip one of the triangles over and fold the top corner down one inch. Carefully, pin the arched bottom up one inch. Sew a seam but be careful to leave an open "tunnel" so you can thread your strip through later. btw, does anyone know the technical term for that...or is it just tunneling? Repeat all those steps to the second triangle. Now take strip 5 and attach the end to a safety pin. Use the safety pin to help you thread strip 5 through the tunnels of your triangles. And you are done with the top! WOOHOO! Take your bottom shirt and cut a rectangle that measures 19 inches by 16 inches. Pin both layers of the rectangle together. Then sketch an hour glass shape onto the fabric. Make a paper pattern first for preciseness. You want the narrowest part of the hourglass to measure 4 inches across and fall 11 inches for the top of the rectangle. Fold in all 4 corners of the hourglass. Stretch and place strips 1,2,3, and 4 over the separate for corners. Fold and pin the front of the bathing suit in one inch, making sure to over lap the strips. Then fold and pin the opposite (back) part of the bathing suit in one inch, again making sure to over lap the strips. Sew the front and back seams. Make several small slits in the curved area of the hourglass. This will help the fabric give easier when you are folding in the edge. Lastly, fold and pin the two sides of the hourglass in 1 inch and sew a seam down both sides. You've just made yourself a bathing suit! New bathing, very little cash!

instruct00384.title: DIY Hammock Stand
instruct00384.text: We recently bought a portable hammock and we've enjoyed so much on our hiking and camping trips that I decided I wanted to hang it at home to enjoy on our backyard. I looked at the available hammock stands and they seemed quite expensive but very simple so I decided to give it a try. I based the design on some of the available commercial options. This is what I used: 2 - 8' 2X4 beams 2 - 6' 2X4 beams 2 - 4' 2X4 beams 8 - 5 and a half inch 3/8" bolts 4 - 6" 3/8" bolts 24 - 3/8" washers 12 - 3/8" tightening washers The first step is to make the angled cuts of the beams that will hold the hammock, the 6' beams. I made a 30 degree cut so that the angle to the floor would be 60 degrees. There are quite a few holes to drill for the bolts. The most tricky ones are the ones to attach the angled beams to the base. The angled beams will be "sandwiched" between the two 8' beams and the bolts will go through all three pieces. To make sure I had a straight hole for the bolt to go through all three I laid down all three four pieces on the floor just as they would when standing and drilled once through all the wood. As you can see in the picture I made the holes 1" from the edges. I should also note that the angled beams are not flush with the base beams. This is because the base will rest on top of the 4" pieces and hence be elevated about 2" from the floor. Having the angled beams reach all the way to the floor adds stability. You could also cut a "bed" in the base beams to fit the two 4" pieces so that the base would rest on the floor. The other holes to be drilled are holes for they eyebolts where the hammock will hang, and the holes to secure the base to the "feet" the two 4" beams. The final step is to bolt everything together. I used a washer on each side the bolt and a tightening washer on the nut side. After using it a few days I've thought of a couple of improvements. The angled beams flex quite a bit when the hammock is rocking so I think some tensioners running from the top of the beams to the edge of the feet would increase the stability. however they could become tripping hazards! I should also note that I choose these dimensions based on my hammock's length. So far it's held pretty well up to 200 pds.

```markdown
# Hammock Stand Construction Summary

- IF YES:
  - PROCESS: Cut a "bed" in the base beams for the 4" pieces.

  - PROCESS: Prepare the base to rest on top of the 4" beams, elevated from the floor.

- OUTPUT: Fully assembled hammock stand.

### DECISION: Are the angled beams stable?
- IF YES:
  - END: The construction process is complete.
- ELSE NO:
  - PROCESS: Consider adding tensioners for stability, while being mindful of tripping hazards.
  - OUTPUT: Enhanced stability of the hammock stand.
```

instruct00618.title: A 3D Printable Pip-Boy 3000
instruct00618.text: Ever wanted a Pip-boy 3000 from the Fallout series? Now is your chance. In this instructable I have all files to print your own. It is hollow and can hold anything. You can put a paper screen in to make it look like a working Pip-Boy, or put a smart phone in to make it functional. It is designed to be as close to an actual Pip-Boy as 3D printing can print. Find a model overview video here: http://youtu.be/-DZEGLmWa2AWhat is included in this instructable The files for this can be downloaded in the attachments or on my thingiverse page. I have two zip fodders. One holds all the STL files to make this Pip-Boy. Simply print one of each. Another Zip file holds the Step file. I have included this so you can modify it to your own personal needs. Also there is a pdf file. The pdf holds the dial of the Geiger counter. The design is not mine, I simply scaled it down from this image.What will you need To make this you will need: All the printed parts; Several nice looking screws for show and for the hinge; 5x M4 screws to assemble it; 2x M3 screws to mount several small parts; Glue; Small magnets; Velcro strips; (Optional) filler to smooth your Pip-Boy; (Optional) Paint to paint your Pip-Boy; (Optional) 3x 5mm (yellow) Leds for the 3 buttons. Build it To make one, simply print out all the parts on any printer (the model is practically supportless, only minor support is needed) and assemble. Some parts need to be glued together (I have included pictures of complete glued assemblies of parts). The screen assembly is held to the body of the Pip-Boy by 5 M4 screws that tap into the plastic. Also 2 M3 screws are needed to rotate the knob and to hold the part with the buttons in place. Two simple wood screws are used in the back for hinges. The Velcro is mounted in the double slot at each side of the front half. the Velcro is strapped around the arm to hold the Pip-Boy in place Several small magnets hold the two halves together.Paint it you can leave this unpainted but that is quite boring and bland. So just paint it. I tried to make the same color as the original, I failed, the gave up, then painted it bronze. I weathered it using black paint and a rag. I think it looks nice in this color, if you disagree, you'll just have to prove me wrong by doing a better job yourself. Also, I never used any filler on this model. I printed it in the highest quality setting of my printer. I actually never intended to paint it. At some point I just decided to paint it anyway. For a better result, I suggest using filler to smooth the model before painting. After painting you can print out the dial and glue it to the Pip-Boy. (PS. be sure to use plastic primer, without, paint might just flake off.)Share it When you do build one, I would love to see it. you can share it at my thingiverse page (or any other place of your liking)What I did extra I also added a small circuit based on a pic628 that has 3 buttons and 3 leds. The leds sit on top of switches. When you push an led, the button beneath is presses. This circuit simply turns on the led that was last pushed. I won't upload this circuit because I use hardware and programming tools for this that are hard to come by in any country other than the Netherlands. It works fairly simple so anyone with even a little bit of programming skills should be able to build something like this. (Original design of the Pip-Boy 3000 belongs to Bethesda Softworks, This model was made by and belongs to me)

instruct00218.title: Make Your Own Colored Sugar
instruct00218.text: I haven't bought colored sugar crystals for decorating baked goods in a long time. I can't imagine spending around $1.50 for 4oz of sugar when it's so simple to color it yourself. You can color regular granulated sugar (which is what I do) or larger crystals if you prefer that look.This is a ridiculously simple concept but it's a cost-saving effort that requires no special supplies and takes just a couple of minutes. You need:SugarFood coloringForkBowlPlateYou can use liquid food color, gel food color or paste food color. Liquid is the easiest to mix into the sugar and only slightly more is needed to get deeper colors. If all you happen to have is powdered food color, mix some powder with a few drops of alcohol such as vodka, and use as you would liquid food coloring. Put the sugar in a bowl and add food color. Mix together using a fork or your fingers. As the color saturates all of the crystals, you'll get a good idea of how deep the color is. Add more color or sugar to adjust the depth of color. When all of the sugar is saturated with color, spread the colored sugar on a plate and let sit out to dry. This may take an hour or so. Once the sugar is dry it will have large clumps. Break these up and the sugar will be free-flowing.

```markdown
# Colored Sugar Crystals System Summary

## Inputs
- Granulated sugar
- Food coloring (liquid, gel, paste, or powdered mixed with alcohol)
- Bowl
- Fork
- Plate

## Outputs
- Colored sugar crystals ready for use in decorating baked goods

## Process Steps

START:
- Place granulated sugar into a bowl.

INPUT: 
- Add the desired amount of food coloring to the sugar.

PROCESS:
- Use a fork or fingers to mix the sugar and food coloring together.

DECISION [IF]: Is the color of the sugar as deep as desired?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: 
  - PROCESS: Add more food coloring to deepen the color or add more sugar to lighten the color.
  - Repeat the mixing process until the desired color depth is achieved.

PROCESS:
- Once the desired color is reached, spread the colored sugar on a plate.

PROCESS:
- Let the colored sugar sit out to dry, which may take about an hour.

DECISION [IF]: Has the sugar dried completely?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: 
  - PROCESS: Continue to let the sugar dry until it is no longer moist.
  - Repeat the decision step until the sugar is completely dry.

PROCESS:
- After the sugar has dried, check for large clumps.

DECISION [IF]: Are there large clumps in the sugar?
- Yes:
  - PROCESS: Break up the clumps to ensure the sugar is free-flowing.
- No: Proceed to the next step.

OUTPUT:
- The final product is free-flowing, colored sugar crystals ready for decorating baked goods.

END.
```

instruct00257.text: How to make your very own waterproof dryer lint fire-starter, for free. Using only household items you can make a 1 oz waterproof fire-starter that burns for 15 minutes. It's perfect for camping, backpacking, or even your backyard fire pit. No need to buy fancyfire starterlogs, here you'll need to gather a fewhouseholditems that wouldhaveotherwise been thrown in trash. First, gather a few materials from around the house. 1. Dryer lint 2. An empty egg carton 3. Old Candle Stubs (or in my case, a box of canning wax - $3*) 4. Dental floss 5. Scissors 6. New Belgium beer (not required, but hey, that's how it happened) *Available at your local hardware store Whether using old candle stubs or bars of canning wax, cut them into small strips/chunks so they can be more easily melted. Take your dryer lint and fill each compartment. Stuff a fair amount into each as it will prolong burning time. Using the scissors, cut each compartment and fold the ends of each on top of each other. Using dental floss (or any disposable string), tie each fire-starter allowing for a few inches ofadditionallength. Drop your wax pieces into a disposable glass jar (or empty aluminum can) and place it into a boiling pot of water. Keep the water level low enough so the jar or can doesn't tip over. Once the water boils, you should have fully melted wax in a few minutes. Turning off your burner, you can now lower the fire-starters into the jar or can of melted wax using the length of dental floss. Make sure the fire-starters are fully submerged until bubbles stop rising to the surface. Note - It may help to use an additional utensil to push them below the wax line. Drizzle any remaining wax onto the fire-starters. This will help ensure waterproofing. Let the fire-starters fully dry. I placed them on a paper towel to prevent a messy cleanup. After about an hour or two, they should be rock solid. Now that they have dried, your fire-starters are ready to go. Just light a corner and bask in the glory. My initial test had a burn time of 15 minutes. I'm a long time lover of this site and it's my first post.. The goal here was to take items around the house that would have otherwise wound up in a landfill and turn them into something useful. Hope you enjoy.

```markdown
# Waterproof Dryer Lint Fire-Starter Process

## START:
Gather materials required for the fire-starter.

## INPUT:
- Dryer lint
- Empty egg carton
- Old candle stubs or a box of canning wax
- Dental floss
- Scissors
- Optional: New Belgium beer

## PROCESS: [Prepare Wax]
1. Cut old candle stubs or canning wax into small strips/chunks for easier melting.

## PROCESS: [Fill Egg Carton]
2. Fill each compartment of the egg carton with a fair amount of dryer lint to prolong burning time.

## PROCESS: [Create Fire-Starter Units]
3. Use scissors to cut each compartment of the egg carton.
4. Fold the ends of each compartment on top of one another to create individual units.

## PROCESS: [Secure Fire-Starters]
5. Use dental floss to tie each fire-starter, allowing a few inches of additional length for handling.

## PROCESS: [Prepare Wax Melting Station]
6. Place wax pieces into a disposable glass jar or empty aluminum can.
7. Set the jar or can into a pot of water and bring to a boil, keeping the water level low to prevent tipping.

## DECISION [IF: Wax is Melted]:
8. Check if the wax is fully melted.

   - Yes: Proceed to next step.
   - No: Continue boiling and check again.

## PROCESS: [Dip Fire-Starters in Wax]
9. Turn off the burner once the wax is melted.
10. Lower the fire-starters into the melted wax using the length of dental floss.
11. Ensure fire-starters are fully submerged until bubbles stop rising.

## DECISION [IF: Fire-Starters Submerged]:
12. Check if fire-starters are fully submerged and bubbles have stopped.

   - Yes: Proceed to next step.
   - No: Use an additional utensil to push them below the wax line and check again.

## PROCESS: [Finalize Waterproofing]
13. Drizzle any remaining wax onto the fire-starters for additional waterproofing.

## PROCESS: [Dry Fire-Starters]
14. Let the fire-starters fully dry, placing them on a paper towel to prevent mess.

## DECISION [IF: Fire-Starters Dried]:
15. Check if fire-starters are rock solid after about an hour or two.

   - Yes: Proceed to next step.
   - No: Allow more drying time and check again.

## OUTPUT:
16. The dried, waterproof fire-starters are ready for use.

## END:
17. Light a corner of a fire-starter and use as intended.
```

instruct00368.title: Frappuccino on a Stick
instruct00368.text: Starbucks gave us the Frappuccino. I give you: Frappuccino on a STICK - the next best thing to happen to a coffee drink! The frappuccino is a super sweet, creamy, strong coffee drink blended with ice. I know, I looked it up. Seems like a perfect vehicle for a frozen treat! Besides, what better way is there to control your daily intake of frappuccino calories than to make it yourself? And freeze it. And put it on a stick. (brain freeze naturally prevents over-consumption!) Follow this super simple frappuccino recipe to whip up a batch of your own frappuccinos on sticks. They're yummier than you might think! And if you're more of a mocha frappuccino person, we can help you with that too. What you need to pull off this trick: Strong coffee or espresso Milk Sugar Cream (optional) Popsicle trays or small cups and sticks Chocolate syrup (for mocha frappuccino) To kick things off, brew up some double-strength coffee or espresso! Frappuccinos come with something called "whip" on top. I know because I've heard the friendly *$s baristas ask customers if they "want that with whip." I took this to be some kind of whipped cream. To simulate "whip," I mixed up some heavy whipping cream with a bit of sugar. You can use milk instead. If you don't have an immersion blender, a whisk will do. Fill the tops of your popsicle molds with a little bit of whip and freeze. This will give your frappuccino a nice topping of whip when it's done. If you're someone who says"no thanks" when the friendly barista offers you "whip," you may skip this part. Ok, I admit I'm still a little baffled by the term frappuccino, but I think I get it. It's part frappe, part cappuccino. Except there's no ice cream in it. Which makes no sense unless you assume it to be derived from the Greek etomology for frape, meaning iced coffee. So. . . In my opinion, it's more like a frozen cappuccino, which I guess would make it a Froccino, which may do more to elicit images of bold hairstyles and the people who wear them drinking cappuccino, than a creamy, frothy, ubersweet drink.I wish I had that picture of my dad when he had an afro. I would so photoshop him drinking a froccino. Right. So, mix your strong coffee or espresso with milk and sugar. I like this ratio:4 parts coffee : 4 parts milk : 1 part sugar or 1 cup coffee, 1 cup milk and 1/4 cup sugar Add some chocolate syrup to your liking for mocha frappuccino. If you have sticks that come with your popsicle mold, use those. I thought mine looked dumb, so I used some stirrers generously provided by the friendly folks at *$s. In order to keep them upright, I wrapped the top of the molds with plastic and stuck the sticks in through little slit. Freeze! After they're good and frozen, your frappuccinos on sticks are ready to enjoy! Running a little warm water over the base of the mold will help them release cleanly. Wasn't that easy? (And delicious!!) Yum!

```markdown
# Frappuccino on a Stick System

## START:
- Begin the process of making Frappuccino on a Stick.

## INPUT:
- Strong coffee or espresso
- Milk
- Sugar
- Cream (optional)
- Popsicle trays or small cups and sticks
- Chocolate syrup (for mocha frappuccino)

## PROCESS: Brew Coffee
- Brew double-strength coffee or espresso.

  - Yes: Proceed to whip topping preparation.
  - No: Skip to mixing coffee mixture.

## PROCESS: Prepare Whip Topping (if "whip" is desired)
  - Mix heavy whipping cream with a bit of sugar using an immersion blender or whisk.

## PROCESS: Fill Popsicle Molds with Whip
  - Fill the tops of popsicle molds with a small amount of prepared whip.
  - Freeze the whip in molds.

## PROCESS: Mix Coffee Mixture
  - Combine the following ingredients in the ratio:
    - 4 parts coffee
    - 4 parts milk
    - 1 part sugar
  - For mocha variation, add chocolate syrup to taste.

## DECISION [IF]: Are you using provided sticks?
  - Yes: Use the sticks that come with the popsicle mold.
  - No: Use alternative sticks such as stirrers.

## PROCESS: Prepare Sticks
  - If using alternative sticks, wrap the top of the mold with plastic.
  - Make slits in the plastic and insert sticks through them to keep upright.

## PROCESS: Freeze Coffee Mixture
  - Pour the coffee mixture into molds over the frozen whip.
  - Freeze until solid.

## OUTPUT:
- Frappuccinos on sticks are fully frozen and ready to enjoy.

## PROCESS: Release Frappuccinos
  - Run warm water over the base of the mold to help release the popsicles.

## END:
- Enjoy your homemade Frappuccino on a Stick!
```

instruct00818.title: How to Make a DIY Spray Paint T-Shirt
instruct00818.text: This week on Thread Heads, we take a look back at our first episode with a fun T-Shirt stencil and spray paint job. If you have any cool DIY projects like this one,send them in! send them in! And don't forget to subscribe to our podcast on iTunes! First, with some poster board, trace a few designs. We picked crosses. Carefully cut out the shapes. Using a plain white T, you can make your own color by using some rit dye and boiling water. On one side of the shirt, use the left over poster board as a stencil and spray paint lightly to prevent the paint from bleeding. On the other side, use the cut outs and spray paint. Give your shirt a personalized look by cutting or poking holes, dying, and/or adding some cool stitching.

instruct00503.title: How To: Clean Your Cast Iron Pan (including How NOT To)
instruct00503.text: Season It First of all, is your cast ironed seasoned properly? Check out my Instructable on how to season your cast iron and why I prefer Flax oil. Done? Good, let's go.Now, let's clean it. Cleaning cast iron is not difficult. So many people over complicate the matter, or worse yet, do detrimental things to their iron without knowing. You essentially just need two things. Heat Water The video is better than the guide below, trust me. There is an entire section of "do not do" I threw an egg into a pan with no butter cooked it on high. It didn't stick too much because my pan is seasoned well, but some small bits stuck. I made a bamboo scraper out of some shish kabob skewers I bought on Amazon. Basically wrap them up in a few rubber bands and you are set.Are you REALLY lazy? $6 & your can buy it pre-made one. It's going to sizzle and go nuts so be careful, but you are effectively deglazing the pan and this will remove 90-100% of the crud stuck to your pan in most cases.I've received a lot of feedback about this step. Some important things to remember is to NEVER dunk your sizzling hot pan into a sink full of water. It will crack eventually. Also use a small amount of water for the deglazing, not 2-3-4-5 cups. That will crack that pan too. If you have any little particulates still left you can wipe them off now with a towel. Everytime I use my pan I do a real quick season just to maintain the surface.Get the pan hotPour in a dollop of Flax OilRub it around.Wait till the pan smokes.Take it off the heat.Wipe the pan one more time.Walk away and let it cool. Kosher salt works get as well, but you are throwing away salt every time you use it so save this method for when something is really stuck in deep.Throw some Kosher salt into your hot and dirty panRub it around with a clothPour the excess salt down the drainHit the hot pan with water and let it deglazePut it back on the stove and do a quick season Walk away and consume hoppy beverages. If you don't already have cast iron it's time you tried it. It better for your health than the non-stick stuff you have been using from the store. I have a lot of Lodge, but if you want that mega shiny and slick surface you see in my steps above you are better off looking for an old Wagner/Erie cast iron pan on eBay. They might even be cheaper than a new pan. You won't regret it, and you can pass the pans onto your kids someday too. Don't forget to check out my other Instructables:How to Season Your Cast Iron How to Make Sriracha SaltOr my YouTube channel:ColumbusCOOKPOV
