instruct00022.title: 5-minute Chocolate Balls
instruct00022.text: Quick and delicious Rum Balls recipe (with or without rum!). These tasty treats whip up in no time, and are completely addictive. Whether you need a chocolate fix or a quick gift, these are sure to please. A food processor will help you cut through this recipe in a cool five minutes or less! 1 1/4 cups (120 grams) vanilla wafer cookies, shortbread, or graham crackers (about 35 Nilla brand wafers) 1/2 cup (55 grams) powdered (confectioners) sugar 2 tablespoons (12 grams) cocoa powder (Dutch processed or regular unsweetened cocoa powder) 2 tablespoons light corn syrup 1/4 cup (60 ml) COLD* liquid: juice; rum; water + rum extract (or your favorite); or whatever else you can imagine -- I did one batch with OJ and one with rum 1 1/2 cups (140 grams) pecans (hazelnuts, walnuts, or almonds can be used - and toasting them beforehand makes them awesome! but will probably result in longer than 5 minutes) 1/2 cup (55 grams) topping - crushed nuts, powdered sugar, cocoa powder, flaked coconut, go crazy Makes about 2 dozen decent-sized chocolate balls.*the liquid being cold will help the balling process and reduce or even eliminate the need to refrigerate before shaping Process the cookies and pecans(opt) in the food processor until finely ground. Add powdered sugar and cocoa powder and process until combined. Add corn syrup and liquid and mix well. Yes, you can do this in the processor too! Blend until it creates one massive lump on the side of the bowl. Grease your hands (trust me on this one) and shape mixture into 1 inch (2.54 cm) balls. Roll the finished balls in the toppings of your choice. (I used powdered sugar and crushed nuts)If the balls are too sticky for you to work with, you can stick 'em in the freezer for a couple minutes or in the fridge for a few hours. I'm guessing that would work. . . I've never had the patience to find out! If you don't eat them all yourself in one sitting, try to remember to bring them in to share with your colleagues/peers the next day. These are perfect little gifts to give too. A sandwich baggie with a colorful ribbon even makes it look like you put a lot of thought into it!

# Step-by-Step Representation of Hiding a File Inside a Picture

## Preconditions
- START: Begin the process.
- INPUT: Ensure you have a .zip or .rar compressor installed.
- INPUT: Have the willingness to learn the process.

## Opening Command Prompt
- PROCESS: Press the Windows start key and R.
- INPUT: Type `cmd` in the run dialog box.
- PROCESS: Click OK to open the command prompt.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the command prompt open?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Use the search bar to find and open the command prompt.

## Navigating to Desktop in Command Prompt
- PROCESS: Type `cd desktop` in the command prompt to change the directory to the desktop.

## Combining the File with the Picture
- INPUT: Type `copy /b picturename.jpg + foldername.rar outputfilename.jpg` in the command prompt.
  - DECISION [IF]: Did you use zip to archive the file?
    - Yes: Type `.zip` at the end of your folder name.
    - No: Type `.rar` at the end of your folder name.
  - DECISION [IF]: What type of picture are you using?
    - IF jpg: Type `jpg` at the end of the output file name.
    - IF png: Type `png` at the end of the output file name.
    - ELSE: Type the appropriate extension for the picture format you're using.
- OUTPUT: The system creates a new picture file with the hidden file inside it.

## Previewing the New Picture File (Optional)
- PROCESS: Navigate to the desktop outside of the command prompt.
- PROCESS: Locate and preview the new picture file to verify it looks as expected.

## Converting the Picture Back to a Compressed File
- PROCESS: Open command prompt and type `cd desktop` to navigate to the desktop directory.
- INPUT: Type `ren picturefilename.jpg outputfilename.rar` in the command prompt.
  - DECISION [IF]: What type of picture did you use?
    - IF jpg: Use `.jpg` as the file extension.
    - IF png: Use `.png` as the file extension.
    - ELSE: Use the appropriate extension for the picture format you used.
  - DECISION [IF]: Did you use zip to compress the file originally?
    - Yes: Type `.zip` at the end of your output folder name.
    - No: Type `.rar` at the end of your output folder name.
- OUTPUT: The picture file is now converted back into a RAR or Zip file.

## Extracting the Hidden File
- PROCESS: Extract the file on your desktop to find the hidden file.
- OUTPUT: The hidden file is successfully retrieved from the picture file.

## Troubleshooting
- PROCESS: If you encounter any problems, view the provided video for assistance.

## End of Process
- END: The process of hiding and retrieving a file within a picture is complete.

instruct00871.title: High Functioning Coat Hooks
instruct00871.text: Back in Los Angeles, any old coat rack or a few hooks by the door would do. Most of us would just toss a jacket in the back of the car in the winter months. But here in Vermont we need a little more. Many of the vernacular farm houses I visit have at least a half dozen hooks per person lined up in their mud rooms. My wife and I each will have several different coats, jackets and vests in play all winter long. Add to that assorted scarves, hats and gloves, several of each for both of us, and your average coat rack doesn't stand a chance. instruct00690.title: How to Build a Cajon
instruct00690.text: A Cajon is a common instrument in South America. It is often related to flamenco music/ samba.But you can use it just as a real drum with a guitar for accompany. When you play the cajon, you are sitting on it an drumming with your hands on the front side of the drum. You can find out a whole technics and learning stuff if you just search on cajon drumming on youtube for example. In this instructable I will tell you how I builded my Cajon! I looked up a whole bunch of sites on how to build cajons on google. There were plenty of people who had nice instructions on how they builded there cajons. But i decided to create one from a construction i found on Orcana Artesania* . It was an easy instruction except it was in Spanish but I did only use the measurements. Instead of having guitar strings in it I bought a snare drum wire that i put in it.*Link : http://www.ocanartesania.com/This is the parts of the box and the measurements: (see the PDF file) The building of the drum box was quite easy. I used plywood as material. For the frontside I used a thinner type of plywood like 3 mm thick. Then i cutted out the parts. I used a circle saw. For the hole I first drilled a small hole then I used a jigsaw to cut out the larger hole. When I had all the parts I used screws/nails and glue to put all the parts together except the front side. The front side i used smaller screws and no glue. The thing is that if you use screws it is useful for tension of the drum surface. Before I screw the frontside I fixed the snare drum wire inside it. It was the trickiest part. I had an idea that I stole from another building site I found. I had two thin iron boards that held the plastic tape of the snare wire. Then i had one screw in the middle of the two boards that I drilled a hole for to the outside of the drum*. When it was done I put the frontside in its place.*See picture This is the finished drum!Look at the pictures! =)

# Cajon Drum Building System

## Summary
This system represents the process of building a Cajon drum as described in a blog post. The Cajon is a percussion instrument that originates from South America and is often associated with flamenco and samba music. It is played by sitting on it and drumming on the front side. The blog post describes a personal experience of constructing a Cajon using plywood, a snare drum wire, and other tools and materials. The construction process involves measuring, cutting, assembling parts, and installing a snare wire for sound effects.

## Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of building a Cajon drum.

### PROCESS: Gather Information
- Look up various sources on how to build Cajons via Google.
- Find a construction design from Orcana Artesania and use it for measurements.

### INPUT: Materials and Tools
- Obtain plywood for the drum box (with a thinner 3 mm thick piece for the front side).
- Acquire a snare drum wire.
- Collect tools: circle saw, jigsaw, drill, screws/nails, and glue.
- Prepare two thin iron boards for securing the snare wire.

### PROCESS: Cutting Parts
- Cut out the parts of the box using the circle saw based on provided measurements.
- Drill a small hole for the sound hole and then use the jigsaw to cut out the larger hole.

### DECISION: Is the front side prepared?
- [IF YES] Proceed to assemble the drum.
- [ELSE] Cut the front side and make it ready.

### PROCESS: Assemble the Drum Box (Excluding the Front Side)
- Use screws/nails and glue to put all the parts together, except for the front side.

### PROCESS: Prepare Snare Wire
- Fix the snare drum wire inside the drum.
- Use two thin iron boards to hold the plastic tape of the snare wire.
- Drill a hole for a screw in the middle of the two boards to the outside of the drum.

### DECISION: Is the snare wire secured inside the drum?
- [IF YES] Proceed to attach the front side.
- [ELSE] Fix the snare wire appropriately.

### PROCESS: Attach the Front Side
- Use smaller screws to attach the front side without glue to allow for tension adjustment.

### OUTPUT: Finished Cajon Drum
- The Cajon drum is completed and ready for use.

### END:
- The process of building the Cajon drum is concluded.
```

instruct00637.title: How to Make a Hot Chilli Sauce, Similar to Carribean Hot Pepper Sauces
instruct00637.text: It's a cheap & easy way to make tasty hot pepper sauce! General guidelines are given, as I've only done this once & can make no claims to the receipe being perfected. This worked first time & it was easy, also very hot... I used: Habanero or Scotch Bonnet chillies (I don't know which, but please see photo) Garlic Vinegar Salt Sugar. You'll also need a food-blender, a sauce pan, graduated jug & a clean bottle. Cut chillies roughly (I used 7), I'd advise removing the seeds for a better flavour to heat ratio. These things will hurt you, take your own precautions...Peel & chop garlic roughly (I used 3 fat cloves)Measure the capacity of your bottle with the jug & water. Add chillies garlic to the jug & enough vinegar to make the volume you need, plus a little more. I made ~ 1/4 pint ~150 mlTransfer these to a pan, add ~ 5 teaspoons of salt, an a teaspoon of sugar, heat to boil & simmer (with a lid) for ~ 15 minBlend this mixture until smooth, reheat in the pan & pour into your bottle using the jug. (I'd keep this in the fridge, but the vinegar salt & sugar should help preserve) For a cooler sauce: Use fewer chillies & thicken with cornflour. Mix a little cornflour with cold water & stir into the simmering liquid a little at a time, remembering that it will be thicker when cooled. Get this wrong & you won't get it out of the bottle... Other ingredients could include: Tomato paste Mustard Pepper Various herbs & spices

# Hot Pepper Sauce Recipe System

## START:
- Begin the process of making hot pepper sauce.

## INPUT:
- Gather ingredients:
  - Habanero or Scotch Bonnet chillies (7 recommended)
  - Garlic (3 fat cloves recommended)
  - Vinegar
  - Salt (approximately 5 teaspoons)
  - Sugar (approximately 1 teaspoon)
- Gather equipment:
  - Food-blender
  - Saucepan
  - Graduated jug
  - Clean bottle

## PROCESS: Prepare Chillies
- Cut chillies roughly.

## DECISION: Remove Seeds?
  - IF Yes:
    - Remove seeds from chillies for a better flavour to heat ratio.
  - ELSE:
    - Proceed with seeds.

## PROCESS: Prepare Garlic
- Peel and chop garlic roughly.

## PROCESS: Measure Bottle Capacity
- Use the jug and water to measure the capacity of your bottle.

## PROCESS: Combine Ingredients in Jug
- Add chopped chillies and garlic to the jug.
- Pour in enough vinegar to make the volume needed for the bottle, plus a little more.

## PROCESS: Transfer to Pan
- Transfer the mixture from the jug to a saucepan.

## INPUT: Add Salt and Sugar
- Add approximately 5 teaspoons of salt.
- Add approximately 1 teaspoon of sugar.

## PROCESS: Cook Mixture
- Heat the mixture to boil.
- Simmer for approximately 15 minutes with a lid on.

## PROCESS: Blend Mixture
- Blend the mixture until smooth.

## PROCESS: Reheat Mixture
- Reheat the blended mixture in the saucepan.

## OUTPUT:
- Prepare to pour the hot pepper sauce into the bottle.

## PROCESS: Pour into Bottle
- Use the jug to pour the mixture into the bottle.

## STORAGE RECOMMENDATION:
- Store the bottle in the fridge.

## DECISION: Make Cooler Sauce?
  - IF Yes:
    - Use fewer chillies.
    - Thicken with cornflour mixed with cold water.
    - Stir in the cornflour solution a little at a time into the simmering liquid.
  - ELSE:
    - Proceed with the current hotness level.

## DECISION: Is Sauce Too Thick?
  - IF Yes:
    - Adjust cornflour amount to ensure the sauce can be poured from the bottle.
  - ELSE:
    - Continue to the next step.

## OPTIONAL INGREDIENTS:
- Consider adding other ingredients such as tomato paste, mustard, pepper, or various herbs and spices for different flavors.

## END:
- The process of making hot pepper sauce is complete.

instruct00758.title: Portable Water Heater for a Hot Tub or Pool
instruct00758.text: I recently purchased a portable hot tub - Intex PureSpa 6-Person Portable Inflatable Bubble Jet Ho t Tub. While looking at the specs and reviews I was concerned about the heating capacity of the unit. The 1,300 Watt heating unit only heats the water 1-2 degrees Fahrenheit an hour. Customer reviews also indicated they had a significant increase in their electrical bill. This information lead me to come up with a portable water heater solution. I am not a handyman by any means so suggestions and optimization ideas are very welcome. Please let me know what you think for my first Instructable. Here are the basic pieces that I used to make the portable hot water heater.Camplux 5L 1.32 GPM Outdoor Portable Propane Tankless Water HeaterFlojet 03526-144A Triplex Diaphragm Automatic W ater System Pump, 2.9 GPM 50 PSI, 12 volt DC4 - 1/2 to 1 1/4 " stainless steel hose clamps2 - 1/2" galvanized coupling2 - 1/2" Male NPT X 1/2" Hose Barb2 - 10' braided vinyl tubing 1/2" inner diameterKastar AC Adapter, Power Supply 12V 6A 72WTeflon TapeWrench and Screw Driver Apply Teflon tape to the threading and hand tighten the 1/2" coupling and 1/2" to hose barb to the water inlet and outlet on the water heater unit. Affix the hose to both of the hose barbs and tighten with the hose clamps. Using the hose barb connections supplied with the pump attach the hoses and tighten with hose clamps. Ensure you follow the directional arrow that indicates the flow of water through the pump so it draws water from the water source and into the water heater. Connect the supplied propane supply line to a 20 lb propane tank and check for leaks by using soapy water on connection points. If you see bubbles turn off the propane and tighten that connection point, do not overtighten. Once no leaks are detected mount it in a safe location. It must be mounted outside where adequate ventilation is provided. I had plenty of space under my deck where the heat could dissipate and not overheat the wood. Attach the power supply to the water pump. The outside of the barrel is negative (-) and the inside is positive (+). Do not plug the pump in until all water connections are attached and the suction end is submerged in the water. Check all connection points to ensure they are adequately tight and not leaking. Ensure propane is turned on. If not already installed place the 2 D cell batteries in the water heater. Ensure both ends of the hose are underwater. The suction hose must remain submerged at all times.When you are ready to connect the pump power supply and water will begin to flow. Once water flow is detected in the water heater it will auto start the flame. You can view this in the flame window on the front of the water heater unit.Relax in whatever you are heating and watch the temperature rise. Be careful, if you have the water flow turned low and the gas high it is capable of producing hot enough water to scold and burn. This should be supervised at all times by a qualified adult.Enjoy! :-) Thank you to everyone who built or provided suggestions for this project. Something that appears to be a reoccurring problem is the pump overheats. Quite a few commenters suggested using a hot water based pump. I am curious to replace that original pump with one designed for hot water. I am not sure if it will have the same water pressure as the original pump above. I am suggesting this pump as a replacement 3 GPM hot water pump

instruct00143.title: Homemade Cadbury Creme Eggs
instruct00143.text: Cadbury Eggs Decoded! Finally, you can make Cadbury-style Creme Eggs at home any time of year. And you want to know the biggest secret? The recipe is incredibly simple! The molding takes some time and patience, but if you're not concerned about looks, these babies are easy to crank out, and possibly more addictive than the real things. Tools:MixerScaleEgg-Shaped Candy MoldChocolate Melter (opt)Ingredients: 170g (1/2 cup) light corn syrup (or golden syrup if you're across the pond) 58g (1/4 cup) butter, room temperature 375g (3 cups) confectioner's powdered sugar (icing sugar) 1 teaspoon vanilla 1/4 teaspoon salt yellow food coloring 1 (12 ounce) bag milk chocolate chipsScoochmaroo provides product links as a participant in the Amazon Services LLC Associates Program, an affiliate advertising program designed to provide a means for sites to earn advertising fees by advertising and linking to amazon.com. You're going to be really astounded at how easy this is. Cream together the corn syrup, butter and vanilla. Sift in the confectioner's powdered sugar and beat until incorporated. Ok yeah, that was it. Now to get fancy and separate the filling into whites and yolks! Take out about a third of the filling and stir in some yellow food coloring. Now you're done! Put the two bowls in the fridge, as they're easier to work with once they're set up a little. This step is sticky! It helps to keep your hands clean and cold. Make little yolk balls out of the yellow mixture. Place them on some parchment (seriously, not foil like I did. It was a mess). Put them back in the fridge or even the freezer to firm up. These babies get soft fast! When the yolks are set up, you can start embedding them in the whites. Scoop an amount of white filling out and flatten it into a circle. Place the yolk ball inside, and wrap the white around it. Know what to do next? Stick it in the fridge. *****If you do decide to use the egg molds instead of the dipping method, a friend recently suggested simply piping the whites and yolks into the chocolate molds with a pastry bag. This would save a LOT of time. Melt the chocolate in a double boiler or in short bursts in the microwave. Fill the molds with the chocolate and swirl to coat the sides. Alternatively, use jorgegunn's method as detailed in Handmade Chocolate Boxes to fill the molds entirely, let the outsides set, and pour out the excess. Once the molds are set, plop a filling ball into half of each mold. Using more melted chocolate, join the two halves of the egg together. Let set and demold. The freezer does wonders for this step. If you aren't using molds, you can try this method. Melt the chocolate + 2 teaspoons of shortening in the microwave in short bursts until just melted. Either dip fillings into the chocolate with a fork and let set on parchment, or skewer the fillings and dip them that way (a'la cake pops). Once the chocolate is set, you can dip them again for an extra chocolatey shell! Not all of my attempts were successful, and I feel it's as important for me to share my failed attempts along side my successes. Here you can see that my shells weren't thick enough or sturdy enough or I didn't let them set up enough. There were a lot of delicious mistakes made this day. And in the end I discovered that the egg shape really isn't necessary to creating a really delicious candy. Chocolate is hard enough to work with. If you have the patience to attempt adding a mold into the process, go for it. The results will be something truly spectacular!

# Cadbury-style Creme Eggs Recipe System

## Ingredients and Tools
- START: Begin the recipe preparation process.
  - INPUT: 170g light corn syrup/golden syrup
  - INPUT: 58g butter, room temperature
  - INPUT: 375g confectioner's powdered sugar
  - INPUT: 1 teaspoon vanilla
  - INPUT: 1/4 teaspoon salt
  - INPUT: yellow food coloring
  - INPUT: 1 (12 ounce) bag milk chocolate chips
  - INPUT: Tools: Mixer, Scale, Egg-Shaped Candy Mold, Chocolate Melter (optional)

## Filling Preparation
- PROCESS: Cream together the corn syrup, butter, and vanilla using a mixer.
- PROCESS: Sift in the powdered sugar and beat until fully incorporated.
- OUTPUT: Basic cream filling.

## Creating Yolks
- PROCESS: Separate about one-third of the filling into a different bowl.
- PROCESS: Add yellow food coloring to the separated filling to create 'yolks'.
- STORE: Place both 'white' and 'yellow' fillings in the fridge to set up, making them easier to work with.

## Shaping Yolks and Whites
- PROCESS: Once set, form little yolk balls from the yellow mixture and place them on parchment paper.
- STORE: Put the yolk balls in the fridge or freezer to firm up.

## Encasing Yolks in Whites
- PROCESS: Flatten white filling into a circle, place a yolk ball inside, and wrap the white around it.
- STORE: Place the encased filling back in the fridge.

## Chocolate Molding Method (Optional)
- DECISION [IF]: Are you using egg molds?
  - YES: 
    - PROCESS: Melt chocolate in a double boiler or microwave.
    - PROCESS: Fill molds with chocolate, swirl to coat, and let set.
    - PROCESS: Place a filling ball into half of each mold.
    - PROCESS: Use melted chocolate to join two halves of the egg.
    - STORE: Let set in the freezer and then demold.
  - NO: 
    - END: Continue with the dipping method.

## Chocolate Dipping Method
- PROCESS: Melt chocolate with 2 teaspoons of shortening in the microwave until just melted.
- DECISION [IF]: Are you using a fork for dipping?
  - YES: 
    - PROCESS: Dip fillings into chocolate using a fork, let set on parchment.
  - NO: 
    - PROCESS: Skewer the fillings and dip them like cake pops.
- PROCESS: Once set, optionally dip again for an extra chocolatey shell.
- OUTPUT: Finished Cadbury-style Creme Eggs.

## Quality Control and Finalization
- PROCESS: Inspect eggs for shell thickness and sturdiness.
- DECISION [IF]: Are there any failed attempts?
  - YES: 
    - OUTPUT: Note the delicious mistakes and learn from them.
  - NO: 
    - OUTPUT: Successfully made Cadbury-style Creme Eggs.
- END: Enjoy your homemade Cadbury-style Creme Eggs at any time of year!
```

instruct00764.title: DIY Cookie Cutters
instruct00764.text: It's time to get creative and make your own cookie cutters! This is a fantastic way to create your own shape without having to cut templates over and over again. Personally - I've never cut a template, but I can imagine that it would be tedious. I'd rather make a cutter if I ever plan on using that shape ever again. I was working on one of these last night and I kinda cut my fingertip off. I urge you to use safety. (Basically, don't try to reshape your cutters with a serrated knife at full force, without gloves on.) You will need: Crop-a-dile. It's a crafting thing forscrap booking. Use a 40 or 50% off coupon! Scrap bookinggrommits, any color. I used 1/8". Sheet metal, aluminum, from Home Depot. Make sure it's not too thick to shape! Tin Snips. I got a set of 3 at Home Depot for $10. Super great/cheap. GLOVES. Yeah. You will get snips of metal stuck in your skin when cutting, if not carefully watching for splinters sticking out. First thing you need to do - is gear up and cut some strips. Try to keep them straight. If you're more professional than me = you may mark some lines and cut them. Try to keep them less than an inch in width, you don't need them to be so thick. Think about the cookie that you need, take into consideration - the size. Freehand it, or if you are more technical - you can think of a professional way to shape them. I've seen boards with nails in them, outline your shape with nails and bend the metal around them. Seems awesome, but a lot of work. When you bend the metal, watch out for splinters and wiggle them off. Also, since you are wearing gloves, you will be protected from any cut edges. I am making this rectangle on purpose, because I need it LOL. :) You will see it in another instructable! :) Now, the Cropadile isn't Hercules, so you have to go easy on it. My technique is to overlap the 1/2' flaps to secure, select my 1/8" PUNCH setting, try to punch through both pieces at the same time. (But they are too thick.) This will dent the two sections where you will need to do each individual punch. Move up to your secondgrommetplacing and FAKE PUNCH that also. Then push them apart, punch each of the 4 holes by themselves. Line your firstgrommetinto the hole, set your Cropadile to ... flatten thegrommet-mode. PUNCH/FLATTEN your grommet in place, which will fray the inside flat-like and secure your cutter shut. NOW...................Take your cutter and press it onto a surface and make sure you have a pretty flat-cutting edge for cutting the dough. THEN, pinch it to hold where it lays flat....CHECK your second punch.....is it a perfect hole? If not, RE-PUNCH it. It will be fine! :) Then set your second grommet and flatten it in place. The two grommets will be totally secure and you will be proud of your new cutter!Trouble-Shooting--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- If you have an overlap on your grommet edge, just clip it off to make it straight - using your snips. If you have splinters or sharp edges, remove them safely! - They wiggle off with some effort. If you use your cutter and it does't fully cut because it wasn't flat enough --- Make sure to flour your surface, roll your dough, then do a wiggle once you've cut and pressed your cutter. That will separate the shape from the dough. Since your surface has enough flour, it will not stick. And if your sugar cookie dough is cold enough, the shape will hold. :)

# Custom Cookie Cutter Creation System

## Process Flow

### START:
- Begin the custom cookie cutter creation process.

### INPUT:
- Gather necessary materials:
  - Crop-a-dile (crafting tool)
  - Scrapbooking grommets (1/8" size)
  - Sheet metal, aluminum (appropriate thickness for shaping)
  - Tin Snips
  - Safety gloves

### PROCESS: Gear Up
- Put on safety gloves to protect hands from metal splinters and sharp edges.

### PROCESS: Cut Metal Strips
- Cut strips from the sheet metal using tin snips.
  - Keep strips straight and less than an inch in width.

### DECISION: Is the shape complex and requires a template?
  - [IF YES]: Use a method such as a board with nails to outline and shape the metal.
  - [ELSE]: Freehand the shape or use a simpler method to bend the metal.

### PROCESS: Shape Metal
- Bend the metal into the desired shape, taking care to remove any metal splinters.

### PROCESS: Overlap Metal Ends
- Overlap the ends of the shaped metal by about 1/2 inch to prepare for securing.

### PROCESS: Prepare for Grommet Attachment
- Use the Crop-a-dile on the 1/8" PUNCH setting to dent the overlapped metal ends.
  - Attempt to punch through both layers to mark where individual punches will be made.

### PROCESS: Separate and Punch Holes
- Separate the dented metal ends and punch holes individually where dents were made.

### PROCESS: Attach First Grommet
- Insert a grommet into the first hole.
- Set the Crop-a-dile to flatten mode and secure the first grommet, closing the cutter.

### OUTPUT: Partially Completed Cutter
- Achieve a cutter shape with one secured end.

### PROCESS: Check Cutting Edge
- Press the cutter onto a surface to ensure a flat cutting edge.

### PROCESS: Pinch and Check Second Hole
- Pinch the cutter to maintain its flatness and check the second hole alignment.

### DECISION: Is the second hole perfectly aligned?
  - [IF YES]: Proceed to attach the second grommet.
  - [ELSE]: Re-punch the second hole to correct alignment.

### PROCESS: Attach Second Grommet
- Insert the second grommet into the hole and flatten it in place with the Crop-a-dile.

### OUTPUT: Completed Cookie Cutter
- Finalize the cookie cutter with two secure grommets.

### TROUBLESHOOTING SUBROUTINE:
- IF there is an overlap on the grommet edge, clip it off with snips.
- IF there are splinters or sharp edges, remove them safely.
- IF the cutter does not cut fully due to uneven edges:
  - Flour the surface before cutting.
  - Roll the dough evenly.
  - Wiggle the cutter after pressing to separate the shape from the dough.

### END:
- The custom cookie cutter is ready to use.
```

instruct00212.title: Homemade Strawberry Rhubarb Pie
instruct00212.text: This is a from scratch strawberry rhubarb Pie, crust and all. It is very good and fairly easy to make. Please vote for me in the pie and book contests! Thank you! To make the pie crust from scratch you will need... 2 1/2 c. all purpose flour 1/2 tsp. Salt 1 c. Butter, chilled and cut into small pieces 1/2 c. Ice Water Make sure that every thing you use is as cold as possible. (flour and Salt excluded) I mixed mine in a stand mixer with a paddle attachment,and I put the bowl and paddle in the freezer about 2 hours before I started. The crust can be done by hand with a pastry blender or a fork and some patience. Combine flour and salt in bowl and mix, then add cut up butter piece by piece slowly increasing speed of mixer to 6 or medium high. (you are trying to get the flour to stick to the dough more than mix completely) When you reach an oatmeal consistency very slowly (about a tablespoon at a time) add in ice water. dough will form a ball. Wrap tightly in saran wrap and refridgerate for 4 hours or more. So through the magic of the internet it has been 3 and 1/2 hours. For the filling you will need... 1 1/2 c. Sugar 3 Tbsp. Corn Starch 1/4 tsp Salt 1/4 tsp. Ground nutmeg 3 c. Rhubarb (about 1 and 1/2 Lbs.) (cut into small cubes) 2 c. of Strawberry's (cut into small cubes) 1 Tbsp. Butter (cut into cubes) I suggest washing the strawberry's and rhubarb first :) and make sure you only cut up the red stem of the rhubarb not any of the leaf as they are poisonous. Mix sugar, corn Starch, salt and nutmeg in a bowl. add cut up strawberry's and rhubarb to bowl and toss gently until coated, let sit about 15 min. (it will take on a syrupy look) So now you take the pie dough out of the refrigerator and cut in half. I suggest rolling it out between 2 pieces of wax or parchment paper. I was out so I used saran wrap (kind of a pain) :) Make a ball out of the first half of dough and set between 2 pieces of wax paper, press down a bit with your hand, Using a rolling pin roll out into a 9" circle Place dough in pie pan and press softly to get it to stay in place. Now you can add the strawberry rhubarb filling,and top with cut up pieces of butter. So with the second half of the dough roll out the same way as you did for the crust, (in a ball between 2 sheets of wax paper.) Roll out until it is about 1/4 inch thick. Cut strips about 1/4 - 1/2 inch wide all the way across. ( I suggest using a pizza cutter.) Please bear with me as I am not sure the best way to explain the lattice process. Lay one strip vertically and one diagonally on the pie with their tops overlapping. Then alternate strip direction going over 1 piece and under the next and so on and so forth until complete. (basket weave) Press edges all the way around the pie to seal and cut off access. Bake pie on middle rack at 350 degrees for 1 hour (oven temperatures might vary) When the pie is done baking, let it cool and enjoy!

instruct00586.title: Roy Rogers and Shirley Temple
instruct00586.text: Oh no! You're having a fiesta today, and you don't know what to serve! Never fear, Roy Rogers and Shirley Temple are here! This Instructable will teach you how to make the drink often served in Mexican restaraunts. Roy Rogers is similer to a cherry Coke, and a Shirly Temple is made with Sprite. Here's what you need:Coke and Sprite (I used Fresca, same thing)Cherry SyrupMaraschino cherries1 Tea spoon2 glasses First thing's first, add ice to your glass. Do this with an ice dispenser, or any creative way you can think of. Set the glass up onto a shelf and play ice basketball. Was that so hard? Now, open the coke (https://www.instructables.com/id/How-to-open-a-sprite/ ). Pour the coke into the glass. Don't miss. Now we turn our boring Coke into a Roy Rogers. Pour your cherry syrup into a Teaspoon. Remember, this stuff is strong. A little goes a long way. You can add as much as you like, though. Pour the whole bottle in if you'd like! (yuck). Add this Teaspoon of sweet cherry goodness to your Coke. To finish, add in two or three Maraschino cherries. Go through the same steps as a Roy Rogers, only this time with Sprite (or anything similer). On one of my trips to Canada for a cousin's wedding, I walk up to the bartender and ask for a Roy Rogers. What he gives me is an orange drink, with an orange slice garnish. Mildly confused, I say thanks and take a sip. Here's what I think it was: Orange Juice with Canada Dry ginger ale. Is this correct?

instruct00723.title: Cheddar Bay Biscuit Recipe
instruct00723.text: Don't trust most of the copycat recipes you see out there - there is a trick to making moist and fluffyCheddar Bay biscuits at home, and most recipes miss the mark. This recipe makes even moister and tastier Cheddar Bay biscuits than those you get at Red Lobster, and they're surprisingly easy to make! What's the secret? I'll tell you! For this recipe, I start with Bisquik baking mix (it's a time saver, ok?). But making biscuits straight from a mix usually means you don't end up with a light or flakey product. This is because most of the fat comes from the dried shortening in the mix. By adding cold butter to the party, we impart a light, airy texture, and a richer flavor. Combine that with a nice grated Cheddar, garlic powder, and parsley, and you've got some better-than-perfect Cheddar Bay biscuits!Ingredients to make 12: 2 cups Bisquick baking mix cup cold whole milk or buttermilk 4 tablespoons cold butter (1/2 stick) teaspoon garlic powder 1 heaping cup grated Cheddar cheeseBrush on Top: 2 tablespoons butter, melted teaspoon dried parsley flakes teaspoon garlic powder pinch saltDirections: 1. Preheat your oven to 400 degrees. 2. Combine Bisquick with cold butter in a medium bowl using a knife and fork or your hands until small chunks of butter the size of peas remain. Add grated Cheddar cheese, milk, and teaspoon garlic. Mix by hand until combined, but don't over mix. 3. Drop approximately 1/4 cup sized mounds of dough onto an ungreased cookie sheet using two large spoons. 4. Bake for 15 to 17 minutes or until the tops of the biscuits begin to turn light brown. 5. When you take the biscuits out of the oven, melt 2 tablespoons butter is a small bowl in your microwave. Stir in salt, garlic powder, and the dried parsley flakes. Use a brush to spread this garlic butter over the tops of all the biscuits. Use up all of the butter for optimal deliciousness! Makes one dozen biscuits.Recipe inspired byTodd Wilbur, "Top Secret Restaurant Recipes 2,"Plume Books.

# Cheddar Bay Biscuits Systematic Recipe

## Ingredients Preparation
START:
- INPUT: Gather ingredients for biscuits and topping.

PROCESS: Measure 2 cups Bisquick baking mix.
PROCESS: Measure ¾ cup cold whole milk or buttermilk.
PROCESS: Measure 4 tablespoons cold butter (1/2 stick).
PROCESS: Measure ¾ teaspoon garlic powder (divided for biscuits and topping).
PROCESS: Measure 1 heaping cup grated Cheddar cheese.
PROCESS: Measure additional ingredients for topping:
  - INPUT: 2 tablespoons butter, melted.
  - INPUT: ¾ teaspoon dried parsley flakes.
  - INPUT: A pinch of salt.

## Biscuit Dough Preparation
PROCESS: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
PROCESS: Combine Bisquick with cold butter in a medium bowl using a knife and fork or hands until butter is pea-sized.
PROCESS: Add grated Cheddar cheese to the mixture.
PROCESS: Add milk to the mixture.
DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture combined without overmixing?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: OUTPUT: Overmixed dough results in less fluffy biscuits. Restart mixing process with caution.
  
## Baking the Biscuits
PROCESS: Drop ¼ cup sized mounds of dough onto an ungreased cookie sheet using two large spoons.
PROCESS: Bake for 15 to 17 minutes or until the tops of the biscuits begin to turn light brown.
DECISION [IF]: Are the biscuits light brown on top?
  - Yes: OUTPUT: Biscuits are ready for topping.
  - No: PROCESS: Continue baking and check every minute until light brown.

## Topping Preparation
PROCESS: Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a small bowl in the microwave.
PROCESS: Stir in a pinch of salt, ½ teaspoon garlic powder, and dried parsley flakes into the melted butter.

## Finalizing the Biscuits
PROCESS: Brush the garlic butter mixture over the tops of all the biscuits using a brush.
DECISION [IF]: Is all the butter mixture used?
  - Yes: OUTPUT: Biscuits are topped and ready to serve.
  - No: PROCESS: Continue brushing until all the butter mixture is used.

END: Biscuits are now ready to be served.
```

instruct00801.title: Apple Cider Cinnamon Rolls
instruct00801.text: Hey Everyone!! I must be in an apple phase cause every recipe with apples is appealing to me lately. I had to make these though. I love hot apple cider when the weather starts to get cold so this takes like my two favorite things and puts them together. I've never made cinnamon rolls before, but they were seriously so easy, and so delicious. The perfect balance of both cinnamon and apple cider flavoring, and the frosting, ugh!! I could eat that stuff by the spoonful. If you try any recipe from my blog, make this the one! You won't be disappointed. Quick tip: When you are ready to cut your roll of dough into individual cinnamon rolls, don't use a knife!! This is so important to keeping your cinnamon rolls from being flattened or lopsided. Instead use a piece of twine or a thin piece of wire {I find that wire works best, but twine will work too}. Place under the roll where you want to cut, loop the wire or twine over the top, crossing each other and pull. You will be amazed how much easier this makes making cinnamon rolls and everyone will turn out beautifully even. Enjoy :) Apple Cider Cinnamon Rolls 3 1/4 cups all-purpose flour 1/4 cup sugar 1 package (1/4 ounce) quick-rise yeast 1/2 teaspoon salt 3/4 cup 2% milk 1/4 cup apple cider or juice 1/4 cup plus 1/3 cup butter, softened, divided 1 egg 2 cups finely chopped peeled tart apples 1 1/4 cups packed brown sugar 3/4 cup finely chopped walnuts 3 teaspoons ground cinnamon Apple Cider Cream Cheese Frosting 2 cups apple cider or juice 1 cinnamon stick (3 inches) 1 package (8 ounces) cream cheese, softened 1/4 cup butter, softened 1 cup confectioners' sugar In a large bowl, combine 2 1/4 cups flour, sugar, yeast and salt. In a small saucepan, heat the milk, cider and 1/4 cup butter to 120 - 130 degrees. Add to dry ingredients; beat just until moistened. Add egg; beat until smooth. Stir in enough remaining flour to form a soft dough (dough will be sticky). Turn onto a floured surface; knead until smooth and elastic, about 6-8 minutes. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes. Roll into a 15-in. x 10-in. rectangle. Spread remaining butter to within 1/2 in. of edges. Combine the apples, brown sugar, walnuts and cinnamon; sprinkle over butter. Roll up jelly-roll style, starting with a long side; pinch seam to seal. Cut into 12 slices. Place cut side down in a greased 13-in. x 9-in. baking dish. Cover and let rise in a warm place for 30 minutes. Bake at 325 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until golden brown. For frosting, place cider and cinnamon stick in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil; cook until liquid is reduced to 1/4 cup, about 20 minutes. Discard cinnamon stick; cool cider. In a large bowl, beat cream cheese and butter until fluffy. Add confectioners' sugar and reduced cider; beat until smooth. Spread over warm rolls. Recipe from Taste Of Home Fall Baking foodsnots.com

# Apple Cider Cinnamon Rolls System

## Ingredients:
- All-purpose flour (3 1/4 cups)
- Sugar (1/4 cup)
- Quick-rise yeast (1 package or 1/4 ounce)
- Salt (1/2 teaspoon)
- 2% Milk (3/4 cup)
- Apple cider or juice (1/4 cup for dough, 2 cups for frosting)
- Butter (1/4 cup + 1/3 cup, softened, divided)
- Egg (1 piece)
- Tart apples (2 cups, finely chopped and peeled)
- Brown sugar (1 1/4 cups, packed)
- Walnuts (3/4 cup, finely chopped)
- Ground cinnamon (3 teaspoons)
- Cream cheese (1 package or 8 ounces, softened)
- Confectioners' sugar (1 cup)
- Cinnamon stick (1 piece, 3 inches)

## Process:

### Dough Preparation
START:
- INPUT: In a large bowl, combine 2 1/4 cups flour, 1/4 cup sugar, yeast, and salt.

PROCESS: Heat the mixture
- In a small saucepan, heat 3/4 cup milk, 1/4 cup apple cider, and 1/4 cup butter to 120 - 130 degrees.

PROCESS: Combine wet and dry ingredients
- Add heated mixture to dry ingredients in the bowl.
- Beat just until moistened.

PROCESS: Add egg
- INPUT: Add 1 egg to the bowl.
- Beat until smooth.

PROCESS: Add remaining flour
- INPUT: Stir in enough remaining flour to form a soft dough (the dough will be sticky).

PROCESS: Knead the dough
- Turn dough onto a floured surface.
- Knead until smooth and elastic, approximately 6-8 minutes.

PROCESS: Rest the dough
- Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.

### Roll and Fill Dough
PROCESS: Roll dough
- Roll dough into a 15-in. x 10-in. rectangle.

PROCESS: Spread butter
- INPUT: Spread remaining 1/3 cup butter to within 1/2 in. of edges.

PROCESS: Prepare filling
- INPUT: Combine chopped apples, brown sugar, walnuts, and ground cinnamon.
- Sprinkle this mixture over the buttered dough.

PROCESS: Roll up dough
- Roll up jelly-roll style, starting with a long side.
- Pinch seam to seal.

### Cutting and Baking
PROCESS: Cut into slices
- Cut rolled dough into 12 slices using twine or thin wire.

PROCESS: Prepare for baking
- Place slices cut side down in a greased 13-in. x 9-in. baking dish.

PROCESS: Let dough rise
- Cover and let rise in a warm place for 30 minutes.

PROCESS: Bake
- Bake at 325 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until golden brown.
- OUTPUT: Baked cinnamon rolls.

### Frosting Preparation
PROCESS: Reduce cider
- In a small saucepan, place 2 cups cider and cinnamon stick.
- Bring to a boil and cook until liquid is reduced to 1/4 cup, about 20 minutes.
- Discard cinnamon stick and cool the reduced cider.

PROCESS: Make frosting
- In a large bowl, beat softened cream cheese and 1/4 cup butter until fluffy.
- Add confectioners' sugar and reduced cider.
- Beat until smooth.

### Finalizing
PROCESS: Frost rolls
- Spread frosting over warm rolls.
- OUTPUT: Apple Cider Cinnamon Rolls with Cream Cheese Frosting.

END
```

To make them from the beginning to the end you need to have basic to intermediate needle or shuttle tatting skills. But if you have no desire to learn tatting you can make these panties yourself, just stick around. If you need to learn needle tatting here's a tutorial http://www.youtube.com/user/agasunset These panties and many more of my tatted creations can be found in my Etsy shop You will need -ball of thread in desired color size 10 -tatting needle size 5 (or shuttle) -satin ribbon: 2x 36", 1x 6" (or customlengthfor your size) -scissors -flame (candle, match etc) For this step you will need to tat a flower with this pattern: R:6ds, p, 6ds, cl, rw C:6ds, p, 6ds, rw R:6ds, join to pr. p, 6 ds, cl, rw C:6ds, p, 6ds, rw repeat last 2 rows 4 more times, join C to thebeginning, hide endings To see a movie with the entireinstruction of this flower please go to http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LAbuBNzTa2M Once you finished first flower,make another one, but remember to join first to one chain picot and then to the next chain picot. Refer to the picture. Repeat joining flowers. Remember to join to picot that isalreadysharing the chain (pic). You will join 21 flowers in front part in form of 6x6x6 triangle. After finishing the large triangle make one more with only 3 flowers for flirty back. Over any kind of flame meltribbonendings to prevent fringing. BE CAREFUL!! Join front and back lace buy sawing the 6" ribbon by hand. Thread thorough the top loops long ribbon. Repeat this step for the back. Tie the sides to your size and voila, panties ready! If you have no desire to learn tatting you can still have these panties made partialy by yourself. I have in my shop complete kit of 24 flowers and cut to size ribbons with instruction. You can buy it in 3 colors: red, black and white. There is many ways to assemble them, it all depends on your imagination. You can hand saw them together, join with jump rings or tie wit tiny ribbons. Here's an example of jump rings. Enjoy.

# Structured Summary of Tatted Panties Creation

## System Inputs:
- Ball of thread in the desired color, size 10
- Tatting needle size 5 or shuttle
- Satin ribbon: 2x 36", 1x 6" (or custom length for your size)
- Scissors
- Flame (candle, match, etc.)

## System Outputs:
- Completed tatted panties

## Process Steps:

START: Begin the process of making tatted panties.

INPUT: Gather materials (thread, needle/shuttle, ribbon, scissors, flame).

PROCESS: Learn basic to intermediate needle or shuttle tatting skills if not already known.

DECISION [IF]: Do you desire to learn tatting?
  - Yes: Proceed to PROCESS step of learning needle tatting.
  - No: Skip to PROCESS step of obtaining a complete kit.

PROCESS: If learning is required, watch needle tatting tutorial on YouTube.

STORE/DATABASE SUBROUTINE: Access tatting pattern for panties.

PROCESS: Tat a flower using the provided pattern:
  - Ring (R): 6 double stitches (ds), picot (p), 6ds, close (cl), reverse work (rw)
  - Chain (C): 6ds, p, 6ds, rw
  - Repeat last 2 rows 4 more times, join C to the beginning, hide endings.

PROCESS: Watch the instruction video for the flower on YouTube if necessary.

PROCESS: Tat a second flower, joining it to the first flower at one chain picot, then the next chain picot.

PROCESS: Continue joining flowers to form a front piece in a 6x6x6 triangle pattern, consisting of 21 flowers.

PROCESS: Tat a smaller triangle with 3 flowers for the flirty back piece.

PROCESS: Use a flame to melt ribbon endings to prevent fraying. Be cautious with the flame.

PROCESS: Join front and back lace pieces by sewing the 6" ribbon by hand.

PROCESS: Thread the long ribbon through the top loops of the front and back pieces.

PROCESS: Tie the sides with ribbon to fit your size, completing the panties.

DECISION [IF]: Do you want to make the panties yourself without learning tatting?
  - Yes: Proceed to INPUT of obtaining a complete kit.
  - No: End the process as the panties are now ready.

INPUT: Purchase a complete kit from the Etsy shop if not tatting yourself.

PROCESS: Assemble the panties using the kit by hand sewing, joining with jump rings, or tying with tiny ribbons.

OUTPUT: Tatted panties are ready to wear.

END: The process of creating tatted panties is complete.
```

instruct00020.title: How to Build a Pallet Mailbox
instruct00020.text: Items needed: (2) 2x6 pieces of wood at 22 in. long for base. (2) 2x6 pieces of wood at 15 in. long for front and back wall. (6) 1x4 pieces of wood at 22 in. long for wall sides. (4) 1x6 pieces of wood at 26 in. long for roof. (1) 4x4 price of wood at 5-6 feet for post. (1) 4x4 piece of wood at 23 in. for angle post. (2) 2x4 pieces of wood at 32 in. for mailbox to sit on. stain and/or paint satin spar urethane for outdoors. wood screws hinge and knob to open door power drill drill bits jigsaw level clamps shovel I got the pallets and wood from a post on craigslist, so this total project cost me less the $10. I had to pay for the address numbers, screws, hinge and knob. layout wood for cutting to desired lengths. Glue and clamp base, front and back of mail box which are your 2x6's and allow glue to set before removing clamps, read glue directions for proper dry time before you start sanding and staining. Once glue is dry and ready, start sanding with 80 or 100 grit and stain whatever look you want. Before you sand and stain front, cut out door. Cut door with jigsaw, then sand and stain. I used my old mailbox door as a outline. Glue and screw, I used 4 screws for the back and 2 for the front. Add wood to the sides. Once I finished I noticed that I forgot at make a angle cut for the roof to line up, so I removed the top, side wood piece , made the cut and then screwed it back on. Sand and stain wood for roof. Use the (4) 1x6 pieces for the roof. I decided to change the roof color so I did it at the end. I also wanted to paint the 2x4's so I did that as well. I dug a hole 2 feet deep because I did not want to use concrete. I used a level to make the post straight. I compacted the dirt down so that the post would not move when I added on the mailbox.

# Custom Mailbox Construction System

## System Inputs:
- Wood pieces:
  - (2) 2x6 at 22 in. for base
  - (2) 2x6 at 15 in. for front/back walls
  - (6) 1x4 at 22 in. for wall sides
  - (4) 1x6 at 26 in. for roof
  - (1) 4x4 at 5-6 ft for main post
  - (1) 4x4 at 23 in. for angle post
  - (2) 2x4 at 32 in. for mailbox support
- Stain and/or paint
- Satin spar urethane for outdoors
- Wood screws
- Hinge and knob
- Tools:
  - Power drill
  - Drill bits
  - Jigsaw
  - Level
  - Clamps
  - Shovel
- Address numbers

## System Outputs:
- A finished custom mailbox with a base, front/back walls, side walls, a roof, and a post set in the ground without concrete.

## Process Steps:

### START:
- Begin the mailbox construction process.

### PROCESS: Layout and Cutting of Wood
- INPUT: Wood pieces as per the required dimensions.
- PROCESS: Use a saw to cut the wood pieces to the specified lengths.

### PROCESS: Assembly of Base, Front, and Back Walls
- INPUT: (2) 2x6 pieces for base, (2) 2x6 pieces for front/back walls.
- PROCESS: Apply glue to the 2x6 pieces.
- DECISION [IF]: Is glue applied to all necessary surfaces?
  - Yes: Proceed to clamping.
  - No: Apply glue to missed surfaces.
- PROCESS: Clamp the glued pieces together.
- STORE: Allow the glue to set as per glue instructions.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the glue dry?
  - Yes: Move to sanding and staining.
  - No: Wait until glue is dry.

### PROCESS: Sanding and Staining
- INPUT: Dried glued wood pieces.
- PROCESS: Sand the wood with either 80 or 100 grit sandpaper.
- PROCESS: Stain the wood with the desired color.
- OUTPUT: Sanded and stained base, front, and back walls.

### PROCESS: Cutting Out the Door
- INPUT: Front wall piece.
- PROCESS: Use a jigsaw to cut out the door.
- PROCESS: Sand and stain the door.
- OUTPUT: Front wall with a door.

### PROCESS: Attaching Front and Back Walls
- INPUT: Sanded and stained front and back walls.
- PROCESS: Attach the walls using screws; 4 for the back, 2 for the front.

### PROCESS: Side Wall Attachment
- INPUT: (6) 1x4 pieces for side walls.
- PROCESS: Attach the side walls to the base, front, and back walls.

### DECISION [IF]: Is an angle cut needed for the roof?
  - Yes: Remove top side piece, make the angle cut, then reattach.
  - No: Continue without modification.

### PROCESS: Roof Preparation
- INPUT: (4) 1x6 pieces for roof.
- PROCESS: Sand and stain the roof pieces.
- OUTPUT: Prepared roof pieces.

### DECISION [IF]: Change in roof color desired?
  - Yes: Paint the roof pieces with the new color.
  - No: Keep the stained color.

### PROCESS: Post Installation
- INPUT: (1) 4x4 main post, (1) 4x4 angle post, (2) 2x4 supports.
- PROCESS: Dig a hole 2 feet deep for the main post.
- PROCESS: Place the main post into the hole.
- PROCESS: Use a level to ensure the post is straight.
- PROCESS: Compact the dirt around the post for stability.

### PROCESS: Mailbox Attachment to Post
- INPUT: Assembled mailbox, painted 2x4 supports, secured 4x4 post.
- PROCESS: Attach the mailbox onto the 2x4 supports.
- PROCESS: Secure the mailbox and supports to the main post.

### OUTPUT:
- A fully constructed and installed custom mailbox.

### END:
- The mailbox construction process is complete.

instruct00865.title: Make Any Sweater an Ugly Christmas Sweater
instruct00865.text: If you've ever tried to find an ugly Christmas sweater at the last minute for the increasingly popular "Ugly Christmas Sweater" party then you might have heard the thrift store employees tell you that they are all sold out. Idid. And of course, i knew i had the skills to make an ugly sweater - maybe not from scratch though. So if you have basic sewing skills and a few hours of time you can make any sweater fit the occasion. You'll need some of this stuff:A sweater (aim for at least having some traditional Christmas colors or patterns)A plush toy (obviously a reindeer would be good but other animals might work too)ThreadNeedleScissorsBellsBattery operated LED light stringOther kitschy decorations I have to credit this reindeer frozen in carbonite (case-modded to look like a stocking) for the inspiration. Cut off limbs and the head of the stuffed animal. Most Beanie Baby type plush toys have fiber in the heads and even in some limbs so your sweater will still be lightweight. Experiment a little with the positioning of the body parts. I found that they worked best on the stomach of the sweater. Sew the head and limbs into position! Once you have an Alien-like stuffed animal protuberance from your sweater you need to add something to catch the ear. Isewed bells around the waist hem and the sleeves of the shirt. Stitch a cheap kitschy wreath on the sweater, throw a bow in your hair, maybe some ornament earrings... I couldn't find a battery powered LED string to add lights to the reindeer's nose or to make the rest of the sweater twinkle but I know they are available.

## START:
- Begin the process to create an ugly Christmas sweater.

## INPUT:
- Gather the following materials:

## PROCESS: Sew the plush parts onto the sweater
- Use the needle and thread to sew the head and limbs into the chosen positions on the sweater.

## PROCESS: Add auditory elements
- Sew bells around the waist hem and the sleeves of the sweater to catch the ear.

## DECISION [IF]: Do you have a kitschy wreath?
  - Yes: Proceed to sew the wreath onto the sweater.
  - No: Skip the wreath and consider other decorations.

## DECISION [IF]: Do you have a battery operated LED light string?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step to add lights.
  - No: Skip the lighting step and move on to final touches.

## PROCESS: Add lights to the sweater (if available)
- Stitch the LED light string to the reindeer's nose or across the sweater to make it twinkle.

## PROCESS: Final touches
- Add any additional decorations to enhance the ugliness of the sweater, such as a bow in your hair or ornament earrings.

## OUTPUT:
- The final product is a unique, handmade ugly Christmas sweater ready for the party.

## END:
- The process of creating an ugly Christmas sweater is complete.

instruct00329.title: Edible Glass in 30 Seconds
instruct00329.text: This fun and easy technique will only take you about 30 seconds to melt the isomalt sticks. Pour it into any mold and you will have beautiful , edible glasslike pieces to top on cupcakes, cakes , or even make your own sculpure. You can use the melted glass to "glue" the pieces together. You can even buy the silicone and cut it to shape letters for wedding cake toppers and more. Important info and tips: *Warning: If the hot liquid touches tour skin it will stick and burn *Wear specialty gloves *Wear long sleave shirt *Do not do this in a hurry take your time and be safe *Do not do around small children or dogs *Any unused product cand be remelted *I like to pour unused melted product into the jewels mold, it is a perfect size to store to reuse later *Glass will get cloudy if exposed to humidty *Store in a airtight container(also cake play sells special silica gel packet to keep the looking great) *If you finished pieces are a little cloudy, just lightly skim the piece with a creme brulee torch and it will be shiny and beautiful * At cakeplay.com they have very helpful videos * Isomalt sticks (You can find them at your local cake supply store or at cakeplay.com) You can buy the colors you want or just buy clear or white and dye it yourself as needed for the particular project that you are working on. * 2 pack gloves from cakeplay (very important to protect your skin from burns) * Microwave safe dish (preferably with a handle) * Any silicone mold - ice cube tray, cupcake or cake shaped pan or you can make your own. (make your own molds.com) * Specialty plastic molds like the on shown for edible gems * Toothpicks *Silicone mat to protect your work surface * Food gel color (optional) * Luster dust (optional) Safety first, put on your cotton gloves then the latex free gloves.Take your isomalt stick and break it up into your silicone container. Microwave it for about 30 -60seconds.(mine just takes 30 sec.) The stick should be completely melted and very bubbly.If you have the clear or white sticks and desire to color them, do so now. Use food gel color. Use a toothpick to mix well.You only need a tiny bit,especially if you want it to be nice and clear. Now just carefully pour into your desired molds. Do not overfill. You can use a toothpick right away to help the isomalt into any corners of the mold if you need to.Now just let cool completely in the mold. # Isomalt Melting and Molding Process

## START:
- Begin the process to create edible glasslike pieces using isomalt sticks.

## PROCESS: Safety Preparations
- INPUT: Cotton gloves, latex-free gloves.
- OUTPUT: Wearer is protected.

- Isomalt sticks.

- Silicone or plastic molds.

- Food gel color (optional).

- Break isomalt sticks into the silicone container.

- INPUT: Silicone container with broken isomalt sticks.

## PROCESS: Cooling Isomalt
- OUTPUT: Solidified isomalt pieces.

## PROCESS: Unmolding Isomalt
- OUTPUT: Edible glasslike pieces.

- OUTPUT: Decorated isomalt pieces.

## PROCESS: Storing Isomalt Pieces
- STORE in an airtight container, optionally with silica gel packets to prevent cloudiness.

## OUTPUT: Final Presentation
- Place finished isomalt pieces onto cupcakes or other desserts.

## END:
- The process of creating edible glasslike pieces from isomalt sticks is complete.

instruct00587.title: Binder Clip Phone Car Mount
instruct00587.text: Yo, this instructable features one of the most undeniably, infinitely useful office objects ever made: The Binder Clip. You can find them almost anywhere, and their uses, both intended and repurposed, are limitless. In this little 'ible, I'll show you how I made a phone mount for pretty darn cheap (college and having money don't usually go together). Read on! Materials: 1 Large binder clip 1-2 Rubber bands or hair ties 2 lengths 6 inches long of Paracord, color your choice Notes on materials: Binder Clip - size it to your phone, the handles should have to open a bit to fit the phone in Rubber bands / hair ties - I used black hair ties (...no, not a girl, just have a sister) because i thought it looked more pro Alright, grab your materials and lets start. In this step, we prepare the fingers that will hold the phone. I am referring, of course, to the silvery parts of the binder clip. Even though this is one of the more crucial steps, it is very easy. Just take the two metal 'handles' off of the binder clip. Put them in a vice and clamp the rounded end up to where it bends. Tap with a mallet of hammer until you have about 20 degrees of bend in the part. Repeat for both fingers. Voila! Next we prepare the protective sheath for the fingers. Nobody wants a scratched up phone! For each of the lengths of paracord do this: - Gut it: remove the inner strands of the paracord to make room for fingers - Fuse or Seal it: Stop the fraying of the sheath by fusing the edge, you don't want to shut it of, just melt the edges. another option is fray check, but I thought it was easiest to insert the hot end of a soldering iron into the end for a quick second, then going around the edges and melting them - Fish the finger through the sheath like pictured: try and get the sides even, at least for aesthetic's sake ;) - Reattach fingers to binder clip That's fancy speak for put rubber bands on it. You may find that you have to take up some slack; in that case, simply put another loop over the finger, or find a smaller rubber band. When properly tensioned, the device should have a light tension with fingers resting on the sides of the binder clip, and should hold your phone snugly. One of the beauties of this mount is its easily reconfigured nature. If its not holding onto your phone, make the tension a little snugger. If you don't like where it is, find a different place. If you don't like people breaking into your car because they see a mount, take the mount down when you leave the car. If you don't like people breaking into your car because they see the ring that a typical GPS suction mount leaves, well...you don't have to worry about that with this mount! Hurray. Placement: The phone goes between the metal fingers, you can rotate your clip for landscape or portrait orientation. FYI: Mine is certainly battle-tested, as I have been on multiple GPS intensive trips (like 20 house calls in a different city...that was fun). I attach mine to the console air vent; no over-heating issues on my phone ;) PS: Also, my girlfriend thought it was funny that I started with yo...so she made a rap: Yo this is my instructable, its so cool and doable, make a neat phone clip, your street cred surely wont dip, youll need paper clip and vice, if you miss you might need ice, dont forget the paracord and hair ties, scratching your phone wouldnt be wise

### START:

  - Reattach the sheathed handles to the binder clip.

- Two metal handles covered with Paracord to prevent phone scratches.

- Wrap rubber bands or hair ties around the binder clip and metal handles to create tension.
- Adjust the tension so that the device holds the phone snugly without over-tightening.

- IF Yes: Proceed to the placement step.
- IF No: Adjust the tension or rubber bands until the mount holds the phone securely.

### PROCESS: Placement of the Phone
- Place the phone between the metal fingers of the clip.
- Rotate the clip for landscape or portrait orientation based on preference.
- Attach the mount to a suitable location, such as a console air vent.

- A fully functional binder clip phone mount ready for use.

- The process of creating the binder clip phone mount is complete.

# Solar-Powered LED Lighted Cookie Jar System

## Overview
This system outlines the process of creating a solar-powered LED lighted cookie jar similar to the Sun Jar designed by Tobias Wong. The Sun Jar collects and stores sunlight during the day to use it at night. The end product is a unique, eco-friendly light source that can be used as a nightlight or a cool gift.

## Components and Tools

### Components
- Ikea glass jar
- Solar garden light
- Rechargeable AA battery
- Blu-tack
- Tracing paper (alternative: Glass Frosting spray)

### Tools
- Screwdriver
- Utility Knife
- Glass Frosting spray (if not using tracing paper)

## Process Steps

### START: Begin the Creation of the Solar-Powered LED Lighted Cookie Jar

### PROCESS: Disassembling the Solar Garden Light
- INPUT: Solar garden light, screwdriver, utility knife
- PROCESS: Use the utility knife and screwdriver to carefully disassemble the solar garden light to extract the necessary components (solar panel, circuitry, LED, and battery housing).
- OUTPUT: Internal components of solar garden light ready for use

### PROCESS: Preparing the Glass Jar
- INPUT: Ikea glass jar, Blu-tack
- DECISION [IF]: Is the glass jar frosted?

  - No: Frost the jar with spray or insert tracing paper

  - PROCESS: If using spray, apply an even coating to the jar. If using tracing paper, cut a strip to fit inside the jar.

### PROCESS: Assembling the Jar with Solar Components
- INPUT: Internal components from the solar garden light, frosted Ikea glass jar, Blu-tack
- PROCESS: Place the solar garden light components inside the jar, using Blu-tack to secure them in place. Adjust the placement for a snug fit.
- OUTPUT: Jar with installed solar components

### PROCESS: Finalizing the Jar
- INPUT: Assembled jar with solar components
- PROCESS: Carefully close the lid of the jar, ensuring the light-sensing diode is positioned correctly.
- OUTPUT: Completed solar-powered LED lighted cookie jar

### PROCESS: Using the Sun Jar
- PROCESS: Place the jar by a window with strong sunlight to charge the rechargeable batteries via the solar panel.
- DECISION [IF]: Is ambient light below a certain threshold?
  - Yes: LED should light up automatically
  - No: Continue charging or wait until ambient light diminishes

### OUTPUT: Enjoy or Gift the Solar-Powered LED Lighted Cookie Jar

# Step-by-Step Representation of Cutting Glass Bottles Lengthwise

## START:
- Begin the process of up-cycling a glass bottle by preparing to cut it lengthwise.

## INPUT:
- Gather the following materials and tools:
  - Dremel Diamond Wheel (EZ lock)
  - Dremel EZ Lock Mandrel
  - Copper Foil Tape
  - Silicon Carbide Powder
  - Suction Vise
  - Cordless rotary tool

## PROCESS: [Safety Precautions]
- Ensure to use a cordless rotary tool for safety to avoid the risk of electric shock near water.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the video version of the Instructable needed?
  - Yes: Provide an alternative link for the video version.
  - No: Continue with the written instructions.

## INPUT:
- Mark the cutting line on the glass bottle using copper adhesive tape.
  - Alternative marking options include a permanent marker or using the existing line on some bottles.

## PROCESS: [Setup for Cutting]
- Attach the suction vise to the sink to hold the bottle firmly in place.

## PROCESS: [Cutting the Bottle]
- Take the cordless rotary tool fitted with a diamond cutting disk.
- Begin cutting the bottle while continuously pouring/running water on the cutting spot to lubricate and cool the bottle.

## DECISION [IF]: Do you want to protect the surrounding area from getting wet?
  - Yes: Cover nearby items with plastic to prevent water damage.
  - No: Proceed with cutting.

## PROCESS: [Cutting Steps]
- Cut one side of the bottle first.
- Next, cut the bottom of the bottle.
- Finally, cut the other side of the bottle.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the cut perfect?
  - No: Proceed to sand the cut edges.
  - Yes: Skip to END.

## PROCESS: [Sanding the Bottle]
- Sand the cut edges of the bottle on a piece of glass using the silicon carbide mixture.
  - Alternatively, use wet sandpaper or a rotary tool with a sanding bit to smooth the edges.

## OUTPUT:
- The result is a smoothly cut glass bottle, ready for up-cycling.

## PROCESS: [Final Usage]
- Use the cut bottle as a dish or planter, such as planting wheatgrass.

## END:
- The process of cutting a glass bottle lengthwise and up-cycling it is complete.

instruct00564.title: DIY Incense (sticks and Cones).
instruct00564.text: Homemade 100% natural incense. Easy to make. 2 tsp. gum arabic.2 tsp. of cinnamon or aromatic herbs (powder).4 tsp. of coal (powder).10 inches of wire or thin bamboo sticks.1 piece of sandpaper.1 little bowl.1 bamboo stick.Cutter and scissors.Vegetable oil.Optional: gloves. Skip this if you are going to make cones.Remove the plastic cover with a cutter and cut the wire (or the bamboo) in pieces of 2 inches each one. Sandpaper the coal until you have enough powder. Use gloves if want to keep your hands and nails clean. Skip this step if you are going to use cinnamon powder.Use a mortar with its pestle to grind the dried herbs (lavender, peppermint, rosemary...). Make a "herbs powder". Use the bowl and the stick to mix the coal and the cinnamon (or herbs), then add all the arabic gum and mix until you have a paste with a "Play-Doh texture" and just a little sticky. If you think that it is pretty dry, add two or three drops of vegetable oil and mix (add more if you need it) and if the mixture is wetter than it has to be, add coal and cinnamon in equal parts.Do not use your hands to mix, the paste is very sticky when you start mixing! Use your hands (with or without gloves, the mixture will not damage your skin or nails and it will be better if you do not use gloves) to make the sticks or the cones.Make thin cones (the base must be smaller than 0,3 inches) or they will not burn well.If you make sticks, put the wire pieces as you see in the image.Let the incense sticks dry for three days (or more) and the cones for one week (or more), under the sun if it is possible. When the sticks and cones are completely dried, make them burn like normal incense. UPDATEIf you can, try with organic coal (I could not find it in my country).The wire I used is safe (I am sure), but if you are not comfortable using wire, try bamboo or suggest me alternatives (I could not find it too).I made cones with lavender organic oil (no chemicals added) and they take too much time drying but smell better than the cinnamon sticks. Do not use oil if it is not organic or if you are not sure that it is safe to burn (we do not want explosions).Do not use peppermint plants! They smell horrible when you burn them! Thanks for the support and the suggestions! And sorry if I wrote something in a wrong way!

# Homemade 100% Natural Incense System

## Summary Representation

### START:
- Begin the incense-making process.

### INPUT: Ingredients and Materials
- 2 tsp. gum arabic
- 2 tsp. cinnamon or aromatic herbs (powder)
- 4 tsp. coal (powder)
- 10 inches of wire or thin bamboo sticks
- 1 piece of sandpaper
- 1 little bowl
- 1 bamboo stick
- Cutter and scissors
- Vegetable oil (optional)
- Gloves (optional)

### PROCESS: Preparing Sticks or Wires
- Use the cutter to remove the plastic cover from the wire or bamboo.
- Cut the wire or bamboo into 2-inch pieces.

### DECISION [IF]: Are we making cones instead of sticks?
- Yes: Skip the wire or bamboo preparation.
- No: Continue to the next step.

### PROCESS: Preparing Coal (if not using cinnamon powder)
- Sandpaper the coal until enough powder is obtained.
- DECISION [IF]: Using gloves to keep hands clean?
  - Yes: Wear gloves during this process.
  - No: Proceed without gloves.

### PROCESS: Preparing Herbs (if using aromatic herbs)
- Grind dried herbs into a powder using a mortar and pestle.

### PROCESS: Making the Incense Paste
- In a bowl, mix coal and cinnamon (or herbs) powder.
- Add the gum arabic to the mixture.
- Mix until a paste with "Play-Doh texture" and slightly sticky consistency is achieved.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the paste too dry?
- Yes: Add 2-3 drops of vegetable oil and mix. Repeat if necessary.
- No: Proceed to the next step.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the paste too wet?
- Yes: Add more coal and cinnamon (or herbs) in equal parts.
- No: Proceed to the next step.

### PROCESS: Shaping the Incense
- Use hands to shape the paste into sticks or cones.
  - For cones, ensure the base is smaller than 0.3 inches.
  - For sticks, insert the wire pieces as shown in the image.

### PROCESS: Drying the Incense
- Let the sticks dry for three days or more.
- Let the cones dry for one week or more.
- Preferably dry under the sun if possible.

### OUTPUT: Usage
- Once fully dried, the incense sticks or cones can be burned like normal incense.

### END: Incense-making process is complete.

## Additional Notes (Update)

### INPUT: Additional Considerations
- Organic coal (if available)
- Safe wire or bamboo alternatives

### PROCESS: Experimentation with Organic Oils
- Try making cones with lavender organic oil for a better scent, but expect longer drying times.

### WARNING: Safety Precautions
- Do not use non-organic oils or oils that are unsafe to burn.
- Avoid using peppermint plants as they produce an unpleasant odor when burned.

### END: Additional considerations and safety precautions acknowledged.

instruct00303.title: MouseTrap Catapult
instruct00303.text: Here is a mouse trap catapult designed for safety and economy. We designed and built it for our project management class. It has a simple design and is easy to construct (we built it in about ten minutes). It has a healthy range for it's size and is fun to fire. One mouse trap--<$1 Eight cheep white rubber erasers--$1 One roll duct tape--$1 Plastic utensils --you probably have them already, one knife, one spoon The erasers are just for absorbing the impact of the mouse trap bar so that the catapult will throw projectiles in the right direction. There are probably many options for substitutions. Any normal mousetrap should be adequate, the same goes for the plasticware. Use only the finest duct tape. After removing the bait mount and trigger rod, bend the snapper (main bar that would hit the mouse) as far as it will go and secure it with duct tape. This will protect your fingers and materials. Place the erasers on the empty side of the trap and stack them so they reach high enough and deep enough to absorb the blow from the snapper. Secure it with plenty of duct tape. The erasers will hold up well under the crushing blows, and the duct tape will be invincible. Release the snapper (carefully). You can test the eraser attachment with a few snaps from the snapper. Put the flat part of the plastic knife across the snapper--this will act as a solid anchor to tape the spoon to and increase the durability of the catapult. Place the handle part of the knife behind the spoon to support it as it flings projectiles at your enemies. Secure all parts with duct tape. Your final product should look like ours--very nice. The video show how far it will throw a rolled marshmallow. Pennies went farther but are more dangerous. Conquer with care.

# Mouse Trap Catapult System

## System Overview:
The system is designed to construct a safe and economical mouse trap catapult using common household items. The catapult is intended to have a good range for its size and provide entertainment.

## System Inputs:
- One mouse trap
- Eight cheap white rubber erasers
- One roll of duct tape
- Plastic utensils (one knife, one spoon)

## System Output:
- A functional mouse trap catapult capable of launching projectiles such as rolled marshmallows or pennies.

## System Process Steps:

### START:
- Begin constructing the mouse trap catapult.

### INPUT:
- Gather all necessary materials: mouse trap, erasers, duct tape, and plastic utensils.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Mouse Trap
- Remove the bait mount and trigger rod from the mouse trap.

### PROCESS: Modify the Snapper
- Bend the snapper (main bar) of the mouse trap as far as it will go.
- Secure the bent snapper with duct tape to protect fingers and materials.

### PROCESS: Attach Erasers
- Place the erasers on the empty side of the mouse trap.
- Stack the erasers to a height and depth sufficient to absorb the impact from the snapper.
- Secure the erasers with plenty of duct tape.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the eraser attachment secure enough?
- [Yes] Proceed to test the eraser attachment.
- [No] Reinforce the eraser attachment with more duct tape and reevaluate.

### PROCESS: Test Eraser Attachment
- Release the snapper carefully to test the eraser attachment with a few snaps.

### PROCESS: Assemble the Catapult Arm
- Place the flat part of the plastic knife across the snapper to act as an anchor.
- Position the handle of the knife behind the spoon to support it during projectile launch.

### PROCESS: Secure the Catapult Arm
- Use duct tape to secure the spoon and knife to the mouse trap, ensuring all parts are firmly attached.

### OUTPUT:
- The final product is a mouse trap catapult ready to launch projectiles.

### DECISION [IF]: Does the final product resemble the intended design?
- [Yes] Proceed to testing the catapult.
- [No] Adjust and secure any loose parts with duct tape and reevaluate.

### PROCESS: Test the Catapult
- Launch a rolled marshmallow using the catapult to check the range.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the range satisfactory?
- [Yes] The mouse trap catapult is complete and ready for use.
- [No] Adjust the tension or the arm configuration and retest.

### END:
- The construction and testing of the mouse trap catapult are complete.
