instruct00809.text: Want to make a flash drive that nobody in a modern office would even think about taking? Hide it in a pink eraser and it's secure in this digital age. You can get a couple of erasers in an office supply store or an art store. They're cheap. The flash drive I got at an office supply store. I got a 1 gig since I barely ever use that much as I use flash drives for moving small files around. I don't need anything bigger for now. This is also pretty cheap. Bonus points for the pink cap on it. It was like this flash drive wanted to be in an eraser from the beginning. One eraser is used for the flash drive and the other will serve as the cap. You'll want to use almost all of one eraser for the drive and about half for the cap. The plastic case on my flash drive was easy to pull apart. Just work a fingernail between the pieces and pull it apart. Once it's open you can behold just how tiny the real flash drive is. I grabbed a rotary tool and quickly dug out a gap in each piece. Keep testing the fit with the flash drive until it's nice and snug. The same thing goes for the cap. Take a moment to admire the results and then put that flash drive to work! Put some files on there to print out elsewhere and make it earn its keep. As people have noted several times in the comments, you can buy something like this at Target now. Checking on the site, I found it here. It's also listed on Amazon here where it shows that it's been offered since July 13, over three months after this was published.Sure, you could buy one for $18, but why would you want to? Here are a few reasons not to be a sucker and just make it yourself: - The case is plastic which means that it doesn't look or feel right at all. - You only get 1GB for $18. You can get 4GB for under $13. - The case says Dane-Elec on it - Dane-Elec!?!

instruct00661.title: Caramel Macchiato Cupcakes
instruct00661.text: My absolute favorite drink from Starbucks is the caramel macchiato. I'm pretty obsessed, actually. So, naturally, I had to try making a caramel macchiato cupcake! The cupcake is a chocolate espresso cake, filled with an espresso cream, and topped with caramel buttercream frosting and caramel drizzle. Here is my recipe - Enjoy!Ingredients:For the cupcake: 1 1/2 sticks unsalted butter, at room temperature 2/3 cup granulated sugar 2/3 cup light brown sugar, packed 2 eggs, at room temperature 2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract 1/2 cup milk, at room temperature 1/2 cup brewed strong coffee 1/2 cup sour cream, at room temperature 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour 1/3 cup cocoa powder 1/3 cup espresso powder 1/3 cup instant espresso 1 1/2 teaspoons baking soda 1/2 teaspoon kosher saltFor the espresso cream filling: 2 cups heavy whipping cream 3 tablespoons (or to taste) strong espresso, at room temperatureFor the caramel buttercream frosting: 2 sticks unsalted butter, at room temperature 3 1/2 cups powdered sugar 1 teaspoon milk 1 teaspoon caramel extract (or 3-5 drops of caramel flavoring) 1/8 teaspoon salt caramel sauce for drizzleDirections: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Using an electric mixer, cream the butter and two sugars on high speed until light and fluffy. Lower the speed to medium, and add the eggs one at a time. Lower the speed to low, and add vanilla. Mix until combined. Scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula to make sure all of the ingredients are incorporated. In a separate bowl, whisk together the milk, sour cream, and brewed coffee. In another bowl, sift together the flour, cocoa powder, espresso powder, instant espresso, baking soda, and salt. On low speed, add the milk mixture and flour mixture alternately in thirds to the butter mixture. Start with the milk mixture and end with the flour mixture. Mix until just combined. Again, scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula to make sure all of the ingredients are incorporated. Line cupcake pans with paper wrappers and fill each cup about 2/3 full. Bake on the middle rack of the oven for 17-20 minutes. Test the cupcakes with a toothpick insert a toothpick through the center of a cupcake. If it comes out clean, the cupcakes are done. If not, leave the cupcakes in the oven for another minute and then test the cupcakes again. Cool cupcakes in the pan for 10 minutes. Remove cupcakes from the pan and cool completely. Using a cupcake corer (I used the Cuisipro Cupcake Corer), hollow out a hole in the center of each cupcake. To do this, twist the corer into the cupcake and then slowly remove it. Push the plunger down to remove the cake from the corer. For the filling: using an electric mixer, whisk the heavy whipping cream on high speed until soft peaks form. Add the espresso and continue to whisk on high speed until stiff peaks form. Put the whipped cream into a piping bag and place in the refrigerator until ready to fill cupcakes. For the frosting: using an electric mixer, mix the butter, powdered sugar, milk, caramel extract (or flavoring), and salt together until completely smooth. Put the frosting in a piping bag. Fill each cupcake with the espresso cream. Frost each cupcake. Drizzle caramel over the frosting.

```markdown
# Caramel Macchiato Cupcake Recipe System

## Ingredients Input
- **Cupcake Ingredients**
  - Unsalted butter: 1 1/2 sticks (room temperature)
  - Granulated sugar: 2/3 cup
  - Light brown sugar: 2/3 cup (packed)

  - Vanilla extract: 2 teaspoons

  - All-purpose flour: 1 3/4 cups
  - Cocoa powder: 1/3 cup
  - Espresso powder: 1/3 cup

  - Baking soda: 1 1/2 teaspoons
  - Kosher salt: 1/2 teaspoon

  - Unsalted butter: 2 sticks (room temperature)
  - Powdered sugar: 3 1/2 cups
  - Milk: 1 teaspoon
  - Caramel extract: 1 teaspoon (or caramel flavoring 3-5 drops)
  - Salt: 1/8 teaspoon
  - Caramel sauce for drizzle

  - Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.

  - Cream the 1 1/2 sticks of butter with granulated and brown sugars on high speed until light and fluffy.

  - Reduce speed to medium and add eggs one at a time.
  - Reduce speed to low, add vanilla extract, and mix until combined.
  - Scrape down the bowl with a spatula.

PROCESS: Preparing Wet and Dry Mixtures
  - In a separate bowl, whisk together the milk, sour cream, and brewed coffee.

  - On low speed, alternate adding the milk mixture and flour mixture in thirds to the butter mixture, starting and ending with the milk mixture.

  - Line cupcake pans with paper wrappers and fill each cup about 2/3 full.

  - Hollow out a hole in the center of each cupcake using a cupcake corer.

  - Add espresso and whisk until stiff peaks form.
  - Transfer to a piping bag and refrigerate.

## Caramel Buttercream Frosting Preparation
PROCESS: Making Frosting
  - Mix 2 sticks of butter, powdered sugar, 1 teaspoon of milk, caramel extract, and salt until smooth.
  - Transfer to a piping bag.

## Assembly
PROCESS: Filling Cupcakes
  - Fill each cupcake with espresso cream.

PROCESS: Frosting Cupcakes
  - Frost each cupcake with caramel buttercream.

PROCESS: Adding Caramel Drizzle
  - Drizzle caramel sauce over the frosting.

END
```

instruct00755.title: Paper Plate Skeleton
instruct00755.text: Simple and festive - this paper plate skeleton can be constructed in an hour, and is a blast to make with the kids. It is also easy to customize You will need: paper plates (mine were 6" diameter) scissors twine (or yarn, or something else to tie the bones together) hole-punch Attached here are images of the plates after I cut out the different "bones." It's not an exact science, so simply use these as guides. You need 1 skull, 1 shoulder, 1 rib cage, 1 hip, 2 hands, 2 feet, and 8 bones. Tip: If you're worried about having symmetrical bones, try cutting out a template paper-snowflake style. Fold a plate in half and cut out the bone that way. Trace the folded plate template on the new plate, and you're good to go! Well the foot bone's connected to the ankle bone! And the ankle bone's connected to the leg bone! Let's connect dem dry bones. Using your hole-punch, make a hole at each end of your bones (consult my end picture, if you need, for where to punch on the skull/ribs/hips ect). Tie together with twine. And you're done! To hang, simply use some tape and hang up on your walls in whatever position you want. Happy Halloween! Side note: My anatomy professors from my undergrad days would be so upset at the inaccuracy of this project. Perhaps a more anatomically correct version would be a fun project if someone's feeling ambitious...and has 206 paper plates lying around.

```markdown
# Paper Plate Skeleton System

## START:
Gather all necessary materials:
- INPUT: Paper plates (6" diameter recommended)
- INPUT: Scissors
- INPUT: Twine, yarn, or similar material for tying
- INPUT: Hole-punch

## PROCESS: Preparing the Bones
1. Use the provided images as guides to cut out the different "bones" from the paper plates.
   - OUTPUT: 1 skull, 1 shoulder, 1 rib cage, 1 hip, 2 hands, 2 feet, and 8 bones
2. DECISION [IF]: Are you concerned about bone symmetry?
   - Yes: Proceed to create a symmetrical template.
     - PROCESS: Fold a plate in half and cut out the bone shape to create a template.
     - PROCESS: Trace the folded plate template onto a new plate to replicate the shape.
     - OUTPUT: Symmetrical bone pieces.
   - No: Continue cutting out bones without a template.
     - OUTPUT: Asymmetrical bone pieces.

## PROCESS: Assembling the Skeleton
1. Use the hole-punch to make a hole at each end of the bones.
```

instruct00121.title: Coffee Roasting With a Hot Air Popper
instruct00121.text: I'm well on my way to complete coffee snobbery. Essential to achieving this is being able to roast your own coffee from green coffee beans, which gives the most amazing fresh flavor and scent. Not to mention the ability to casually mention you roasted this particular cup of coffee yourself... Here's my inventory for home roasting: Hot air popcorn popper Green coffee beans 1/4 cup measuring cup medium strainer round bottom stainless steel bowl flat bottom stainless steel bowls (I use 2 of them) The popcorn popper is an "Air Crazy" by West Bend - I got mine at Target for about $20. Ignore the terrible reviews - you aren't using it for popcorn. I got the strainer and round bowl from the kitchen aisle at Smart N Final - any big retailer should have them. The flat bottom bowls came from Petco - yes, they are dog food bowls. I get my Green Coffee Beans from Sweet Maria's in Oakland California - they have a great mail order website. I recommend a 4 lb sampler to get started - that's plenty of coffee to learn how to roast. I do my coffee roasting outside for a couple of reasons. Firstly, the hot air method expels a lot of chaff, and secondly, She Who Must Be Obeyed doesn't like the interim smell (which resembles either grass or charcoal, depending upon who you ask). I have a bistro table outside, right next to a power outlet. I usually roast in small batches, and I have found that a quarter cup or a little more is a good starting point for this machine. Your mileage may vary, due to ambient temperature and (more importantly) the voltage at your outlet. Pour the beans into the popper, and turn on the switch. It will be noisy -- another good reason to be outside. In a minute or less the beans will change from green colored to a light brown. This process will continue and the beans will darken as the roast. Chaff will fly up out of the top of the popper as well. We are listening for the beans to crack -- it is a popping sound, and is a bit like popcorn. You need to continue the roast until all the beans have cracked once - if you don't roast long enough, your coffee will taste like hay or dry grass. (Bleah!) Depending upon how dark you want your roast, you can stop after the first crack is done or you can continue the roast a while longer, waiting for a second, more subtle crack. Here's a very short youtube video of the process -- the ambient noise level is high, but the cracking is audible as clicks. Notice the flying chaff as well. Once you are satisfied that the beans are fully roasted, turn off the popper and dump the beans into a bowl. Pour them back and forth between the bowl and strainer to cool the beans and to allow any remaining chaff to blow away. Don't stress about the chaff - it doesn't affect the flavor too much is you don't get it all out. Once the beans are mostly cool I dump them into one of the dog food bowls to further cool. I usually roast about four batches at one session, and having two spare bowls allows me to fully cool two batches while a third is roasting. Pour the cooled beans into an air-tight storage container. Sweet Maria's labels come off the ziploc bags easily, making it simple to label your beans. And you should label them - imagine the horror some morning if you are expecting a nice light Costa Rica blend and you accidentally grind up some Dark Roasted Java! Shudder the thought.... All my supplies fit neatly into a flip-top storage box, making it easy to store between roasting sessions. Now, go have a cup of good coffee, eh?

```markdown
# Home Coffee Roasting System

## Ingredients and Tools
- Hot air popcorn popper (Air Crazy by West Bend)
- Green coffee beans
- 1/4 cup measuring cup
- Medium strainer
- Round bottom stainless steel bowl
- Flat bottom stainless steel bowls (2 units)
- Power outlet (preferably outdoors)
- Air-tight storage container
- Flip-top storage box for supplies
- Bistro table (optional)

## Steps

### START: Prepare for Coffee Roasting
1. Acquire a hot air popcorn popper, such as the "Air Crazy" by West Bend.
2. Purchase green coffee beans from a supplier like Sweet Maria's.
3. Gather a 1/4 cup measuring cup, a medium strainer, a round bottom stainless steel bowl, and two flat bottom stainless steel bowls.
4. Find an outdoor location near a power outlet to set up the roasting station.
5. Prepare a storage box to organize and store roasting supplies.

### PROCESS: Measure and Load Beans
6. Use the 1/4 cup measuring cup to scoop the green coffee beans.
   - INPUT: Green coffee beans
   - OUTPUT: Measured beans for roasting

### PROCESS: Begin Roasting
7. Pour the measured beans into the popcorn popper.
8. Turn on the popcorn popper to initiate the roasting process.
   - INPUT: Measured beans, electricity
   - OUTPUT: Roasting beans

### PROCESS: Monitor Roasting
9. Observe the beans as they change from green to light brown and then progressively darker.
10. Listen for the first crack, a popping sound indicating the beans are roasting.

### DECISION: Determine Roast Level [IF] [ELSE]
11. IF the desired roast level is reached after the first crack:
    - OUTPUT: Light to medium roast coffee beans
    - END: Proceed to cooling the beans
12. ELSE continue roasting until the second crack for a darker roast:
    - OUTPUT: Medium to dark roast coffee beans

### PROCESS: Cooling the Beans
13. Once the desired roast level is achieved, turn off the popcorn popper.
14. Dump the hot beans into the round bottom stainless steel bowl.
15. Use the medium strainer to pour the beans back and forth between the bowls to cool them and remove chaff.
    - INPUT: Hot roasted beans
    - OUTPUT: Cooled beans with less chaff

### STORE: Transfer to Cooling Bowls
16. Transfer the beans to the flat bottom stainless steel bowls for further cooling.
    - OUTPUT: Further cooled beans ready for storage

### PROCESS: Repeat Roasting (Optional)
17. IF roasting multiple batches, repeat steps 6 through 16 for additional beans.

### STORE: Storage of Roasted Beans
18. Place the cooled beans into an air-tight storage container.
19. Label the container with the type of roast and origin of beans.
    - INPUT: Cooled roasted beans
    - OUTPUT: Labeled and stored roasted beans

### END: Clean-up and Storage
20. Clean the roasting equipment and store it neatly in the flip-top storage box.
21. Enjoy a cup of freshly roasted coffee.
```

instruct00534.title: Minecraft World Cake
instruct00534.text: Here is a minecraft world cake I put together. Really quite easy and very popular! We went out for laser tag for my son't birthday and several people came up to take pictures of the cake! I made a double batch of chocolate cake (I only make cakes from scratch, I use the Betty Crocker Best Chocolate Cake recipe) I baked this in a 1/4 sheet cake pan. I then cut out hunks of cake and assembled them on a Simple Additions large platter from Pampered Chef. The plate measures 15 inches squareto give you an idea how big the cake was. Underneath and in between layers, I put a thin layer of chocolate filling to keep the layers from shifting. Then I put a flat layer of green frosting on the top of each section. The recipe I use is 1/2 cup shortening, 1/2 cup butter, 1 Tbsp vanilla, 1/2 Tbsp meringue powder, 4 cups powdered sugar and approximately 2 Tbsp milk to thin. I thinly sliced rice krispie treats to create the beach. I used a sharpie to draw the squid directly on the plate, then covered the water area with blue gel icing. The trees are make of cut up rice krispie treats. I then mixed food coloring, 1 Tbsp corn syrup and 1 Tbsp water to make a paint for the trees. I'd let this dry at least a day before using, as it was a little gooey. Otherwise, dry them with a hairdryer. The tree trunks are kit kat bars. I inserted toothpicks at each end to attach the tree top and to stabilize in the cake. Steve, the Creeper and the pig came from http://www.fps-x-games.com/2012/04/minecraft-mob-printable-cut-out.html However, the creeper is bigger than Steve, so you may want to google minecraft papercraft to find a different set.

instruct00457.title: The Portal Door
instruct00457.text: I will show you how to put portals on your door or wall. You will need the template somewhere under this text. It is very big (7500 x 500 pixels), because it has to be printed on a very big paper (makes sense, huh?). What it contains: - 2 portals in orange and blue. They have a transparent background that has to be replaced with the pictures from step 2. - 2 Portal logos. One is bigger than the other one, I cut the letters out and glued them under and over the portals, this looks a lot more professional ;) - A nice picture of my favorite cube, the Companion one! I just don't like the feeling of wasting space, cut it out or throw it away, I don't mind. The template is available for a white and a (dark) brown background, because the boundary of the portals are blurred. The picture down there shows what it looks like, but please don't use this, because it is way too small. Here you can get the template in both colors:https://dl.dropbox.com/u/21203905/Papercraft/portaldoor.zip Make 2 pictures, from the 2 views you will hang your portals, for example like this one. If you can, go a bit behind the point where the portal will be, so you can get more of the room behind it on the photo (This does only work with doors, don't try to take a photo through the wall ;)). ...of the photos with the template. Put them under the portals (Does that work in Paint? Guess not, if you can, use Paint Shop, Photo Shop, Gimp or something else) and resize them that they fit. Therefore, you will have to create new layers under the portal-layer where you can put your photos. You may have to erase some parts of one picture, so that it doesn't cover the other one. Save this as a png or something that is not jpeg and bmp (Or you can spend years while uploading). This is what it should look like: You will have to get this picture on a poster, either you print it yourself or you let it print (online is cheap and easy). You wouldn't care about where I bought my poster, because I live in Germany ;) I ordered the size 150 x 100 cm, so the portals are ~100 x 50 cm big (In fact it's a bit lower but wider) That should cost about 30 - 40 $ (please mind the forwarding charges). You can play Minesweeper or drink some coffee until your poster arrives. After you are happy about your portals having arrived, you have to cut them out. Don't cut away too much, otherwise you have a hard transition that doesn't look nice. Attach your portals flat on the surface you want to be portaled, that works best when you use 5 - 10 pieces of double-sided tape, 2 of them in the middle and the rest close to the boundary. First, only use the 2 pieces of tape on the top to fix it and see if it hangs correctly. Then you can fix it with the other tapes. You can add the Portal-Logo if the portal looks too paltry. Just cut the letters out and attach them above or under the portal.If you also want the GLaDOS-camera on the photo, this is just a papercraft and can be downloaded here: http://paperkraft.blogspot.com/2008/03/portal-papercraft-security-camera.htmlI assambled it with 155% of the size.And now you're done! Have fun with your portals.

```markdown
# Portal Decoration System

## System Overview
This system details the process of creating portals on a door or wall, which involves downloading a template, taking pictures, editing images, printing a poster, and attaching the decoration to a surface.

## Steps

### START: Begin Portal Creation Process

### INPUT: Gather Materials
- Download and print the portal template.
- Take two photographs of the area where the portals will be placed.
```

instruct00570.title: Nerf Sledgefire Lever-action Mod
instruct00570.text: Welcome to my "lever -action " mod instructionfor the Nerf Sledge Fire. This tutorial includes: - Conversion to lever action - Construction of an In- Line ClipFor understandingThe Blaster in this tutorial is not made for children.It is made for Larp. (life action role play) Needed tools and materials.tools: - Dremel tool - Hot glue gun - Craft knife (cutter) possibly - angle Grinder - Weldermaterials: - Nerf Sledge Fire - Sledge Fire shell - 16mm cable duct with connector - 16mm PVC pipe - 20mm cable duct - 2mm sheet steel On Blaster housing itself is not much needs to be changed. It must only be cut a little hole You have to make sure that will not damage the screw (This serves later as a bearing for the cocking lever . ) The cut should be about 10mm wide and centered over the entire length of the section. A hole must be cut into the inner mechanics just like the blaster housing. The front edge of the housing is the reference point for the inner hole. (red mark) Based on this reference mark, cut the hole in the centre of the mechanic. (observes the housing halves are not equal) Now we must made even more space for the lever. locate the holder for the reversing lever (blue arrow) and take it as a mark. cut the plastic as shown in the blue box. The bracket for the mechanic (green arrow) must also be tuned to this height. (This step must be done on both housing halves) the parts that were previously installed in this area are now unnecessary. My lever consists of a 10mm wide and 2mm thick strip steel plate which I cut to size with an angle grinder . As bearing serve me 2 drilled M5 nuts that I have welded on the Iron stripe. The part of the lever in the Blaster is the most important. everything that looks out of the Blaster can be designed by your own taste. - The inner part of the lever must run in a gentle arc to the release lever. (from anchorage about 60 mm) - The inner piece of the lever must be tapered to fit probably good in the mechanic The lever can probably also made of plastic , but then the material must be significantly thicker. ( In my case has plastic does not work) The shell must be cut with the dremel that the cable duct fits into it. (do not damage the sealing surface) - If it is prepared glue the 20mm cable duct in the shell. - wrap tape around the 16mm cable duct and push it in the prepared shell as clip. (or glue it in) - push a piece of pvc in the cable duct To use the final in-line clip now in the Sledgefire some adjustments have to be done now. The ejection mechanism for the shells must be removed and the corners needed to be trimmed where the shell rests in the gun barrel. (that the clip can fit thru it) Of course you can find a different (or better) manual for the clip from the internet but my shows how the finished clip fits into the Sledgefire. Here now some pictures of the finished blaster.if you like my instructable vote for me in the Gadget hacking Contest.https://www.instructables.com/contest/gadgethacking/

```markdown
# Lever-Action Mod Instruction for Nerf Sledge Fire

## System Overview
The system converts a Nerf Sledge Fire into a lever-action blaster suitable for LARP (Live Action Role Play). The process involves modifying the blaster housing, creating an in-line clip, and constructing a lever mechanism.

## Required Tools and Materials
- START: Begin the modification process.
  - INPUT: Gather all necessary tools and materials.
    - Tools: Dremel tool, hot glue gun, craft knife, angle grinder, welder.
    - Materials: Nerf Sledge Fire, Sledge Fire shell, 16mm cable duct with connector, 16mm PVC pipe, 20mm cable duct, 2mm sheet steel.

## Blaster Housing Modification
- PROCESS: Modify the blaster housing.
  - Cut a 10mm wide hole centered over the entire length of the section, ensuring not to damage the screw.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the hole cut without damaging the screw?
    - Yes: Proceed with the modification.
    - No: Correct the error and ensure the screw is intact.
  - Cut a hole into the inner mechanics based on the reference mark at the front edge of the housing.
  - DECISION [IF]: Are the housing halves cut equally?
    - Yes: Continue to the next step.
    - No: Adjust cuts to ensure symmetry.
  - Remove unnecessary parts in the area where the lever will be installed.

## Lever Construction
- PROCESS: Construct the cocking lever.
  - Use an angle grinder to cut a 10mm wide, 2mm thick strip of steel for the lever.
  - Weld M5 nuts onto the steel strip to serve as bearings.
  - Shape the inner part of the lever in a gentle arc to reach the release lever.
  - Taper the inner piece of the lever to fit the mechanic.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the lever functioning properly within the blaster?
    - Yes: Move on to modifying the shell.
    - No: Adjust the lever until it operates smoothly.

## In-Line Clip Construction
- PROCESS: Create an in-line clip.
  - Cut the Sledge Fire shell with a Dremel to fit the cable duct, avoiding damage to the sealing surface.
  - Glue the 20mm cable duct into the shell.
  - Wrap tape around the 16mm cable duct and insert it into the shell as a clip (or glue it in).
  - Insert a piece of PVC pipe into the cable duct.
  - DECISION [IF]: Does the in-line clip fit securely in the shell?
    - Yes: Proceed to modify the blaster for the in-line clip.
    - No: Adjust the in-line clip until it fits properly.

## Final Blaster Adjustments for In-Line Clip
- PROCESS: Modify the blaster to accommodate the in-line clip.
  - Remove the ejection mechanism for the shells.
  - Trim the corners where the shell rests in the gun barrel to allow the clip to fit through.
  - DECISION [IF]: Does the in-line clip fit into the modified blaster?
    - Yes: The modification process is complete.
    - No: Continue trimming until the clip fits.

## Completion and Documentation
- OUTPUT: The modified lever-action Nerf Sledge Fire is now complete.
- PROCESS: Document the finished blaster with pictures.
- DECISION [IF]: Are you satisfied with the modification?
  - Yes: Share and enter the Gadget Hacking Contest.
    - END: The system concludes with a modified lever-action blaster.
  - No: Make further adjustments until satisfied.
    - Repeat the evaluation process.
```

```markdown
# Faux Fur Creation System Using Yarn

## Step-by-Step Process

### START:
- Begin the process to create faux fur using yarn.

### INPUT:
- Gather materials:
  - Yarn (any kind, inexpensive yarn recommended)
  - Scissors
  - Scrap fabric (color matching the yarn)
  - Sewing machine or fabric glue
  - Cardboard scrap
  - Wire brush

### PROCESS: [Prepare Yarn Bundles]
- Lay the end of the yarn on the work surface.
- Pinch the end and fold it to the opposite side to determine the length of the fur fibers.
- Bundle the yarn until the desired thickness is reached.
  - IF using glue: Make sure the bundle is thin.
  - ELSE: Any thickness is acceptable for sewing.

### PROCESS: [Create Fur Fibers]
- Tie the middle of the yarn bundle with a piece of yarn.
- Cut each loop at the end to create individual strands.
- Brush the yarn fibers with the wire brush until a soft, fur-like texture is achieved.

### PROCESS: [Detach Bundles]
- Cut the yarn that is holding the bundle together at the tied end.
- Repeat for each yarn bundle.

### INPUT: [Prepare Base Fabric]
- Cut the scrap fabric to the desired size.

### PROCESS: [Attach Yarn to Fabric]
- Sew or glue the yarn bundle at the top edge of the fabric in a row, placing them closely together.
- Continue until the first row is complete.

### DECISION: [Is the first row done?]
  - IF Yes: Proceed to the next layer.
  - IF No: Continue attaching yarn bundles until the row is complete.

### PROCESS: [Add Additional Layers]
- Use a heavy object to flip and weigh down the completed fur layer.
- Glue or sew the next row of bundles just above the first row on the fabric.
- Ensure the new row is very close to the previous row.
- Continue layering until the entire piece of fabric is covered with fur.

### PROCESS: [Finish the Faux Fur Fabric]
- Shake the fabric to free the fibers and check for fullness.
  - IF the fur fabric looks sparse:
    - Sew or glue in the middle of the yarn bundles for stability and to prevent the base from showing.
    - Alternatively, cut the yarn bundle fur shorter to increase fluffiness and fullness.
  - IF the fur fibers are to be fixed in place:
    - Iron down the yarn bundles in the direction of the fur.

### OUTPUT:
- The final product is a piece of faux fur fabric made from yarn.

### END:
- The faux fur creation process is complete and can now be used for various applications such as plushies, costumes, sculptures, or clothing.
```

I was a bit insecure about writing this instructable, since there are a lot of great wire wrapping tutorials on here, new ones are even being published while I'm typing this. But, I just figured everyone wraps a stone differently :) I hope you like it!2020 update: I revisited this project and made a new instructable about it! Check it out here :). To make a pendant like this, you will need:- a stone / probably the most common location I see these is on markets, but you can also find them online (e.g. here) - wire, for a stone of about 2 cm high I used 25 cm of wire- pliers Take the piece of wire and hold it with the top of the round nose pliers. Turn it around to make a loop. Holding it with flat nose pliers, you can now continue your swirl, until it has reached the size you want it to be. Take your stone and hold it as shown in the second image. Place the swirl you just made against it with the remaining wire pointing down. Place your thumb against the swirl, so it can't move. Wrap the wire around the bottom to create a kind of bed for the stone. Stop wrapping after about two or three rounds. To bring the wire to the top of the stone, bend it up on the back of the stone. Start wrapping the top by just bending the wire to the side on the right height and wrapping it around again. Here you can also wrap about three times. I adjusted the position of the swirl here as well, I thought it was just a bit too low. To make sure you can put this charm on a necklace, bend the wire straight up and make a loop using your round nose pliers. I prefer to make double loops, this will also prevent the charm from falling off your necklace. That's it, you're done! I hope you liked it, and maybe will try it yourself :)

```markdown
# Wire Wrapped Gemstone Pendant Creation Process

## Materials Needed:
- Stone (approximately 2 cm high)
- Wire (25 cm length recommended)
- Round nose pliers
- Flat nose pliers

## Process Steps:

### START:
- Begin the pendant creation process.

### INPUT:
- Select a stone and measure a 25 cm piece of wire for wrapping.

### PROCESS: Create the Swirl
1. Grasp the wire with the top of the round nose pliers.
2. Twist the wire around to form a loop.
3. Hold the loop with flat nose pliers.
4. Continue twisting the wire into a swirl until the desired size is achieved.

### PROCESS: Position the Swirl
1. Take the stone and position it as shown in the guiding image.
2. Place the swirl against the stone with the remaining wire pointing downwards.
3. Secure the swirl with your thumb to prevent movement.

### PROCESS: Create the Stone's Bed
1. Wrap the wire around the bottom of the stone to form a bed.
2. Stop after completing two or three rounds.

### DECISION: Is the swirl correctly positioned?
- IF Yes: Proceed to bend the wire upwards.
- ELSE: Adjust the swirl's position before proceeding.

### PROCESS: Secure the Top
1. Bend the wire up along the back of the stone to reach the top.
2. Start wrapping the top by bending the wire to the side at the correct height and wrap around again three times.

### PROCESS: Create the Loop for Necklace
1. Bend the wire straight upwards above the stone.
2. Use round nose pliers to create a loop at the top of the wire.
3. (Optional) Create a double loop for added security.

### OUTPUT:
- The finished wire wrapped gemstone pendant.

### END:
- The pendant creation process is complete.
```

instruct00475.title: Sand "Clay" - Preserve Your Sand Creations Forever!
instruct00475.text: Did you just make that perfect sand castle only to be disappointed when you had to leave the beach? Wouldn't you like some memory of the beach other than the seemingly endless piles of sand coming out of your shoes and socks? Well now that's a thing of the past...safely preserve your sand memories using 3 easy ingredients. You will need:- 2 cups of sand- 3/4 to 1 cup of white glue- 1/2 to 1 cup of cornstarch- A mixing bowl and a mixing tool that will be easy to clean glue and sand off of- Any modelling tools you wish to use to shape your sand- Gloves (if you want) First, add your sand and cornstarch to the bowl and mix them together. Slowly add glue and continue to mix until it all starts to combine. Your goal is to get this mixture to turn into a dough-like substance. If it starts to get to a breadcrumb-like texture try "kneading" it together with your hands. If it starts to get too dry, you can add a little water if your sand was pretty dry, otherwise just add more glue. If it feels too moist and won't hold its shape, add some more cornstarch (unless you've completely overdone it, in which case you may need to add more sand instead). By now the sand mixture should start to feel like a dough. Now that it's all mixed up, you can go ahead and do whatever you want with it! Our goal was to make footprints in the sand, so we shaped the sand into rectangles and then added small rocks to look like feet (it's easier to understand if you look at the picture of it above). Depending on how long it took for you to mix the sand up and how moist it is, you may want to hurry, or else it could start to dry and harden while you're still working. Once you've completed your amazing designs, there are two ways to dry the sand out. You can either just set them out to dry overnight, or if you're a bit impatient (like me), you can put them in the oven on a baking sheet (I lined mine with parchment paper so that the sand wouldn't stick) at around 210 degrees for 2-3 hours, depending on how thick/moist your sand designs are. If you opted to put them in the oven, simply take them out, let them cool, and voila, your awesome sand creations are permanently preserved!Oh and by the way, don't forget to vote for me! I'll be your best friend! ;)

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Sand Memory Preservation

## Ingredients and Tools
- START
  - INPUT: 2 cups of sand
  - INPUT: 3/4 to 1 cup of white glue
  - INPUT: 1/2 to 1 cup of cornstarch
  - INPUT: A mixing bowl
  - INPUT: A mixing tool for glue and sand
  - INPUT: Modelling tools (optional)
  - INPUT: Gloves (optional)
- END INPUTS

## Mixing Process
- PROCESS: Add sand and cornstarch to the mixing bowl.
- PROCESS: Mix sand and cornstarch together.
- PROCESS: Slowly add glue while continuing to mix.
- DECISION [IF]: Does the mixture have a breadcrumb-like texture?
  - Yes: PROCESS: Knead the mixture with hands.
  - No: GOTO NEXT STEP
- DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture too dry?
  - Yes: PROCESS: Add a little water to the mixture.
  - No: GOTO NEXT STEP
- DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture too moist and not holding shape?
  - Yes: PROCESS: Add more cornstarch to the mixture.
  - ELSE: DECISION [IF]: Did you overdo the moisture?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Add more sand to the mixture.
    - No: GOTO NEXT STEP
- OUTPUT: Dough-like sand mixture ready for shaping.

## Shaping and Drying Process
- PROCESS: Shape the sand mixture into desired forms using modelling tools if necessary.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture starting to dry and harden while working?
  - Yes: PROCESS: Hurry with the shaping process.
  - No: GOTO NEXT STEP
- PROCESS: Complete the sand designs.
- DECISION [IF]: Will you dry the sand creations overnight?
  - Yes: PROCESS: Set them out to dry overnight.
  - No: GOTO NEXT STEP
- DECISION [IF]: Will you dry the sand creations in the oven?
  - Yes: 
    - PROCESS: Preheat the oven to 210 degrees.
    - PROCESS: Place sand creations on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
    - PROCESS: Bake for 2-3 hours depending on thickness and moisture.
    - PROCESS: Remove from oven and let them cool.
  - No: GOTO NEXT STEP
- OUTPUT: Permanently preserved sand creations.
- END
```

instruct00881.title: How to Make a Paper Hat
instruct00881.text: Ever wanted to be like those hip kids in paper hats? Or Popeye? Well, now you can! With this majestic hat, you can be the coolest thing on two legs! (or one, you amputees, you!) To make this super-hip hat, you only need one thing: A large piece of paper! For an adult sized hat, cut a piece of packing paper down to a 18" x 24" sheet. For a kid sized hat, make the paper 15 x 20".If you don't have packing paper, you can use wrapping paper or newspaper, but beware that the ink from the newsprint will get on your hands! Another option is to open up a paper shopping bag and use that. Fold it in half, horizontally, like in the pictures above, making sure that all the edges line up with each other. To form the peak of the hat, first you'll need to find the center of the folded sheet so you know where to fold the corners to.To do this, fold the paper in half and make a crease half way down from the folded top, pressing gently. Then fold the 2 corners to the center, so that the two flaps line up in the middle. Press the folded edges down. Carefully fold the two "flaps" at the bottom up. This forms the brim and helps the hat keep it's shape once opened. Add some cool designs to jazz up your new hat. You can use paint, markers, stamps, or... WASHI TAPE! Now be cool in your awesomely simple paper hat!

```markdown
# Comprehensive Step-by-Step Summary of Making a Paper Hat

## START:
- Begin the paper hat-making process.

## INPUT:
- Obtain a large piece of paper.
  - For an adult-sized hat: 18" x 24" sheet.
  - For a kid-sized hat: 15" x 20" sheet.
- Alternative paper options:
  - Wrapping paper.
  - Newspaper (note: ink may transfer to hands).
  - Paper shopping bag (unfolded to a flat sheet).

## PROCESS: [Prepare the Paper]
- Cut the paper to the appropriate size based on the hat size needed.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the paper a paper shopping bag?
  - Yes: Unfold the bag to a flat sheet.
  - No: Proceed with the paper as is.

## PROCESS: [Fold the Paper Horizontally]
- Fold the paper in half horizontally, ensuring all edges align.

## PROCESS: [Find the Center]
- Fold the paper in half again to find the center but only make a crease halfway down from the folded top.
- Unfold this center crease to have a visible line marking the center.

## PROCESS: [Create the Peak]
- Fold the two top corners of the paper to the center crease to form two triangular flaps that meet in the middle.
- Press down the folded edges firmly.

## PROCESS: [Form the Brim]
- Fold the two flaps at the bottom of the paper upwards.
- Press these folds to secure the brim and help maintain the hat's shape.

## DECISION [IF]: Would you like to decorate the hat?
  - Yes: Proceed to decorate.
  - No: Skip decoration and proceed to the final step.

## PROCESS: [Decorate the Hat]
- Use paint, markers, stamps, or washi tape to add designs to the hat.

## OUTPUT:
- The completed paper hat is now ready to wear.

## END:
- The paper hat-making process is complete.
```

instruct00201.title: Cookie Brownie Pie
instruct00201.text: I'm not a big pie person (especiallythe crusts), so I made up my own "pie" that is delicious and I am not the only one who thinks so. So if you love brownies, chocolate chip cookies, and caramel, there is no reason for you to not love this pie. It also doesn't really require many ingredients and you can make two pies depending on the size of your pie pan. You don't need anything too fancy for this.Cookie dough: homemade or from the store (I had a 30oz. package and did not use it all for two pies)Brownie mix: (1 box of 19.4oz. was enough for two pies)Caramel: I ended up using Dulce de Leche which was great, but expensive (1lb. and didn't use it all for one pie)Pie Pans: 2 or you can use the same one twice (Mine is 7 inches in diameter on the bottom) (Some of my ingredients were for two pies because I experimented first and failed which you will see in the last step.) Mix up your cookie dough and brownie mix (don't mix them together though). Pour your brownie mix into a pie pan, you want to use about half the mix. Bake according to the package. Take your cookie dough and push it down into the pie pan. You don't want it thick at all. It will puff up. I pushed it down with the size of the chocolate chips being the thickest it got. Bake it. Let both your brownies and cookie cool. If they are too warm the brownie might fall apart when you take it out of the pan. I put my brownie on top of the cookie to get an idea of how well it was going to fit. To get it to fit in snugly, I cut around the brownie taking off about 1/4-1/2 an inch and cut at an angle. Once it is the size you want it, set it aside and get your caramel. I said earlier that I used the Dulce De Leche pictured, but you can probably use other caramels. They will just sit in the pie differently. This caramel spread on like creamy butter; it was so smooth. Once I had the caramel spread and the brownie on top, I pushed down the brownie. It is nice and soft so it should cooperate with you. I pushed the edges, too, so they would match up better with the cookie crust. Now spread a nice layer of caramel on top of the pie. If you have a runnier caramel, I am unsure of how it will react, but if you have the cookie sides up a little higher than the brownie, it should be fine. You're done! What a lovely simple pie! So when I first made this I put the raw cookie dough in the pan and the brownie mix on top. It didn't work, but Ibelieveit could if you baked it at 300 degrees for half an hour, but don't quote me on that. I did eat the outcome, but I think the brownie was undercooked. It wasn't bad, but the otherversionwas much better. The plan for this version was to melt caramel candies, pour it out to harden flat, and cut into strips to criss cross on the top, but that didn't turn out either so the fancy caramel wasn't wasted on this pie.
instruct00201.summary:
```markdown
# Chocolate Chip Cookie Brownie Caramel Pie System

## Inputs:
- Cookie Dough (homemade or store-bought, 30oz. package, not all used)
- Brownie Mix (1 box of 19.4oz., enough for two pies)
- Caramel/Dulce de Leche (1lb., not all used for one pie)
- Pie Pans (2 or use the same one twice, 7 inches in diameter at the bottom)

## Outputs:
- Two Chocolate Chip Cookie Brownie Caramel Pies

## Process:

START:
1. Preheat oven according to brownie mix package instructions.

PROCESS:
2. Prepare cookie dough if homemade, or open package if store-bought. STORE cookie dough.

PROCESS:
3. Mix brownie batter according to package instructions. STORE brownie mix.

PROCESS [Brownie Layer]:
4. Pour half of the brownie mix into a pie pan.

PROCESS:
5. Bake brownie layer in preheated oven according to package instructions. OUTPUT: Baked brownie layer.

PROCESS [Cookie Layer]:
6. Press cookie dough into a second pie pan, ensuring it's not too thick.

PROCESS:
7. Bake cookie layer in oven. OUTPUT: Baked cookie layer.

PROCESS [Cooling]:
8. Allow both brownie and cookie layers to cool. STORE both layers.

DECISION [IF]: Is the brownie layer too warm?
    - Yes: Continue cooling.
    - No: Proceed to next step.

PROCESS [Assembling Bottom Layer]:
9. Place brownie layer on top of cookie layer to measure fit.

PROCESS:
10. Trim around the brownie layer, removing 1/4-1/2 an inch at an angle for a snug fit. OUTPUT: Trimmed brownie layer.

PROCESS [Caramel Layer]:
11. Spread caramel/Dulce de Leche onto cookie layer in pie pan.

PROCESS [Assembling Top Layer]:
12. Place trimmed brownie layer on top of caramel layer.

PROCESS:
13. Press down brownie layer for a snug fit with the cookie crust. OUTPUT: Brownie layer fitted onto caramel layer.

PROCESS [Final Caramel Layer]:
14. Spread another layer of caramel on top of the brownie. OUTPUT: Completed Chocolate Chip Cookie Brownie Caramel Pie.

END.

## Notes:
- If using a runny caramel, ensure cookie sides are higher than the brownie layer to contain the caramel.
- Failed Experiment: Baking raw cookie dough with brownie mix on top at 300 degrees for half an hour is not recommended.
- Alternate Decoration Plan: Melt caramel candies, pour out to harden flat, cut into strips, and crisscross on top was not successful.
```

instruct00517.title: Embroidered Chain Bracelet
instruct00517.text: This is a really simple way to spruce up a basic chain bracelet. I'm not a big fan of chunky jewelry, so this is a nice way to add some color without adding bulk. :D All you need is some embroidery floss or thin yarn and you're ready to make a whole new bracelet! embroidery floss thick chain (1/8-1/4 inch wide) embroidery needle jump rings closures glue (optional, but helpful!) measuring tape or ruler I got both silver tone and gold tone chain and chose embroidery floss that complemented them. :) Measure your wrist - mine is 6 inches around. I cut my chain to 6.5 inches - you always want to go a little longer - it'll help you get the bracelet on easier later. :D Now cut a piece of embroidery floss that's double the length of your chain. Attach a lone jump ring to one end of the chain, and then attach a jump ring and the closure to the other end. I like to tie the first link of chain to the jump ring on the end. Make a few knots and then cut the short end of the string. You can add a drop of glue here for extra security. :) Pull the thread in and out of the links, being careful to go all the way through the link and not get it tangled. It's like a running stitch, but wil go a little slower. :D I like to only do one link at a time, trying to get multiple links on the needle caused tangling. Keep going until you reach the other end, and then tie it off again like we did at the beginning. :) You can see here that I didn't use a long enough piece of embroidery floss the first time I tried this, but I really like it anyway! :D

```markdown
# Embroidered Chain Bracelet Creation Process

## START:
- Begin the process of creating an embroidered chain bracelet.

## INPUT: Gather Materials
- Embroidery floss or thin yarn.
- Thick chain (1/8-1/4 inch wide).
- Embroidery needle.
- Jump rings.
- Closures.
- Glue (optional).
- Measuring tape or ruler.

## PROCESS: Measure Wrist
- Use measuring tape or ruler to measure wrist circumference.

## OUTPUT: Wrist Measurement
- Obtain wrist measurement (Example: 6 inches).

## PROCESS: Cut Chain
- Cut the chain to a length 0.5 inches longer than wrist measurement.

## OUTPUT: Chain Cut to Length
- Obtain chain cut to the desired length (Example: 6.5 inches).

## PROCESS: Cut Embroidery Floss
- Cut a piece of embroidery floss that is double the length of the chain.

## OUTPUT: Embroidery Floss Cut to Length
- Obtain embroidery floss cut to the desired length.

## PROCESS: Attach Jump Rings and Closure
- Attach a jump ring to one end of the chain.
- Attach another jump ring and the closure to the other end of the chain.

## DECISION [IF]: Is Glue Being Used for Extra Security?
- Yes: Proceed to apply glue.
- No: Skip glue application.

## PROCESS [IF YES]: Apply Glue
- Apply a drop of glue to the knot for extra security.

## PROCESS: Start Embroidering
- Tie the embroidery floss to the first link of the chain next to the jump ring.
- Make a few knots and trim the short end of the floss.

## PROCESS: Continue Embroidery
- Weave the floss in and out of each chain link using a running stitch technique.
- Ensure to pass completely through the links without tangling the floss.
- Focus on one link at a time to prevent tangling.

## DECISION [IF]: Has the End of the Chain Been Reached?
- Yes: Proceed to tie off the embroidery floss.
- No: Continue embroidering the chain.

## PROCESS [IF YES]: Tie Off Embroidery Floss
- Once the end of the chain is reached, tie off the embroidery floss securely.
- Trim any excess floss and add a drop of glue if desired for extra security.

## OUTPUT: Finished Embroidered Chain Bracelet
- The result is a spruced-up chain bracelet with added color and no added bulk.

## END:
- The embroidered chain bracelet creation process is complete.
```

instruct00110.title: How to Make Vinaigrette
instruct00110.text: Once you start making your own vinaigrettes, you'll never want to buy another bottle of salad dressing. A good vinaigrette is just about the easiest thing you can make in the kitchen. :DI've also included a list of great tasting mix ins on step three to help you up your vinaigrette game even more! oil - olive, canola, sunflower, safflower, etc.vinegar - white wine, red wine, apple cider, rice wine, balsamic, etc. salt + pepper to tastea bowl + a whisk OR a small jar to shake everything together inI use an old jam jar for mine most times, but there are actually nice bottles made just for mixing up dressings with recipes on the side. Pretty fancy!You can also mix in all kinds of yummy things - skip to step three for some ideas. :DMy favorite vinaigrette is olive oil and white wine vinegar with salt, pepper and lemon zest - it tastes like summer! 3 parts oil to 1 part vinegar.BOOM. That's it. Easy, right? Of course there will always be some exceptions, but this ratio should never steer you too far off course. It's very easy to correct, no matter how strong the vinegar is! :D If you want to go above and beyond there are so many things you can mix in to a vinaigrette! I love shallots and fresh herbs the most, but you've got loads of options:fresh herbs - dill, parsley, cilantro, basil - anything that's not too woody! fresh citrus juice - lemon is lovely. just replace some of the vinegar with the juice.fresh citrus zest (I do this almost every time!)mustard - a bit of dijon or yellow mustard adds a little extra tang.nut oils like hazelnut, almond or walnut in small amounts add lots of flavor - mix them in with your base oil.sugar - adding a pinch of sugar will give you a sour and sweet vinaigrette - great for dressing coleslaw or marinating meat.honey - even better than sugar in some cases! tahini - add some to your oil for a punch of sesame flavorbacon fat and pan drippings - adds loads of flavor! Just mix a little into the oil you're using.minced sun dried tomatoes - lots of color and a little smoky flavor. :)grated cheese - a little Parmesan goes a long way.minced garlic - start with a teeny bit and work your way up!You can also add in dried herbs and spices, but I find that it's best to add them to the oil first and warm it slightly. Otherwise you won't get as much flavor from them.I do all of these to taste every time - just keep adding and mixing and tasting! Once you've got everything measured out, you'll want to whisk it in bowl OR pour it into a jar with a tight lid and shake to emulsify the vinaigrette. I much prefer the jar method. :DKeep in mind that your vinaigrette will separate fairly quick, so having it in a container for easy mixing is best.Storing your vinaigrette:plain vinaigrettes (just oil, vinegar, salt, pepper - nothing fresh!) can be stored for a looooong time. Months, even! I like to keep mine in the fridge just to be safe. Just keep an eye on it - if you see something growing in there don't eat it. ;)vinaigrettes with fresh mix-ins will keep well in the fridge for 2-3 days, but after that they begin to lose flavor and freshness.to warm up cold vinaigrette, set the container in a bit of hot water for a moment. That'll make it easy to emulsify it again.I have to admit I don't often store my vinaigrettes, though! I tend to make just enough for a meal instead of loads at once. That way none of it goes to waste or ends up in the back of the fridge growing a glorious mane of mold hair. :D

```markdown
# Vinaigrette Making System

## START:
- Begin the vinaigrette preparation process.

## INPUT:
- Gather the following ingredients and tools:
  - Oil (olive, canola, sunflower, safflower, etc.)
  - Vinegar (white wine, red wine, apple cider, rice wine, balsamic, etc.)
  - Salt and pepper to taste
  - Optional mix-ins (herbs, citrus juice/zest, mustard, nut oils, sugar, honey, tahini, bacon fat, sun-dried tomatoes, cheese, garlic)
  - A bowl and a whisk OR a small jar with a tight lid (like an old jam jar)

## PROCESS: [Ratio of Ingredients]
- Use the ratio of 3 parts oil to 1 part vinegar as the base for the vinaigrette.

## DECISION [IF]: Is a mix-in desired?
  - Yes: Proceed to add mix-ins.
  - No: Skip to whisking or shaking step.

## PROCESS: [Adding Mix-ins]
- If using fresh herbs, choose non-woody types (dill, parsley, cilantro, basil).
- If using citrus juice, replace some of the vinegar with the juice.
- If using dry herbs or spices, warm them in the oil first to enhance flavor.
- Add mix-ins such as mustard, nut oils, sugar, honey, tahini, bacon fat, sun-dried tomatoes, grated cheese, or minced garlic to taste.
- Continue adding and mixing until satisfied with the flavor.

## PROCESS: [Emulsifying the Vinaigrette]
- Whisk the vinaigrette in a bowl OR pour into a jar and shake until emulsified.

## OUTPUT:
- The result is a freshly made vinaigrette.

## DECISION [IF]: Will the vinaigrette be stored?
  - Yes: Proceed to storage instructions.
  - No: END.

## PROCESS: [Storing Vinaigrette]
- Store plain vinaigrettes (without fresh mix-ins) at room temperature or in the fridge for several months. Monitor for spoilage.
- Store vinaigrettes with fresh mix-ins in the fridge for 2-3 days for optimal flavor.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the stored vinaigrette cold?
  - Yes: Warm it up slightly for easy emulsification.
  - No: END.

## PROCESS: [Warming Up Cold Vinaigrette]
- Set the container in hot water for a moment to warm up the vinaigrette.

## END:
- The vinaigrette making and storing process is complete.
```

instruct00362.title: Homemade Twix Candy Bar Recipe
instruct00362.text: I love Twix candy bars, but I'm not crazy about all the additives. This recipe is like Twix candy bar goes gourmet, but super easy to make. In fact, it's probably the easiest copycat candy bar recipe I've made! I fiddled with this recipe quite a bit. The problem is in the shortbread. That's what makes or breaks a homemade Twix bar in my opinion. Most shortbread recipes are very flaky and crumbly, and that's just not going to work here. So I decided to add an egg and increase the flour content of a more traditional shortbread recipe. The process remains simple and the result is near perfect, if a little softer than the original. These are great for a party, and freeze up well too. You could make this whole thing totally simple by buying prepackaged shortbread cookies, but I decided to try and do it from scratch! What follows is the shortbread recipe I used. What I realized (had realized, forgotten, and just now remembered) is that the perfect cookie recipe for this is actually here.TOOLS:MixerBaking SheetSilpat or ParchmentChocolate Melter (opt)SHORTBREAD: 1 cup (2 sticks) (227 grams) unsalted butter, room temperature 3/4 cup (85 grams) powdered sugar 1 egg 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract 2 1/4 cups (250 grams) all purpose flour 1/2 teaspoon saltCARAMEL FILLING: 3 - 5.5 ounce bags (15.5 ounces total) soft caramels (or make your own) 2 tablespoons milk or cream dash salt (opt)CHOCOLATE TOPPING: 12 ounces (240 grams) milk chocolate, cut into piecesScoochmaroo provides product links as a participant in the Amazon Services LLC Associates Program, an affiliate advertising program designed to provide a means for sites to earn advertising fees by advertising and linking to amazon.com. Preheat oven to 300oF (150C) and place rack in center of oven. With an electric mixer or hand mixer, beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add egg and beat until combined. Beat in the vanilla extract. Add the flour and salt and beat until the dough just comes together. Refrigerate the dough until firm. Roll out the dough or press onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 20 - 30 minutes, turning the baking sheet front-to-back half-way through baking. Place your caramels, milk and salt in a microwaveable bowl and nuke for 1 minute at a time, stopping to stir, until nice and melty (3-4minutes) If you're using homemade caramels, you can reduce the amount of milk and microwave time. If you are using hard caramels, increase the milk. Pour caramel over the baked cookie. Once the caramel has set, cut into whatever size pieces you desire. For best results, chill them in the freezer to firm up before dipping. Temper your chocolate using this tutorial as a guide. Dip the bars in the tempered chocolate and place on waxed or parchment paper to set. Do not attempt to move your Twix bars before they are set or they're liable to come apart. Once they've set, you're ready to share and enjoy! For best results, store in the fridge.

```markdown
# Homemade Twix Candy Bars Recipe System

## Ingredients Input
- START
  - INPUT: 1 cup (2 sticks) (227 grams) unsalted butter, room temperature
  - INPUT: 3/4 cup (85 grams) powdered sugar
  - INPUT: 1 egg
  - INPUT: 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
  - INPUT: 2 1/4 cups (250 grams) all-purpose flour
  - INPUT: 1/2 teaspoon salt
  - INPUT: 3 - 5.5 ounce bags (15.5 ounces total) soft caramels
  - INPUT: 2 tablespoons milk or cream
  - INPUT: Dash salt (optional for caramel)
  - INPUT: 12 ounces (240 grams) milk chocolate, cut into pieces

## Tools Input
  - INPUT: Mixer
  - INPUT: Baking Sheet
  - INPUT: Silpat or Parchment
  - INPUT: Chocolate Melter (optional)

## Shortbread Preparation
  - PROCESS: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C) and place rack in center of oven.
  - PROCESS: Beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy using a mixer.
  - PROCESS: Add egg to the mixture and beat until combined.
  - PROCESS: Beat in the vanilla extract.
  - PROCESS: Add the flour and salt and beat until the dough just comes together.
  - PROCESS: Refrigerate the dough until firm.
  - PROCESS: Roll out the dough or press onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  - PROCESS: Bake for 20 - 30 minutes, turning the baking sheet front-to-back halfway through baking.
  - OUTPUT: Baked shortbread base.

## Caramel Filling Preparation
  - PROCESS: Place caramels, milk, and optional salt in a microwaveable bowl.
  - DECISION: Are you using homemade caramels?
    - IF Yes:
      - PROCESS: Reduce the amount of milk and microwave time.
    - ELSE No:
      - PROCESS: If using hard caramels, increase the milk.
  - PROCESS: Microwave for 1 minute at a time, stopping to stir, until caramels are melted (approximately 3-4 minutes).
  - PROCESS: Pour melted caramel over the baked cookie base.
  - PROCESS: Allow the caramel to set.
  - OUTPUT: Shortbread base with caramel layer.

## Cutting and Chilling
  - PROCESS: Once the caramel has set, cut into desired size pieces.
  - DECISION: Are you going to dip the bars in chocolate?
    - IF Yes:
      - PROCESS: Chill the bars in the freezer to firm up before dipping.
    - ELSE No:
      - END: Finish without chocolate coating.

## Chocolate Topping Preparation
  - PROCESS: Temper chocolate using a tempering tutorial as a guide.
  - PROCESS: Dip the bars in the tempered chocolate.
  - PROCESS: Place dipped bars on waxed or parchment paper to set.
  - DECISION: Have the Twix bars set?
    - IF Yes:
      - PROCESS: Once they've set, you're ready to share and enjoy!
      - OUTPUT: Finished homemade Twix bars.
      - PROCESS: For best results, store in the fridge.
      - END
    - ELSE No:
      - PROCESS: Do not attempt to move the Twix bars before they are set to avoid them coming apart.
      - DECISION [LOOP]: Check periodically if the Twix bars have set.
        - IF Yes: Go to the next step where they are set.
        - ELSE No: Continue to wait until they set.
```

instruct00349.title: How to Make Mexican Discada
instruct00349.text: Discada is a typical dish from northern mexico, it gets its name because traditionally you make in a used plow disc thats been welded shut. Anyway discada is an alternative to a barbecue and the perfect excuse to have a beer with your friends. The most important part of the discada is well the disco that in reallity is a used plow disk that has been welded shut and in this case it has an added border and handles. But you can get creative and use another thing for cooking it, maybe a large wok , skillet or something like that could work out. Ok so now we need the ingredients to make our discada. For each kilogram of meat you will need about 300-350 grams of everything else (except for the seasonings). So heres the list: Meat ( i use a cut thats called pulpa bola thats taken from the back and shoulder area of the cow). Bacon Ham. Sausage. Chorizo. Bell peppers. Onions. Tomato. The seasonings: Jalapetional) Ok now comes the fun part, cooking the whole thing. Turn on your gas burner and set it at a low(ish) flame you don't want it to hot, then you add some beer to the disco (from the same beer your drinking), and you add the bacon to that and let it simmer for a while, when it's been sitting a while in the beer (about 5 to 10 minutes) you take the bacon out of the beer and just move it to the side of the disco so it releasesome grease and keep cooking on the side. Add the sausage to the beer broth and let it cook for about 5 to 10 minutes, after that move the sausage to the side and add the ham to the broth and again let it cook for around 10 minutes just like the sausage and again move it to the side of the disco. Add the choriso to the broth, stir it a bit and let it simmer 10 to 15 minutes, and again move it to the side, you can also put it on top of the others meats. And now to this broth you add the meat and also the seasonings (garlic, salt and pepper), stir it a bit so the meat gets full of flavor but don't mix it with the other ingredients just yet. This is the part were the meat releases its juices and some of its flavor, so to hold it in a little more we put a lid on top of the meat and leave it there for a while (about 10 minutes) till it releases some of its flavors. Now remove the lid stir the meat a little and let some of the broth reduce. Once the broth has reduced a little mix everything up, if your a real carnivore like me give it a try now it tastes meaty and great. So in this step we are gona put some color to it. First we make a little crater in the middle of the meats and put the chopped bell peppers and about 3 jalapesome kick to it. Then we add the onions mix it up a bit and add the tomato and mix it some more. Now that everything's cooked put some tortillas on top of ity heat up, make some tacos and enjoy (who needs plates and fork when you have tortillas and your hands). Have a great time and enjoy your new love fot discada.

```markdown
# Discada Cooking Process

## START:
- Begin the process of cooking a traditional Mexican dish called Discada.

## INPUT: Ingredients and Equipment
- [INPUT] Collect the following ingredients per kilogram of meat:
  - 300-350 grams of bacon, ham, sausage, chorizo, bell peppers, onions, and tomato.
  - Seasonings: garlic, salt, pepper, and optional jalapeños.

## PROCESS: Cooking Sequence
- [PROCESS] Turn on the gas burner to a low-medium flame.
- [PROCESS] Add beer to the disco and let it warm up.
- [PROCESS] Add bacon to the beer, simmer for 5-10 minutes.
- [DECISION IF] Is the bacon simmered for 5-10 minutes?

  - No: Keep simmering until time is reached.
- [PROCESS] Move the bacon to the side of the disco to release grease and continue cooking.
- [PROCESS] Add sausage to the beer broth, cook for 5-10 minutes.
- [DECISION IF] Is the sausage cooked for 5-10 minutes?

- [END] Enjoy the meal and the experience of making and eating discada.
```

instruct00100.title: Chocolate Molten Lava Cake - in the Microwave!
instruct00100.text: Warning: the dessert you are about to create and consume is extremely chocolatey. It will kill your chocolate craving really fast. That aside, enjoy the most awesome 5-minute chocolate molten lava cake you've ever tried! The secret here is using melted dark chocolate. Cocoa powder doesn't hold a candle to it, and using bar chocolate negates the need for adding milk or oil while producing a really moist cake. - 2 oz. dark chocolate bar (60% cocoa) - 2 oz. butter - 3 tbsp sugar - 3 tbsp. flour - 1 egg - 1 chocolate truffle (Lindt truffles work great) The chocolate truffle creates the warm oozy chocolate center of your cake. Be sure to freeze it ahead of time and it will melt just perfectly once the cake is finished cooking. Break up the chocolate into pieces and place that along with the butter into a microwaveable bowl. Heat for 30 seconds, then remove and stir to melt the chocolate. If it's not quite melted, microwave for an extra 5 seconds and stir again. Be sure not to microwave the chocolate too long or it will thicken up; let it melt by stirring. In a separate bowl, beat the egg thoroughly and mix in the sugar until it whitens a bit. Mix the egg/sugar into the bowl of chocolate, then slowly incorporate the flour. The finished batter should be fairly liquidy. The best container for microwaving the chocolate batter is, of course, the giant mug. Spray some cooking spray into it first, then pour the batter in. The cake will rise during the cooking process so make sure you use the largest mug you can find. Finally, stick the frozen chocolate truffle into the mixture, about halfway in. Cover up the "hole" with some of the batter. Microwave for about 1 minute and 30 seconds. If you have a less than 1000W microwave try a slightly longer cook time. The kitchen should smell deliciously chocolatey now. But, patience! Let the cake rest for a minute in the microwave before you dig in so that it cooks completely. Use a fork to loosen the cake from the edges of the mug, then place a plate over the mug and flip it out. Nom. HINT: Vanilla ice cream and chocolate syrup.

```markdown
# 5-Minute Chocolate Molten Lava Cake Recipe

## Ingredients:
- 2 oz. dark chocolate bar (60% cocoa)
- 2 oz. butter
- 3 tbsp sugar
- 3 tbsp flour
- 1 egg
- 1 chocolate truffle (Lindt truffles recommended)
- Cooking spray

## Equipment:
- Microwaveable bowl
- Separate mixing bowl
- Fork or whisk
- Large microwaveable mug
- Plate (for serving)

## Instructions:

### Preparation:
START:
- INPUT: Gather all ingredients and equipment.

### Melting Chocolate and Butter:
PROCESS: Break the dark chocolate bar into pieces.
- INPUT: Place chocolate pieces and butter in a microwaveable bowl.
PROCESS: Heat in the microwave for 30 seconds.
DECISION [IF]: Is the chocolate completely melted?
  - YES: Proceed to the next step.
  - NO: 
    - PROCESS: Microwave for an additional 5 seconds.
    - DECISION [IF]: Is the chocolate now completely melted?
      - YES: Proceed to the next step.
      - NO: Repeat the 5-second microwaving and stirring until melted.

### Preparing Egg and Sugar Mixture:
PROCESS: In a separate bowl, beat the egg thoroughly.
- INPUT: Mix sugar into the beaten egg.
PROCESS: Continue mixing until the mixture whitens slightly.

### Making the Batter:
PROCESS: Combine the egg/sugar mixture with the melted chocolate/butter mixture.
- INPUT: Slowly incorporate the flour into the mixture.
DECISION [IF]: Is the batter fairly liquidy?
  - YES: Proceed to the next step.
  - NO: 
    - PROCESS: Adjust by gently mixing until the batter reaches a liquidy consistency.

### Preparing Mug:
PROCESS: Spray the inside of a large mug with cooking spray.
- INPUT: Pour the batter into the mug.
PROCESS: Ensure the mug is large enough to allow the cake to rise during cooking.

### Adding Chocolate Truffle:
PROCESS: Freeze the chocolate truffle beforehand.
- INPUT: Push the frozen chocolate truffle halfway into the batter.
PROCESS: Cover the truffle with some of the surrounding batter.

### Microwaving the Cake:
PROCESS: Microwave the mug with the batter for approximately 1 minute and 30 seconds.
DECISION [IF]: Is your microwave less than 1000W?
  - YES: 
    - PROCESS: Try a slightly longer cook time.
  - NO: Proceed to the next step.

### Finishing Touches:
PROCESS: Allow the cake to rest for a minute in the microwave post-cooking.
PROCESS: Use a fork to loosen the cake from the edges of the mug.
PROCESS: Place a plate over the mug and flip it to turn out the cake.

OUTPUT: The chocolate molten lava cake is ready to be served.

### Serving Suggestions:
HINT: Serve with vanilla ice cream and chocolate syrup for added indulgence.

END: Enjoy your deliciously chocolatey 5-minute chocolate molten lava cake!
```

instruct00802.title: Modified IKEA GALANT Desk
instruct00802.text: I had to plan this modification from the start, before even assembling the new IKEA Galant desk. Since the desk was so large and I couldn't really flip over the frame, I had to attach all items, including the pegboards, while laying on my back. I had to drill holes in the pegboard for the legs and the areas where I'd be screwing the desktop to the metal frame. I'm no construction pro so my larger holes in the pegboard were sometimes off, but it all worked out in the end. I attached everything - including the pegboard to the metal frame - with medium and large zip ties. I believe I spent a good 6+ hours on this project, but I'm really happy with the results. I even installed a USB hub near the front of my desk so I can plug in extra equipment easily. When it's all said and done, I spent only $30-40 on supplies (zip cables, 2x4 pegboards (x2). Attaching the two 2x4 pegboards is a bit tricky and you'll find yourself on your back often. The trick is adding the pegboards into the construction of the desk AFTER completion of the desk's metal frame but BEFORE the legs are attached to the frame. Larger holes need to be made in the pegboard where the leg attaches to the frame from the bottom and where the tabletop is attached to the metal frame from the top. Due to the size and shape of the desk, one of the 2x4 pegboards need to be shaved so it is not exposed beyond the edge of the desk. Once I attached my pegboards, I laid into place some of my electronics. To have maximum separation between the left and right computer speaker, I set it up prior to installing the table top. In hindsight, this wasn't such a good idea: if I want to switch out my speakers, I have to either cut the speaker cable or unscrew the desk top in order to remove them. Here's some shots of the underside of the pegboards. Medium and long zip cords are all I used to attach anything from a coil of extra cable to heavy external harddrives. They come in packs of 15-20 at hardware and home improvement stores. I daisy-chained two power bars. Each white power bar is connected to a black power bar, which in turn is plugged into a separate wall plug-in as to not blow a fuse. Here's the desk after completion.

```markdown
# IKEA Galant Desk Modification Summary

## System Overview
The system represents the process of modifying an IKEA Galant desk by adding pegboards for organization and a USB hub for connectivity. The modification requires careful planning, drilling, and attachment of components using zip ties.

### Inputs
1. IKEA Galant desk
2. 2x4 pegboards (2 pieces)
3. Medium and large zip ties
4. Drill and appropriate drill bits
5. USB hub
6. Computer speakers (optional)
7. Power bars (2 white, 2 black)
8. Tools for shaving pegboard (if necessary)

### Outputs
1. Modified IKEA Galant desk with attached pegboards
2. Installed USB hub
3. Organized cables and electronics attached to the pegboards
4. Daisy-chained power bars for electrical supply

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the modification process before assembling the new IKEA Galant desk.

### PROCESS: Prepare Pegboards
- INPUT: 2x4 pegboards
- PROCESS: Measure and drill holes in the pegboard for the desk legs and areas where the desk top will be screwed to the metal frame.
  - DECISION [IF]: Are the drilled holes correctly aligned?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Adjust as necessary until the holes align correctly.
- PROCESS: Shave one of the 2x4 pegboards if it extends beyond the edge of the desk.

### PROCESS: Assemble Metal Frame of Desk
- INPUT: IKEA Galant desk metal frame components

- OUTPUT: Assembled metal frame ready for further modification.

### PROCESS: Attach Pegboards to Metal Frame
- INPUT: Prepared pegboards, zip ties
- PROCESS: Attach the pegboards to the metal frame using medium and large zip ties while lying on your back.
- OUTPUT: Metal frame with attached pegboards.

### DECISION [IF]: Are the legs attached to the frame yet?
  - No: Proceed to attach legs to the frame.
  - Yes: Do not proceed; legs should be attached after pegboards.

### PROCESS: Attach Legs to Metal Frame
- INPUT: Desk legs
- PROCESS: Attach the legs to the metal frame through the holes in the pegboard.
- OUTPUT: Desk with metal frame and legs attached.

### PROCESS: Set Up Electronics and Power Bars
- INPUT: Electronics, computer speakers, power bars
- PROCESS: Lay out electronics and speakers, then daisy-chain two power bars (white to black) and plug into separate wall outlets.
  - DECISION [IF]: Are speakers to be installed before the tabletop?
    - Yes: Install speakers now, but be aware of future difficulty in switching them out.
    - No: Install speakers after the tabletop is attached.
- OUTPUT: Electronics and power bars set up.

### PROCESS: Attach Desk Top
- INPUT: Desk top
- PROCESS: Attach the desk top to the metal frame, securing it to the pegboards.
- OUTPUT: Complete desk with top attached.

### PROCESS: Install USB Hub
- INPUT: USB hub
- PROCESS: Install a USB hub near the front of the desk for easy access to plug in equipment.
- OUTPUT: Desk with installed USB hub.

### END:
- The IKEA Galant desk modification is complete with pegboards, electronics organization, and USB hub installed.
```

instruct00477.title: Build a Cardboard Tank
instruct00477.text: My buddies and I were trying to think of something we could build out of cardboard and duct tape. We came up with a tank. It was a little more costly than originally estimated, but it was fun and the end result is amazing. It'll blow your friends away! This instructable will go through each step in the process, and hopefully you'll be able to build your very own tank for you to play in (or your kids/pets/neighbors/neighbor's cat to play in). BTW, please hit the vote button for the cardboard and duct tape contest!!!! For this job, all you really need is cardboard, duct tape (regular gray, dark gray, white, and black), and something to cut with (utility knife works great). We also used a few power tools along the way, just to speed the job up--they're not required. Also, get as much cardboard as you can get your hands on. We went to or calledevery appliance store in town begging for cardboard. Ask for fridge boxes, washer/dryer boxes, anything big works great. Also, be sure to ask for the extremely hard cardboard used to protect the corners of the appliances. These are a must in a first couple steps. And, as for the duct tape, I think we ended up using about 60 rolls. Take those tough corner pieces, the strong tubes, the duct tape and start putting it together. We cut slots in the tubes to help support the corner pieces, then wrapped the joint in duct tape in a X shape. Once the frame is built, grab some of the fridge boxes and start piecing it all together. At this point, it doesn't look much like a tank at all, but remember, this is just the skeleton!You have to keepthe vision in your mind. The turret is made the same way as the main body of the tank (frame and skin). The wheel are cardboard concrete forms used for footings in construction work. They are 16" in diameter, and 10" deep. There's 7 wheels per side. We were going for a snow camo look. And of course we wanted to do the new digital camo styling. So, we taped the whole body in white, the tracks and behind the wheels in cheap gray tape, the wheels were black with a white hub, and we used multiple shades of gray and black for the camo patterns. We took ours down a tube run. It was a blast.

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Tank Construction from Cardboard and Duct Tape

## System Overview
The system represents the process of building a cardboard tank using duct tape, cardboard, a utility knife, and optional power tools. The end result is a tank for recreational use.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of building a cardboard tank.

### INPUT:
- Gather materials: cardboard, duct tape (regular gray, dark gray, white, and black), utility knife, and optional power tools.
- Collect large cardboard boxes (e.g., from appliance stores) and hard cardboard for corners.

### PROCESS: [Acquire Cardboard]
- Visit or call appliance stores to request cardboard boxes and hard corner protectors.

### PROCESS: [Calculate Duct Tape]
- Estimate the amount of duct tape needed (approximately 60 rolls).

### PROCESS: [Prepare Frame]
- Take tough corner pieces and strong tubes for the frame.
- Cut slots in the tubes to fit the corner pieces.

### PROCESS: [Assemble Frame]
- Connect the tubes and corner pieces.
- Secure the joints with duct tape in an 'X' shape.

### PROCESS: [Construct Tank Skeleton]
- Use fridge boxes to start piecing together the tank's skeleton.

### DECISION [IF Skeleton Looks Like a Tank]:
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: Maintain the vision and continue building.

### PROCESS: [Build Turret]
- Construct the turret using the same method as the tank's main body (frame and skin).

### PROCESS: [Create Wheels]
- Use cardboard concrete forms (16" diameter, 10" deep) for wheels.
- Attach 7 wheels per side.

### PROCESS: [Apply Camouflage]
- Tape the whole body in white for a snow camo look.
- Tape the tracks and area behind the wheels in cheap gray tape.
- Paint wheels black with a white hub.
- Use multiple shades of gray and black for the digital camo patterns.

### OUTPUT:
- The completed cardboard tank is ready for use.

### PROCESS: [Test Tank]
- Take the cardboard tank for a run, such as down a tube run.

### OUTPUT:
- Enjoy the fun experience with the cardboard tank.

### END:
- The process of building and enjoying the cardboard tank concludes.
```
