instruct00045.title: Multi-Color Monkey Fist
instruct00045.text: This multi-colored monkey's fist I discovered while trying to find out a way to remove flaws in the original monkey's fist when making turns from one direction to the next. I realized by cutting the cord it enabled me to use different colors and take out the flaw. In the next step I added a diagram on how to create the original monkey's fist for those that may be attempting this for the first time and want to see the difference between mine and the original. here you can see an illustration of a monkey's fist done all with one string. It was used originally as a heaving line for sailors. This one we will create is more for decorative purposes. Here, I have 3 pieces of para-cord, you may use rope or any knotting cord. Dice for the core of the monkey's fist. Pic or a pointed tool to help negotiate the material. This home made tool will aid you in tying a monkey's fist. It is easily made by cutting a wire clothes hanger with a pair of wire cutters and bending it into a "U" shape as shown in this picture. Now we can begin to start the monkeys fist. Start by holding a piece of cord as shown below as you begin to wrap the paracord around the tool you just made. Now you will make four complete turns making sure all sides have 4 strands before continuing to the next step. Now you will begin making the next wrap of color making your way around the gray with the orange as shown. Again making 4 complete rounds and making sure that each side have 4 strands showing. here you see the second layer taking shape after you have made your rounds. Now you will start with the final strands looping over and under the orange feeding the cord as you make 4 more rotations. before you completely finish the final strands slip in your core. This time I'm using dice as the core. In this step you will begin to tighten the cord. You will pull slack to work with and begin working the slack out of the line toward the other end of the blue cord. Remember, don't pull the cord too tight at first, your goal here is to only gradually snug up the cord one color at a time in a rotation while attempting to keep the other colors in mind by keeping the strands in shape and order. As you get the knot tighter, this is where the pic comes in handy, helping pull the cord. I know it sounds confusing and complicated, but the more of them you do the faster and better you get the hang of it. "ANY THING WORTH HAVING TAKES TIME TO ATTAIN". "ALSO, DON'T FORGET... YOU MUST GRADUALLY TIGHTEN EACH COLOR AND REPEAT THE PROCESS TO AVOID OVER TIGHTENING. IF YOU OVER TIGHTEN, IT WILL RESULT IN YOUR OTHER CORD TO DISFIGURE AND GET OUT OF ORDER." Now that you have the knot snug as I do here, you will start to cut and tuck . As illustrated, you can see that I have cut the blue cord and push the pic through on the opposite side to recess the cut end, to conceal it. HERE I USUALLY CUT ALL BUT THE LONGEST CORD AND USE IT TO TIE INTO A KNOT TO BE USED FOR A KEY CHAIN."Finishing: you may also add a touch of glue at the recessed cuts to keep it from moving, I have experimented with wetting the cord and letting it dry which also seems to tighten the cord even more. If you use water don't use it after just applying the glue, it will create a white pasty color and ruin the hidden effect. You can use the water technique and after drying use the water. I have mad them without using glue or water and they seem to last without coming undone.

```markdown
# Multi-Colored Monkey's Fist Creation Process

## START:
- Begin the process of creating a multi-colored monkey's fist.

## INPUT:
- Gather materials:
  - 3 pieces of para-cord (or rope/knotting cord)
  - Dice (for the core of the monkey's fist)
  - Pic or pointed tool (to help negotiate the material)
  - Homemade tool (made from a wire clothes hanger, cut and bent into a "U" shape)

## PROCESS: [Create the Tool for Monkey's Fist]
- Cut a wire clothes hanger with wire cutters.
- Bend the cut hanger into a "U" shape.

## PROCESS: [Start Wrapping the First Cord]
- Hold a piece of cord and wrap it around the homemade "U" shaped tool.
- Make four complete turns, ensuring all sides show 4 strands.

## PROCESS: [Add Second Color]
- Begin wrapping the second color (orange) around the first (gray).
- Make four complete turns with the orange cord, ensuring 4 strands on each side.

## PROCESS: [Add Third Color]
- Start with the final color, looping over and under the previous color (orange).
- Make four more rotations with the final color.
- Before finishing the final strands, insert the dice as the core.

## PROCESS: [Begin Tightening the Cord]
- Pull slack to create working room.
- Gradually tighten the cord, one color at a time, while maintaining the shape and order of the strands.

## DECISION: [Is the cord too tight?]
  - IF YES: Loosen slightly to avoid disfiguring and disorder of the other cords.
  - IF NO: Continue tightening.

## PROCESS: [Use the Pic]
- Use the pic to help pull and tighten the cord.

## PROCESS: [Cut and Tuck the Ends]
- Once the knot is snug, cut the excess cord.
- Use the pic to recess the cut end and conceal it.

## DECISION: [Is there a longest cord remaining?]
  - IF YES: Use it to tie a knot for a keychain.
  - IF NO: Proceed to finishing touches.

## PROCESS: [Finishing Touches]
- Optionally, add a touch of glue at the recessed cuts to secure them.
- Alternatively, wet the cord and let it dry to tighten it further.

## DECISION: [Has glue been applied?]
  - IF YES: Do not use water immediately after to avoid a white pasty effect.
  - IF NO: Proceed to use water if desired.

## OUTPUT:
- The final product is a multi-colored monkey's fist, potentially used as a decorative item or keychain.

## END:
- The process of creating a multi-colored monkey's fist is complete.
```

instruct00516.title: Rice Krispie Treat Watermelon
instruct00516.text: We were invited to a couple of 4th of July parties this year and needed a treat to bring. So I came up with the Rice Krispie Treat Watermelon. My kids love faux-foods, and this one we came up with on our own. Strawberry flavored marshmallow Rice Krispie treats with dried blueberry "seeds" covered with fondant. I used the standard Rice Krispie Ceral Treat recipe. I had to double it to make mini watermelon. So buy 1 large box of cereal and 2 bags of strawberry marshmallows. You still need to make in two separate batches to make it easier to handle. Watermelon Filling 3 Tablespoons of butter 6 Cups of Rice Krispie Treat Cereal 1 10 oz. bag of Kraft Jet-Puffed Strawberry Marshmallows 1/4 Cup of dried blueberries Watermelon Skin 8 oz of mini marshmallows (half a bag) 1 pound of powdered sugar water shortening (for your hands) The skin of the watermelon is made from fondant. Do not use pre-made fondant from a bucket. Make you own. The recipe I used is from Peggy Weaver's site.http://whatscookingamerica.net/PegW/Fondant.htm Just follow the directions on her site. It is the best tasting fondant and is easy to make. Once you have the base fondant made start adding color. I started with equal parts green and yellow. Add just a few drops at a time and work it in. Once you have a good yellowish-green put a third of it in a plastic bag. Now start darkening the remain 2/3 with more green and some blue. Again work in the colors a few drops at a time before adding more. If your green is too bright add a drop of red. Compare to you light green to judge your colors. Put the darker green in a baggie and place them in the refrigerator. Clean up from the previous step. I made my treats using the microwave. I first melted three tablespoons of butter. Then add one bag of StrawberryMallows and coat with butter. I heated them in 30 second increments. Stir in between each heating. After a minute most of them should be melted, if not continue to mix. There should be enough heat to melt the rest. I added about 5 drops of red food coloring, I wanted the inside to be a little more pink. Now add 6 cups of Rice Krispie Cereal. Stir them in with the dried blueberries. (Our first thought was to use chocolate chips, but they would have melted too easily.) Spread the mixture on to a greased cookie sheet to let it cool. Now repeat the recipe again and add the second batch on top of the first. When it has cooled enough to handle, roll it up into a log and cover with waxed paper. It needs to cool for an hour or longer. If it is too warm it will loose it's shape. Use your hands and starting shaping in to melon. My wife thought it looked like raw hamburger and my daughter thought it looked like a brain. If it holds it shape then your are ready for the fondant. If it starts to sag, let it dry out some more. Get the fondant it out and knead it some. It will warm up quickly. Use powdered sugar to keep it from sticking to the counter and rolling pin. I used a piece of plastic wrap to get the size I need to roll out. Make sure your stripes are in the right direction. Wrap the Rice Krispie shape up in the fondant and work out and seams. You can add more stripes over the green and just smooth them in. If it is getting sticky add a little powdered sugar and rub it in. If you have it outside slice it quick, the humidity make the "skin" stick together. It may not be as refreshing as a good watermelon, but you can make them year round.

```markdown
# Rice Krispie Treat Watermelon System Summary

## Ingredients and Materials
- Large box of Rice Krispie Cereal
- 2 bags of strawberry marshmallows
- 3 tablespoons of butter
- 1/4 cup dried blueberries
- 8 oz mini marshmallows
- 1 pound powdered sugar
- Water
- Shortening
- Red, green, yellow, and blue food coloring
- Wax paper
- Microwave
- Cookie sheet
- Rolling pin
- Plastic wrap

## Fondant Preparation (from Peggy Weaver's site)
- START:
  - INPUT: 8 oz mini marshmallows, 1 pound powdered sugar, water, shortening
  - PROCESS: Follow Peggy Weaver's fondant recipe to make the base fondant
  - OUTPUT: Base fondant
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the base fondant made?
    - Yes: Proceed to color the fondant
    - No: END

- PROCESS: Color the base fondant
  - INPUT: Green, yellow, blue, and red food coloring
  - PROCESS: Mix equal parts of green and yellow food coloring into the fondant
  - STORE: A third of the light green fondant in a plastic bag
  - PROCESS: Darken the remaining fondant with more green and some blue food coloring
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the green too bright?
    - Yes: Add a drop of red food coloring
    - No: Continue
  - OUTPUT: Light green and dark green fondant
  - STORE: Dark green fondant in a separate plastic bag
  - PROCESS: Refrigerate both fondants

## Rice Krispie Treat Watermelon Filling
- PROCESS: Make the watermelon filling in two separate batches
  - INPUT: 3 tablespoons of butter, 1 bag of strawberry marshmallows, red food coloring, 6 cups Rice Krispie Cereal, 1/4 cup dried blueberries
  - PROCESS: Melt butter in the microwave
  - PROCESS: Add marshmallows and coat with butter
  - PROCESS: Heat marshmallows in 30-second increments, stirring in between
  - PROCESS: Add red food coloring to the melted marshmallows
  - PROCESS: Stir in Rice Krispie Cereal and dried blueberries
  - OUTPUT: Rice Krispie mixture
  - PROCESS: Spread mixture onto a greased cookie sheet to cool
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the first batch cooled?
    - Yes: Repeat the recipe for the second batch
    - No: END

- PROCESS: Create the watermelon log
  - INPUT: Second batch of Rice Krispie mixture
  - PROCESS: Combine both batches into a log shape
  - PROCESS: Wrap the log in wax paper
  - PROCESS: Let it cool for an hour or more
  - DECISION [IF]: Does the log hold its shape?
    - Yes: Proceed to fondant wrapping
    - No: Let it dry out more

## Wrapping the Watermelon in Fondant
- PROCESS: Prepare the fondant for wrapping
  - INPUT: Light and dark green fondant, powdered sugar
  - PROCESS: Knead the fondant to warm it up
  - PROCESS: Use powdered sugar to prevent sticking
  - PROCESS: Roll out the fondant using plastic wrap as a size guide
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the fondant rolled out to the correct size?
    - Yes: Proceed to wrap the Rice Krispie log
    - No: Continue rolling

- PROCESS: Wrap the Rice Krispie log in fondant
  - INPUT: Rolled out fondant, Rice Krispie log
  - PROCESS: Cover the Rice Krispie shape with fondant
  - PROCESS: Work out any seams and add stripes as needed
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the fondant getting sticky?
    - Yes: Add powdered sugar and rub it in
    - No: Continue

- OUTPUT: Finished Rice Krispie Treat Watermelon
- DECISION [IF]: Will the treat be served outside?
  - Yes: Slice quickly due to humidity
  - No: Serve as desired
- END
```

instruct00535.title: How to Process Carob
instruct00535.text: Carob Trees grow all over North America. I was able to forage a shopping bag full for free from the streets in Los Angeles and process about 3 pounds of powder in one weekend. The stuff is fairly easy to process at home, with the proper equipment. It helps to have a dehydrator and a VitaMix or some other kind of high powered blender, but a regular blender and a low temp oven might just do as well. Clean your pods. They have probably been out in the world collecting all kinds of lovely smog and dust. I scrubbed 'em with some veggie wash. Carob is subject to mold and critters, but the ones I collected seemed pretty clean. I only picked the pods still on the trees, and only if they looked healthy and shiny. The pods are kind of hard, and you want to get the seeds out, so unless you are fanatical about keeping your carob raw, boil them for about 20 minutes. Once boiled, The pods can be slit with a sharp knife, longways to shuck the seeds. You are going to be eating the pods, not the seeds. You can even munch on the pods in this state as a kind of snack. The seeds are pretty uniform in size and really hard. One can further process these to make an emulsifier for smoothies and ice cream, or use them in bean bags. Once you have all your pods clean and de seeded, grind 'em up. I used a Cuisinart for this step. The pods are full of sugar, and if they are still damp from boiling that sugar can carmelize from the heat of blending. Then you end up with little sticky balls of sawdust, but that is ok, dried out these too will blend into powder. You can dry the ground pods in the oven at low temp or in a dehydrator overnight. The dryer the stuff, the smoother your powder. Don't rush this step, it is key! Once your dried gound pods are nice and crispy, whip it up in small batches in a blender. I used a VitaMix, and about one or two cups at a time. I sifted the finished powder, and re-ground anything that was too big to go through. This helps get any lumps out. That is about it! Now you can make delicious raw halvah like this with The zest and juice of one orange 1cup carob powder 3/4 cup of Tahini 2 tablespoons honey 1pinch of salt throw it all in a bowl, mix well, roll out and freeze. Cut into cubes when solid.

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Carob Powder Processing

## START:
### INPUT: Gather Carob Pods
- Collect healthy and shiny carob pods from trees.

### PROCESS: Clean the Carob Pods
- Scrub the collected carob pods with vegetable wash to remove dirt and smog.

### DECISION [IF]: Check for Mold and Critters
- IF carob pods are infested with mold or critters,
  - [ELSE]: Proceed if pods are clean.

### PROCESS: Boil the Carob Pods
- Boil the carob pods for approximately 20 minutes to soften.

### PROCESS: Remove Seeds from Pods
- Slit the boiled pods with a sharp knife to remove the seeds.

### DECISION [IF]: Decide to Eat Pods as Snack
- IF you want to eat the pods as a snack,
  - [ELSE]: Continue with processing for powder.

### PROCESS: Grind the Carob Pods
- Use a food processor (e.g., Cuisinart) to grind the deseeded pods into smaller pieces.

### DECISION [IF]: Check for Moisture in Ground Pods
- IF ground pods are damp and clumping,
  - OUTPUT: Dry the clumps to blend into powder later.
  - [ELSE]: Continue if ground pods are not damp.

### PROCESS: Dry the Ground Carob Pods
- Dry the ground pods using a dehydrator or an oven set to a low temperature overnight.

### PROCESS: Blend the Dried Ground Pods
- Blend the dried ground pods in small batches (1-2 cups at a time) using a high-powered blender (e.g., VitaMix).

### PROCESS: Sift the Carob Powder
- Sift the blended powder to remove any lumps.
- Re-grind any particles too large to pass through the sifter.

## OUTPUT: Carob Powder Ready for Use
- The carob powder is now ready for use in recipes.

## END: Carob Powder Processing Complete

# Additional Recipe for Raw Halvah Using Carob Powder

## INPUT: Ingredients for Raw Halvah
- Zest and juice of one orange
- 1 cup carob powder
- 3/4 cup of Tahini
- 2 tablespoons honey
- 1 pinch of salt

### PROCESS: Mix Ingredients for Halvah
- Combine all ingredients in a bowl and mix well.

### PROCESS: Shape and Freeze the Halvah
- Roll out the mixture and freeze until solid.

### PROCESS: Cut into Cubes
- Once frozen, cut the halvah into cubes.

## OUTPUT: Raw Halvah Ready to Eat
- The raw halvah is now ready to be enjoyed.

## END: Raw Halvah Preparation Complete
```

instruct00752.title: 1-ingredient Ice Cream
instruct00752.text: This ice cream recipe is almost too good to be believed - so rich, creamy and luscious, you'd never know it's fat-free, dairy-free, and with no added sugar or preservatives, is even good for you!It only takes one ingredient to make this dreamy dessert - can you guess what it is?? (without looking at the next step)You may argue that without dairy, this has no place being called "ice cream." But I challenge you to try this recipe, and tell me it doesn't taste EXACTLY like ice cream! Prepare to be amazed.Thanks to everyone who pointed out the link to thekitchn's great post on this time-honored recipe! Did you guess our secret ingredient?BANANAS! I find bananas that have turned brown work best for this. You may already peel and freeze your bananas for smoothies or breads or dipping in chocolate. Now you can use them to make this luscious ice cream in no time at all! At first, the bananas resist the blending. Don't panic.Chop them up a few at a time, adding more bit by bit. They'll reach that nice chunky stage that you can use in smoothies. But you're not done yet! Keep that blender running for another 3-4 minutes, and watch in amazement as what you once saw as frozen bananas turn into a rich, creamy, silky blend.AMAZED!!! For the first go-round, try this recipe as-is. Thereafter, feel free to consider this a blank canvas for all of your ice cream dreams. Try adding honey, chocolate syrup, maple syrup, peanut butter, flavored extracts, or additional frozen fruits! Go to town, and make sure you share your favorite remixes in the comments!

instruct00154.title: Backpacking Toiletries
instruct00154.text: Toiletries can take up quite some space and weight in your rucksack. Even "travel sized" products are often bulky and come in differently shaped containers making it difficult to pack them with as little empty space as possible...One nice solution is to fill everything you need in syringes, put a cap on the tip and cut off the plungers:Now you have uniform, space saving containers...You can fill them with just the right amounts for your trip...You see immediately how much is left...And they allow you to dose and ration precisely... Filling the syringes:High-viscosity liquids like toothpaste or shaving gel are best poured in from the back. Just remove the plunger completely...Filling from the back is also the best choice if the original containers opening is too small for the syringe. Just don't forget to put a cap on the tip first like I did just a few minutes ago ;-) Cutting the plunger:pull the plunger back until it almost falls out, then cut it off with a sharp knife...This saves a lot of space and more important: you can't spill the contents accidentially...Keep one of the plungers to squeeze the syringes and throw the rest away...Saving even more space:You can even cut the syringe itself if it is only partially filled and throw away the last plunger - just use your toothbrush as replacement... Sunscreen:I prefer transparent, alcohol based products - they have some advantages:Alcohol based sunscreen is very thin - it applies evenly and dries within seconds. But most important: you need much less compared to traditional products.They are easy to dilute with water. A 20ml syringe with 50 SPF alcohol based sunscreen can last several days if you need full protection and weeks if the conditions allow you to dilute it.Always take more sunscreen with you than you expect to need in the worst case. Running out of toothpaste or deodorant? well... shit happens... But running out of sunscreen can be serious trouble...Shaving gel:Don't use shaving foam - you can't put it out of its container for obvious reasons. Use shaving gel instead...Deodorant: Use liquid deodorant instead of spray. You'll need very little: 5ml is more than enough for a week...Toothbrush and razor cover:I also use a syringe as toothbrush and razor cover. It protects them from dirt but still allows them to dry during the day...Measure the amounts you'll need before traveling:Put the original container on a scale and note its weight...Use the product for a few days...Weigh it again and divide the difference by the days you've used it...

instruct00277.title: Pinwheels - Easy Summer Lunch
instruct00277.text: Pinwheels - it seems are a popular appetizer people buy from the store and bring to events. But, every time I've had them in the past, the store-bought ones, I haven't liked them too much. They put some weird stuff in them. Sometimes less is more! :) I made these the other day for my son and he loved them! They're pretty filling and really simple to make - great for a summer day! Ingredients: Flatbread (I bought Pinwheel Lavash Flatbread - near the Deli at Walmart) Lunch Meat - turkey, chicken - or whatever you like Lettuce Cheese slices Cream Cheese - the whipped variety is easiest to spread *Optional - you can add anything else that you like! This is pretty simple. Take out the cream cheese and spread it on the flatbread. It's ok if you want to go easy on it - but be sure to have it coating the flabread at both edges of the bread (so it will not fall apart). After coating it with cream cheese, then you'll want to take out your lunch-meat. Add a nice little layer of lunch meat at the left edge of your flatbread. Try to keep it within 3-4 inches of the edge. Then put lettuce on top of that and cheese to top it off. Fold the pinwheel tightly over itself two times. Then, you can add more toppings. I add a little more meat and lots of lettuce. If you skimp out on the lettuce, it will taste too dry. This gives it some great texture and crunch! Finish folding it up to the end. Then, use a sharp knife to cut it into slices and you are done! I really didn't need to add anything else to it - they were very delicious with these few simple ingredients! I Hope you enjoy them!

instruct00088.title: Brownie Recipe
instruct00088.text: The easiest brownie recipe for making perfect brownies every time. This recipe produces a rich, well-balanced chocolate brownie with a perfect crust. WhileI like them fudgey and gooey with a crisp top, there are simple alterations you can make for a cakier or softer result. Use this recipe as your platform for customizing your perfect brownie! Making brownies from scratch doesn't have to be hard. Don't be afraid of flour and chocolate - the rewards you reap will be well worth the effort. Hardware: Scale - with this scale, you'll never need a set of measuring cups again. It's so much easier, and more accurate! Mixing bowls9x13" baking pan I love my Kitchenaid, but a wooden spoon works just as well for this recipe Rubber spatula WhiskSoftware: 1 cup (225 g) butter, melted 3 cups (600 g) white sugar 1 tablespoon (15 mL) vanilla extract 4 eggs (add one more for a cakier result) 1 1/2 cups (180 g) all-purpose flour 1 cup (70 g) unsweetened cocoa powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon baking soda (to give them a nice crust - omit if you don't want that) 6 oz chopped semisweet chocolate or 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips (180 g)Scoochmaroo is a participant in the Amazon Services LLC Associates Program, an affiliate advertising program designed to provide a means for sites to earn advertising fees by advertising and linking to amazon.com. Preheat oven to 350oF (175o C). Melt butter in the microwave or on the stovetop. Lightly grease a 9x13 baking dish with the paper from the butter. It's a real time saver to measure everything before you get started. So get out that scale and a couple bowls, and let's get everything ready! Turn on your scale, and place the bowl for your sugar on it. Tare the scale so it reads 0g. Pour in the sugar until it reaches 600g. Repeat for the flour and cocoa. You can tare the scale again after adding the flour and before adding the cocoa, but I just added the numbers together to get the weight I'd need. Whisk flour and cocoa together with soda and salt. See, you never need to dirty up measuring cups again! Combine the melted butter, sugar, and vanilla in a large bowl. Mix! Beat in the eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each, until thoroughly blended. Gradually stir in the flour and cocoa mixture on low speed. Toss the chocolate chips in a light dusting of flour, and stir into the mix with a spoon or spatula. The flour will keep them suspended in the batter and prevent them from all sinking to the bottom! Pour into prepared pan. Spread the batter in the pan, slightly mounding on the sides so it will all bake evenly (avoiding the typical mound you get in the middle after baking). Bake for 35-40 minutes. The brownies are done when a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean. My batch initially crowned well over the pan, but later sunk back down into dense fudgey deliciousness. Enjoy hot with a cool glass of milk or a la mode!

```markdown
# Brownie Recipe System

## Ingredients (Software)
- 1 cup (225 g) butter, melted
- 3 cups (600 g) white sugar
- 1 tablespoon (15 mL) vanilla extract
- 4 eggs (add one more for a cakier result)
- 1 1/2 cups (180 g) all-purpose flour
- 1 cup (70 g) unsweetened cocoa powder
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon baking soda (optional for crust)
- 6 oz chopped semisweet chocolate or 1 cup (180 g) semisweet chocolate chips

## Equipment (Hardware)
- Scale
- Mixing bowls
- 9x13" baking pan
- Wooden spoon or mixer
- Rubber spatula
- Whisk

## Instructions
START:
- Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
- Melt butter in the microwave or on the stovetop.
- Lightly grease a 9x13 baking dish using the butter wrapper.

PROCESS: Measuring Ingredients
- Turn on the scale and place a bowl on it.
- Tare the scale to read 0g.
- INPUT: Add sugar until the scale reads 600g.
- Repeat taring and measuring for flour and cocoa powder.
- OUTPUT: Prepared sugar, flour, and cocoa mix.

PROCESS: Mixing Dry Ingredients
- Whisk together flour, cocoa, salt, and optionally baking soda in a bowl.
- OUTPUT: Dry ingredients mix.

PROCESS: Mixing Wet Ingredients
- In a large bowl, combine melted butter, sugar, and vanilla.
- Beat in eggs one at a time, ensuring each is well mixed before adding the next.
- OUTPUT: Wet ingredients mix.

PROCESS: Combining Wet and Dry Ingredients
- Gradually stir in the dry ingredients into the wet mix on low speed until thoroughly blended.
- OUTPUT: Brownie batter.

PROCESS: Preparing Chocolate Chips
- Toss chocolate chips with a light dusting of flour.
- Stir chocolate chips into the batter using a spoon or spatula.
- OUTPUT: Final brownie batter.

PROCESS: Baking
- Pour batter into the prepared baking pan.
- Spread batter evenly, with a slight mound on the sides.
- Bake for 35-40 minutes.
- DECISION [IF]: Is a toothpick inserted in the middle clean after being removed?
  - Yes: OUTPUT: Baked brownies.
  - No: PROCESS: Continue baking, check periodically.

END:
- Enjoy brownies hot with milk or a la mode.
```

instruct00114.title: Air-dry Clay Ornaments
instruct00114.text: If you discover how easy it is to use air-dry clay you will never have to buy small decor ornaments and accessories ever again! In this tutorial featured on Home-Dzine.co.za I am going to show you how easy and simple it is to make your own decor accessories using air-dry clay. Cut off a piece of clay and mold this into a circular shape for the base of your candleholder. Mine is 5cm in diameter and 5mm thick. This part will be the thickest part and will provide strength for the layered leaves. Break off another pieces of clay for the first leaf. This does not need to be as thick as the base, make it about 2mm thick. Use your fingers and thumb to shape it. If you need to smooth out any defects, dip your finger into a little water to work the surface of the clay. Repeat the previous step to add more leaves. Press each leaf firmly to the base so that it all sticks securely together. Again, if you need to smooth out any defects, a wet finger works well. A small container with water and the rounded end of a paintbrush can be used to press down and smooth out before you put the candleholder in a sunny spot to dry out during the day. Once dry, spray on a couple of coats of Rust-Oleum 2X gloss spray paint in your choice of colour. Wasn't that easy!

```markdown
## START:
- Begin the process to create a candleholder using air-dry clay.

## PROCESS: Prepare the Workspace
- Ensure that the workspace is clean and ready for crafting.

## INPUT: Gather Materials
- Air-dry clay
- Water container
- Paintbrush (rounded end)
- Rust-Oleum 2X gloss spray paint (color of choice)

- Cut off a piece of air-dry clay.

  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Adjust the clay size to meet the required dimensions.

## PROCESS: Mold the Base
- Shape the cut piece into a circular base for the candleholder.

## STORE: Set the Base Aside
- Place the base aside to prepare for adding leaves.

## PROCESS: Create the First Leaf
- Break off another piece of clay for the first leaf.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the leaf piece approximately 2mm thick?
  - Yes: Proceed to shape the leaf.
  - No: Adjust the clay thickness to approximately 2mm.

## PROCESS: Shape the Leaf
- Use fingers and thumb to shape the leaf.

## PROCESS: Smooth Out Defects
- Dip a finger into water if necessary to smooth out any defects in the clay.

## PROCESS: Attach the Leaf to the Base
- Press the first leaf firmly onto the base.

## DECISION [IF]: Are there any defects on the leaf after attachment?
  - Yes: Use a wet finger to smooth out defects.
  - No: Continue to add more leaves.

## PROCESS: Add Additional Leaves
- Repeat the leaf creation and attachment process for additional leaves.

## DECISION [IF]: Are all leaves attached and smoothed out?
  - Yes: Proceed to drying step.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the candleholder completely dry?
  - Yes: Proceed to painting step.
  - No: Allow more time to dry completely.

- Spray on a couple of coats of Rust-Oleum 2X gloss spray paint in the chosen color.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the paint coverage even and complete?
  - Yes: Proceed to the final step.
  - No: Apply additional coats of paint as needed.

## OUTPUT: Completed Candleholder
- The final product is a handmade candleholder, ready for use or decoration.

## END:
- The process of creating a candleholder with air-dry clay is complete.
```

instruct00439.title: Cleaning Your Oven Without Poisonous, Earth Destroying Chemicals
instruct00439.text: A few steps on how to quickly get rid of the grime and debris that make your kitchen smell horrible every time you turn on your oven.Things You Will NeedBaking SodaVinegarA bowl or a squirt bottle (Preferably a squirt bottle) A dirty oven A spatula First things first Remove the racks. Using a spatula, scrape up as much of the debris as you can, and throw it away. Most of the big stuff should come up pretty easy. Tip: move the trash can closer to the oven.... THEN Using about a cup of baking soda, more or less depending on the size of your oven, sprinkle it all over the floor of your oven. THEN This is where a squirt bottle comes in handy. Spray vinegar all over the baking soda. Use your fingers or a rubber spatula to spread the baking soda around so that it comes into contact with the vinegar and every dirty part of your oven floor. Let sit for 10-20 minutes. (alternative: Mix vinegar and baking soda in a bowl to form a paste, and then spread that over your oven floor. Make sure to pour the vinegar slowly because it fizzes up pretty high.) Get a scrubbing pad (I used one of those metal curly wiry ones...) and scrub in a CIRCULAR motion, rather than back and forth -- this will make your job go by so much more quickly. Grime should come off pretty easily... When you can slide the pad gently all over the oven floor and no longer feel any rough patches, you are ready to clean up the excess baking soda/vinegar mixture. Use a damp sponge and get it all out of there! You will have to keep rinsing off the sponge...

```markdown
# Oven Cleaning Process

## START:
- INPUT: Gather materials: baking soda, vinegar, bowl or squirt bottle, dirty oven, spatula, scrubbing pad, sponge.

## PROCESS: Remove Oven Racks
- Remove the racks from the oven.

## PROCESS: Scrape Debris
- Using a spatula, scrape up as much debris as possible.
- OUTPUT: Big debris should be removed.
- DECISION [IF]: Is trash can far from the oven?
  - Yes: Move trash can closer to the oven.
  - No: Continue to the next step.

## PROCESS: Apply Baking Soda
- INPUT: Measure about a cup of baking soda (adjust quantity based on oven size).
- Sprinkle baking soda all over the floor of the oven.

## PROCESS: Apply Vinegar
- DECISION [IF]: Are you using a squirt bottle?
  - Yes: Spray vinegar over the baking soda.
  - No: Mix vinegar and baking soda in a bowl to form a paste.
    - DECISION [IF]: Is the vinegar fizzing up when mixed?
      - Yes: Pour vinegar slowly.
      - No: Continue to mix to appropriate consistency.
- Spread the mixture or sprayed baking soda with fingers or rubber spatula to cover the dirty parts of the oven floor.

## PROCESS: Let Mixture Sit
- Let the mixture sit for 10-20 minutes.

## PROCESS: Scrub Oven Floor
- INPUT: Use a scrubbing pad (preferably metal curly wiry one).
- Scrub the oven floor in a circular motion.
- OUTPUT: Grime should be loosened and removed.
- DECISION [IF]: Are there any rough patches left?
  - Yes: Continue scrubbing.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

## PROCESS: Clean Up Mixture
- INPUT: Use a damp sponge to clean up the excess baking soda/vinegar mixture.
- OUTPUT: Oven floor is cleaned of the mixture.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the sponge getting dirty?
  - Yes: Rinse the sponge and continue cleaning.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

## END:
- The oven cleaning process is complete. Oven should be free of grime and debris.
```

instruct00522.title: How to Unclog Sink Pipes
instruct00522.text: My sink took 15 minutes to fully drain. This, needless to say, was getting ridiculous. So I cleaned it out. This instructable will show you how to remove all that gunk that's keeping your sink from draining properly, without pouring nasty chemicals down the drain that cost monies and kill all the good bugs in the septic tank.This isn't for the faint of heart, however. I have a strong stomach, but this one made me gag. So this might be a job you sweettalk/bribe/force someone else to do for you. ;-) You will need:Pliers or other pinchy thingLong screwdriver or other poky thingBucket O' HappinessTowels or other absorbant thingsA strong stomachAn air freshenerMusic/podcasts to take your mind off thingsIf you are a (Wo)Man, you will not need any of the last three items. If you are a Wuss, you will need all of them. If you are a Muss, you could turn on the bathroom fan and hum to yourself. Unscrew the pipes under the sink and set aside the ones that can come completely out. They will have water in them, so set the bucket on some towels and hold underneath to catch the water. Now take the pliers and screwdriver and poke, pull, push and scrape alll the disgusting goo and hair out of the sink, and dump it right in that Bucket O' Happiness. Be sure to get the bottom pipe leading from the sink as well as all the stuff out of the top. Remember those pipes we laid aside in the first step?Oh. No, that's okay. I'll wait here. I should have told you we weren't throwing them away forever. It sure looked like we were.Got 'em?Alrighty then, take them outside (so you don't start a horrible game of musical pus by dumping the goo from one sink down another so you have to clean up that sink) and spray them out with a hose. Put all the pipes back the way they were and screw all fittings nice and tight. Run the water to make sure the pipes are clear and there are no leaks.That's it, you're done! Go reward yourself with something awesome. You deserve it. You totally do. This was not a fun job.

```markdown
# Sink Drain Cleaning Process

## START:
- Begin the process of cleaning the sink drain.

## INPUT:
- Gather the required tools and materials:
  - Pliers or other pinchy tool
  - Long screwdriver or other poky tool
  - Bucket (referred to as "Bucket O' Happiness")
  - Towels or other absorbent materials
  - Optional: Air freshener, music/podcasts, and a resilient attitude

## PROCESS: Prepare Work Area
- Place towels on the floor to protect the area and prepare for any water spillage.
- Position the Bucket O' Happiness underneath the sink pipes to catch draining water.

## PROCESS: Disassemble Sink Pipes
- Use pliers to unscrew the pipes under the sink.
- Carefully remove pipes that can be fully detached, being cautious of the water inside.

## STORE:
- Set aside the detached pipes in a safe location, ensuring not to discard them.

## PROCESS: Clean Sink and Pipes
- With the pliers and screwdriver, remove all debris from the sink and remaining pipes.
- Scrape out the gunk, hair, and any other obstructions.
- Dispose of the collected waste into the Bucket O' Happiness.

## DECISION: Are there pipes set aside that need cleaning?
- IF Yes: Proceed to cleaning the detached pipes.
- ELSE No: Skip to checking for leaks.

## PROCESS: Clean Detached Pipes
- Take the detached pipes outside.
- Use a hose to spray and clean the inside of the pipes thoroughly.

## PROCESS: Reassemble Sink Pipes
- Reattach all cleaned pipes under the sink.
- Tighten all fittings securely to ensure they are properly reassembled.

## PROCESS: Test for Functionality
- Run water through the sink to test the drainage.
- Observe if the water drains smoothly without any backups.

## DECISION: Is the water draining properly without leaks?
- IF Yes: Proceed to final step.
- ELSE No: Re-tighten pipes and re-test until the issue is resolved.

## OUTPUT:
- A clean and fully functional sink drain with proper water flow and no leaks.

## END:
- The sink drain cleaning process is complete.
- Reward yourself for completing this challenging task.
```

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Blog Post: Making Beef Stuffed Dough

## Ingredients:
- Flour: 5 1/2 cups
- Oil: 1 cup (plus some for the table)
- Warm Water: 2 cups
- Black Pepper: 1/4 teaspoon (plus 1 teaspoon for stuffing)
- Salt: 1 teaspoon (plus 2 teaspoons for stuffing)
- Chopping Beef: 3/4 kilogram
- Tomatoes: 2 big (seeded and chopped)
- Green Pepper: 2 big (chopped)
- Carrot: 1 big (chopped)
- Onion: 1 big (chopped)
- Celery: Some (chopped)
- Paprika: 1 teaspoon
- Beef Spice: 1 teaspoon

## Process Steps:

### Dough Preparation:
START:
- INPUT: Flour, 1 cup Oil, Warm Water, 1/4 teaspoon Black Pepper, 1 teaspoon Salt
- PROCESS: Mix flour, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 cup oil together.
- PROCESS: Gradually add 2 cups warm water and mix well with hands.
- PROCESS: Divide the dough into 16 equal parts.
- PROCESS: Let the dough parts rest.
- END of Dough Preparation.

### Stuffing Preparation:
- INPUT: Beef, Tomatoes, Green Pepper, Carrot, Onion, Celery, 1 teaspoon Black Pepper, 1 teaspoon Paprika, 1 teaspoon Beef Spice, 2 teaspoons Salt
- PROCESS: Prepare and chop the vegetables - tomatoes, green pepper, onion, carrot, and celery.
- PROCESS: Add 1 teaspoon black pepper, 1 teaspoon paprika, 1 teaspoon beef spice, and 2 teaspoons salt to the beef.
- PROCESS: Mix the chopped vegetables with the seasoned beef.
- PROCESS: Divide the meat mixture into 16 equal parts.
- END of Stuffing Preparation.

### Assembly and Cooking:
- PROCESS: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
- PROCESS: Place some oil on the table.
- PROCESS: Take a ball of dough and roll it out into a circle on the oiled table.
- INPUT: One part of the meat mixture.
- PROCESS: Place one part of the meat mixture in the center of the rolled-out dough.
- PROCESS: Shape the meat mixture into a circle.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the dough fully enclosing the meat mixture?
  - YES: Continue to the next step.
  - NO: Adjust the dough to fully enclose the meat.
- PROCESS: Place the stuffed dough on a baking tray.
- PROCESS: Repeat the assembly process for the remaining dough and meat parts.
- PROCESS: Bake in the preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
- OUTPUT: Cooked beef-stuffed dough.
- END of Assembly and Cooking.

### Serving:
- PROCESS: Serve the beef-stuffed dough hot.
- PROCESS: Accompany with a vegetable salad if desired.
- END of Serving.

## Final Output:
- OUTPUT: Beef-stuffed dough ready to be served hot with an optional side of vegetable salad.
END of Process.
```

instruct00682.title: How to Make a Latte
instruct00682.text: Most of us are avid coffee drinkers; am I right? I thought so. I will explain how to make a simple milk and coffee drink, also called a latte. For this process, I will be using an espresso machine, a grinder, coffee beans and last but not least, milk. The very first thing that needs to be done is turning on the espresso machine.The "on" switch is on the right-hand side of the machine, located towards the back, on the lower half. Make sure to switch on the steamer as well, for later. For pulling an espresso, usually wait until it's up to 200 F. Once it heats up, it's ready to go! Step number two is grinding the beans.Use beans made especially for espresso pulling, usually it says so on the package. The grinder has settings depending on how fine the grounds are wanted, recommended is a fineness that resembles salt. Take the portafilter and set it into the grinder machine prongs to make sure it stays in place. Grind about 18 grams of coffee, using a scale to weigh. Alright, on to step number three! This is an important one.Once the portafilter is taken out of the grinder put it on a scale; the grounds should weigh about 18 grams. Before making the shot, pack it in. In coffee terms that means to tamp. To do this, just press down into the portafilter with a coffee tamper with about 30lbs of force for a few seconds. This process ensures uniformity of extraction by evening out and packing the grounds to ensure equal, consistent water contact when it is forced through the portafilter. Now it's time to pull a lovely shot of espresso! One step closer to enjoying a delicious latte. For this step, just set it into the espresso machine and lock it in place. The handle should be turned slightly to the left, pushed up into the machine then turn it the right, centering it, to secure it. Next, pull the lever up and wait as the water gets pushed through the portafilter. This will take about 20-30 seconds for a single shot. Once the shot is done, pull the lever back down to the starting position. Take the shot of espresso and pour it into any cup. Time to turn this into a latte! Do not just pour the milk in; it needs to be steamed. Pour the milk into a frothing pitcher and then submerge the froth assistor deep into milk. Turn the steamer on and let it do its thing. Get a thermometer and check the temperature of the milk, which should be around 140 F. Be careful not to burn the milk, it will ruin the shot. Go ahead and pour the milk into the cup with the espresso and enjoy.

```markdown
# Making a Latte Using an Espresso Machine

## System Inputs:
- Espresso machine
- Grinder
- Coffee beans (especially for espresso)
- Milk
- Portafilter
- Coffee tamper
- Scale
- Cup
- Frothing pitcher
- Thermometer

## System Outputs:
- A freshly made latte

## Process:

### START:
- Turn on the espresso machine and steamer.

### PROCESS: Heating the Espresso Machine
- Wait for the espresso machine to heat up to 200 F.

### PROCESS: Grinding the Coffee Beans
- INPUT: Coffee beans into the grinder.
- Set the grinder to the fineness level resembling salt.
- Place the portafilter in the grinder machine prongs.
- Grind about 18 grams of coffee using a scale for accuracy.

### PROCESS: Tamping the Coffee Grounds
- Remove the portafilter from the grinder.
- Confirm if the grounds weigh approximately 18 grams.
- Tamp the grounds with about 30lbs of force to ensure even extraction.

### PROCESS: Pulling the Espresso Shot
- Lock the portafilter into the espresso machine.
- Pull the lever up to start water flow through the portafilter.
- Wait for 20-30 seconds for the espresso shot to be pulled.
- Push the lever back down to stop the flow.

### OUTPUT: Espresso Shot
- Pour the shot of espresso into a cup.

### PROCESS: Steaming the Milk
- Pour milk into a frothing pitcher.
- Submerge the froth assistor into the milk.
- Turn on the steamer.
- Monitor the temperature of the milk to reach 140 F.

### DECISION: Is the milk temperature 140 F?
- IF Yes: Proceed to next step.
- IF No: Continue steaming until 140 F is reached.

### PROCESS: Combining Milk and Espresso
- Pour the steamed milk into the cup with the espresso shot.

### OUTPUT: Latte
- Enjoy the freshly made latte.

### END
```

instruct00476.title: QR Code Love Note Needlepoint
instruct00476.text: True Geek Love Valentine's Gift!! 1 - Cross stitch material 2 - Crochet thread 3 - Large eye needle 4 - Embroidery hoop 5 - Square frame All the stitch counts and size of material depends on the size of frame being used. I found a 10"x10" frame with 7.5"x7.5" opening. The crochet thread is heavier than embroidery thread so it was faster to fill in the spaces and complete the project. 1 - install a scan app onto your smartphone that can scan QR codes and also try to sneak the app onto your Valentine's phone. 2 - Google search to find one of many free QR code generators 3 - generate your QR code love note and download it The downloaded QR code has a white background and I planned on using Excel to help me visually keep track of my stitches. I suppose you could directly transfer/draw the QR code onto the fabric but I didn't want pencil markings to show. Below I will show how to use either Photoshop or Powerpoint to quickly edit your QR code before placing it into Excel. Also, I suppose there may be software out there to quickly create needlepoint patterns but this is an easy work around for those who don't have it. And I never did needlepoint before this project. So I winged it! 1 - open your QR code in Photoshop 2 - select it and copy into the clipboard 3 - open a new Photoshop canvas with the settings: Preset: Clipboard Background Contents: Transparent 4 - paste in the QR code 5 - use the magic wand to select and delete all the white areas 6 - save your now transparent background QR code as a png format For people who don't have Photoshop but have access to PowerPoint either at home or at work. 1 - open a new Powerpoint slide 2 - inert QR code 3 - format slide background to change the color to anything but white 4 - select the QR code and go to the Format tab 5 - select Recolor and Set Transparent Color 6 - select the white background to remove it 7 - right-click on your altered QR code and save it as a png format 1 - Open a blank Excel sheet 2 - insert your QR code with the transparent background 3 - resize the QR code as big as you need it to be for you to see the excel cells as stitch markers 4 - resize the Excel rows and columns to line up to the QR code squares I made a 4x4 stitch for every square of the QR code. In the sample QR code shown here it will be 100 x100 stitches when complete. So I also numbered the Excel Rows and Columns by 4s to see the total number of stitches. Having this on the computer screen I could make it as large as I needed to see the stitch count and pattern so it was much easier to see than a small print out. Using the thicker Crochet thread helped to fill in the areas quickly and I didn't need to use a cross stitch either. I used a simple "half-cross" or diagonal stitch. Fold the edges to fit within the frame being used and press flat. Frame it and place it somewhere for your Valentine to find. My Valentine now keeps this on his desk to remind him of his Geek Love!

instruct00574.title: Farmhouse Coat Hanger From Pallet Wood
instruct00574.text: In this instructable I will show you how I made a farmhouse style coat hanger all from reclaimed pallet wood. This reclaimed pallet wood project is relatively simple to make with no fancy joinery or woodworking skills need.First you will need to dismantle 1 or 2 pallets. You will also want to clean and prep the planks by removing all nails or screws, also give the wood a good sanding. (Planks size 4 x 1 inch)My household has four members, so I'm going to use four hooks and have four cubby holes, but you can make yours to suit.I then cut four planks to length for the backboard (30 inch) and attached them together with PVA wood glue and dowels. clamped and left to dry.Next I worked on the shelf and cubby holes section. Each cubby hole is approx 6 x 4 inch. I also left the top shelf overhanging about 1 inch. (see images)Once the shelving section was complete, I then attached the two parts together using more PVA and screws.I then gave it some more sanding, working up the grades to about 240 grit. Once I was happy with the sanding surface I gave it a coat of Danish oil.Now for the hooks. I eyeballed the hooks so they were evenly spaced and screwed them in.To finish I mounted to the wall. Be sure to watch the YouTube video for a better understanding.More pallet wood projects from me BearWoodWorkJobs a gooden...

instruct00442.title: Cardboard Folder/creaser
instruct00442.text: I like to make stuff from cardboard. from cutting down a big box to a smaller one for shipping, to making props, storage solutions etc. The hard part with corrugated cardboard is in bending it nicely. someone else has shown how to cut the inside ply and corrugations to make a neat bend, but I have a problem with that method. #1 it's weak, and #2 Have you ever seen a commercially made box made that way? I used to try holding a yardstick down on it and bending up that way, but it was very unpredictable and often I got poor results. At some point I took a straight board and cut a bevel on one edge to crease the bend. it worked sorta. since the pressure was spread over a large area,I had to really lean on it hard.the sharpsquare end made it hard tooextend the crease if a long fold was needed. Recently, I had an epiphany! If a made the creaser curved like a pizza knife, it would apply the pressure to a small area at a time and it would require a lot less force to do the job. Also, if I needed a long fold, the curve would let me ease out of and back into the work for a smoother transition. I used a scrap of MDF 1x6 trim board. Mostly because it's what I had and it's easy to work. also it's stable and wont cup or twist.any wood would work if it is flat. solid wood is stronger and hardwood probably would last longer. I cut a piece about 18" long and about 4 1/2" wide. To mark the curve, I put a small nail about 2" down from one edge, one on each end of my piece. I then used a thin strip of wood about 1/4" thick and 3/4"wide as a spline and layed it against the two nails then bowed it to the curve I wanted and marked it with a pencil. Simple step, cut the curve. I used a jigsaw, but you could use a coping saw, scroll saw, bandsaw, or whatever you have. Probably not a chainsaw. You now need to make the curved edge a sharp V. this is what creases the cardboard for a neat bend.. I did this by hand with a block plane. You could use a router with a chamfer bit, or just carve it with a utility knife. You could also have tilted the table on your scrollsaw or bandsaw when you cut the curve. The angle is not critical as long as the point is fairly sharp and straight. To start, I used a pencil and finger guide to mark a line about1/8" from the edge both on the edge and the face. then I planed to the line. Now I flipped the board over and planed a bigger taper to meet that one and make the point. On the first model, I made the V centered on the board, and it worked, but I had to stand on my head to see the line. Thus on this model I moved the point over close to one side for visiblility sake. For durability, you might want to soak up the mdf with some shellac or wood hardener, but I didn't. it's simple enough to make another if I wear this one out. Now just get your piece of corrugated, and mark a line where you want to bend it. Start with the tool rocked up on one end of the line and roll it down the line. that's it! If you need a longer fold than the tool, just move it over and start again. Now that you have it creased, just grab your cardboard and fold. NIce straight clean bend every time.

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Cardboard Bending Blog Post

## System Overview
The system described in the blog post is a method for creating neat bends in corrugated cardboard. The process involves creating a custom tool from MDF or any flat, stable wood that will allow for an easier and more precise bending process compared to traditional methods.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin with the intention to create neat bends in corrugated cardboard.

### INPUT: Materials and Tools
- Corrugated cardboard
- MDF or any flat, stable wood
- Nails
- Thin strip of wood (spline)
- Jigsaw or other saws (coping saw, scroll saw, bandsaw)
- Block plane, router with chamfer bit, or utility knife
- Pencil
- Optional: Shellac or wood hardener for durability

### PROCESS: Create the Bending Tool
1. Cut a piece of MDF or wood approximately 18" long and 4 1/2" wide.
2. Drive two small nails about 2" down from one edge at both ends of the piece.
3. Use the spline to create a curve between the nails and trace with a pencil.
4. Cut the curve using the jigsaw or another appropriate saw.
5. Create a sharp V-edge along the curve to act as the creasing edge.
   - Mark a line about 1/8" from the edge on the face and edge of the board.
   - Plane to the marked line to create the initial angle.
   - Flip the board and plane a larger taper to meet the initial angle and form a sharp point.
   - Adjust the point location closer to one side for visibility.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the tool meant for long-term use?
- IF YES: Apply shellac or wood hardener to the MDF for durability.
- IF NO: Proceed without applying hardener.

### PROCESS: Use the Tool to Bend Cardboard
1. Mark a line on the corrugated cardboard where the bend is desired.
2. Position the tool at one end of the line, with the V-edge facing down.
3. Roll the tool down the line, applying pressure to crease the cardboard.
4. DECISION [IF]: Is the fold longer than the tool?
   - IF YES: Move the tool over and continue the crease.
   - IF NO: Proceed to the next step.
5. Fold the cardboard along the crease to achieve a neat bend.

### OUTPUT:
- A neatly bent piece of corrugated cardboard with a straight, clean fold.

### END:
- The process concludes once the desired bend is achieved in the cardboard.
```

instruct00319.title: Fried Tomato Sandwiches.
instruct00319.text: Thick slices of large, hard, red tomatoes. Filled with creamcheese and garlic, parsley, salt - pepper. Ingredients: 4 Tomatoes 1 egg 1/2 cup flour 1/2 cup breadcrumbs 1/2 cup parsley 1 pack cream-cheese 1 clove of garlic salt pepper Cut tomatoes in thick slices. Chop parsley. Combine flour and breadcrumbs. Mix cream-cheese with parsley and pressed clove of garlic. Beat the egg. Fill tomatoes with one teaspoon of mixture. Make sandwich. Dip in beaten egg. Then dip in flour mixture. Fry on both sides. Flip carefully! As you remove the sandwhiches from frying pan place them on paper napkin to absorb excess oil. Serve immediately. Finger licking good !! :)

```markdown
# Comprehensive Step-by-Step Representation of Tomato and Cream Cheese Sandwiches

## Ingredients:
- 4 large, hard, red tomatoes
- 1 egg
- 1/2 cup flour
- 1/2 cup breadcrumbs
- 1/2 cup parsley
- 1 pack cream cheese
- 1 clove of garlic
- Salt
- Pepper

## Instructions:

### START:
- Begin the process of making tomato and cream cheese sandwiches.

### PROCESS: Prepare Ingredients
- INPUT: Wash and dry 4 large, hard, red tomatoes.
- INPUT: Chop 1/2 cup of parsley.
- INPUT: Peel and press 1 clove of garlic.
- INPUT: Measure 1/2 cup of flour and 1/2 cup of breadcrumbs, then combine them in a bowl.
- INPUT: Take 1 pack of cream cheese.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the pack of cream cheese at room temperature?
  - Yes: Proceed to next step.
  - No: Let the cream cheese soften at room temperature before proceeding.

### PROCESS: Make Cream Cheese Mixture
- PROCESS: Mix the softened cream cheese with the chopped parsley and pressed clove of garlic in a bowl.
- PROCESS: Season the mixture with salt and pepper to taste.
- OUTPUT: Cream cheese mixture is ready.

### PROCESS: Prepare Tomatoes
- PROCESS: Cut the tomatoes into thick slices.
- DECISION [IF]: Are the slices approximately the same thickness?
  - Yes: Proceed to next step.
  - No: Adjust the thickness of the slices for consistency.

### PROCESS: Beat the Egg
- INPUT: Crack 1 egg into a bowl.
- PROCESS: Beat the egg until well mixed.
- OUTPUT: Beaten egg is ready for use.

### PROCESS: Assemble Sandwiches
- PROCESS: Place one teaspoon of the cream cheese mixture on a tomato slice.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture spread evenly?
  - Yes: Place another tomato slice on top to make a sandwich.
  - No: Spread the mixture evenly before proceeding.

### PROCESS: Coat Sandwiches
- PROCESS: Dip each tomato sandwich in the beaten egg, ensuring it is well coated.
- PROCESS: Then dip the egg-coated sandwich in the flour and breadcrumb mixture.
- OUTPUT: Tomato sandwiches are coated and ready to fry.

### PROCESS: Fry Sandwiches
- INPUT: Preheat the frying pan over medium heat.
- PROCESS: Carefully place the coated tomato sandwiches in the pan.
- PROCESS: Fry on one side until golden brown.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the underside golden brown?
  - Yes: Carefully flip the sandwich to fry the other side.
  - No: Continue frying until golden brown, then flip.

### PROCESS: Remove and Drain Sandwiches
- PROCESS: Once both sides are golden brown, remove the sandwiches from the frying pan.
- PROCESS: Place them on a paper napkin to absorb excess oil.
- OUTPUT: Tomato sandwiches are cooked and drained of excess oil.

### END: Serve Immediately
- OUTPUT: Serve the hot and crispy tomato and cream cheese sandwiches immediately for best taste.
- Finger licking good!
```

instruct00213.title: Skateboard Bookshelf
instruct00213.text: The skateboard bookshelf can be made from new or old skateboard decks. With just a bit of time you can have a neat adjustable-height bookcase that will make your friends envious. Perfect for the dorm or as a holiday present for your favorite skater. for this project you will need: 2 threaded rods 16 bolts 16 washers 2 L shelf brackets drill or right angle driver (we used a Craftsman RAID) 2 skateboards Our threaded rods were a bit big for the skateboard truck holes so we expanded the holes with our RAID driver. First put nuts about 4 inches up. Put a washer on each one. Put the rod through the first skateboard, and then put another nut on the opposite side. Make sure the rods are even and tighten down. Screw on 4 more nuts to the other side and slide the skateboard onto that side. Go about 7 inches down. And again, tighten down the bolts. Next you want to attach the L brackets to the bottom of the top deck. A drill isn't likely to fit between the decks; this is the real reason we used the right angle driver. Finally, attach it to the wall and fill it with your favorite books! Show off the art on the bottom of your old skateboard decks, and bask in the admiration of your friends. If you need to adjust the bookshelf height, just move the bolts, slide the deck, and retighten in the new position.

```markdown
# Skateboard Bookshelf System

## Summary Representation

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a skateboard bookshelf.

### INPUT: Materials and Tools Required
- 2 threaded rods
- 16 bolts
- 16 washers
- 2 L shelf brackets
- Drill or right angle driver (Craftsman RAID)
- 2 skateboards

### PROCESS: Preparing the Skateboard Decks
- Use the RAID driver to expand the holes in the skateboard decks if the threaded rods are too big to fit.

### PROCESS: Assembling the Rods and Decks
- PLACE NUTS: Put nuts about 4 inches up on the threaded rods.
- ADD WASHERS: Place a washer on each of the nuts.
- INSERT RODS: Put the rod through the first skateboard.
- SECURE WITH NUTS: Add another nut on the opposite side of the first skateboard and tighten down to ensure the rods are even.

### PROCESS: Adjusting the Height of the Second Deck
- ATTACH NUTS: Screw on 4 more nuts to the other side of the threaded rods.
- SLIDE ON DECK: Slide the second skateboard onto the rods.
- SET HEIGHT: Position the second skateboard approximately 7 inches below the first one.
- TIGHTEN BOLTS: Tighten down the bolts to secure the second skateboard in place.

### PROCESS: Attaching L Brackets to the Top Deck
- DECISION [IF]: Is there enough space to use a regular drill between the decks?
  - IF YES: Use the drill to attach the L brackets to the bottom of the top deck.
  - IF NO: Use the right angle driver to attach the L brackets due to limited space.

### PROCESS: Mounting the Bookshelf to the Wall
- MOUNT: Securely attach the L brackets to the wall to hang the bookshelf.

### OUTPUT: Completed Skateboard Bookshelf
- Display the skateboard bookshelf on the wall and fill it with your favorite books.

### PROCESS: Adjusting the Bookshelf Height (If Necessary)
- LOOSEN BOLTS: Loosen the bolts on the threaded rods.
- MOVE DECK: Slide the deck to the desired new position.
- RETIGHTEN BOLTS: Retighten the bolts to secure the deck in the new position.

### END:
- The skateboard bookshelf is now ready to use and show off.
```

instruct00644.title: Clear Snow the Laziest Way Imaginable
instruct00644.text: In the true Olympic spirit I wanted to test a truly effortless method of clearing snow off your car, steps or driveway that even Homer would be proud of. This is a concept that I've wanted to try out for over a decade and finally got around to it. I found a few links and videos that describe the method (after the fact); so this is not an original idea. The idea is very simple: put out a tarp or plastic sheet prior the snowfall and pull it away at a strategic time. The original concept was to have a really giant tarp which covers the driveway (cars), walkways and steps which could be pulled into the street with a vehicle. This is actually against the law in most jurisdictions (transferring your snow onto the street). So if you are going to do this, you'll need to figure out a way to pull it into your yard. If you try this please let me know how it went and expect people to think you are crazy (check out the guy stopped in his tracks in the animated gif above!).***Safety Warning: The tarp or plastic sheet is extremely slippery when covered in snow. Make sure that any potential pedestrian doesn't take a major spill on your property!*** All you really need is a tarp, plastic sheeting (even the bag your mattress came in). I needed the firewood to keep the tarp from flying away and the twine is to provide some towing options. The fully scaled version of this concept will cover a lot more ground, and I was considering using my van to pull out the tarp. If you get to that scale you should consider a more robust tarp tie off (wrap a ball in the corners and tie around the ball or rock as explained inthis bookand image). In this case I just used the existing grommets with a couple lengths of twine. The name of the knot is a "Lark's Head" (thanks to mhjii for the name). You basically want to cover the area in question and make sure the tarp does not fly away. If you are covering a car you could use some bungee cords to tighten around the bottom; I used some firewood to keep the tarp down in this case. After there was a good coat of snow down, I pulled out all the logs so I didn't have to deal with them later. I tied the twine onto the handle of a shovel so I wouldn't have to dig around to find them after the storm. If you scale this up to cover a wider area, you may end up needing some serious horsepower to move the snow. I envisioned using a car to pull the load into the street, but this is not legal and has many potential safety issues. The best approach would be to pull it onto your yard somehow. Let me know if you try this out or if you have a variant on this approach; and remember spring is just around the corner.

```markdown
# Effortless Snow Clearing System Summary

## System Overview
The system is designed to clear snow from surfaces such as driveways, walkways, and cars using a tarp or plastic sheet. The process involves placing the tarp before snowfall and removing it after the snow has accumulated, thus clearing the snow effortlessly.

### System Inputs
- A tarp or plastic sheeting
- Firewood or weights to hold the tarp down
- Twine for towing options
- A shovel with a handle (to tie twine onto)
- Bungee cords (if covering a car)

### System Outputs
- Cleared area free of snow

### Process Steps

START:
1. Acquire a tarp or plastic sheeting suitable for covering the desired area.

PROCESS:
2. Place the tarp or plastic sheet over the area you want to keep clear of snow.
3. Secure the tarp to prevent it from flying away using firewood, weights, or bungee cords.

STORE/DATABASE SUBROUTINE:
4. If covering a car, use bungee cords to tighten the tarp around the bottom of the vehicle.

PROCESS:
5. Wait for the snow to fall and accumulate on the tarp.

DECISION [IF SNOW HAS ACCUMULATED]:
6. IF snow has accumulated on the tarp THEN proceed to step 7.
   ELSE return to step 5 and continue waiting.

PROCESS:
7. Remove any weights or firewood from the tarp to avoid dealing with them later.

PROCESS:
8. Tie the twine onto the handle of a shovel to create a towing mechanism.

PROCESS:
9. Pull the tarp away from the cleared area, bringing the snow with it.

DECISION [IF LEGAL AND SAFE]:
10. IF using a vehicle to pull the tarp is legal and safe THEN proceed to step 11.
    ELSE pull the tarp manually into your yard (go to step 12).

PROCESS:
11. Use a vehicle to pull the tarp with the snow into the street or a designated area.

OUTPUT:
12. The area is now clear of snow.

END:
13. Store the tarp and other materials for future use.
14. System process is complete.

### Safety Warning
- Ensure the tarp or plastic sheet does not pose a slip hazard to pedestrians.
- Do not transfer snow onto the street if it is against local laws.
- Consider the safety implications if using a vehicle to pull the tarp.

### Feedback Loop
- If you try this method, share your experiences to improve the system.
- Be prepared for the possibility that others may find the method unconventional.

### Seasonal Reminder
- Remember that spring is approaching, implying less need for the system in the near future.
```

instruct00520.title: Turn a Pencil Drawing Into a Capacitive Sensor for Arduino
instruct00520.text: Did you know? You can make pencil drawings reactive to touch for use with your projects! It's really easy, and gives you a lot of flexibility in making interfaces for whatever microcontroller project you're making. I put this together as part of my UnoJoy project, where we're using the Arduino as a platform from which to explore how we interact with video games. You can check out more of our projects for UnoJoy at unojoy.tumblr.com, or more of our other projects at the Exertion Games Lab. You'll need the following: A pencil - the softer the lead, the better Some 1+Megaohm resistors Paperclips - make sure they're bare metal, not coated in plastic Wire An Arduino Clear tape (optional) There are 3 ideas going on here: 1 - When you touch a conductive object, you create a certain degree of capacitance. This increases the ability of the conductive material you touched to store a charge. 2 - We can create a cheap capacitive sensor by measuring how long it takes for a piece of conductive material to go from a grounded state to a higher potential state when pulled up to that higher state through a resistor. The higher the capacitance, the longer it will take the conductive material to be pulled up to the high state. 3 - Graphite conducts electricity. You may have seen this before in the Drawdio project, where they use a pencil trace to create sound. Therefore, if we take our conductive pencil line, pull it to ground, then try and pull it to a higher state, we can measure how long it takes, and if we're touching the drawing, it will take longer to get to a high state than usual. Conveniently, we can use the Arduino to automatically pull our trace to ground on and off. If we attach a pull-up resistor to our line, when the ground connection inside the Arduino is turned off, everything attached to the pin will start to be pulled up to VCC. So, our circuit diagram will look something like the above. We use an external pull-up resistor rather than the Arduino's internal pin pull-up resistors since we need much more resistance than the 30K ohm internal ones, otherwise, the resistance of the graphite tends to dominate and prevent the sensor from working. Now to put everything together! First, draw something - You'll want to follow the following rules: - Make a big filled area at the edge of the paper - this is where you'll connect your wire to the drawing via paperclip. - Make sure all of your drawing is connected - you'll only be able to read from parts that are all touching. - Re-trace over your lines at least once or twice - you'll want to get some nice, thick lines of graphite on the paper. Now take one side of your wire and connect it to a paper clip - you can just strip it and wrap the wire around the clip, but you might want to solder it make sure it stays on. Connect the wire up like so: Then load the attached code to your Arduino. You may need to make some changes at the top of the code to get the correct cutoff value for your particular drawing, and you may need to go and re-trace over your drawing some more to get the parts of your drawing that are further away to work properly. Once you get it working, you can take some clear tape and cover up your drawing - this will decrease its sensitivity a bit, but it will keep your drawing from smudging as people touch it. I've put together a full video game controller with this as part of the UnoJoy project, and there will be a video over at unojoy.tumblr.com in a couple of days.

```markdown
# Touch Reactive Pencil Drawing System

## System Overview
This system allows the creation of touch reactive interfaces using pencil drawings, which can be used with microcontroller projects. The pencil graphite acts as a conductive material to create a capacitive sensor that interacts with an Arduino. Changes in capacitance are measured by the time it takes for the pencil trace to change from a grounded state to a higher potential state. The system requires a pencil, resistors, paperclips, wire, an Arduino, and optional clear tape.

## System Requirements
- START: Begin system setup.
  - INPUT: Pencil (softer lead recommended).
  - INPUT: 1+ Megaohm resistors.
  - INPUT: Bare metal paperclips.
  - INPUT: Wire.
  - INPUT: Arduino.
  - INPUT: Clear tape (optional).
- END: System requirements are now established.

## Drawing Preparation
- PROCESS: Create a conductive drawing.
  - PROCESS: Draw a filled area on the edge of the paper for wire connection.
    - DECISION [IF]: Is the filled area large enough?
      - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
      - No: Increase the size of the filled area.
  - PROCESS: Ensure all parts of the drawing are connected.
    - DECISION [IF]: Are all parts of the drawing connected?
      - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
      - No: Connect separate parts of the drawing.
  - PROCESS: Retrace over lines to thicken the graphite.
    - DECISION [IF]: Are the lines sufficiently thick?
      - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
      - No: Retrace over the lines again.
- END: Drawing is prepared and ready for connection.

## Circuit Assembly
- PROCESS: Connect wire to paperclip.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the connection secure?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Solder the wire to the paperclip for a secure connection.
- PROCESS: Connect the paperclip to the drawing.
- PROCESS: Attach the other side of the wire to an Arduino pin with a pull-up resistor.
- END: Circuit assembly is complete.

## Code Configuration
- PROCESS: Load provided code onto the Arduino.
- PROCESS: Adjust the cutoff value in the code to match the drawing's capacitance.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the correct cutoff value found?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Retrace the drawing or adjust the value again.
- END: Code is configured and the system is operational.

## Final Touches
- DECISION [IF]: Is the drawing working properly?
  - Yes: Proceed to optional taping.
  - No: Troubleshoot the connections and code configuration.
- PROCESS: Optionally, apply clear tape over the drawing to prevent smudging.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the sensitivity acceptable with tape?
    - Yes: Finish the setup.
    - No: Remove tape or adjust sensitivity in the code.
- END: The touch reactive pencil drawing system is now complete and ready for use.

## Additional Resources
- OUTPUT: Links to UnoJoy project and Exertion Games Lab for further exploration.
- END: Additional resources provided.
```

instruct00525.title: German Potato Salad
instruct00525.text: German potato salad is the best potato salad in the world. It's sour and sweet and wonderful. And best of all - NO MAYO! :D (Mayo is the worst. Remember that.) German potato salad is great hot or cold, and it's really easy to throw together. I'm using the recipe from Joy of Cooking, but slightly altered so it's more like my grandmother's. Her German potato salad had whole mustard seeds and no celery, so that's the way I make it too. 2 pounds new or yellow potatoes (I prefer red skinned new potatoes because they're so sweet) 1/2 cup vinegar 1/4 cup water or chicken stock 1 teaspoon mustard seed OR 1/2 teaspoon mustard powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon sugar pinch of paprika 4 slices of bacon 1/2 onion green onions parsley You want to cook them with the skins on - I chose to steam mine in a pressure cooker. (12 minutes at high pressure) You can also boil them on the stove or cook them in the microwave. When they're easily pierced with a knife, they're ready to go! Don't use a fork for testing, you'll break them up too much. :) Once they're cooked, set them aside so they can cool down a bit. Cook the bacon until it's a crisp as you like - I like mine a little more fatty for this salad. Set it aside on paper towels when done. If you're using whole mustard seeds, put them in the saucepan first over medium heat and shake the pan around for a couple minutes until they get a little astringent! If you're using mustard powder, just add it along with everything else. Combine the vinegar, water, mustard, paprika, salt and sugar together in a saucepan and bring to a boil then turn off the heat. While that's coming to a boil, chop up your bacon, a couple of green onions and a few sprigs of parsley. You'll be cooking the onions in the bacon fat - I pour most of it out and keep it for later in the fridge. You really only need 1-2 teaspoons of fat in the pan. I like to cook my onions over medium high heat so the edges will brown just a little bit. It adds extra sweetness to the salad and balances the vinegar out a little bit. :D Just keep an eye on them and don't let them burn! While the onions are cooking, peel and cut your potatoes. It's traditional to peel them, but I tend to leave some of the skins on because they're yummy. Cut the potatoes into eighths - that should give you nice bite size pieces. Eat any bits that fall apart. In the pan you just cooked the onions in, add the potatoes, bacon, parsley and green onions. Mix to combine, and then pour in the dressing and mix again. It will look like too much liquid at first - but don't worry! Just keep it over medium heat and mix it gently and the potatoes will soak up the liquid. :D Once it's all combined, taste test and then serve! It's fantastic hot, but also great out of the fridge. I think it tastes even better the next day.

```markdown
# German Potato Salad System Representation

## Ingredients
- 2 pounds new or yellow potatoes (preferably red-skinned new potatoes)
- 1/2 cup vinegar
- 1/4 cup water or chicken stock
- 1 teaspoon mustard seed OR 1/2 teaspoon mustard powder
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon sugar
- A pinch of paprika
- 4 slices of bacon
- 1/2 onion
- Green onions
- Parsley

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of making German Potato Salad.

### INPUT: Prepare Ingredients
- Gather all necessary ingredients.

### PROCESS: Cook Potatoes
- Cook the potatoes with skins on using one of the following methods:
  - Steam in a pressure cooker for 12 minutes at high pressure.
  - Boil on the stove.
  - Cook in the microwave.
- Check if potatoes are done by piercing with a knife.
- Once cooked, set potatoes aside to cool.

### PROCESS: Cook Bacon
- Cook bacon until desired crispness.
- Set aside on paper towels to drain.

### DECISION [IF]: Using Whole Mustard Seeds?
- [YES]: Toast mustard seeds in a saucepan over medium heat until astringent.
- [NO]: Skip to the next step.

### PROCESS: Prepare Dressing
- Combine the following in a saucepan:
  - Vinegar
  - Water or chicken stock
  - Mustard seed or mustard powder
  - Salt
  - Sugar
  - Paprika
- Bring the mixture to a boil, then turn off the heat.

### PROCESS: Prepare Additional Ingredients
- Chop the bacon, a couple of green onions, and a few sprigs of parsley.

### PROCESS: Cook Onions
- Pour most bacon fat out, keeping 1-2 teaspoons in the pan.
- Cook onions in the bacon fat over medium-high heat until edges brown slightly.

### PROCESS: Prepare Potatoes
- Peel and cut the cooled potatoes into eighths.
- Eat any bits that fall apart.

### PROCESS: Combine Salad
- In the same pan used for onions, add the following:
  - Potatoes
  - Bacon
  - Parsley
  - Green onions
- Mix to combine.

### PROCESS: Add Dressing to Salad
- Pour in the dressing over the potato mixture.
- Mix again, keeping it over medium heat.
- Allow potatoes to soak up the liquid.

### DECISION [IF]: Salad Combined Successfully?
- [YES]: Proceed to taste testing.
- [NO]: Continue mixing over medium heat until combined.

### PROCESS: Taste Test
- Adjust seasoning if necessary.

### OUTPUT: Serve Salad
- Serve hot, or refrigerate and serve cold.
- Note that the salad may taste better the next day.

### END:
- The process of making German Potato Salad is complete.
```
